Ratnarāma Bhāro and his wife Caṃpāvatī Mayī, residents of Sikochẽ, Cāpāgāũ, established the Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa statue and constructed this temple in front of their home in 1681 CE (NS 801). They also installed statues of Hariśaṅkara to the right of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa and Bhavānīśaṅkara to the left, following a day-and-night fire oblation. The donor couple donated 12ropanis of land to sustain the temple's operations. They specified that donations should be made during the annual Vajrabārāhī procession in Caitra and theYẽnyāḥ(IndraJātrā) festival. Lamps were to be lit during these events, as well as throughout the month of Kārtika. Additionally, lamps were to be lit on the first day of the bright fortnight of Bhādra at the temple of Buṅgadyaḥ and during the second annual Vajrabārāhī procession in Kārtika. A ritual offering (dakṣiṇā) of onepaisāwas required on the first day of each solar month. Fruits were also to be displayed at the temple during theYẽnyāḥfestival.

Another inscription, recovered from the house located to the south of Tāpālāchi has been preserved. This inscription is not related to Tāpālāchi Phalcā, but rather records that in 1850 CE (NS 970), a three-bay phalcā was built on the ground floor of the very house from which it was recovered. In the name of Anirudra, his wife had constructed that veryphalcāand endowed land for maintenance by aguṭhī.फल्चामा तापालाछिको दक्षिणतिर भएको घरबाट बरामद अर्को एक अभिलेख सुरक्षित राखिएको छ । उक्त अभिलेख यस फल्चासँग सम्बन्धित नभई बरामद गरिएकै घरको भूमि तलामा नेसं ९७० (सन् १८५०) मा तीन कवलको फल्चा बनाइएको प्रसंग छ । आफ्ना पति अनिरुद्रका नाममा उनकी पत्नीले उक्त फल्चा बनाई जग्गा गुठी राखेका थिए ।

An inscription on Tāpālāchi Phalcā provides information about its construction. According to this inscription, the Phalcā was built with the purpose of facilitating rituals in the name of Viṣṇurāja Bharo (Jośi), his brother Mānyaraja, and their descendants. The installed deities are labeled with numbers ‘1, 2, 3’ (instead of their names being given). These numbers were commonly written above the inscription or lālamohara during the Śāha/Rāṇā period. However, in this case, although the numbers are present, no deity names are mentioned. The inscription details that land was allocated as a guṭhi to support annual rituals, and it includes the names of the guṭhiyāra.यस फल्चाको प्रारम्भिक निर्माणबारे खुल्ने अभिलेख फल्चामा प्राप्त छ । उक्त अभिलेख अनुसार विष्णुराज भारो (जोशी), उनका भाई मान्यराज र तिनका सन्तानहरूको नाममा संस्कार गर्न सुविधा होस् भन्ने हेतु  यो फल्चा बनाइएको प्रसंग छ । नेसं १०३१ (सन् १९११) मा बनाइएको फल्चामा स्थापि मूर्तिहरूको नाम नदिई अङ्कमा ‘१,२,३’ भनी लेखिएको छ । ती अङ्कले जनाएको शब्द अभिलेख या लालमोहरको माथिल्लो भागमा दिइएको हुन्छ । शाह-राणाकालमा अभिलेख र लालमोहर लेखन कार्यमा यस्तो चलन थियो । यहाँ भने अङ्क लेखिए तापनि तिनले जनाएको शब्द अभिलेखमा नखुलाइएका कारण कुन देवदेवीका मूर्ति स्थापना भए भन्ने कुरा अज्ञात छ । अभिलेखमा वार्षिक कर्माका खातिर जग्गा पनि गुठी राखी गुठीयारका नाम खुलाइएका छन् ।

About 80 years after its construction, the Phalcā had dilapidated . In 1990 CE, it was rebuilt with a reduced size by the descendants of the original builders, Nārāyaṇarāja and Badrīrāja Jośi.During this restoration, they replaced the disappeared statue of Viṣṇu with a new one (LAL4055-001).निर्माणको करिब ८० वर्ष पश्चात् फल्चा भत्की बसेको अवस्थामा थियो । नेसं १११० (सन् १९९०) मा प्रारम्भिक निर्माताकै दरसन्तान नारायणराज र बद्रीराज जोशीबाट फल्चाको आकार घटाई पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । यस पुनर्निर्माणका दौरान विगत हाराई सकेको विष्णुमूर्तिको ठाउँमा नयाँ मूर्ति (LAL4055-001) प्रतिस्थापन गरिएको थियो ।

Yakṣa Malla fortified the city of Bhaktapur with defensive walls, gatehouse bastions, and protective moats. Following their construction, the annual repair and maintenance of these structures was delegated to local residents and fortress officials in each respective area. Historical accounts emphasize that members of all four castes contributed significantly to this collective endeavor. This inscription holds particular historical significance as it documents both the Malla kingdom's defensive strategies and the active participation of local communities in safeguarding their city. It stands as an important record of civic-military cooperation during this period.

Raṇajita Malla and his wife Jayalakṣmī conducted a grand fire ritual of 10 million oblations (koṭyāhuti yajña) for their tutelary deity, culminating in the donation of a goldentoraṇa, decorative panels, finials, and roof elements to the Golden Gate. The specific mention of gilded additions rather than full construction suggests this project likely involved the renovation and embellishment of an existing gate rather than building an entirely new structure. The gate features dual inscriptions - one in Sanskrit and another in Newar - flanking its entrance. The present inscription under discussion is the Sanskrit version.

The specific mention of gilded additions rather than full construction suggests this project likely involved the renovation and embellishment of an existing gate rather than building an entirely new structure. The gate features dual inscriptions - one in Sanskrit and another in Newar - flanking its entrance. The present inscription under discussion is the Newar version.

The principal artisans involved in the construction of the Golden Gate were Sabhākara, Karaṇākara, and Ratikara, who performed monthly worship of Mañjuśrī throughout the construction period. Upon completion, they presented ahelepho(a type of metal ornament) to Mañjuśrī as an offering to mark the project's successful conclusion. Interestingly, King Raṇajita Malla also gifted an ornament of identical name and form to Mañjuśrī. Both offerings bear the same inscription date: the 10th of the bright fortnight of Kārtika, NS 875 (1754 CE).

The third inscription on the site, located on the pedestal of five donor statues carved on a single stone, is also in poor condition. As a result, the full details of the inscription cannot be discerned due to letter breakage. However, names such as Gopīdeva, the primary donor of the shrine, along with others like Śaṅkaradeva (also written as Saṃkharadeva) and Vīradeva (also written as Viradeva), can still be identified. This confirms that the statues belong to the donor family. The precise event recorded by this undated inscription remains unclear. It is likely that Gopīdeva commissioned these statues for himself and his family when he established the shrine back in 1663 CE (NS 796).

Four stone inscriptions are engraved on the façade of the temple. In addition to these, inscriptions are also found on the stone surfaces used around the middle tier of the temple, which contain references related to its construction. However, it remains unclear which of these inscriptions specifically pertains to the temple’s construction. This uncertainty arises because the central portions of the inscriptions—where dates would typically be found—are difficult to read due to repeated annual whitewashing and erosion. According to Pruscha (1975, p. 202), the Dyaḥnani temple was constructed slightly earlier, around 1617 CE (NS 737–38) by Sanjajena Śākya, though no primary source is cited.
Among the inscriptions found here, the only one with a legible date is from 1664 CE (NS 784), which records the establishment of aguṭhī(Pruscha 1975, p. 202).

On either side of the western entrance of the temple are four stone slabs bearing inscriptions. One of these is carved on the same pale-yellow stone used in the temple’s construction, suggesting that it dates back to the temple’s original building phase. However, due to lime plastering and erosion, the text is difficult to read, and the date is no longer visible. The inscription lists ritual duties to be performed at the temple and names the responsible individuals.

event_name: Direction for rituals and land endowment
event_description: Another of the four inscriptions on the façade also has an eroded date, though its script indicates it belongs to the late medieval period. It mentions that offerings and meals should be provided to the goddess Cakreśvarī of Ināyalã, to Manideva of Cakrabāhāḥ, and to representatives of Haḥbāhāḥ and Bhinchẽbāhāḥ. It also states that rice-filledpiṇḍapātrasshould be donated to Buṅgadyah and the monastic community of Kwābāhāḥ. In addition, the inscription details ritual items to be offered during the temple’s annual festival (varṣavardhana) and on days of special observances (possiblysaṃvaradiśi(?). The location and measurements of land allocated to finance these activities are also given, though the donor’s name and date are no longer readable.

This inscription details the formation of aguṭhīto carry out annual rituals for the temple, along with the regulations and names of theguṭhiyāras. However, the portion containing the date is eroded and illegible.

The inscription dated to 1710 CE (NS 831) carved on the aniconic stone identified with Indrāyaṇī indicates that the stone was established in that very year. It remains uncertain, however, whether the stone was installed at an already venerated site of Indrāyaṇī or whether thepīṭhaoriginated at this time. Although the date is legible, other portions of the short inscription are fragmentary, rendering the context unclear.

The historicalphalcā(public rest platform) located to the south of thepīṭha—previously renovated by thrice venerable great queen Kṛṣṇakumārī—had deteriorated and was therefore reconstructed as a cement structure under local supervision. At that time, ritual observances were also formally prescribed for the occasions of Śivarātri, Navarātri, Maṅgal Cauthī, and Bālācaturdaśī.
A local family of the Silwal lineage undertook maintenance of the pit containing thepīṭha, adorning it with marble slabs brought from Godāvarī.
With the support of the District Development Committee (Lalitpur), various new structures were added to thepīṭhaprecinct, and the surrounding area was paved with stone.
Residents of Patan, Śaṅkhmūla, and Devakhyaḥ Ṭola jointly organized apīṭhaworship ceremony and, upon its completion, installed a copper inscription (tāmrāpatra) at the Indrāyaṇīpīṭha.
A concrete structure was constructed on the southern side of thepīṭhacomplex and namedIndrāyaṇī Bhajan Ghar(House for Devotional Songs).

When the pinnacle was removed during the renovation of the Bhairavī temple at Nuwakot, sacrificial animals—including buffaloes, goats, and ducks—were dispatched for offerings to various deities. On that occasion, Goddess Taleju also received ritual worship accompanied by the offering of two ducks.नुवाकोट भैरवी मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गर्न गजूर निकाल्दा बलि दिनको लागि विभिन्न देवीदेवतालाई राँगो, बोका, हाँस पठाइएको थियो । सोही क्रममा तलेजु भवानीलाई पनि दुईवटा हाँससहित पूजा गर्न पठाइएको थियो ।

event_name: Endowment of lands for daily worship
event_description: In order to ensure the continuity of worship at the Taleju shrine, Dāmodara Pāṇḍe endowed fields yielding a total of fortymurīof produce to the priest Bhājurāma for the performance of rituals at Taleju.दामोदर पाँडेले तलेजुमा हुने पूजालाई निरन्तरता दिनको लागि पुजारी भाजुरामलाई जम्मा ४० मुरी उब्जनी हुने खेत दिएका थिए ।

event_name: Order to prevent jungle around the Taleju Ghara
event_description: King Rājendrāvikrama Śāha issued a royal directive to protect Ṛṣivana—the area where the Taleju Ghara stands—recognizing it as a site sanctified by the austerities ofṛṣis and as an important location associated with the Bhairavī Procession.राजा राजेन्द्रविक्रम शाहले ऋषिहरूले तपस्या गरेको र भैरवीको जात्रासँग सम्बन्धित महत्त्वपूर्ण ठाउँ हुनाले तलेजु घर रहेको ऋषिवनलाई संरक्षण गर्न आदेश दिएका थिए ।

event_name: Theft of the statue of Taleju
event_description: The image of the Goddess Taleju, which had been kept in a concealed manner on the second floor of the Taleju Ghara, was stolen. Following the theft, a new image was made and installed; however, the original stolen image has never been recovered.तलेजु घरको दोस्रो तलामा गुह्य रुपले राखिएको तलेजुको मूर्ति चोरी भएको थियो । मूर्ति चोरी भएपछि नयाँ मूर्ति बनाएर स्थापना गरिएको थियो । चोरी भएको पुरानो मूर्ति अहिलेसम्म पनि फेला परेको छैन ।

The Taleju Ghara, already in a dilapidated condition, suffered severe cracking during the earthquake. Although the roof on the eastern side sustained damage, the structure itself did not collapse at that time.पहिले नै जीर्ण भइसकेको तलेजु घर भूकम्पले नराम्ररी चर्केको थियो । पूर्वपट्टि छानामा केही क्षति पुगेपनि घर भत्केको थिएन ।

As timely repairs were not undertaken, the building was temporarily covered with plastic sheets to protect it from rain. When these coverings later tore, rainwater entered the structure, resulting in the collapse of the eastern portion of the building.भूकम्पले चर्किसकेको तलेजु घरको समयमै मर्मतसम्भार नभएपछि पानीबाट बचाउनको लागि प्लाष्टिकले छोपेर राखिएको थियो । पछि प्लाष्टिक पनि च्यातिएर वर्षात्‌को पानी पसेपछि पूर्वपट्टिको भाग भत्केको थियो ।

The Government of China expressed its commitment to assist in the restoration and reconstruction of heritage sites damaged by the earthquake in Nuwakot. Accordingly, an agreement was concluded between China and Nepal for the reconstruction of the Taleju Ghara and the conservation and restoration of other damaged monuments. The agreement was signed on behalf of China’s Agency for International Economic Cooperation (AIEC) by Zhang Fan, and on behalf of Nepal’s National Reconstruction Authority by Pitāmbar Ghimire. Responsibility for the conservation work was entrusted to the Chinese Academy of Cultural Heritage, with the stipulation that restoration and reconstruction be completed within forty-five months of the agreement.भूकम्पले क्षति भएका नुवाकोटका सम्पदाहरूको जीर्णोद्धार र पुनर्निर्माण गर्न चीनले सहयोग गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको थियो । त्यसै क्रममा तलेजु घरको पुनर्निर्माण गर्ने लगायत अन्य सम्पदाहरूको जीर्णोद्धार, पुनर्निर्माण गर्न चीन र नेपालबीच सम्झौता भएको थियो । सम्झौतामा चीनको Agency for International Economic Cooperation (AIEC) को तर्फबाट Zhang Fan ले हस्ताक्षर गरेका थिए भने नेपालको राष्ट्रिय पुनर्निर्माण प्राधिकरणको तर्फबाट पिताम्बर घिमिरेले हस्ताक्षर गरेका थिए । जीर्णोद्धारको जिम्मेवारी चीनको Chinese Academy of Cultural Heritage लाई सुम्पिएको थियो । सम्झौता भएको ४५ महिनाभित्र सम्पदाहरूको पुनर्निर्माण, जीर्णोद्धार सम्पन्न गर्ने सम्झौता भएको थियो ।

As part of the restoration process, akṣamāpūjāwas performed for the reconstruction and conservation of the Taleju Ghara and other earthquake-damaged monuments of Nuwakot. The ceremony was attended by the Mayor of Bidur Municipality, Rājan Śreṣṭha, and the Deputy Mayor, Prabhā Bogaṭī.तलेजु घर लगायत भूकम्पले क्षति भएका नुवाकोटका सम्पदाहरूको पुनर्निर्माण र जीर्णोद्धार गर्न क्षमापूजा गरिएको थियो । उक्त पूजामा बिदुर नगरपालिकाका प्रमुख राजन श्रेष्ठ र उपप्रमुख प्रभा बोगटी पनि सहभागी भएका थिए ।

Abhūmipūjā(worship to strengthen the foundation) was conducted for the protection of the foundations of the Taleju Ghara under reconstruction and the seven-storey palace undergoing conservation, with the support of the Government of China. This ritual was attended by the Director General of the Department of Archaeology, Saubhāgya Pradhānāṅga, the Mayor of Bidur Municipality Rājana Śreṣṭha and Deputy Mayor of Bidur Municipality Prabhā Bogaṭī, and other elected representatives.चीन सरकारको सहयोगमा पुनर्निर्माण भइरहेको तलेजु घर एवं जीर्णोद्धार भइरहेको साततले दरबारको जग संरक्षणको लागि भूमिपूजा गरिएको थियो । उक्त पूजामा पुरातत्त्व विभागका महानिर्देशक सौभाग्य प्रधानाङ्ग, बिदुर नगरपालिकाका प्रमुख राजन श्रेष्ठ, उपप्रमुख प्रभा बोगटी लगायत जनप्रतिनिधिहरू पनि सहभागी भएका थिए ।
An inscription on the eaves board records that Judha Thāpā, his wife Bijayālakṣmī, and their children—residents of Thimi—renovated the temple’s roof and installed brass sheets.
A bell was installed in front of the temple entrance.
Locals renovated the temple.
The temple was renovated through the combined efforts of the local government and residents.
Deṣānārāṃ (Dekhānārāyaṇa), Jitanāṃ (Jītanārāyaṇa), Ratnabahādur, Saṣavira, Śaṃkhavīra, Āsāmadu, and others donated a bell at thepīṭhaof Seto Bhairava.
A local couple, Bhāi Śreṣṭha and Sānumāyā Śreṣṭha, installed a stone image of Gaṇeśa at the Hāsadyaḥpīṭhaitself.

Previously, only the abstract stone known as Hāsadyaḥ existed at this site. The then ward chairman of Ward No. 2 of Tokha Municipality took a vow to construct a temple over the stone and built the new temple in 2024 CE (VS 2080). On the ninth day of Caitra of that year, consecration ceremony was performed in the newly constructed temple.
After the completion of the temple, local artists painted an image of white-complexioned Bhairava on the wall of the temple facing the main road.
In memory of the late Kṛṣṇalāla Śreṣṭha, Ratnadevī Śreṣṭha dedicated apatāḥto the new temple.

Prime Minister Bhīmasena Thāpā, together with his wife Bhaktakumārī, constructed the temple at the Janaralabāga (lit. general’s garden). He also endowed lands to form aguṭhīfor performing daily and other periodic rituals at the temple, along with feeding mendicants on various occasions and brahmins on the occasion of Bhīmasena Thāpā’s birthday.
Raṇavīrasiṃha Thāpā (text: Raṇabila), younger brother of Bhīmasena Thāpā, offered a bell at the temple.

The second wife of Bhīmasena Thāpā endowed 77ropanīs of land from various parts of Nepal for theguṭhīto perform various rituals at the temple. The inscription instructs the concerned persons to keep track of the expenses for the rituals and enter the remainder into the deity’s treasury.
The Bhīmasena Thāpā Foundation and the Department of Archaeology collectively renovated the temple.

The old priest house of theBhīmabhakteśvara Guṭhīwas renovated and the office of the Nepal Hotel Byawasayi Samaj, an organization of hotel entrepreneurs, was set up here with the assistance from the Sundhārā Āmā Samuha, a group of elderly ladies from Sundhārā area.

The construction of a temple at the site, previously consisting only of a natural cave, was undertaken in 1859 CE (NS 979) by a Buddhācārya family from Ināco (Indravat Mahāvihāra), Bhaktapur. The inscription preserved in the temple records several names of the donor family, including Amṛtamuni, Dharmavatī, and Maṇithaku, although the portion bearing the name of the principal patron has been worn away. A later inscription dated 1883 CE (NS 1003), recording the construction of asataḥat the same site, reveals that the principal builders of the temple were Jogamuni and his wife Jñānīthaku.गुफामात्र हुने गरेको ठाउँमा मन्दिर बनाउने कार्य नेसं ९७९ (सन् १८५९) मा भक्तपुर इनाचो (इन्द्रवत् महाविहार) निवासी एक बुद्धाचार्य परिवारले गरेका थिए । मन्दिरमा भएको अभिलेखमा निर्माता परिवारमध्ये मुख्य कर्ताको नाम कुँदिएको भाग खिइएको छ । अभिलेखमा अमृतमुनि, धर्मवती, मणिथकु आदि नाम पढ्न सकिन्छ । यस पछि यही स्थानमा सतः बनाई राखिएको नेसं १००३ (सन् १८८३) को अभिलेखमा मुख्य मन्दिर निर्माताको नाम खुल्दछ । ती जोगमुनि र उनकी पत्नी ज्ञानीथकु थिए ।

Members of the same temple-building family later constructed asataḥnear the temple. According to the inscription, the construction work began in 1882 CE (NS 1002) and was completed one year later.मन्दिर निर्माता परिवारबाटै मन्दिर नजिकै एक सतः बनाउने कार्य भयो । नेसं १००२ मा निर्माण कार्य थालिएको थियो भने एक वर्ष पश्चात् समापन भएको कुरा अभिलेखको अन्तमा भनिएको छ ।

Caityarāja and Vikuratna, descendants of the temple builders, later renovated the temple in recognition of their ancestors’ contributions.मन्दिर निर्माताका सन्तति चैत्यराज र विकुरत्नले आफ्ना पूर्खाको कृतिलाई महत्व दिँदै मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरे ।

event_name: Renovation, new construction, land endowment  and guṭhī formation
event_description: Further restoration was carried out in 1949 CE (VS 2006) by descendants of the same family. During this work, the temple and the adjacentcaitya(BKT0710-009) were repaired, and ahiti, a boundary wall, and anothersataḥto the left of the temple were constructed. Lands located in Ināco, Bhaktapur, along with properties in other places, were endowed asguṭhīin the name of the temple. According to the inscription, the income from these endowments was intended to support priests, attendants (avāla), and other necessary personnel, who were to reside at the site and annually celebratevarṣavardhanawith a communal feast on the full-moon day of Kārtika.मन्दिर निर्माताकै सन्ततिले विसं २००६ (सन् १९४९) सालमा मन्दिर र मन्दिरसँगैको चैत्य (BKT0710-009) जीर्णोद्धार गर्नुका साथै हिति, पर्खाल र मन्दिरको बायाँ अर्को सतः थपेका थिए । यिनले भक्तपुर, इनाचोस्थित आफ्नो विर्ता र अन्य विविध ठाउँका जग्गा मन्दिरका नाममा गुठी राखेका थिए । तिनको आयबाट पुजारी, अवाल र अन्य आवश्यक व्यक्तिहरू बसी प्रतिवर्ष कर्तिक शुक्ल पूर्णिमाका दिन वर्षवर्धन मनाई भोज खानुपर्ने कुरा अभिलेखमा परेको छ ।

With the wish for universal well-being, a Mānandhara family from Kathmandu installed a white image of Mañjuśrī in front of the cave within the sanctum.जगत उद्धारको कामनाले काठमाडौंका एक मानन्धर परिवारबाट गर्भगृहको गुफा अगाडि सेतो वर्णको मञ्जुश्री मूर्ति स्थापना भययो ।

event_name: Addition of a pair of metal lion sculptures
event_description: Puṣpakumāra Mānandhara installed a pair of metal lion sculptures in the sanctum in memory of his deceased relatives.आफ्ना मृतक आफन्तजनका नाममा पुष्पकुमार मानन्धरले गर्भगृहमा एक जोडा धातुको सिंह प्रतिमा स्थापना गरे ।

event_name: Installation of pedestal for the statue
event_description: A white marble pedestal was placed within the sanctum, upon which an image of Mañjuśrī was installed in the name of the late Nhuchẽnārāyaṇa Mānandhara of Ḍhokāṭola, Kathmandu.गर्भगृहमा सेतो मार्वलको पेटी हाली त्यसमाथि मञ्जुश्रीको मूर्ति काठमाडौं ढोकाटोल निवासी स्वर्गीय न्हुछेँनारायण मानन्धरको नाममा हालियो ।

King Lakṣmīnarasiṃha Malla himself, issuing a royal decree, installed the inscription, warns that killing is prohibited within the land west of the Svayambhū Caitya, north of the Agnihotra brahmin, east of the wide road, and south of the “old area,” and anyone who does so will incur the sin equivalent to killing Mahādeva. Brahmins, Pradhānas, Khasa, Magaras, andpañcas (local council of five or more members) are kept as witnesses in the royal decree. This inscription is considered the earliest inscription in the Nepali language found in the Kathmandu valley.
The government renovated the temple for the coronation of King Vīrendra.
The temple sustained multiple cracks in the 2015 earthquakes with its western part severely damaged. The temple stood with wooden supports for many years after the earthquakes.
The renovation work of the temple was carried out with the assistance of NRs. 37.1 million received from the Bagmati Provincial government.
Due to the full erosion of text, the content of this inscription cannot be deciphered.

The Phalcā was built as a concrete structure by Rāma Prasāda Śreṣṭha. He had served aspradhānapañca, a post equivalent to a mayor during the Pañcāyata rule. Before the construction, there was open land and some elements of the Phalcā that proved there used to be aphalcāin traditional architecture.
This Phalcā completely collapsed during the 1934 earthquake. Its original function was abandoned and the remnants of the building were used as a platform before it was finally rebuilt in 2012.
The Phalcā was rebuilt in 2012 with the financial support of the Lalitpur Metropolitian City Office and under the supervision of Khapiṃchẽ Youth Club.
The Pashupati Area Development Trust undertook the renovation of the temple's cracked walls. The temple had fallen into disrepair even before the 2015 earthquakes, which further damaged it.

राजा सुरेन्द्र विक्रम शाहको राज्यकालमा खोकनाको कोथुपुषुली निवासी काश्यप गोत्रका भिख्वाल र उनकी श्रीमती बिसलक्ष्मिले परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर पहिले नै निर्माण गरिएको चैत्यको जीर्णोद्धार गरेका थिए । प्रत्येक वर्ष आश्विन शुक्ल ४ को दिनमा वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । त्यसको लागि ३ जव खेत गुठी राखिएको थियो । ललितपुरको चक्र महाविहारका जीवराज वज्राचार्यले चैत्य जीर्णोद्धार गर्दा पूजाको विधिविधान गर्ने पुरोहितको काम गरेका थिए ।
The Department of Archaeology had started reconstructing this Temple before the 2015 earthquakes. The reconstruction halted due to the earthquakes and was completed only in 2018 CE.

The floor in front of the main entrance is paved with tiles made of marble. 28 tiles are inscribed with the names of Prime Minister Bam Bahādura Rāṇā and his descendants. The inscriptions bear no date.

The temple had aged over time before the 2015 CE earthquake. Reconstruction was undertaken after the earthquake, funded by the Asian Development Bank and the Urban Development Ministry's Bagmati Civilization conservation committee. Though the overall restoration was completed in October 2022 (Kartik 6, 2079).
"Māhā" Viṣṇu and his wife Manamayi, residents of Bholāchẽ (text: Bhulāche) Ṭola in Bhaktapur, established the Bhīmasena statue and built the temple.
A Brahmin named Candra and his family built the Pauḍela Pāṭī (object no. DPC0010-005).

Lakṣmī, a resident of Dāpcā, donated a land parcel with an annual yield of 10murīsspecifically for the worship of Viśvakarmā. However, as of July 2024 CE, no statue of Viśvakarmā is present at the temple. It remains unclear whether the statue was stolen or relocated elsewhere.
The locals converted thepāṭīinto a temple by establishing a Kṛṣṇa statue inside (see 'description').

Following the theft of the original metal Kṛṣṇa statue in 1970 CE (VS 2027), a replacement was installed for the procession. The Kṛṣṇa statue enshrined in thepāṭīwas a personal donation from a local Brahmin named Khilarāja, intended for daily worship (see 'description').
The temple was renovated at the initiation of locals.
Rāṇā Prime Minister Candra Śamśera renovated thehiti.
The Pashupati Area Development Trust carried out reconstruction of the temple, as it was badly damaged in the 2015 earthquakes.

The Saṅkaṭā Ilānani was renovated with financial support (totalling 13,000 rupees) offered by thesaṅghamembers, some Brahmins, the Ṭhakurī Kings, Daivajñas and Dhaṃgūs. These funds also allowed a large metal statue of Saṅkatā to be established on the Ilānani's ground floor. The statue is a replica of the smaller one kept in a secret space dedicated to Cakrasamvara. It was designed by Bahādura Vajrācārya of Aki Bāhāḥ. Local women donated the metals which were used for its construction.
The copperplate inscription on the Digi’s first floor informs its reader that theāḥjusrenovated the secret space dedicated to Cakrasamvara. It lists the name of theāḥjusresponsible.
The rectangular courtyard located to the south of the Digi was renovated by the members of the Kvāḥ Bāhāḥsaṅgha.
The inscription mentions that Padmaratna Dhākhvāḥ and his wife Sānunānī offered a crown to Saṅkaṭā.

event_name: Construction of a dedicated place (pura) to Cakrasamvara
event_description: The inscription records that Dhanadevaju, Satamuniju, Ratnacandraju, Dhanapatiju, Desarājaju and Ratnadevaju constructed a dedicated place (pura) for Cakrasamvara. This can be found on the topmost floor of one of the buildings in the courtyard. In doing so, they also made an offering of a gilded pinnacle, garlands and three-layered umbrella. The inscription mentions that this cost 140mohora taṃkā.

event_name: Construction of wall, offering toraṇa and a pinnacle
event_description: During the reign of King Pārthivendra Malla, two brothers Śivakalyāṇa (text: Śivakaryāna) and Nvamisiṃha built walls and installed a door at thedyaḥchẽwhile also offering an ornamented arch (toraṇa). They also offered a stone throne and a finial in the name of the Ajimā. Moreover, they established their statues at thedyaḥchẽ.

Mādhavasiṃha and his family from the Vatuṭolaconstructed the god house for Lũmadhi Ajimā and installed a finial. As thedyaḥchẽis known to be already in existence in 1684 CE (NS 804), they may have rebuilt it on this occasion.

During the annual procession of Lũmadhi Ajimā, a fight broke out between the Vatu and Te Bāhāḥ factions of the members associated with thedyaḥchẽand the Vatu faction was defeated. Afterward, both factions came to an agreement not to cause any dispute again in the future.
Mānandhara Gunavanta and his family members offered two tiers of brass roofs to the Ajimā.
Rasasiṃ and his wife Vārasvabhā from the Vatuṭolaoffered a palanquin with a cover of gilded sheets to be used for the procession of the Ajimā.
Bhāranarasiṃ of Te Bāhāḥ endowed lands to set up a trust (guthi) for offering a he-goat to both palanquins of Vatu Lũmadhi Ajimā and Te Bāhāḥ Bhadrakālī during their annual procession.

Mānandhara Lakṣamana and his wife Nhuchemāyā from Ḍillībajāra renovated the lion throne of Lũmadhi Ajimā in the name of his deceased grandfather Kulamāna, grandmother Mejumatī, father Nhuchenārāyaṇa, and mother Lakṣmīkumārī.
The Ratnaloka Memorial Trust offered a copper flag on either side of Lũmadhi Ajimā in memory of the deceased Lokamāna Jośī and Ratnakumārī Jośī.
Thedyaḥchẽwas renovated with the assistance of NRs. 100 thousand from King Gyanendra and donations from various people. Locals contributed to the renovation with voluntary labor.
The 2015 earthquakes left thedyaḥchẽwith multiple cracks.
In the course of rebuilding thedyaḥchẽ, the Ratnaloka Memorial Trust offered a metal ornamented arch (toraṇa) on top of the entrance to thedyaḥchẽ.

event_name: Completion of reconstruction of the dyaḥchẽ
event_description: It was rebuilt with funds from the Kathmandu Metropolis and the participation of the locals. A total of NRs. 16.6 million was spent on the reconstruction.

event_name: Constructionof a stone pillar with a statue of monkey
event_description: Rudrasiṁha Bhāro and his family installed a stone pillar with a statue of a monkey holding an oil lamp.

There is a bell hanging on a stone beam. The bell was donated in NS 918. The stone beam retains the date NS 830. It appears that the earlier bell was donated in NS 830 and after it was broken or lost the second one was installed in NS 918.
Hari Bhāro (son of the Rudrasiṁha Bhāro) donated theśikharakūṭa caitya.
A person named Kṛṣṇa installed a bell in front of theśikharakūṭa caitya.
Bhīmadeva constructed the Nṛtyeśvara Temple.
Donation of the embossed metaltoraṇain front of the three small holes which are worshipped as Nṛtyeśvara.
Renovation of the temple
The temple suffered major damage during the 1934 CE earthquakes. Photos taken afterward reveal significant structural harm, yet the temple remained standing and did not collapse.

In the aftermath of the 1934 CE earthquakes, the temple underwent reconstruction under the direction of Prime Minister Juddha Śamśera. The rebuilding process took place eight years after the earthquakes. Notably, the new bricks used for reconstruction were inscribed with the words “Śrī 3 Juddha 1998,” signifying the restoration in the year 1941 CE (VS 1998).

The temple restoration was made possible through funding from the US Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation. The temple was restored in a collaborative effort between the Department of Archaeology, the Kathmandu Metropolitan City and the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust (KVPT).Guided by historical photographs the temple's original appearance prior to the 1934 CE earthquakes was recreated.

Following the damage caused by the 2015 CE earthquakes, the US Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation once again provided the financial support for the renovation. Collaboratively, the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust (KVPT) and the Department of Archaeology carried out the restoration.
The Phalcā collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes.
The Department of Archaeology rebuilt the Phalca and a water tap next to it in cooperation with the Shankharapur Municipality at a cost of NRs. 2.3 million.

Rāṇā Prime Minister Jaṅga Bahādura's queen from Gorakhpur built this temple and donated a vast tract of land as a religious endowment. A detailed account of the land allocated by the Gorakhpur queen for daily worship, annual rituals, cleaning, regular music, and temple maintenance is inscribed on the large stone slab installed in the south wing of thesataḥ. The temple was built six years after Jaṅga Bahādura's death. The queen had made arrangements for daily, periodic, and anniversary rituals, and even provided for the musicians and workers by allocating specific crops.
The Gorakhpur queen installed a bell on the plinth in front of the temple after the construction of the temple.
The temple was severely damaged in the 2015 earthquakes and consequently restored by the Department of Archaeology in 2022.
The Temple was renovated as part of the Bhaktapur Development Project, which was funded by the Federal Republic of Germany.

All bays of the phalcā were closed. The Ṭola Sudhārā Samiti installed doors on the eastern and northern sides, allegedly to prevent the monument being used by homeless persons. In a photo published inPruscha(1975, vol. 2, p. 181, P-186), the Phalcā can be seen in the rightr corner without doors and closed bays.

event_name: Installation of two lionsin Dupāt Gaṇeśa Mandira and formation of a group of devotees.
event_description: This historical event is related to the Dupāt Gaṇeśa Mandira(LAL2110). For more details see the historical events of the monument.
The Capaḥ was dismantled and replaced by a four storey concrete structure with seven bays and concrete pillars (Maharjan2018, 299).
This historical event is related to the Dupāt Gaṇeśa Mandira (LAL2110). For more details see the historical events of the monument.
This inscription is attached to the wall of the ground floor. This inscription no longer legible.

event_name: Installation of an Gaṇeśa image inside the Dupāḥ Gaṇeśa Mandira
event_description: A stoneGaṃśalawas installed in thecapāḥ.Dhanavajra Bajracharya(2056) has interpreted this as beingGaneśa. The name of thethakāliis given as Parīdeva Bhāvo. The inscription is attached to the wall of the ground floor.

event_name: Installation of a stone toraṇa and matakārana in Dupāt Gaṇeśa Mandira and formation of a group of devotees.
event_description: This historical event is related to the Dupāt Gaṇeśa Mandira (LAL2110). For more details see the historical events of the monument.

Around VS 2040-45, members of the local Jyāpu community established a library in this Capāḥ. The photo published by Pruscha (1975 II: 188) used for describing the Dupāt Gaṇeśa also shows the board of the library.The library is currently housed in the Pichū Phalcā at the rear of the same building.

event_name: Regulation of irrigation management in a rural area of eastern Lalitpur and the Sanāḥ Guṭh's role in this
event_description: This inscription is attached to the eastern wall of the first floor. The historical event mentioned in this inscription is not related to thiscapāḥ. Rather, the inscription mentions the rules and regulations around the management of an irrigation canal in a rural area of eastern Lalitpur. This is the responsibility of the Sanāḥ Guṭhī. The text in this inscription has been partly copied from the inscription dated NS 803 referring to King Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur. The same text is also mentioned inNepālikabhūpavaṁśāvalī(19.1.116a/I).
This inscription is attached to the wall of the ground floor. This inscription is no longer legible.

event_name: Installation of the Statue of Bhīmasena
event_description: Toyūju Thaku, amahāpātraof the lower Kvāḥ Bāhāḥ, installed the Bhīmasena Statue, formed aguṭhī,and made a land endowment.

This event is not related to the Bhīmasena Temple. On the bottom part of the copperplate inscription, which records the consecration of the Bhīmasena Statue, it is mentioned that King Mahendra Malla constructed theTao Devala(the Taleju Mandira) in 1564 CE (NS 660).The copperplate inscription only mentions NS 684 Mārgaśīrṣa. The date mentioned on a record that details themandira’s construction, also mentions tenth day of the dark fortnight in Mārgaśīrṣa on NS 684 (Vajrācārya G.2033, 116).

event_name: Installation a Stone Inscription, Praising Bhīmasena, and Establishment of a Statue of Draupadī
event_description: King Pratāpa Malla established this stone inscription praising Bhīmasena. It also records the installation of the Draupadī Statue in the sanctum.
A Mānandharaguṭhī, comprising of thirty-seven members and headed by Mānandhara Jesta Taosi, offered thistoraṇato Bhīmasena.
Mānadhra Jayadeo (Mānandhara Jayadeva) offered it to Bhīmasena.
Rañjikā (Rañjitakāra) Jayadharmma from Cikãmugala Ṭola offered it to Bhīmasena.

The temple was renovated during the reign of King Mahendra, when Pannā Māna Siṃha Malla, one of the descandants of Toyūju Thaku, was the Ward Chairperson. The local community also actively participated in the renovation process.

event_name: Replacing Jhĩgaṭī Roof with Copper Sheets
event_description: The upper two roofs of the temple were already cladded in gold-plated brass. Thejhĩgaṭītiles of the first roof were also replaced with copper sheets. This work was supported by the office of the Ward Number 20, the Department of Archaeology, and local patrons.

event_name: Installation of a Lion Pillar and Offering a Patāḥ
event_description: During the reign of King Rājendra Vikrama Śāha, Tulādhara Rāvata and Mānandhara Jaganārāyaṇa (Jagannārāyaṇa), residents of Maru Ṭola, offered the lion pillar including a gold-plated lion statue resting atop of it. They also offered thepatāḥto the deity.
Dhanalakṣmī, her son Saṅkhanārā̃, and other family members jointly repaired the Jalaharyoparijinālaṅkṛta Caitya (KAT0920-005) during the reing of King Surendra Śāha (r. 1847-1881).
Since the inscription is heavily damaged, its content remains obscure.
Bhelāchẽ Phalcāwas renovated in VS 2032 (1975 CE), this time using concrete.
In 2017 CE, Bhelāchẽ Phalcā was renovated by the Bhelāchẽ community and Lalitpur Metropolitan City in a traditional Newar style.

Guhya Lakṣmī Brāhmaṇī commissioned this Phalcā. He instructed that beaten rice 1phã, syābaji1mānā, soy beans 1mānā,bean 1prasthafish and 1prasthaginger should be distributed at Bhelāchẽ Phalcā on the full moon day of Bhādra. Three lamps should also be lit on this day.
Bhelāchẽ Phalcāwas completely destroyed in the 1934 earthquake. Pūrṇalāla Mahāju and his wife and son organised for it to be rebuilt.
The deterioratingsataḥwas reconstructed through the collaborative efforts of Nepal's Department of Archaeology, the Bālakumārī Guṭhī, and the local community.
The Hanumandhoka Palace Supervision Office sponsored the repair of Pīra Pāṭī.

Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā commissioned the establishment of Jaṅganandabhogeśvara. It is possible that he built the temple together with his wife, Nandakumārī, as the temple's name includes the term "Nanda" attached to Jaṅga Bahādura's name.
The Pashupati Area Development Trust undertook the renovation of Jaṅganandabhogeśvara.
A donor got a stone pillar with a figure of Garuḍa on top erected in front of the Temple. The name of the donor is unclear because the inscription on the pillar is not readable.

During the reign of Prime Minister Mohana Śamśera, a person named Komala Prasāda Gautama got a stone pillar erected south of the Ādinārāyaṇa Temple. Devotional songs were performed throughout the night on that occasion, along with offering food to Brahmins and grains to the poor.

event_name: Construction of the present temple structure
event_description: As mentioned above in the description, this place was a small shrine under an open sky before the present temple structure was constructed by Ratnamāna Śreṣṭha and Īndramāna Śreṣṭha in 1955 CE.

event_name: Offering cakra, gaḍā, śaṅkha and padma
event_description: Prabhu Nārāyaṇa, Karga Nārāyaṇa, Tulsī Māyā Śreṣṭha and their family members from Tājāchẽ in Sunṭola erected stone pillars in front of the Temple with figures ofcakra,gadā,śaṅkha, andpadmaon their top.
Mādhava Nārāyaṇa, Īśvara Bhagata, and Śiva Bhagata, the sons of Nārāyaṇabhakta and Herāmāyā Śreṣṭha of Sunṭola, offered the bell to the Temple.

This Garuḍa statue is installed by Nārāyaṇabhakta Śreṣṭha as a replacement of the initially enshrined Garuḍa statue, which was stolen sometime before 1991 CE. Locals recall that the newly installed statue is half the size of the previous one.
The family members of late Haribhakta Śreṣṭha and Ṭikāmāyā Śreṣṭha funded the renovation.
Just a few days after the renovation, the 2015 earthquakes collapsed the Temple.
The Department of Archaeology reconstructed the Temple that collapsed during the 2015 earthquakes.
The roof of the Temple started to leak soon after it was reconstructed by the Department of Archaeology following the 2015 earthquakes. The Department repaired the roof in 2021 CE.
Māhīlā and his wife Pañcamāyā constructed adharmadhātu maṇḍalato the north of the Licchavicaitya.

The mantraOṃ maṇi padme hūṃis engraved in low relief on the eastern side of the stūpa. It is inscribed in Rañjana script.It does not bar a date but it is possible to compare it with other inscriptions, dated from the 1350's.

event_name: Initial construction of the first Dharaharā
event_description: Bhīmasena Thāpā constructed the Bhīmasena Stambha in the form of a minaret in front of Bāga Darabāra. The inscription recording the event is at the National Archives. It states that Bhīmasena Thāpā constructed Dharaharā in 1824 CE (VS 1881).

event_name: Initial construction of the second (this) Dharaharā
event_description: A year after the construction of the first Dharaharā, Queen Lalitatripurāsundarī also built a similar tower a stump of which still survives. A gold-plate inscription posted on top of its entrance mentions that she built the tower and offered a finial in 1825 CE (VS 1882).
Dharaharā was struck by lightning in 1856 CE and was renovated in 1869 CE.
The tower collapsed again in the 1934 earthquakes. It broke into a few pieces and the rubbles fell inside the boundary wall of Dharaharā.

A photo taken soon after the 1934 earthquake shows Dharaharā’s lower four stories intact. However, the inscription installed by Juddha Śamśera after the renovation of Dharaharā in 1936 CE (VS 1992) states that ‘only two stories had remained intact after the earthquake and the upper floors were raised during the renovation’ (Tevārī and others VS 2019, p.8-9). Probably, the upper two of the four floors that remained intact were not in good condition and were dismantled before the renovation.
The outer walls of Dharaharā received a whitewash in 1945 CE (VS 2002), which then cost NRs. eight thousand.
Dharaharā collapsed in the 2015 earthquake, killing a few people and injuring dozens of others.
The stump of Dharaharā that now survives is covered with glass from the sides and metal sheets on top. Meanwhile, a new concrete tower has been erected next to the remaining stump of Dharaharā.

Within a decade of its construction, the tower constructed by Bhīmasena Thāpā collapsed in the earthquakes of 1833 CE. On the other hand, the tower built by the queen survived the earthquakes but was cracked from top to bottom as seen in a painting byOldfield.

monument_name: Nāulegāũ fountain and stone memorial pillar
event_description: The pillar contains at least 15 lines of text inscribed in a Nāgarī script. The text is eroded in some places.No date could be identified.

event_name: Instructions for maintaining the pond, Nāgapokharī
event_description: The inscription is not related to the temple itself but is associated with the adjacent Nāgapokharī. This inscription outlines the annual obligation to clean the Nāgapokharī on the 1st day of dark fortnight of Śrāvaṇa. Oversight of this task is assigned to the localpramāṇa(official), and households situated along the northern water channel are responsible for its upkeep. Failure to comply results in a fine of twodamma, imposed as royal penalty by thepramāṇa. Furthermore, buffaloes are explicitly prohibited from entering or bathing in the pond.

event_name: Damages from the 1934 earthquakes and renovation
event_description: According to local informants, a portion of the Sataḥ's roof collapsed in the 1934 earthquakes and was renovated by the concerned Guthi a few months later.

event_name: Damages to the roof and renovation
event_description: Local informants say that parts of the roof began leaking during the rainy season in mid-2010 CE. As a temporary solution, the concerned Guthi installed corrugated tin sheets on the roof.

The Sataḥ was badly damaged in the 2015 earthquakes and subsequently dismantled. It is yet to be reconstructed even after six years of its collapse in the earthquakes. The Department of Archaeology had initiated the administrative process for the reconstruction of the Sataḥ but the process was halted due to the dispute with the Guthi members regarding the Sataḥ’s ownership. The woodworks of the Sataḥ are stored behind the Sataḥ for safety.
Santakumārī, the wife of Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā, constructed the temple and bestowed upon it the name Santabhogeśvara in her own honor.

event_name: Offering of a pāṭī and an okhala
event_description: An inscription dated of 1908 CE (ŚS 1965) installed along the wall of the north wing records the donation of apāṭīand anokhalaby one Vāsudeva Jyotirvid (astrologer) and his wife Aṃvikā.Reading of the inscription by Rajendra Shakya:स्वस्तिश्री शाके १८३० श्रीसंवत् १९६५ साल कार्तिक शुदि ११ वुधवाररे कार्तिक २० गतेमा गोर्षा लुइटेल वस्ने लेफटें वासुदेव ज्योतिर्विद्... ... ... ... ... अंविका देकं तस्य तृतिय जात दिट्ठा देविभगत ज्योतिर्विद् ...... ... तस्य वागांगि भार्ज्यायां पुर्णकुमारि देव्यांतत्पुत्रलेफटें भुमिनंदनं १ पुन्यराज १ लिलावल्लभ १ कालिकाप्रसाद १ पुत्रियां मनोरमा १ कृष्णमाया १ नर्मदा १ रत्नकुमारी १ पौत्रायां दामोदर शहित सकल परिवाराःयां आयुरारोग्य सांत्यर्थं इहलोके सुखप्राप्ती परलोकेःमोक्ष प्राप्ती कामनया श्री गुरु महाराज चंदंनाथ स्वामि प्रशन प्राप्ती कामनार्थं यहमकान श्री चंदंनाथ स्वामि पृतय समर्पंयामि गोगृहप्रलोकशुधारणानिमित्त डिट्ठा देविभक्त डिट्ठेनि पुर्णकुमारिले श्री परमेश्वर प्रीति गरि चढायाको जस्ले भत्काइ विगारि देला तेसलाइ माहापातक लागि कुहिहेला फकिर फकेडा वाहेक दुनिञाले यो पाटिमा रहनाको मन गया श्री गुरुकी संवार तोतलाई ... ...को घ्यू धार्नि ६ पठाइ भत्के विग्रेको वनाउनु पुण्य होलापुजाहारि भंडारी कोठारिले पजनी गर्दा सो पाटी वीग्य्रानन परमेस्वरले सजाय गरुं भनि पाटि र वषलस्मेत चढाञ्यू सो दत्तपरदत्त वा नोहरोच वसुंधरा सद्धी वर्ष सहा... णि विष्ठायाजायत्तकमि ॥ १ ॥Synopsis:On Wednesday, the 11th of the bright fortnight of Kārtika in 1908 CE (ŚS 1965), Lieutenant Vāsudeva Jyotirvid (astrologer) and [his wife] Aṃvikā, along with their family, from the Luiṭela of Gorkha offered a pāṭī along with an okhala (stone mortar) in the name of venerable guru Mahārāja Candananātha.

Synopsis of the inscription:On Thursday, the 5th of the bright fortnight of Māgha in 1878 CE (VS 1934), Harkadeva Upādhyā made a certain donation in the name of venerable Candananātha of Dīpāyalagāũ of Jumlā.
Although no records have been found regarding the construction of the temple, local residents say that it was built by Vira Śamśera Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā (1852-1901) and the temple was named after him.
Since 20-30 years, the temple was slightly tilted. The 2015 earthquake damaged it heavily.
The temple was rebuilt by the Department of Archaeology of Nepal in 2020.

event_name: Dispatching of woodcutters to cut down tree
event_description: The woodcutters were dispatched to cut down the trees in the jungle for timbers to build the temple.
Timbers of thesāla(shorea robusta) variety were obtained from various places like Nālā, Panautī, Caukoṭa, Vābhudvã, and Yãlādvã for building the temple.

event_name: Beginning of making of temple bells
event_description: The crafting of the temple bells (phaygaṃ) to be hung below the eaves of the temple roof started from this day onward.

event_name: Beginning of works related to timbers and foundation
event_description: Carpenters began their woodworks. Digging the pits for the foundation also began from this day onward.
The temple named “Ṅātāpula” was demolished to build a new “Ṅātāpola” temple.
From this day onward, the brick-firing process began in various locations throughout Bhaktapur. Brick firing continued uninterrupted until the 11th of the dark fortnight of Jyeṣṭha.
The digging for the temple’s foundation commenced from this day onward.
The foundation stone was laid, marking the beginning of the temple’s construction. The foundation stones were consecrated, and multiple levels of plinths were built.
The crafting of the temple’s finial commenced.

event_name: Obtainment of woods form various places
event_description: Timbers of thethāsĩandmūsĩvariety were obtained from Vābhu and Nhaygāṃ (lit. seven villages, which are Banepā, Nālā, Sāṃgā, Dhulikhela, Panautī, Caukoṭa, and Khaḍpu) for the construction of the temple.
To build the temple, groups led by soldiers, including Rājaphauḍa, Dhana Khārisā, Śaṃkarasiṃ, and Bhāyadeva, brought in the finest quality stones from Kotkhālvahaṃ (Hāttīvana).
The topmost roof of the temple was installed.

event_name: Completion of roofing on topmost tier and performance of propitiatory rituals
event_description: The topmost roof tier was completely tiled with traditional materials. Supplies for raising the ceremonial banner (betālipatāḥ) atop the finial were sent from the Nhaygāṃ (literally, "seven villages") cluster east of Bhaktapur. Following the completion of the top tier's roofing, special propitiatory rituals (śānti-svasti) were performed, and the necessary ritual paintings were commissioned.

During the construction of the temple, King Bhūpatindra Malla performed akoṭyāhutiyajña, a fire oblation of 10 million oblations. He gifted a golden crown to the priest who performed the rituals. This crown is still safely kept by the Karmācārya priests of the Tripura Vidyāpīṭha Āgama.

The statue of Siddhilakṣmī, the main deity, was established inside the sanctum on this day. The finial was also installed on top of the uppermost tier on the occasion, marking the completion of the construction. The three miniature temples were also built around the temple.
On this day, a bell was offered to the temple. The fact that there was a large bell inside the temple is known from a survey conducted by Surendra Jośī in 1977 CE.

event_name: Collapse of upper tier in 1934 earthquakes
event_description: The uppermost tier of the temple collapsed in the 1934 earthquakes. The damage inspired a still-popular rhyming proverb: "Ṅātāpola chatā madu, Bhailaḥdyaḥ patā madu." This translates to "One roof of Ṅātāpola [was lost], and the Bhairava temple was completely gone," vividly illustrating the earthquake's impact.

A significant renovation was carried out in 1963 CE. During this renovation, the brick face of the stepped plinth was replaced with red-colored cement mortar, and the face of the sanctum was also renewed.

The Bhaktapur Municipality renovated the temple, aiming at reducing the roof load. The thickness of the mud layer was decreased, the spacing of the rafters was doubled, and the cross-section of the rafters was reduced. Additionally, the two central struts on the lowest level facing south, thetoraṇafacing north and west, the northern bracket of the western door, and the 36 plaques on the capitals and lintels were all renewed.
The uppermost roof sustained damage in the 2015 earthquakes.

Following earthquake damage, the Bhaktapur Municipality undertook a comprehensive renovation of the temple. The public participated extensively in volunteer efforts, and significant financial and material contributions were received, enabling the project's completion by the end of 2020 CE.

event_name: Arrangement of grant for the Rāmeśvara
event_description: Aṃśuvarman classified the prominent sacred sites of his time into three categories and arranged for state financial grants, as recorded in the stone inscription at Hāḍīgāũ. In the first category were Paśupatinātha, Cāṅgunārāyaṇa, Guṃvihāra, Mānavihāra, and Rājavihāra, each receiving a grant of six purāṇa and two paṇa. In the second category were Rāmeśvara, along with Haṃsagr̥hadeva and Māneśvara, each receiving a grant of threepurāṇaand onepaṇa.अंशुवर्माले तत्कालीन समयमा प्रसिद्ध रहेका देवस्थलहरूलाई तीन श्रेणीमा विभाजन गरी राज्यको तर्फबाट आर्थिक अनुदान दिने व्यवस्था गरेका थिए । त्यो कुरा हाँडीगाउँमा राखिएको शिलापत्रमा उल्लेख गरिएको छ । पहिलो श्रेणीमा पशुपतिनाथ, चाँगुनारायण, गुंविहार, मानविहार, राजविहारलाई राखी ६ पुराण २ पण रकम अनुदानको व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । दोस्रो श्रेणीमा रामेश्वर लगायत हंसगृहदेव, मानेश्वरलाई पनि राखी ३ पुराण १ पण रकम अनुदानको व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो ।

To facilitate the singing of devotional songs at the Tyāṅgā Bhairava sacred site, land was granted to thirteen individuals.त्याङ्गा भैरव देवस्थलमा भजन गाउनको लागि १३ जना व्यक्तिलाई जग्गा दिइएको थियो ।

With the aim of raising funds for the preservation of Tyāṅgā Bhairava and the Rāmeśvara Śivaliṅga, a largeyajñawas organized. The funds collected from this ritual were used to install a brass roof over the Tyāṅgā Bhairava shrine and a copper roof over the Rāmeśvara Śivaliṅga.त्याङ्गा भैरव र रामेश्वर शिवलिङ्गको संरक्षण गर्न चन्दा उठाउने उद्देश्य राखेर ठूलो यज्ञको आयोजना गरिएको थियो । यज्ञबाट संकलित रकमले त्याङ्गा भैरवलाई पित्तलको र रामेश्वर शिवलिङ्गलाई तामाको छाना हालिएको थियो ।

Due to excessive rainfall, floods in the river swept away the structures built at the Tyāṅgā Bhairava sacred site. The flood washed away the roofs offered to both Tyāṅgā Bhairava and Rāmeśvara, as well as the wall bearing the painted visage of Tyāṅgā Bhairava. After this destruction, as of November 2025, theghyāmporepresenting Tyāṅgā Bhairava has been placed behind Rāmeśvara within a temporary shelter.अधिक वर्षा भएर नदीमा बाढी आउँदा त्याङ्गा भैरव देवस्थलमा बनाइएको संरचनालाई बगाएको थियो । बाढीले त्याङ्गा भैरव र रामेश्वरलाई चढाइएको छाना लगायत त्याङ्गा भैरवको मुखाकृति लेखिएको गारो समेत बगाएको थियो । बाढीले बगाएपछि अहिले (सन् २०२५ नोवेम्बर) त्याङ्गा भैरवको प्रतीक स्वरूपको घ्याम्पोलाई अस्थायी टहरा बनाएर रामेश्वरको पछाडिपट्टि राखिएको छ ।

At the upper level of thehiti, a west-facing inscription has been placed. The inscription contains the term "water system" (jala pranali), indicating that it is related to thehiti. However, due to the illegibility of the text, it is difficult to determine whether the inscription pertains to the construction of the hiti or its renovation. The year mentioned in the inscription is also unclear. The lower part of the inscription appears to be engraved with "Samvat9??."
During the earthquake of 2015 CE (VS 2072), the steps at the lower part of thehitisubsided. With the financial support of Tarkeshwar Municipality, thehitiwas renovated in 2022 CE (VS 2079).

The temple underwent a rebuilding process led by the High-Powered Committee for Integrated Development of the Bagmati Civilization, an entity operating under the Ministry of Urban Development. Financial support for the project was extended by the Asian Development Bank. The comprehensive reconstruction effort was officially concluded in October 2022 CE.

King Mahendra Malla built the grand temple for his tutelary deity, Taleju Bhavānī on the 10th of the dark fortnight of Māgha in 1564 CE (NS 684). TheDevamālāVaṃśāvalī, a 19th century chronicle, records the temple's completion as the 5th of the bright fortnight of Māgha in 1549 CE (NS 669). The chronicle's account appears inaccurate, as historical evidence places Mahendra Malla's reign between 1562 and 1574 CE (NS 682-694). Both Gutschow (2011, p. 428) and Slusser (1982, p. 191) also concur with the 1564 CE date, which is now considered the most accurate.
King Pratāpa Malla erected a stone pillar with a statue of a metal winged lion on top right in front of the Taleju temple in the south.
King Pratāpa Malla offered a bell installed on the southern side of the uppermost plinth of the temple.

event_name: Installation of stone pillar with Pratāpa Malla statue
event_description: Pratāpa Malla erected a stone pillar in front of the temple with his statue flanked by his two sons, Nṛpendra and Cakravartīndra.
Pratāpa Malla installed the two gold door leaves of the central entrance to the temple, bearing depictions of various deities like Mahākāla, Gaṇeśa, Śiva-Pārvatī, among others.
Pratāpa Malla installed the flanking, non-functional doors beside the main entrance, bearing an inscription on golden plates with verses dedicated to goddess Bhagavatī that he himself composed.

event_name: Addition of pillar by Pārthivendra Malla
event_description: Pārthivendra Malla erected a pillar with a tortoise at its base. It bears the statues of King Pārthivendra, Queen Mother Indramatī, the young Prince Bhūpālendra, Queen Ṛddhilakṣmī, and Queen Rājalakṣmī. However, only four of these figures remain today.

King Bhāskara Malla installed a bell on the southern side of the uppermost plinth. Of the two bells installed here, this is the one on the eastern side while the western bell was installed by Pratāpa Malla.
The uppermost tier collapsed in the 1934 earthquakes while also damaging other parts of the temple.
Prime Minister Juddha Śamśera renovated the uppermost tier that collapsed in the 1934 earthquakes.

Rājabhāi Vajrācārya, his wife Lakṣmī Vajrācārya and other family members jointly offered 21 praying wheels to four Caityas and two Dharmadhātu Maṇḍalas in the memory of their deceased parents Buddharatna Vajrācārya and Bekhāmāyā Vajrācārya.
Vajrācārya Jinadeva and his wife Vimalā together with their children constructed the Śikharakūṭa Caitya. They also endowed some plots of land to perform worship.
The Phalcā was constructed under the initiative of Dīryavīra Siṃha from Kirtipur. He also had statues of Viṣṇu and Gaṇeśa installed at the same time inside the Phalcā.

The roof of the Phalcā was renovated by replacing a wooden beam, strut and eaves board. The project was handled by local youths supported with funding from the Lāyakū Village Development Committee, ward no. 9.
To protect the Viṣṇu statue (KIR4021-001) and other musical instruments from theft or damage, the three bays of the Phalcā were covered with an iron grill.

Prajāpati Thakura Śaṅkhadhara, resident of Cvachẽ, constructed the monastery with his wives Bhakhvāla Thakũ and Yacu. On that day, acaityaand adharmadhātumaṇḍalawere also installed in front of thedyaḥchẽ.

event_name: Cladding the Caitya with copper repousse plate
event_description: The Caitya was clad in copper repousse plate.
Due to the temple's deterioration, the Chaudhary Foundation and the Pashupati Area Development Trust collaborated its reconstruction.

Locals reconstructed the Phalcā in 2011. In the reconstruction process, the Phalcā was moved five feet back from its original position to protect it from road-widening. The statues of Gaṇeśa and Sarasvatī were also added during this time.

event_name: Offering of a female attendant for the temple?
event_description: जीवराज रावुतले मन्दिरमा 'कसागारिका' चढाएका थिए । कसागारिकाको अर्थ भित्री कोठामा हेरचाह गर्ने परिचारिका हुनाले उनले मन्दिरको सेवा गर्ने महिलालाई मन्दिरमा चढाएको हुनसक्छ ।

event_name: Offering of lions (PNT0010-002, PNT0010-010, PNT0010-011, PNT0010-012)
event_description: राजा नरेश मल्लको राज्यकालमा भक्तपुरका चैत्रकार (चित्रकार) कृष्णरामले मन्दिरको पश्चिमपट्टि एक जोडी सिंह ((PNT0010-002, PNT0010-012) र दक्षिणपट्टि एक जोडी सिंह (PNT0010-010, PNT0010-011) गरी दुईजोडी सिंहको मूर्ति चढाएका थिए ।
अभिलेखमा मितिबाहेक अन्य कुनै कुरा लेखिएको छैन । जुन सिंहको पादपीठमा अभिलेख कुँदिएको छ उक्त सिंह नेसं ७५९ (सन् १६३९) मा स्थापना भइसकेको हुनाले सिंहको जीर्णोद्धार गर्दा उक्त अभिलेख राखिएको हुनसक्छ ।
मुक्तिराज भारोले इन्द्रेश्वर मन्दिरमा तीनतह भएको सुवर्ण छत्र चढाएका थिए ।

event_name: Handover the rights of the temple to the Maṭhādhīśa of Jaṅgama Maṭha
event_description: राजा जितामित्र मल्लले इन्द्रेश्वर मन्दिरको सम्पूर्ण अधिकार भक्तपुरमा रहेको जङ्गम मठका मठाधीशलाई सुम्पेका थिए ।

event_name: Offering of utensils and a cow
event_description: भुजबल थापाले श्रीमती इन्द्रावतिदेवीसँग मिलेर इन्द्रेश्वर मन्दिरको लागि काँस, फलाम र तामाको गरी जम्मा २५ वटा भाँडाकुँडा सहित एउटी दुहुनी गाई चढाएका थिए ।
जयसिं खत्रीले इन्द्रेश्वर महादेवको लागि घण्टा चढाएका थिए ।
जसराय मानन्धरको नाममा आमा धनलक्ष्मीले नन्दीको मूर्ति चढाएकी थिइन् ।

event_name: Offering of a gilded roof on the west side of the temple
event_description: पनौती निवासी भैरवसिंहले मन्दिरको सबैभन्दा माथिल्लो तलामा पश्चिमपट्टि सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको छाना चढाएका थिए । उनी भक्तपुरको खौमा टोलमा बस्ने भाजुदत्तका छोरा थिए ।

event_name: Offering of a gilded roof on the south side of the temple
event_description: आफ्नो छोरा भैरवसिंहको मृत्यु भएपछि उनकी आमा लानि थकुंले पति भाजुदत्त, छोरा भैरवसिंह लगायत बुहारीहरू लानिमयेजु र चकुधी थकुंको मुक्तिको कामना गरी मन्दिरको सबैभन्दा माथिल्लो तलामा दक्षिणपट्टि सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको छाना चढाएका थिए ।

पनौती, दरिनचोक बस्ने सुबेदार रघुबिर बस्न्यात क्षेत्रीले विभिन्न ठाउँमा खेत गुठी राखिदिएका थिए । उक्त खेतको आयस्ताले इन्द्रेश्वर मन्दिरमा प्रत्येक महिनाको शुक्ल पक्षको चतुर्दशी तिथिमा रुद्री गर्नुपर्ने, त्रिवेणी घाटपारि रहेको ब्रह्मायणी मन्दिरमा प्रत्येक महिनाको शुक्ल र कृष्ण पक्षको अष्टमीको दिनमा रुद्री गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । उनले त्रिवेणीघाटमा रहेको सतःमा सरसफाइ गर्न र बिग्रेमा मर्मत गर्न पनि व्यवस्था गरिदिएका थिए ।
गोरा जङ्गमले मन्दिरको दक्षिणपट्टि घण्टा (PNT0010-011) चढाएका थिए ।
रत्नमान कर्माचार्यले गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने भित्रपट्टिको ढोकामा तामाको पाताले मोडेर सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइदिएका थिए ।

Amarakānteśvarī is credited for the construction of the temple. The inscription on a bell installed south of the temple states that Princess Amarakānteśvarī offered the bell through Captain Juddhamānasiṃha Rājabhaṇḍārī. Michaels and Tandon (2017, p.70), however, mention that she offered the bell through Siddhimānasiṃha Rājbhaṇḍārī. The bell is no longer at the site. Therefore, it could not be ascertained if it was Juddhamānasiṃha or Siddhimānasiṃha, who assisted Amarakānteśvarī in offering the bell. Usually, the donor of the bell is also the person to commission the construction of the temple the bell was donated to.
The temple was reconstructed by the Pashupati Area Development Trust after it was badly damaged in the 2015 earthquakes.
Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā built the Udāsī Akhaḍā, along with two otherakhaḍās for thevairāgīandsanyāsīascetics following the construction of the Jaṅge Hiraṇya Hema Nārāyaṇa temple (KAT2800).

The earliest known record from the Udāsī Akhaḍā is an inscription from 1889 CE (VS 1945) that documents the completion of a well within the premises. The inscription uses both Gurmukhi and Devanāgarī scripts.

Following the 2015 earthquakes, the Akhaḍā was reconstructed from ground up. The reconstruction was managed by the High-Powered Committee for Integrated Development of the Bagmati Civilization under the Ministry of Urban Development with the loan assistance of the Asian Development Bank.
The Āgaṃchẽ suffered heavy damages during the 2015 earthquakes.
The Guṭhī Saṃsthāna and the Department of Archaeology jointly renovated the Āgaṃche building in 2019.

Motimāyā Śākya performed a pacification ritual aimed at auspiciousness after the restoration of the Bāhāḥ was completed.
Dhruvaratna Śākya, Tārāśobhā Śākya, and other family members renovated the Bāhāḥ's sanctum.

Three brothers, Kāśī Bhāro, Gaṃgārāma Bhāro, and Śiva Bhāro, established thisjaḥdhuṃwater tank.
