A bell was donated.

Candra Śamśera launched a project under the name "Chandra Loka Water Works" in the joint name of himself and his wife, Candralokabhakta Lakṣmī Devī. Colonel Kiśora Narasiṃha Rāṇā served as the executive engineer.

Further details about the objectives of constructing this tank in Kirtipur are not found here but in an inscription (KAT2841_I_003) at the Bagmati Bridge in Thapathali. Candra Śamśera, who rebuilt the Bagmati Bridge in a modern style, included details in this laudatory inscription about the project to supply water from Kirtipur to Patan. The inscription notes that while Kathmandu and Bhaktapur already had public water taps (kaladhārā), Patan lacked them, forcing residents to drink well water, which caused illness and weakness. In fulfillment of the resolve of his late wife, Candralokabhakta Lakṣmī Devī, water was brought to Patan through iron pipes from a location 19,900 feet away. Necessary reservoirs were constructed along the route, and a 300-foot-long bridge was built over the Bagmati to support the pipeline. The project resulted in 50 public water taps in Patan, with prayers that the merit would grant the late queen salvation and Candra Śamśera a 100-year lifespan. Thus, this tank was built as part of a major initiative by the prime minister and his wife to supply water to Patan.
The Vihāra was constructed by Pūrṇa Śākya, resident of Oku Bāhāḥ Lāchicāka, Dundugṛha.

event_name: Donation of the statue of devotees
event_description: Locke(1985,112) quotes the date as NS 851 butŚākya(1994,111) mentions NS 861. Since the stone inscription is damaged the date cannot be read anymore. Members of the monastery believe that the statue represents the donors who constructed the Buddha temple in the courtyard.

Cidhimāyā and her two sons Rājamāna and Ratna Bahādur consecrated the Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala. The Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala was originally in front of thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥbut was later moved between the Buddha Temple and the Dharmadhātu Jinālaya Caitya.
Before thebāhāḥwas established, the Mūladuvā clan had already established aguṭhīto organise worships and feasts.

event_name: Donation of bell, toraṇa and throne
event_description: Ratnarāja Vajrācārya, the founder of thebāhāḥ, donated a bell, a lion’s throne for the main deity, and a gildedtoraṇa.
Ratnarāja Vajrācārya, a member of Mūladuvā, founded thisbāhāḥ.

Before thisbāhāḥwas established, Dhana Thakũ had consecrated statues of Dīpaṅkara and Tārā in memory of her late husband Bhājudeva. She also installed aguṭhīto organise the worship, feast and donation ceremony (pañcadāna) on the 8th day of the bright fortnight of Bhādra.
Vajrarāja Śākya established thecaityain thebāhāḥ'scourtyard.
Due to the derelict condition of the temple, it was reconstructed in 1985 CE. The cost for the restoration was covered by the government and local community members.
Nowadays, the stonetoraṇais covered by a brass plate making the inscription invisible. Thus, the replica of the inscription was in the newer copperplate and attached inside the sanctum.
Pruscha(1975,17), without referring to sources, mentions that the temple was restored in 1961 CE.
Śukadeva Prajāpati living in Chhetrapati, paved tiles and marble to adorn the temple.
Lakṣmaṇa Śreṣṭha living in Chhetrapati, installed a hundred eight bronze light lamps around the temple in the memory of his wife Ratna Māyā Śreṣṭha.
Jñāna Bahādura Śreṣṭha offered thekikīpāto Gaṇeśa.
In 1996 CE, the silver statue of Gaṇeśa was installed by raising funds from devotees.
Haridāsa Mānandhara living in Thãhiti offered the silverkikīpāto Gaṇeśa.
As stated in the 'description' above, the Temple was built by Cautārā Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Jośī, a powerful minister of King Bhupatīndra Malla.
In 1958 CE, the 'Food for Work' Project renovated the Temple (Pruscha, on the other hand, gives the years as 1959 CE).
In collaboration with the Metropolitan City Office, the 'Jaiśīdevala Jīrṇoddhāra Upabhoktā Samiti,' a local committee, renovated the Temple.
The earthquakes of 2015 CE completely destroyed the Temple.
Following the earthquakes in 2015 CE, the Department of Archeology reconstructed the Temple. It is in the final stages of completion as of November 2022 CE.

event_name: Regulations Laid Down for the Organization of Annual Celebrations of the Bhairava Shrine
event_description: This inscription records the regulations laid down for organising various annual celebrations of Ākāśa Bhairava (KIR0050-009). The names of donor couple have been mentioned as Gaṃgānātha Darśandhārī and his wife Chikunī Juginī (Joginī) of Kvathajora (Kutujvaḥ Ṭola). They also formed aguṭhīto sustain the prescribed tradition as mentioned in this inscription.

Something was offered or built to the name of Gorakhanātha. The part where it is detailed is in poor condition and very hard to decipher. Names of ten donors from the Kapāli community are mentioned in the inscription. The group also offered a pair of lion statues (siṅacāandbyāṅacā) to Bhairava (KIR0050-009).

A pair of donors, carved on a single stone slab, was placed inside the Pīṭha. Names of the donor couple have been inscribed at the arch-shaped top of the statue. It is very difficult to decipher the names in the present-day. However, Shokoohy et all (2014, 86) have read the names as Joganātha and Gaṃgāvati (Gaṅgāvatī).

event_name: Renovation of the Temple and Formation of a Guṭhī
event_description: Chikadhi and his other family members jointly offered a pinnacle to the previously existing Gorakhanātha temple. They also made an arrangement of a budget for the annual rituals and the renovation of the temple when necessary. Those, whose duty is to take care of the temple, are mentioned as a group of four Darśanadhārī (synonymous with Jugī or Jogī, Kusale and Kapālī) including Cikadhaki, Sūryanātha, Bhāginātha, and Cikavīra. Name of the priest for theguṭhīis mentioned as Laghupati Darśanadhārī. Other details record the position of the planets and a list of things which must be used for the annual rituals.

The inscription records the installation of Gorakhanātha along with Bhairava statue by one Yāṅā Darśanadhārī and other four Jogīs (Dhalama, Devīdāsa, Śirāma, and Lathanadāsa) of Kirtipur and Balambu. They also built a temple for the deities.
A wall was constructed somewhere in the complex. The exact place and the donor, who constructed it, are not clearly mentioned in the inscription.
Statue of a devotee couple, crafted on a single stone slab, was placed inside the Pīṭha. The couple is named Gaṃgānātha Jugi (Jugī/Yogī) and Cikuṃ Jugiṃni (Joginī).
Statue of a devotee couple, crafted on a single stone slab, was placed inside the Pīṭha. The couple is named Mohaṃdāsa and Ranhāvati (Ratnāvatī).

event_name: Construction of a Stone Miniature Temple
event_description: This inscription records the construction of a stone temple for Isṭhaconi Mahākāla (KIR0050-006) by Hākurāma Bhāro and others.

The trident kept on a tall stone slab was installed to the west of the Bairava Shrine (KIR0050-009). Three individuals, Ṣupā Jugi (Jogī) of Kothujora (Kutujhvaḥ Ṭola), Gaṃgāvatti, and Joganātha, are named as donors in the inscription.

The inscription records that Bhuyū Cībhāḥ was commissioned in 1705 CE (NS 825) by Śivarāma Mahān Bhāva, a resident of Mikhabāhāḥ (LAL0810).The inscription is embedded in the wall of the entrance area of the newly constructed shopping center immediately to the east of the caitya. The shopping center replaced the historic Cībhāḥ Phalcā (LAL4211).
The Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala was established in 1962 by a predecessor of the Jyāpu family living in one of the houses to the south of the monument.
The stone statue of Buṅgadyaḥ was installed on the north plinth. It was commissioned by Gopi Maharjan from Mikhābāhāḥ (LAL0810), a member of the caitya'sguṭhī.
Tulasī Ḍaṅgola donated a brassvajrafor the Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala (LAL0821-007).
Kājī Ḍillīsiṃha Basneta built the temple and installed a bell (PPK0516-015) to commemorate the event.

Kājī Ḍillisiṃha Basneta donated land parcels to establish a trust for the performance of daily and periodic rituals at the temple. King Surendra issued a copperplate inscription detailing the land parcels Ḍillīsiṃha donated in the name of the temple.

event_name: Politically motivated damage of the Phalcā
event_description: The Phalcā was damaged in 1979, and since then has been turned into an elevated open space.This important Phalcā was located in the heart of Sundhara Patan. It was occupied by a local police station before it was vandalised in 1978-9. The youths of Nugaḥ Ṭola used to hold regular gang fights with the youths from neighbouring quarters in this area. One such fight took place in 1978-9. The local police arrested the youths involved in the gang fight and detained them in the Phalcā building itself An aggressive group of local people attacked the police office, demanding the release of the detainees. After this incident, the local police station was moved to another Phalcā located to the west of Lũ Hiti. Pvāḥsyāḥ Phalcā was abandoned completely and was no longer maintained (source: a resident of Yanāmugaḥ, male, age 45). Though the Phalcā had aguṭhī(established by Cipālus (Śreṣṭha) of Caṃki Ṭola), this group no longer exists today. The idol of Pvāḥsyāḥdyaḥ is also no longer present; it appears that the statue of this deity was stolen and never replaced.

Pvāḥsyāḥ Phalcā was one of fourphalcāsselected for the first PhotoKathmandu Festival in 2015 and became a major success among locals and passers-by. Positioned at a main road in Patan, it became a spectacular object of attention during the days of the festival. Many people articulated the desire to hold on to it and for it to stay beyond the festival time. The Pvāḥsyaḥ Phalcā (Pāṭī) at Sundhara was removed in the 1970s and has stood as platform since then. Art students from Kathmandu University's Art and Design Centre were involved in the PhotoKathmandu project and studied its previous form through old postcards, and conversations with locals before reconstructing it. The aim of the reconstruction was to encourage future perspectives on the post-earthquake city, referencing what has been lost, but also what can be gained again, and how important the ‘institution’ of thepatican be in this context.

event_name: Formation of a committee to reconstruct the temple
event_description: As the temple had fallen into a dilapidated condition, a reconstruction committee was formed under the chairmanship of ward chair Vidyāsundara Śākya.मन्दिर जीर्ण भएकोले पुनर्निर्माण गर्न वडाध्यक्ष विद्यासुन्दर शाक्यको अध्यक्षतामा समिति गठन गरिएको थियो ।

Owing to its deteriorated state, the temple was reconstructed with financial assistance from the Kathmandu Metropolitan City and donations collected from devotees. Prior to reconstruction, the temple was a single-storey structure with a tiled roof. During reconstruction, it was rebuilt as a two-storey temple and the roof was clad with brass sheets.मन्दिर जीर्ण भएकोले काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाको आर्थिक सहयोग र भक्तजनसँग चन्दा उठाएर मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । पुनर्निर्माण गर्नुभन्दा अगाडि मन्दिर एक तलाको मात्र थियो र छानामा झिङ्गटी राखिएको थियो । पुनर्निर्माण गर्दा दुईतलाको मन्दिर बनाई छानामा पित्तलको पाता राखिएको थियो ।

event_name: Covering wall with copper and brass plates
event_description: Sanubhāi Mānan­dhara, together with his wife Jānakīdevī Mānan­dhara, sheathed the interior walls of the sanctorum with copper and brass sheets in memory of his late mother, Lakṣmīdevī Mānan­dhar.सानुभाइ मानन्धरले श्रीमती जानकीदेवी मानन्धरसँग मिलेर दिवंगत आमा लक्ष्मीदेवी मानन्धरको स्मृतिमा मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्रको भित्तामा तामा र पित्तलको पाताले मोडिदिएका थिए ।
Prabhāta Mahāju of Parsa District offered apatāḥto the temple.पर्सा जिल्ला निवासी प्रभात महाजुले मन्दिरमा पताः चढाएका थिए ।

Sureśa Prasāda Mānan­dhara and Bhānu Prakāśa Mānan­dhara of Gofal tole, Kathmandu, gilded the pinnacle offered to Bhagavatī and thekṣepuon thetoraṇainside the sanctorum with gold plating.ठमाडौं, गोफल टोलका सुरेश प्रसाद मानन्धर र भानु प्रकाश मानन्धरले मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र भगवतीलाई चढाइएको गजूर र तोरणमा रहेको क्षेपुमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइदिएका थिए ।
Along the front of thepīṭha, a row of brass lampstands (pālcā) was installed for lighting oil lamps.
Bīrabahādūra dedicated a bell in the name of Bālakumārī.
A donor from Kelaṭola offered a bell in the name of Bālakumārī.
On the façade of the pyramidal wall at the rear of thepīṭha, gilded metal images of the Aṣṭamātṛkās were affixed. This work was carried out jointly by Rāmadāsa and Rāmabhakta.

Kumāraju Śākya commissioned the construction of thebāhāḥon the fifth day of the bright fortnight of Māgha (Śrīpañcamī) in 1678 CE (798 NS) during the joint reign of King Śrīnivāsa and Yoganarendra Malla. During the initial construction, a statue of Akṣobhya was installed in the sanctum as thebāhāh’s primary deity (kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ), and the statues of Cakrasaṃvara-Vajravārāhī, Gaṇeśa and Mahākāla were installed inside theāgaṃ.

event_name: Damage during the 1934 CE earthquakes and repair
event_description: The first floor of thekvāḥpāḥchẽwas damaged during the 1934 CE earthquakes and was repaired by the Bāhāḥsaṅghamembers.
Some of thekvāḥpāḥchẽhas considerable cracks. Thesaṅghamembers are struggling to receive financial aid for the repair work.

In front of the Phalcā stands the slate of a Licchavi inscription recovered in 2004 CE. It was issued during the reign of King Gaṇadeva in the Śaka Era year 482 i.e., the Vikrama Era year 616. The inscription records a royal order given to the Mukhiyās, Brahmins and other householders of the administrative unit Theñco Grāma (seeŚ. Rājavaṃśī2061, p. 94-95 for an edition and translation of the text).
The restoration work of the Phalcā was carried out in 1904 CE (NS 1024) by a lady, Lakṣmithakuṃ, and her son Hari.
The traditional Phalcā was demolished in 2001 CE (2058 BS), the present concrete structure has since been erected.

During the reign of Candraśamśera, the local moneylender (sāhu) Pṛthvīvilāsa Sāpakoṭā constructed Kālesāhu Pāṭī and the nearby temple (devala) dedicated to Naravadeśvara Mahādeva, and endowed substantial parcels of land asguṭhīto support the performance of annual rites.चन्द्रशम्शेरको शासनकालमा स्थानीय साहु पृथ्वीविलास सापकोटाले यस सतःका साथै समीपैमा नरवदेश्वर महादेवको देवल बनाई वार्षिक कर्मका खातिर प्रसस्त जग्गा गुठी राखे ।

From the surplus remaining from the income of the lands endowed in 1914 CE( VS 1971) in the name of Kālesāhu Pāṭī  and thedevala, a bell was installed in the name of Naravadeśvara and the lineage deity.पृथ्वीविलासले विसं १९७१ (सन् ९१४) मा  सतः र देवलका नाममा राखेको जग्गाको आयबाट बचेको जगेडाले नरवदेश्वर र कुलदेवताको नाममा एक घण्ट स्थापना गरियो ।

The 2015 CE earthquakes severely damaged the Gārada Ghara, with half of the uppermost floor and a significant portion of the roof collapsing. The Department of Archaeology engaged the Chinese Academy of Cultural Heritage (CACH) to supervise restoration efforts for Raṅgamahala and adjacent monuments. Scaffoldings and corrugated metal sheets were deployed to shield roofs from rain. However, as of March 2024 CE, renovation has yet to commence.
King Siddinarasiṃha Malla built the palace including a hiti with a golden spout and many tantric statues. He also established the statues of Pañcamukhī Gaṇeśa and Narasiṃha.

The Government of Nepal renovated the palace during the reign of King Mahendra and established a police post with a small jail in the building. In 1993, the police was moved to the former municipal building on the south side of the square. Sundarī Coka was closed to the public till 2007.

The metal image of Mahiṣāsuramardinī on the eastern façade was added to replace one that had long been lost. The image of Mahiṣāsuramardinī placed in the spout was also lost, though this one was later found. However, a new image was installed after it went missing, and the original one is now kept in the museum.

At this shrine, where daily worship had ceased for many years, the daily worship was restarted on the initiative of the 'Daśamahāvidyā Bhaktibhāva Parivāra' organization by a Rājopādhyāya Brāhmaṇa, and it has been continuing without interruption. The same organization is managing the priest's remuneration.

विसं १९३१ (सन् १८७४-७५) मा राजा सुरेन्द्रबाट जारी एक लालमोहरमा काशीनाथले बनाएको सतःका खातिर ४ रोपनी जग्गादान सिफारिस भएको थियो । यस प्रसंगबाट यस मिति अगावै यहाँ सतःहरू बनिसकेको तथ्य खुलदछ (K_0021_0016) ।

In the wake of the 2015 CE earthquake, thesataḥsuffered extensive damage, necessitating the evacuation of its inhabitants and eventual reconstruction, which were completed by 2022 CE. This revitalization of thesataḥwas made possible through the collaborative efforts of the Integrated Development of the Bagmati Civilization project, an initiative under the Nepal Government's Ministry of Urban Development, along with financial support from the Asian Development Bank. The restoredsataḥwas inauguration in October 2022 CE (2079 VS).

Abhimāna Siṃha Basnyāta began the construction of this house three days after he received the ownership of the land in 1777 CE (B. ĀcāryaVS 2060, p. 95) and completed it in January 10, 1777 CE. The inscription recording this event was formerly installed at Nārāyaṇa Cuka (the courtyard behind the Palṭana Ghara) but no one knows its whereabout now (as of December 2021).

event_name: Donation of a pair of metal flags
event_description: Kulamānasingh, Ratnamāna and Gaṇeśa Bahādur donated a pair of flags to Akṣobhya.

Jīvanṛsiṃha, a member of the Cikã Bahī, established this Bāhāḥ together with thecaityain 1878 (NS 998). He wished that his father Bhājudhana and mother Mayju Thakunī would dwell in the Sukhāvatī Bhuvana. Jīvanṛsiṃha was supported by his stepmother Dhana Thakunī, his wife Lakṣmī Thakunī, his sons Kulamāna Siṃha, Ratnamāna Siṃha, Kulabahādura Siṃha, Gaṇeśabahādura Siṃha, and his daughter Yogamāyā.
The roof was renewed by the Sanāḥguṭhī, the local community and the KVPT.
The pillar 003 (see MUG0150-003 above) contains an inscription of five lines. Although eroded, it is possible to read the first two lines:1. [Oṃ (?)] svasti... sā2. ke 1404 (ma?)

"Nārāyaṇa Vāsudeva Om Sarana Rāmarāma" is engraved on a stone slab located in front of Kalmochanaghāta Sataḥ West, intended for the placement of deceased bodies. The inscription does not specify any ritual activities or dates.यस सतः अगाडिको घाटमा मृत शरीर राख्न बनाइएको ढुङ्गाको फलकमा ‘नारायण वासुदेव ૐ सरन रामराम’ लेखिएको छ । धार्मिक विश्वास अनुरुप लेखिएको यस लिखतमा कुनै ऐतिहासिक क्रिया एवं तिथिमिति उल्लेखित छैन ।

An inscription installed in February 2024, records the construction of Kalmochanaghāta Sataḥ West by Durgānātha Miśra in 1945-46 CE (VS 2002). Another inscription records that the Sataḥ was established to care for the terminally ill and conductkriyāputrīrituals. It also mentions that anyone can contribute to its maintenance for spritual merit since it serves as a public site. Local individuals suggest that Miśrabāje, believed to be the builder, resided here. But other sources claim that the actual constructors were members of a family living in Asana ṭola (local residents: Śreṣṭha, male, age 77 and Maharjana, male, age 56).सतःमा हालसालै (फेब्रुवरी २०२४) राखिएको अभिलेख अनुसार विसं २००२ (सन् १९४५-४६) सालमा दुर्गानाथ मिश्रबाट यो सतःको निर्माण भएको भनिएको छ । सतःमा भएको अर्को अभिलेखमा निर्माणको उद्धेश्य खुल्नेगरी विरामीको उपचार गर्न वा घाटमा क्रियापुत्री बस्ने हेतु बनाइएको भनिएको छ । अभिलेखमा यो सार्वजनिक सतः भएकाले जोकसैले पनि पुण्यका खातिर संरक्षण गर्नसक्ने कुरा पनि भनिएको छ । स्थानीयका अनुसार यो सतःमा मिश्रबाजे (निर्माता भनिएका) बस्ने मात्र गर्दथे तर सतःका निर्माता असन टोलस्थित एक परिवार थिए (local resident, Śreṣṭha, male, age 77, Maharjana, male, age 56) ।

A glass board affixed to the front facade of Kalmochanaghāta Sataḥ West displays information regarding the availability of complimentary medicine, underscoring its contribution to healthcare services.सतःको मोहोडामा शिशामाथि लेखिएको एक लिखत छ जसमा विरामीहरूलाई सित्तैमा औसधि लिन आउन आह्वान गरिएको छ । यसर्थ यो सतः स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्रको परोपकारको खातिर पनि प्रयोग हुने गर्दथ्यो कि भन्ने अनुमान हुन्छ ।

Kalmochanaghāta Sataḥ West underwent renovation in 2014 CE (2017 VS), made possible by donations. The names of major donors are engraved on the marble slab.सतःको पछिल्लो जीर्णोद्धारकार्य विसं २०७१ (सन् २०१४) सालमा चन्दा संकलनबाट गरिएको थियो ।
The courtyard was paved withteliabricks by Avaladeva and Caṇḍikā.

event_name: Donation of a pair of lion statues
event_description: A pair of lion statues were donated and installed in front of the sanctum.
Nepal's Department of Archaeology reconstructed thebāhāḥwith the support of the German government.

event_name: Donation of a brass lhegā (cloth) to kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ
event_description: Prajāpati Thakura Lakṣmī and his wife Santalakṣmī donated a brasslhegā(outer garment made of metal) tokvāḥpāḥdyaḥ
A bell was donated by Pūnadhãju, Lāni Thakũ and others.

event_name: Repair of the monastery and the digichẽ
event_description: Daivajña Motirāja, Daivajña Durggārāja, Daivajña Caṇḍīrāja, Daivajña Rāmarāja, Daivajña Ciṣarāja and Daivajña Girirāja renovated thevihāraand thedigi. The floor of thedigichẽwas also added. At that time, thetharapāof thevihārawas Amaradeva.

event_name: Donation of a golden face to Akṣobhya
event_description: Sūryarāja, Paru, Dharmmajoti, Bhairava and Hākurāja donated a golden face to Akṣobhya. It was agreed that if the golden face goes missing  the person responsible for performing the daily ritual worship must pay for its replacement. In this inscription, thebāhāḥis referred to as Jerabāhāra.
Kṛṣṇavīr Nāike, his wife Thakũmati, son Bekhārāja and daughter Siddhilakṣmī donated pillars and capital of a main pillar (methā̃) to hang the bell.

event_name: Donation of a pair of door panels
event_description: Jujulāla donated a pair of door panels to be fixed to the entrance of the sanctum.
Keśavarāja and Viṣṇumāyā donated the oil-lamp balustrade.
The courtyard of thebāhāḥwas paved withteliabricks thanks to the help of the District Development Committee and local people.

event_name: Reconstruction of digichẽ after the earthquakes of 2015
event_description: Thedigichẽcollapsed in the 2015 earthquake. It was rebuilt with the financial support of Lalitpur Metropolitan City and local people.
Devamuni Śākya, asaṅghamember of Si Bāhāḥ ordered the construction of this Bāhāḥ. He was from the Mākaḥ lineage of the Śākya clan.
Nayana Bhāro of Cikaṃmugaḥ, Ponde Ṭola, established a grand stone image of Nārāyaṇa adorned with akadambavṛkṣa-prabhāand constructed the temple to enshrine it.
Harinandan Joshi erected a pillar supporting a Garuda statue in front of the temple. Today, only the pillar remains, as the Garuḍa statue was likely stolen.

Rudrasiṃha Bhāro donated his residential house and adjoining land for religious purposes dedicating to his ancestralāgama-devatā(family tutelary deity). Although the exact date of the inscription is unclear, the language and script suggest that it belongs to the late medieval period.

Verse 1:In the year 1776 CE (ŚS 1698), on an auspicious day in the month of Kārtika, under theUttarabhādrapadāconstellation and the holy occasion ofHaribodhinī Ekādaśī, when the moon was in Mīnarāśi, and both Jupiter (Guru) and Venus (Śukra) were in favorable positions—at that propitious moment, the minister Śrīkīrtisiṃha commenced the construction of this grand Jaya Maṇḍira.Verse 2:The king, sovereign of the Gaurśācala realm, had a contented land and a joyous populace. His minister, the learned and valiant Kīrtisiṃha, was served by his attendant, Sarūpasiṃha. In thisJayamaṇḍira, Lord Śaṅkara Mahādeva himself dwells in full glory; may the blessings of Lambodara Gaṇeśa ever abide here.Verse 3:May horses and elephants playfully roam here; may dancers perform in every direction; may hymns, devotional songs, andpurāṇarecitations resound daily; may children and subjects remain ever joyful; may kinsmen and women vie in beauty; and may all reside fearlessly in thisJayamaṇḍira, thereby increasing its glory (kīrti).

This inscription does not originally belong to the temple but has been brought from elsewhere. The upper portion of the stone stele is engraved with avajra(thunderbolt) and the text records that a family of Dhījavirasiṃha from Kāntipura (Kathmandu) constructed avajradhātu caitya.
Karmakumārīdevī, wife of Deva Śamśera, consecrated the mainśivaliṅgain her honor and named it Karmabhakteśvara Mahādeva.
The statue of Jalaśayana Nārāyaṇa (a replica of the one in Buḍhānīlakaṇṭha) was consecrated in 2012 by the local residents.

event_name: Construction of a statue of Hanumān
event_description: Local residents collected donations and established this Hanumān statue in 2015.
This inscription of Bhīmārjunadeva and Jiṣṇugupta (r. 631-633 CE) is not directly related to this temple. It mentions that modern Sunaguthi was called Bhṛṅgāra Pāñcālī during the Licchavi period.

event_name: Management of ponds and water channels
event_description: This inscription of King Śivadeva (694-705 CE) mentions the management of ponds and water channels in Bhṛṅgāreśvara.

The inscription mentions that the temple was destroyed. It was reconstructed by Viṣṇu Siṃha in NS 674. It further informs the readers that his attendants excavated two copper vessels inscribed with the name of the deity Bhṛṅgāreśvara.
A Brahmin named Śrīnārāyaṇa offered a trident to Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mahādeva.

event_name: Establishment of a Gaṇeśa and Kumāra statue
event_description: A Brahmin named Mahādeva established a statue of Gaṇeśa and Kumāra near Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mandira. This event is also mentioned in the inscription from NS 734.
A Brahmin named Kṛṣṇadeva offered a golden parasol to Bhṛṅgāreśvara.
The temple was reconstructed in a dome shape by the goverment after it collapsed during the 1934 earthquake.

Hiraṇyagarbhakumārī, also known as Jyeṭhā Maiñā Mahārānī, established thisśivālayaand named it Hiraṇyabhakteśvara in honor of herself. She built the temple five years after her marriage to Jaṅga Bahādura.

event_name: Construction of a  small water tank representing the Capĩgāḥ
event_description: The traditional Capĩgāḥ was covered up during the road construction process. Its name arises from the Newari language, in which a mud mound with grass on top of it is calledcapĩand the water which is stored in a pit is calledcapĩgāḥ. A small water tank has been built 1 m away from the original Capĩgāḥ’s location.

The Śikharakūṭa Caitya (KIR0012-002), which is located at the centre of thebāhāḥcourtyard, used to bear an inscription recording its installation in 1633 CE (NS 573). This inscription is now missing on thecaitya.
The saṅghamembers of thebāhāḥoften recite a religious text,cacā, inside itsdyaḥchẽ. This text also records that a person called Bhāgisiṃha and his family constructed Kvay Bāhāḥ in 1701 CE (NS 821).

event_name: Use of space for classroom of a primary school
event_description: Sankhu Primary School was established in 1976 CE at the Calākhu Ṭola. It ran its classes on Nhāykaṃ Sataḥ. As there was not enough space for the students at the Sataḥ, the Phalcā was used as classrooms for three years.
The Phalcā was badly damaged by the 2015 earthquakes. The roof and the walls of the Phalcā were renovated by the local residents.
A local resident from the Bālakumārī area renovated the north-facing phalcā (object no. THI0110-002) during the reign of King Raṇajita Malla.

Even though thephalcāwas not heavily damaged in the 2015 CE earthquake (VS 2072), it was reconstructed by the Madhyapura Thimi Municipality in 2024 CE (VS 2080). As discussed above in 'Description', the elders used to say that there had once been ahitiin the phalcā, and people also used to call it Hitiphalcā. Based on this, the reconstruction plan was modified. Using the water stream, a new hiti was included in the design of thephalcā. As part of the reconstruction, the original structure of thephalcāwas slightly changed.

event_name: Establishment of the Patan Guṭhī Office
event_description: Before the establishment of the Guṭhī Saṃsthāna in 1964 CE (VS 2021), there were 15 separateguthioffices in operation, each under the jurisdiction of various magistrate offices. The Macchendra Guṭhī Office was one of them. It operated from this building. In 1971 CE (VS 2028), the Lalitpur Branch of the Guṭhī Saṃsthāna was also stationed here.

The Lalitpur Municipality allocated funds for reconstruction of both the Jhatāpvaḥ Gaṇeśa Mandira and thesataḥ(LAL4189). The reconstruction process started in June 2023 and is ongoing (January 2025).

This sign board displays the name of the temple maintained by Lalitpur Metropolis.यो कुनै अभिलेख नभई सम्पदा मार्गको अवधारण अन्तर्गत ललितपुर महानगरपालिकाको रोहवरमा राखिएको मन्दिरको नामोल्लेख बोर्ड मात्र हो ।

event_name: Establishment of Maṇivināyaka statue and construction of phalcā
event_description: Śivasiṃha Bhāro installed the Maṇivināyaka statue (BKT0181-006) and built aphalcārest house, wishing for his long life, health, progeny, and wealth. It also warns that anyone harming the Maṇivināyaka orphalcāwill face the consequences of committing the five great sins.

event_name: Establishment of Śiva, Garuḍanārāyaṇa and Pāñcāyaṇa statues
event_description: This inscription records Gaṃgārāma Bhāro and Purandra Bhāro, two brothers from Bhaktpur’s Yāchẽ Ṭola, installing statues of Śiva, Garuḍanārāyaṇa, and Pāñcāyana. The Śiva statue they installed may be the Umāmaheśvara statue in thehiticomplex, and the Garuḍanārāyaṇa likely refers to the Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa statue, as the inscription is carved beside it. However, the Pāñcāyana statues, which include Gaṇeśa, Sūrya, Viṣṇu, and Durgā, are not visible in the complex.
During the reign of King Narendradeva, Viṣṇudeva established ajaḥdhuṇ(stone water spout) for Brahmins and other people to bathe. For thejaḥdhuṇ, he also arranged a water-drawing mechanism and a well.

During the reign of King Raṇabahādura Śāha, Bhīma Ṭaksārī (chief officer of the mint) undertook the renovation of theNaksāla Bhagavatītemple. He performedpūjāandyajñato various deities and Brahmins, gave generous sacrificial fees, and completed the restoration in a proper ritual manner. The supervision of the work was carried out by Prema Giri Gusāiṃ. Since the inscription states that bricks were used in the renovation, it suggests that prior to Bhīma Ṭaksārī’s intervention, the temple had been constructed using other materials.

Bhīma Ṣavāsa (Khavāsa) of Makhan Tole, Kathmandu, constructed asataḥ(resting platform) in front of the Naksāla Bhagavatī temple at his own expense from the property he possessed. The work was supervised by Dhanadatta Newār from Asan. The Bhīma Ṭaksārī who renovated the temple in 1782 CE (VS 1839) and Bhīma Ṣavāsa who built thesataḥappear to be the same individual.
In memory of his late father Ratna Bahādura Kasaju and late mother Nānībābā Kasaju, Dr. Prema Kasaju, together with his wife Sudhā Kasaju, dedicated a bell (KAT3390-032) within the temple premises.

An inscription records that Nārān (Nārāyaṇa) and Sīva (Śiva), descendants of Kājī Bhīmā, jointly carried out restoration work, though the inscription does not specify what exactly was restored. Since the inscription is carved on ajaḥdhun, it is probable that they renovated the water spout itself. The Kājī Bhīmā mentioned in the inscription could well be the same Bhīma Ṭaksārī who renovated the temple in 1782 CE (VS 1839).
Colonel Prakāśa Śamśera Ja. Ba. Rā.’s son, Major General Mahāvīra Śamśera Ja. Ba. Rā., offered a bell (KAT3390-012) to Naksāla Bhagavatī.

event_name: Offering of a pair of flags
event_description: Four devotees—Sāhu Durgādāsa, Dvārikādāsa, Siddhīlāla, and Bhairava Siṃ—performed worship to Naksāla Bhagavatī and dedicated a pair of flags inside the sanctum, spending 482tolas of silver for the purpose.
Hīrākājī Vajrācārya, Prāṇamāyā Vajrācārya, and others collectively offered a metallicpatāḥ(bunting) to the temple.

event_name: Establishment of the statue of Hanumān
event_description: In memory of his late father Rāma Lāla Śreṣṭha and late mother Viṣṇu Kumārī Śreṣṭha, Matsyendralāla Śreṣṭha, along with his family members, established an image of Hanumān within the temple premises.

event_name: Establishment of the statue of Śanideva
event_description: In memory of his late father Mohana Lāla Śreṣṭha and mother Maiyā Śreṣṭha, Maniṣa Śreṣṭha, together with his wife Tejaśvī Śreṣṭha, installed an image of Śanideva in the temple courtyard.

In the name of his late father Ānanda Maharjana and late mother Śāradā Maharjana, Canaka Maharjana and his wife Līlā Maharjana offered various silver ritual objects necessary for the worship (pūjā) of Naksāla Bhagavatī.

An inscription mentions that Nārān (Nārāyaṇa) and Śiva, the great-grandsons of Kājī Bhīmā, carried out a restoration; however, the inscription does not clarify what specific part of the structure they restored.

The seven-bay Phalcā came into existence only after its reconstruction in 2021 CE. It used to be a three-bay Phalcā that remained in a poor state of repair for some time. A small building of one floor that stood next to the Phalcā was also merged into the Phalcā to expand the rest house into a seven-bay structure in the course of the reconstruction.

The inscription commemorating the initial construction of this monument records that the two-storeydharmaśālāwas built using bricks, measuring 266 cubits in length and supported by 11 columns, stretching from Kālamocanaghāṭa to Purohitaghāṭa.

Following the 2015 earthquakes, the Dharmaśālā was reconstructed by the Bāgamatī Civilization Integrated Development Committee under the Ministry of Urban Development, with a loan from the Asian Development Bank. The reconstruction was completed on October 23, 2022 CE (VS 2079).

On June 4, 2023 CE, the Dharmaśālā was formally handed over to the Nepal Police by Uddava Prasāda Timalsenā, Chairman of the Bāgamatī Civilization Integrated Development Committee, to Inspector General Mirā Chaudharī.
The lion statues at the entrance were established in 1654 CE.
A person named Jayadarta established his tutelary deity at thepīṭha.
A stone archway (toraṇa) was installed over the aniconic stones representing Brahmāyaṇī.

This inscription documents the renovation of aphalcā, which collapsed during the 1934 earthquakes, in 1940 CE (VS 1997). Although the inscription mentions that it was a renovation, it probably was a reconstruction of thephalcā.
The Buddha Dharma Saṅgha Nāmasaṅgīti Sevā Khalaḥ was formed. This committee arranges for Nāmasaṅgīti recitations to take place in the temple.
A painting made by Henry AmbroseOldfieldin 1857 shows this temple in a traditional two-tiered style. It can be assumed that this temple was severely damaged in the 1934 earthquake.
The Buddha Dharma Saṅgha Nāmasaṅgīti Sevā Khalaḥ offered alhegā(an outer garment made of metal) to Buddha.
The statue of Śākyamuni Buddha was enshrined in the temple.
वलाछेँ टोल निवासी शान्तमाया बासाले नासःद्यः प्राङ्गणमा गणेशको मूर्ति स्थापना गरेका थिए ।

event_name: Installation of the statue of Buḍānīlakaṇṭha (PNT0220-006) and Macchenārāyaṇa (PNT0220-007)
event_description: वलाछेँ टोलका राधाकृष्ण वासी र शान्तमाया वासीले नासःद्यःको प्राङ्गणमा बुढानीलकण्ठ र मच्छेनारायणको मूर्ति स्थापना गरेक थिए ।

An inscription documents the installation of a Śivaliṅga in 1813 CE (VS 1869), followed by the excavation for the construction of a boundary wall in 1813 CE (VS 1870) during the eleventh fortnight of Kārtika (N. Panta VS 2022, p.58). Within the inscription, a lady referred to as "Śrī Sāhīlā Nānīsāheba" is mentioned among the numerous queens of Raṇabahādura, indicating her position as the third queen in the sequence. She is noted to be the daughter of Gaṇeśadatta Bā̃ḍīdvā’s daughter from ‘Gumiñā’, a village near Patna.क्ष्मीदेवीले विसं १८६९ (सन् १८१३) मा शिवलिङ्ग स्थापना गरिसके पश्चात् विसं १८७० (सन् १८१३) कार्तिक शुक्ल एकादशीका दिन चौघरा सतःका खातिर चौतर्फी जग खन्न लगाएको कुरा अभिलेखमा उल्लेख छ (N. Panta VS 2022, p.58) । राजा रणबहादुरकी अनेकन रानीमध्ये उनीलाई यहाँको अभिलेखमा ‘श्री साहिला नानीसाहेब’ भनिएबाट उनको वरीयता क्रम थाहा हुन्छ । उनलाई यहाँ पटनाबाट अलि परको जिल्लाभित्रको कुनै ‘गुमिञा’ नामक गाउँ निवासी  गणेशदत्त बाँडीद्वाकी छोरी भनिएको छ ।

event_name: Partial rebuilding of the north and west wings
event_description: In 1982 CE (VS 2039-40), renovations were undertaken on the north and west wings of thesataḥ.विसं २०३९-४० (सन् १९८२-८२) तिर सतःको उत्तरी र पश्चिमी खण्डलाई भत्काई पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।

Following the devastation caused by the earthquakes of 2015 CE (VS 2072), both the temple and sataḥ were reconstructed simultaneously. The reconstruction work, completed with the support of the Ministry of Urban Development of Nepal, the empowered Bagmati Civilization Integrated Development Committee, and loan assistance from the Asian Development Bank, was inaugurated by the then Minister of Urban Development, Ramkumari Jhakri, on January 23, 2022 CE (VS 2078).विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पमा मन्दिर र सतः दुबैलाई क्षति पुर्‍याए पश्चात् दुबै संरचना एकैसाथ पुनर्निमाण गरिएको हो । नेपाल सरकार शहरी विकास मन्त्रालय, अधिकार सम्पन्न वागमती सभ्यता एकीकृत विकास समितिद्वारा एशियाली विकास बैंकको ऋण सहयोगमा पुनर्निनिर्माणकार्य सम्पन्न गरी विसं २०७८ पौष आठ गतेका दिन (सन् २०२२ जनवरी २३) तत्कालीन शहरी विकास मन्त्री रामकुमारी झाक्रीबाट यसको समुद्घाटन गरिएको थियो ।

As mentioned above in the 'description, Queen Satajīva offered the wooden toraṇa (placed atop the sanctum door) depicting Nāmasaṅgīti in memory of her husband King Dhaṃta to replace the old dilapidated one.

The inscription on the pedestal of the Kālabhairava statue documents its consecration during the reign of King Lakṣmīnarasiṃha Malla (r. 1619-1641 CE). Despite erosion obscuring parts of the inscription, the term "jajamāna," meaning "the sponsor," is discernible before the donor's name. This indicates that the donor was an ordinary citizen, not a member of the royal family.
The marble inscription records that Pavana Khatrī, chief of the First Rifle Gaṇa of the Nepali Army, renovated thepāṭī(rest house) at the premises of the Kālabhairava shrine.
Davalasī, Jagatavīra, Kulāvīra and his family members offered a bell to Gaṇeśa.

event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātu (see object number LAL2130-007)
event_description: Cīrīmāyā Maharjana, Bulāla, Sujamāna and her family members from Tyāgala Ṭola constructed the Dharmadhātu.
The last renovation of the temple took place in VS 2060 (2003 CE) by the Department of Archeology.

event_name: Donation of land for annual worship
event_description: A plot(s) of land was endowed to theguṭhīto sponsor the annual worship for Gaṇeśa and also for Caitya erected in the temple premises.
The Caitya was renovated by the Cībhā Guṭhī which belongs to a Jyāpu family from Dhālchẽ Ṭola.

event_name: Unknown event (probably the construction of the Śikharakūṭa Caitya)
event_description: The letters of this inscription are defaced. It is probable that this records the construction of the Śikharakūṭa Caitya.
Pruscha(1975, 189) mentions that aguṭhīrelated to this temple was established in NS 768 (1648 AD). However, no evidence is so far traced out to verify this event.
Pruscha(1975, 189) mentions that the struts supporting the roofs were replaced in NS 863 (1743 CE). It could be the case that the temple was renovated during that time.
A woodentoraṇawas offered to Gaṇeśa. Since the letters inscribed on it are defaced, it is not clear when and by whom it was offered.

The inscription inscribed on the strut supporting the lower roof on the eastern side of the temple records the date Nepāla Saṃvat 1001 (1881 CE). It is probable that the temple was renovated during this time.
Rāma Maharjana, resident of Hiti Ṭola in Bulu, offered an oblong banner (patāḥ) to the temple.
The temple was reconstructed with funds from the local government.

On the southern wall of the circumambulatory path of thepīṭha, there is a sculpture carved on a single stone slab depicting six figures in the gesture of reverence (namaskāra mudrā). This sculpture was installed in the name of Mahādeva and Caṇḍeśvarī. Among the donors’ names, Manisiṃ (Maṇisiṃha) can be read.

On the southern wall of the circumambulatory path of the pīṭha, there is a sculpture carved on a single stone slab depicting six figures in the gesture of reverence (namaskāra mudrā). This sculpture was installed in the name of Mahādeva and Caṇḍeśvarī. Among the donors’ names, Manisiṃ (Maṇisiṃha) can be read.
To please Caṇḍeśvara Mahādeva and Caṇḍeśvarī, one crown, onepira(?), and onepatāsiwere offered. This act of donation was carried out by Viśva Bhāro of Tokha during the reign of Nṛpendra Malla.

During the reign of Bhūpālendra Malla, a pair of stone lion statues was installed at the front of thepīṭha. Among the donors’ names, Sivakinha (Śivakṛṣṇa) and his wife Si_śvarimayi (Siddheśvarī?) can be read.

This inscription is located on thetoraṇapositioned on the upper part of a small stone shrine constructed around the central area where the aniconic stone of the goddess is enshrined at the Caṇḍeśvarī pīṭha. Apart from the complete date NS 809 recorded in the inscription, the remaining text cannot be clearly read or meaningfully interpreted. Among the names of the donors, Manasiṃ (Manasiṃha) can be read.
The devotees of Tokha built a small stone shrine dedicated to Caṇḍeśvarī, positioning the main stone of thepīṭhaat its center.

This inscription bears a date NS 836 carved at the end of the text. In order to donate thepīṭhawith the intention of seeking liberation for a family member, certain arrangements were made within thepīṭhaprecinct. Written entirely in Sanskrit, the full meaning of this inscription has not been fully deciphered.

This inscription is carved at the feet of the donor figure, indicating that it pertains to the installation of that very statue. Although the date can be read, the remaining letters are no longer legible.

This inscription is preserved inside aphalcāwithin the Caṇḍeśvarī precinct. A trident is carved at the upper part of the inscription, while donor family figures carved in thenamaskāraposture appear in the lower part. Based on its overall characteristics, this inscription can be identified as belonging to the Late Medieval period. However, since all of its letters have been severely eroded, the written information has become unknown.
Due to severe erosion, it has become impossible to comprehend the written information on this inscription. Based on the script, it can be identified as belonging to the Late Malla period.

Padmakumārī, daughter of Narabhūpāla and sister of Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa, commissioned the construction of aphalcāwithin the Caṇḍeśvarī pīṭha precinct. That the sister of Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa created a work at this location is noteworthy. It is likely that her marital home was in or around Tokha.

The wife of Bhairavasiṃha, a resident of Pukhūlāchi, Tokha, reconstructed a phalcā within the Caṇḍeśvarī pīṭha precinct that had fallen into a dilapidated state. For its long-term maintenance, aguṭhīwas also established, and annual ritual obligations were prescribed through an inscription.
Ratnamān Śreṣṭha, a resident of Golkhopākhā, Thamel, offered eighty-four bells within thepīṭhaprecinct in the name of his deceased family members.

Centering around thepīṭha, a pillar was erected and a lion statue installed atop it. This act was jointly carried out by Indrarāja Jośī, Prakāaś Maharjan, and Alifa Ḍaṅgol, residents of Tokha, in the names of their respective deceased family members.

event_name: Addition of a toraṇa and flags
event_description: Maniṣarāj Jośī offered a metaltoraṇaalong with a pair of flags on the right and left sides atop thepīṭhain the name of his deceased family members.
Maniṣarāj Jośī offered a metaltoraṇaalong with a pair of flags on the right and left sides atop thepīṭhain the name of his deceased family members.

Maniṣarāj Jośī placed a stone seat bearing his name at the feet of the aniconic stone worshipped as Caṇḍeśvarī. Although no date is mentioned, the donor Maniṣarāj is the same individual who offered the metaltoraṇaand flags here in VS 2078 (2022 CE).

Mahān (soldier) Bilhāma Bhāro, along with his sons Siddhirāma and Praśurāma (Parśurām), daughter Sarasuti (Sarasvatī), and grandson Kṛṣṇarāma, performed a sacrifice (yajña) and established the deities Kumārī (Bālakumārī) and Vighneśvara (Gaṇeśa).

event_name: Offering of a pair of stone lions (LAL3010-008, LAL3010-009)
event_description: Yajñanārāyaṇa Bhāju, Gaṅgādhara Bhāro, Dhansing, Cikudhik, and others dedicated a pair of stone lions to the shrine.
Puṇyārāja Śreṣṭha, son of Mukhiyā Siddhimāna Śreṣṭha of Cāka Bāhāla, Lalitpur, offered a bell.
Mukhiyā Puṇyārāja Śreṣṭha, son of Siddhimāna Śreṣṭha of Cāka Bāhāla, Lalitpur, offered a stone pillar adorned with a peacock.

event_name: Offering of a new statue of peacock
event_description: Since the peacock image placed on top of the Peacock Pillar had been stolen, Subbā Puṇyarāja’s son, Kṛṣṇarāja Śreṣṭha, commissioned and installed a new peacock image.

event_name: Offering of a brass toraṇa to Gaṇeśa
event_description: A brasstoraṇawas offered for the Gaṇeśa shrine inside thepīṭha. The donor’s name has been erased.
Aphaygaṃ(wind chime) that rings with the breeze was installed at the Bālakumārī Pīṭha. The inscription does not mention the donor’s name.

The bell installed by Puṇyarāja Śreṣṭha in 1897 CE (NS 1953) later became damaged. The damaged bell was repaired and reinstalled by Buddhimāyā Tāmrakāra’s sons, Ratnalāla Tāmrakāra and Kīrtilāla Tāmrakāra. Buddhimāyā Tāmrakāra had the bell repaired in memory of her late husband, Miṭhāi Tāmrakāra.

event_name: Replacing the wooden pole of the flag
event_description: The wooden flagpole at the Bālakumārī Pīṭha had deteriorated, so a new pole was made and installed.

event_name: Kṣamāpūjā for the construction of shrine
event_description: The Bālakumārī Pīṭha, which was previously open along the roadside, was made secure by adding a roof and enclosing it from all sides. Akṣamāpūjā(penance) was performed before starting the work.

event_name: Offering of brass crown to Gaṇeśa
event_description: Mantalāla Maharjana, Urumilā (Urmilā) Maharjana, and others collectively offered a brass crown to the Gaṇeśa shrine inside thepīṭha.

event_name: Offering of Offering of a pair of metal lions (LAL3010-006, LAL3010-007)
event_description: In memory of the late grandfather Jitalāla Tāmrakāra and late grandmother Majjālakṣmī Tāmrakāra, their son Vaśantalāla Tāmrakāra and daughter-in-law Ratnamāyā Tāmrakāra offered a pair of metal lions to the Bālakumārī Pīṭha.

Narmadādevī and her sons Gumānsiṃ, Māthavarasiṃ, and Ghavojamānasiṃ built the Phalcā near their residence as per the wish of her husband Pratimāna Khatrī (text: Ṣatri), who passed away before fulfilling his wish. They also built ajaḥdhuṃtank and a well to supply water to the tank at the premises. An inscription at the Phalcā recording the event also instructs a person named Suratha Daṅgola from Theco to observe the anniversary of thephalcāout of the income from the land endowment made by the Khatrī family.

The private trust (guthi) run by the descendants of Pratimāna Khatrī reconstructed the Phalcā. Initially, the three-bayrest house used to stand by fields and a small street. However, when the trust reconstructed it, it was shifted a few meters to the west.

event_name: Construction of a śivaliṅga (SKH0020-003), a hiti and a phalcā.
event_description: A certain individual named Jayanārāyaṇa (text: Jayanārāyana) funded the construction of aśivaliṅgaalong with aphalcāand ahiti. Thephalcāmentioned in the inscription has since vanished, the other two structures remain intact.

event_name: Initial construction of the temple, consecration of statues of Mādhavanārayaṇa and Hanumān and land endowment
event_description: Five brothers, including Harikṛṣṇa Bhāro of Dhvakara Ṭola in Sankhu, commissioned the construction of thisśikhara-style temple during the reign of King Bhūpālendra Malla in 1699 CE (NS 819). They also consecrated statues of Viśveśvara Mahādeva, Mādhava Nārāyaṇa (SKH0020-004), and Hanumān (SKH0020-006) on the same occasion, in memory of their parents Madhusudana and Lakṣmīmayi. Upon completion the temple, they endowed several plots of land in order to serve as sources of income for conducting its anniversary celebrations and other obligatory and occasional rituals.

Before the 2015 earthquakes, this temple was in a state of disrepair: a small tree had grown on its roof, and cracks had emerged on the walls, causing thetoraṇas to deteriorate. The Department of Archaeology (DoA) undertook the reconstruction of the temple around 2013 CE.
Despite being rebuilt in 2013, the temple sustained significant damage during the 2015 earthquakes.
The Department of Archaeology rebuilt the temple in 2016 CE.

A group of eight individuals, led by Raṇhuju, established thecaityaat Kvātha Nani (Kvāḥ Nani). The group included Devasiṃ, Devajoti, Cintāmuni, and Manahorī, who were associated with the Diguri Sivā (a religious trust related to the lineage deity). It was decreed that no one should litter or damage thenaniwhere thecaityastood.
Santa and Herāmuni, along with others, collectively established one of thecaityas (BDG0050-008) within thebāhāḥcourtyard surrounding the Ratna Caitya.

Herā, Juju, Puṣpa, Caitya, and Nīlakumārī established threecaityas (BDG0050-003, BDG0050-004, BDG0050-005) surrounding the Ratna Caitya, symbolizing the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṃgha, the Buddhist trinity, respectively.
Theśivālayawas built in honor of Mahārānī Śubhakumārī (text: Śrubhakumārī), one of the multiple wives of Rāṇā Prime Minister Jaṅga Bahādura.

मार्बलमा उत्कीर्ण अभिलेखअनुसार यो विहार भिक्षुसंघलाई दानस्वरूप प्रदान गरिएको उल्लेख पाइन्छ। अभिलेखले जनाएअनुसार भिक्षु सुबोधानन्द, भिक्षु महास्थविर, भिक्षु प्रज्ञारश्मि, भिक्षु समंगल तथा भिक्षु सुदर्शनको प्रेरणा र पहलमा गणमहाविहारको निर्माण सम्पन्न भएको हो। साथै जापानस्थित क्योडान संस्थाको सहयोगमा विहार नजिकैको जग्गा खरिद गरी आवश्यक भवन संरचना निर्माण गरिएको तथ्य पनि यस अभिलेखमा उल्लेख गरिएको छ।

Bhājulāya Buddhācārya (text: Buddhācāyya Bhājulāya) and his wife, Pamalachimi, both from the Paśupati Mahāvihāra, Pasu Bāhāḥ (BKT0220) constructed thesataḥ. They also undertook the restoration of thehitilocated in the Āḥjudyaḥ Bāhāḥ courtyard.
Locals generously contributed both funds and labor to renovate thesataḥ.
Śrī Dīpaṅkara Ārya Nāmasaṃgīti Jñānamāla Bhajana Maṇḍala was formed for the perfromance of devotional songs at thesataḥ.

event_name: Construction of the phalcā and donation of land
event_description: According to the inscription, thephalcāwas built by a couple from Kutu Bāhāḥ in the name of their late son and is dedicated to Śrīnārāyaṇa. Locals say that the statue said to have been installed at the time of construction has since been lost. Threeropaniand 3yavaland of Pākubuṃ, 3ropanis of land of Tasiṃ Dhuṣacābuṃ and 7 karṣa of land of Dholosikvaṃ are offered.The inscription prescribes that the Bhāro (noble) brothers must offer burning wick lamps to the deity of thephalcāduring the entire month of Vaiśākha, including during the festival of the Rato (Red) Matsyendranātha. Moreover,japa(mantra)andpāṭha(sacred texts) shall be recited at this time. A lamp shall be offered for the whole month of Kārtika. Nowadays, these rituals are no longer performed.
The original statue of Trivikrama Viṣṇu was stolen sometime in 1985/86.

event_name: Damage suffered from the earthquakes and rebuilding
event_description: The Temple suffered heavy damages during the 2015 earthquakes, therefore the above-mentioned Śreṣṭha (Mehera) clan rebuilt it and consecrated a new statue of Trivikrama Viṣṇu in the sanctum.
This Caitya was demolished by Shams-ud-din in 1350. This inscription states that Meghapāla Varmā reconstructed thiscaitya, established the image of Buddha, and organised its ritual worships in 1357.
This inscription informs readers that Minister Jagatpati donated money so that a large parasol can be offered to thecaityaon an annual basis. He also donated money for theyajñaperformance.

During the reign of Śrīnivāsa Malla, the Caitya was renovated by Jayamaṅgala, Vijayadeva, Jideva and others. Thetrayodaśabhuvana(13 circular shaped portion on top) was replaced. The main priest (purohita) was Śiromuni of Nyākhācoka and the collaborator (as anupādhyāya) was Rachemana.

event_name: Consecration of stone statue of Buddha in niches
event_description: The stone statues of Buddha in the niches of the Caitya were consecrated by Vijaya, Gyānasingh, Jugideva and others.

Vajrācārya Dharmajoti established thisdharmadhātu maṇḍaladuring the reign of King Yoganarendra Malla. During the consecration ritual, Vajrācārya Dhajajoti took the role of the Ācārya, Vajrācārya Ratnakara played Upādhyāya, and the hymns were recited by Mahāmuni.

event_name: Replacement of trayodaśabhuvana(13 circular shapes on top)
event_description: During the reign of Gajapati Mahindrasiṃha (Bhāṣkara Malla), Ratnaśrī, Upādhyāya Bhikṣumuni, Tharapā Devalathaṃ, Latnadeva, Lahasiṃ and Śokṣasiṃha changed thetrayodaśabhuvana(13 circular shapes on top) of thecaitya. This is mentioned inRegmi(1966, 268-269).

event_name: Replacement of the harmikā and eight circles of thetrayodaśabhuvana
event_description: During the reign of King Rajandravikrama Śāhadeva, theharmikāand eight circles of thetrayodaśabhuvanawere replaced. Thapāju …dhānanda led this work and Dhanacandra, Govindasiñ, and Jīvanarasiñ assisted him.
Pūrṇalāla Śreṣṭha resides in the vicinity of the Pimbāhāḥ pond. He erected this stone pillar.
The bell to the south of Akṣobhya shrine was donated by Khaḍgamāna Singh Rājbhaṇdārī.
In 2002, thiscaityawas established by Aśoka Caitya Kṣetra Jīrṇoddhār Samiti, using archaic materials found in the nearby pond.
Thetrayodaśabhuvana(upper part with 13 circular shapes) of theaśoka caityawas repaired by Aśoka Caitya Kṣetra Saṃrakṣaṇa Samiti.

event_name: Renovation of the Temple and consecration of the main statue in the sanctum
event_description: The inscription on the pedestal of the Viṣṇu statue inside the sanctum records that a person named Budhimāna of the Calākhu Ṭola consecrated the statue and  renovated the Temple.

According to the Devamālā Vaṃśāvalī, King Ratna Malla established this village with 300 houses in 1513. He initiated an annual procession on the full moon day of Caitra, and it is likely that this procession was known as Pekhaḥ Jātrā back then.

event_name: Donation of a brass Canra-Sūrya, dalū and iron gate
event_description: In the memory of their mother, Lakṣmijati Dhanasĩ and his wife Bha Thakũ donated a brass moon and sun,dalūand made an iron gate.
Jugī Bhāro donated a metaltoraṇa.
In the memory of deceased Suryarāja Śākya (Triśulī) his wife Hirājyāna Śākya and other family members donated a metalpatāḥto the temple.
Dharmmaśrī, Rāma Bhāro and others donated three layered umbrella during the reign of King Yoganarendra Malla.
Śivarāma Maharjan, his wife Lakṣmī Maharjan and their sons donated metaljhallar(frill) below roof to all three roofs.
The temple was renovated with help of Lalitpur Metropolitan City and local people.

event_name: Establishment of the statue of Gaṇeśa
event_description: Originally there was no temple at Yanāmugaḥ Ṭola. Jisiṅha Bhāro, Ulhāśiṅha Bhāro, Cikuti Bhāro and other people jointly established the statue of Gaṇeśa.
Rāmadāsa Seṣṭa (Śreṣṭha), Kājīmāna, Bhagatīdāsa and others donated a bell which is installed in front of the temple.

event_name: Construction of the temple and establishment of a statue of Gaṇeśa
event_description: Viṣṇu Bhāro, Kāśirāja Bhāro, Devidāśa Bhāro and others jointly constructed the temple and established the statue of Gaṇeśa. Vajrācārya Mañjudeva was the priest of the event.
King Raṇabahādura Śāha installed the bell in honour of Goddess Taleju.

event_name: Empact of 1934 CE earthquake on the Bell
event_description: As recorded in the later chronicleDevamālāvaṃśāvalī, a chain of the bell broke in 1933 CE (VS 1990) due to the earthquake's effect. Consequently, the practice of ringing the big bell twice daily was suspended. The tradition was reinstated a year later following the completion of necessary renovations.

event_name: Restoration and continuation of bell ringing tradition
event_description: After a prolonged interruption, the practice of daily bell ringing was reestablished in 2009 CE (VS 2066). Presently, as of March 2023 CE, Bābukṛṣṇa Maharjana from Damāī ṭola in Kathmandu undertakes the responsibility of ringing the Taḥgaḥ Gaṃ every morning at 9 am, performing 108 strikes. In recognition of this duty, he receives NRs. 7,000 for each morning's bell ringing session.
In ca. 2010, the previously free-standing, five bay Phalcā with a pitched roof was dismantled and replaced by a concrete structure. It has been beautified with conical verneer bricks (dāci-apā).
The first floor was added to provided space for the community.
A Kṛṣṇa shrine is embedded in the southern wall of the Phalcā. A stone statue of Kṛṣṇa and Viṣṇu have been placed in a niche of the shrine. A gilttoraṇawas installed on top of this shrine.
Cikudhika Prajāpati, including 13 others from the Cavadaśa Guṭhī and Sukhuri Prajāpati - and ten others from the sameguṭhī- donated two golden finials to the temple.
Dhanamāsĩ (Dhanamāna Siṃha) Prajāpati donated land to light oil lamps and distributedsamayabajiat thephalcā.
This inscription is damaged in many places and therfore difficult to read. It mentions the donation of a golden pinnacle by Ragusiṃha Thakura in one place but the details are missing.

event_name: Pavement of stone in front of Bhīmasena
event_description: The stone in front of Bhīmasena was paved by Prajāpati Lakṣyasiṃha Thakura, Prajāpati Viṣṇusiṃha Thakura and Bhavadeva Thakura.
Local people widened the first floor of the god house by removing the window of the western side.
Gaumi Siṃha and others donated this bell to Bhīmasena. In this inscription Bhīmasena is called Mahāhindu Bhīmarājeśvara.
The temple was rebuilt by Lalitpur Metropolitan City, GIZ/UDLE - with the help of local people.

The earthquake of 2015 caused a crack to appear on the back of the Bhīmasena statue. The statue began to be refurbished in VS 2075, Āśvina 6. Artist Rajkumar Maharjan performed a worship at the Mhepi temple of Kathmandu and brought soil from the temple to repair this statue. The work ended with a special worship on VS 2075, Phālguna 1-3.
Jitavīra and his wife Methakuṃ jointly paved the Bāghabhairava Temple premises with stones.

A stone inscription is installed on the eastern side of the Ārīthāy Jaḥdhuṃhiti, but it does not belong to the Hiti itself.  The inscription recounts the history of water management in Kirtipur. Since Kirtipur always had shortage of water sources, Juhārī Kumārī, mother of Prime Minister Juddha Śamśera expressed her interest in supplying water to this area. However, she passed away before her interest was materialized. Therefore, her son constructed this hydrant under discussion in memory of his mother and named it after her as ‘Juhārī Kumārī Dhārā’ (see the inscription below).
As mentioned above, the hydrant constructed by Prime Minister Juddha Śamśera in memory of his mother was named after her as ‘Juhārī Kumārī Dhārā’.
The Phalcā was in a dilapidated condition. However, it is has a great ritual importance, and so local donations were collected so that it could be reconstructed.

event_name: Damage as a result ofroad traffic
event_description: A vehicle passing through the street struck the Phalcā on its western side and caused damage. Afterwards, a brick pillar was added to further support the upper slab.

While there is no inscription that records the temple’s construction, two stones—one in the southeast plinth and another above the door—bear the date “Samvat787,” aligning with Śrīnivāsa Malla’s rule. With the lack of historical sources, the identity of its builder in unknown, but the area was home to affluent communities like Jośī, Pradhāna, and Śreṣṭha castes during the Malla period, suggesting a wealthy patron from the area funded it.

While there is no inscription that records the temple’s construction, two stones—one in the southeast plinth and another above the door—bear the date “Samvat787,” aligning with Śrīnivāsa Malla’s rule. With the lack of historical sources, the identity of its builder in unknown, but the area was home to affluent communities like Jośī, Pradhāna, and Śreṣṭha castes during the Malla period, suggesting a wealthy patron from the area funded it.
Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan City, locals, and Gtz/Udle jointly rebuilt the temple after it fell into poor state of repair.

Wall paintings on the building show tales of Rāmāyaṇa, Viṣṇu’s reincarnations and Buddha’s Lumbini visit.The current wall painting is a copy of the original painting and was done after the reconstruction in 1995 CE.
The old structure was demolished and a concrete building was constructed.

event_name: Mention of the Balaṃpū Priest House
event_description: A manuscript record shows that a Brahmin of Brahmapurī (text: Brahmapuli) in Sankhu went through the initiation ritual, stretching its history back to the late medieval period.
After its roof collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes, the Priest House remained in a state of disrepair and was reduced to rubble after failing to survive years of sun and rain.
The Shankharapur Municipality has recently started (as of December 2021) reconstruction of this monument.
Commander Colonel Śoṇajaṅga Rāṇā, son of Bakhatajaṅga Kũvara Rāṇā, built the Rakṣāmukteśvara temple, along with anotherśivālaya, Bakhatamukteśvara, in memory of his father Bakhatajaṅga.
The Pashupati Area Development Trust initiated restoration efforts after the temple walls were damaged during the earthquakes in 2015.

This inscription details that the previous, dilapidated Sataḥ, was used by all castes for death rituals. It was replaced with the current Phalcā with the help of public donations totaling NRs. 2,332.68.

event_name: Installation of metal enclosure for Viṣṇu statue
event_description: With financial contributions from local donors, the Ward No. 12 office of the Kathmandu Metropolis enclosed the Viṣṇu statue with metal bars.
Kṛṇasiṃha Bhāro and his followers made this temple in 1681 during the reign of King Śrīnivāsa Malla.
Bisaṃdāsa and his wife Phulamāyā established thisdharmadhātujinālaya caityain memory of their parents Haridāra and Jogamāyā.
The temple was renovated with the use of donations made by the residents of Sunaguthi Ṭola.

event_name: Replacing brick steps with stone ones
event_description: Bisanārā of the Māhābo Ṭola in Pāṅgā, along with his wife Cidhi and sons Kṛsanbahādura, Jitabahādura, and Lokabahādura, replaced the brick steps leading to the first floor of thedyaḥchẽwith stone steps during the reign of the Rāṇā Prime Minister Candra Śamśera.

In 1649 CE (NS 769), King Pratāpa Malla undertook the construction of the temple and placed a statue of Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by his consorts, within the sanctum. This arrangement symbolized the king's desire to replicate himself and commemorate his two deceased queens, Rūpamatī and Rājamatī.
The temple suffered complete collapse during the earthquake of 2015 CE.

Following its complete collapse due to the devastating earthquakes in 2015 CE, the temple was reduced to rubble. Subsequently, the Department of Archaeology undertook its reconstruction, completing the restoration efforts in 2017 CE (VS 2074).

An unfortunate incident occurred when a mentally unstable woman dislodged the inscription that recorded the temple's construction from its original position, causing it to shatter into pieces. In response, the Hanumandhoka Palace Supervision Office promptly collected all the fragmented pieces of the inscription to ensure their safety. Although the broken pieces have been preserved, the restoration of the inscription within the temple is still pending.
Partly renovated by the family of Dhayiniche͂, who offered avimānawindow to the deity of Cyāsal Hiṭi Phalcā.
GTZ/udle and local residents donated money for the restoration of Cyāsal Hiti Phalcā.
A Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala was constructed by Kiraśīrāja.
The Bāhāḥ was constructed by Śākyavaṃśa Dhanasiṃha.

This inscription only mentions the date without providing details of the events that occurred on that particular date. Some activities related to the crafting of a work of art appear to have taken place on this date.
This inscription is unclear, but certain activities were carried out to make a new kind of machinery and for fire oblation.
Stones from Khohodola (a reference to this site) were taken in 1649 CE (NS 769). The objective for the procurement is not mentioned in the inscription.
Timbers were inspected for a certain construction work to be carried out by a person named Rāghava.
Something was done on this date. The inscription does not mention the event.

event_name: Selection of the stone for Cā̃gu
event_description: Stones from this site were selected for the installation of figures of elephant and lion intended for the Garuḍanārāyaṇa statue in Cā̃gu.
Stones from here were selected, as Jitāmitra Malla had intended to build a stone temple and organize fire oblation.
Something was done in 1697 CE (NS 817) to construct a stone pillar.
This inscription contains four numbers but does not mention the event that took place then.
This inscription contains a few letters but does not mention the event that took place then.

event_name: Construction of a statue of Akṣobhya
event_description: The statue of Akṣobhya was constructed in memory of the donors' teachers and parents and for the eternal welfare of all beings. The inscription mentions Candrabhava and Vibhūticandra as the donors.

event_name: Installation of a statue of Amitābha
event_description: Maṅgalalāla, Lakṣmīdāsa and others made a donation for the establishment of this statue. It was established after the old one was stollen.

event_name: Installation of a statue of Amoghasiddhi
event_description: Āśālāla, Herā and Bekhālāla donated funds for the installation of the statue. It was installed after the old one was lost.

event_name: The earliest mention of the Chinnamastā
event_description: A treaty was concluded among the sons of King Yakṣa Malla—Ratna Malla, Raṇa Malla, Ari Malla, and Jayabhīma Malla—pledging to live in harmony without internal conflict, and this agreement was recorded on a gold plate. In this inscription, Chinnamastā was listed as a witness alongside Cāṅgunārāyaṇa, and she is referred to as “Yetā Bhaṭṭārikā.”राजा यक्ष मल्लका छोराहरू रत्न मल्ल, रण मल्ल, अरि मल्ल र जयभीम मल्लबीच एकआपसमा झैझगडा नगरी मिलेर बस्ने भनी सन्धि गरी सुवर्णपत्र लेखेर राखिएको थियो । उक्त अभिलेखमा साक्षीको रूपमा चाँगुनारायणसँगै छिन्नमस्तालाई पनि राखिएको थियो । अभिलेखमा छिन्नमस्तालाई 'येता भट्टारिका' भनिएको छ ।

event_name: Offering of wooden toraṇa behind the temple
event_description: Khvāramānasiṃha Bhāju, Giridhala Bhāju, together with the temple priest Gaṅgārāma Bhāro, jointly installed a woodentoraṇaabove the door on the rear side of the temple.ख्वारमानसिंह भाजु, गिरिधल भाजु लगायत मन्दिरका पुजारी गंगाराम भारोले मिलेर मन्दिरको पछाडिपट्टि रहेको ढोकामाथि काष्ठतोरण चढाएका थिए ।

During the reign of King Girvāṇayuddha, Hanumantasiṃha Amātya, Bhājudhana, Sadāśiva, and Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha jointly installedbhagiṃand flags (dhvajā) on the roof of the Chinnamastā Temple.राजा गीर्वाणयुद्धको शासनकालमा हनुमन्तसिंह अमात्य, भाजुधन, सदाशिव र लक्ष्मीनृसिंह गरी चारजनाले मिलेर छिन्नमस्ता मन्दिरको छानामा भगिं र ध्वजा चढाएका थिए ।

Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha Amātya and Mānyalakṣmī Amātya together installed a gildedtoraṇafor the image of Chinnamastā within the sanctum. They also donated ritual vessels required for daily worship, as well as sevenropanīof agricultural land to support the offering of food in the daily worship.लक्ष्मीनृसिंह अमात्य र मान्यलक्ष्मी अमात्य दुईजनाले मिलेर गर्भगृहभित्र रहेकी छिन्नमस्तालाई सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको तोरण चढाएका थिए । उनीहरूले नित्यपूजाको लागि चाहिने भाँडाकुँडा लगायत नित्यपूजामा भोजन चढाउनको लागि ७ रोपनी खेत पनि चढाएका थिए ।

Nīlasundara Amātya of Daubahā Tole, Lalitpur, son of Mānakumārī and Kṛṣṇagovinda, together with his grandson Jitahari, installed a metalilāṃwithin the sanctum of the temple.मानकुमारी र कृष्णगोविन्दका छोरा ललितपुर, दौबाहाः टोल निवासी नीलसुन्दर अमात्यले नाति जितहरिसँग मिलेर मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र धातुको इलां चढाएका थिए ।

Captain Caturmānasiṃha, grandson of Jagannāthasiṃha Amātya of Lalitpur and son of Sanmānasiṃha, together with Sanakmānasiṃha Amātya of Bhosi Tole, Kathmandu, jointly installed three gildedtoraṇaabove the three doors on the northern side of the temple.ललितपुरका जगन्नाथसिंह अमात्यका नाति र सनमानसिंहका छोरा कप्तान चतुरमानसिंह र काठमाडौं भोसिको टोलमा बस्ने सनकमानसिंह अमात्यले मिलेर मन्दिरको उत्तरपट्टि रहेका तीनवटा ढोकामा तीनवटा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको तोरण चढाएका थिए ।

Mānakumārī of Daubahā Tole, Lalitpur, offered a bell (ghaṇṭa) to her personal chosen deity (sveṣṭadevatā), Chinnamastā. In this act, she was assisted by her sons, Jitagovinda Amātya and Harigovinda Amātya.ललितपुर दौबाहाः टोल निवासी मानकुमारीले आफ्नो स्वेष्टदेवता छिन्नमस्तालाई घण्टा चढाएकी थिइन् । त्यस काममा उनलाई छोराहरू जितगोविन्द अमात्य, हरिगोविन्द अमात्यले सहयोग गरेका थिए ।

Jitagovinda Amātya and Harigovinda Amātya of Daubahā Tole, Lalitpur, donated a gilded gateway (dvāra) to the Chinnamastā Temple. They were assisted in this undertaking by Jitagovinda Amātya’s sons, Kīrtigovinda and Pūrṇagovinda.ललितपुर, दौ बाहाः टोल निवासी जितगोविन्द अमात्य, हरिगोविन्द अमात्यले छिन्नमस्ता मन्दिरको लागि सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको द्वार चढाएका थिए । त्यस काममा जितगोविन्द अमात्यका छोराहरू कीर्तिगोविन्द र पूर्णगोविन्दले सहयोग गरेका थिए ।
Dvāre Manpadī donated a bell (ghaṇṭā; CAN0030-016) to Chinnamastā.द्वारे मनपदीले छिन्नमस्ताको लागि घण्टा (CAN0030-016) चढाएका थिए ।

Rāmadāsa Amātya, together with his wife Yogamāyā, gilded the copper roof of the Chinnamastā Temple.रामदास अमात्यले श्रीमती योगमायासँग मिलेर छिन्नमस्ता मन्दिरमा राखिएको तामाको छानामा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइदिएका थिए ।

Kīrtibahādura Amātya, together with his wife Jogamāyādevī, undertook the decoration of the Chinnamastā Temple. The inscription does not specify the particular works carried out for this decoration.कीर्तिबहादुर अमात्यले श्रीमती जोगमायादेवीसँग मिलेर छिन्नमस्ता मन्दिरलाई सजाइदिएका थिए । मन्दिर सजाउनको लागि उनीहरूले के के काम गरेका थिए भन्ने कुरा अभिलेखमा खुलाइएको छैन ।

In memory of their late grandfather Badrī Govinda Amātya and late grandmother Lakṣmī Amātya, Raśanā, Indu, and Śamira jointly commissioned and installed a newtoraṇaabove the doorway leading into the sanctum. This was done after the originaltoraṇaabove the sanctum entrance had been stolen.दिवंगत बाजे बद्री गोविन्द अमात्य र दिवंगत बज्यै लक्ष्मी अमात्यको स्मृतिमा रशना, इन्दु र शमिरले मिलेर मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने द्वारमाथि नयाँ तोरण बनाएर चढाएका थिए । गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने द्वारमाथि राखिएको पुरानो तोरण चोरी भएपछि उनीहरूले नयाँ तोरण बनाएर चढाएका थिए ।

In memory of their late grandfather Badrī Govinda Amātya and late grandmother Girijā Lakṣmī Amātya, Raśanā Śreṣṭha and Śamira Vikrama Jośī sheathed the pedestal (peṭī) on which the deities are installed inside the sanctum with brass plates.दिवंगत बाजे बद्री गोविन्द अमात्य र दिवंगत बज्यै गिरिजा लक्ष्मी अमात्यको स्मृतिमा रशना श्रेष्ठ र शमिर विक्रम जोशीले मन्दिरको गर्भगृभित्र देवीदेवताहरू राखिएको पेटीलाई पित्तलको पाताले मोडिदिएका थिए ।

event_name: Covering the walls with brass plates
event_description: Rameśacandra Vaidya of Mahābauddha, Kathmandu, together with his wife Rośanī Vaidya and other family members, lined the interior wall of the sanctum with brass plates.काठमाडौं महाबौद्ध निवासी रमेशचन्द्र वैद्य, उनकी श्रीमती रोशनी वैद्य लगायत परिवारका सदस्यहरूले मिलेर मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र भित्तामा पित्तलको पाताले मोडिदिएका थिए ।

An inscription in Licchavi script is carved on the pedestal (pādapīṭha) of the Gaṇeśa image installed within the Chinnamastā Temple. The inscription is undated and contains only the phrase:oṃ prāṇadhāra śarmmesyaḥ.छिन्नमस्ता मन्दिरभित्र स्थापना गरिएको गणेश मूर्तिको पादपीठमा लिच्छवि लिपिमा यो अभिलेख कुँदिएको छ । अभिलेखमा तिथिमिति छैन, केवलॐ प्राणधार शर्मेस्यःमात्र लेखिएको छ ।

The roof of the temple can be seen completely damaged in the 1850s painting of Henry Ambrose Oldfield (see,http://www.bl.uk/onlinegallery/onlineex/apac/other/019wdz000002844u00000000.html; accessed on 21.10.2020). It is probable that the temple collapsed during the 1833 CE earthquakes and was not renovated until 1850s.

event_name: Installation of a Pair of Elephant Statues
event_description: The temple can be accessed through a long flight of stone steps flanked by two stone elephants installed in 1662 CE. They are about five-feet tall including the remains of the broken riding figures on top of them.
Laṣkmīnātha Bābu (a younger brother of Viśvanātha who initiated the construction of the temple) installed the statue of Umāmaheśvara in the sanctum.

event_name: Installation of the First Viṣṇu Statue (A)
event_description: Someśvara Bābu installed the first Viṣṇu statue in the sanctum in the memory of Viśveśvara Bābu.
It is probable that Someśvara Bābu offered something to the temple. Since the last line of the inscription recording the event can hardly be deciphered, its content remains unclear.
In the memory of late Triratna and Rāmayāyā Maharajana, their son Surjamāna and other family members offered a brass banner (patāḥ) to the temple.
In the memory of late Triratna and Rāmayāyā Maharajana, their son Surjamāna and other family members offered the brassmaṇḍalato the temple.
The Kirtipur Metropolitan Office and the local community jointly adorned the temple in 2006 CE by carving its plain pillars and struts.

event_name: Installation of the Second Viṣṇu Statue (B)
event_description: Someśvara Bābu installed the second Viṣṇu statue in the sanctum.
The temple was again destroyed by the 1934 CE earthquakes but then was immediately renovated by Jagata Bahādura Pradhāna (known as Sipāĩ Bāje) using corrugated pewter sheets for its roof.
In 1947 CE, the pinnacle, crowning the third floor of the temple, was damaged by a heavy storm.
The temple was renovated by the Lāyekū Village Pañcāyata in collaboration with the local community and the Pañcāyata Ministry.
The stone gate of the temple was constructed in 1715 CE.
The plinths of the temple were renovated in 1719 CE.

event_name: Initial Construction, Land Grant, and Establishment of a Guṭhī
event_description: The temple was constructed by Viśvanātha Bābu from Tumbāhāḥ, Patan. He also endowed some land to maintain the temple as well as established aguṭhīto perform its annual rituals.

According to the local memory, the original bell of this temple was stolen by people from Bhaktapur. The original bell is also missing in the watercolour painting by Oldfield (1855 CE).The contemporary bell was installed following the 1994 CE earthquakes. This bell is originally a quarter striking bell from the previous Ghaṇṛāghara built by Bīra Śamsera. When the clock tower collapsed during the 1994 CE earthquakes, then prime minister, Juddha Śamsera, gave the bell at the request of current Dvāre of Kirtipur, Jagata Bahādura Pradhāna (also known as Sipāhi Bājyā). The inscription on the bell records that it had been cast by Gillet and Johnstone Founders of Croydon, England in 1895 CE.
Bhīma Bahādura Citrakāra of Bhaktapur, together with his family members, offered two metal lions to Goddess Bālakumārī in memory of his father Bhairava Siṃha and grandmother Gaṃgālakṣmī.
Bhīma Bahādura Citrakāra of Bhaktapur, along with his family, donated two metal lions to Goddess Bālakumārī in remembrance of his father Bhairava Siṃha and grandmother Gaṃgālakṣmī.

Above thispīṭha, a stonetoraṇafeaturingChepuhas been installed. According to the inscription located on the northern side of thetoraṇa, it is understood that thistoraṇawas offered to Goddess Bālakumārī by an individual named Kājimāna.

Thispīṭhaalso sustained damage during the earthquake of 2015 CE (VS 2072). The reconstruction of thepīṭhawas subsequently completed through the collaborative efforts of the Puri Foundation and supporters from Virginia.

This inscription is located on the northern side of thetoraṇa. The inscription bears the names “Naswalām Nānīmāyā.” Naswalām (Naswarām) and Nānīmāyā are presumed to be the donors who installed thistoraṇa. Beneath the inscription, a carved figure of a couple innamaskāra mudrācan also be observed.

On the southern side of the carved stonetoraṇafeaturingChepuinstalled above thepīṭha, an inscription reading “Kājimāna Dhanathakũ” is found. Below this inscription, sculpted figures of a couple innamaskāra mudrāare visible. On this basis, it may be concluded that the toraṇa was offered through the joint contribution of the couple named Kājimāna and Dhanathakũ.

Directly in front of the Bālakumārī pīṭha, an upright stone slab with a smalltoraṇahas been installed. Such stone slabs are commonly found atpīṭhas. At the center of this stone, the inscription “Kājimānaṃ Prīti” is carved, which indicates that it was offered by Kājimāna. Below the inscription, a carved triangular symbol can also be seen, which represents a symbolic emblem of the goddess.

On the southern side of thepīṭha, a small stone slab with a toraṇa bears the inscription “Kājimānṃ Prīti,” signifying that it was offered by Kājimāna. Beneath the inscription, a carved triangular symbol is visible, which serves as a symbolic representation of the goddess.
Rudranārāyaṇa Rājalavaṭa built the Siddhigaṇeśa Dyaḥchẽ.
The Department of Archaeology renovated the upper two floors of thedyaḥchẽ.
The statue was stolen from the temple in 1984.
A committee was formed to renovate the Nārāyaṇa temple of Patan. It also renovated the Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa temple in VS 2065 with the support of the Lalitpur Metropolitan City and local residents.

Jitāpurī (Jitāpura Gaṃcā) was constructed in Khokanā, the residence of the goddess Rudrāyaṇī, by a group of 38 individuals affiliated with three guṭhīs under the leadership of Siddhisiṃha Bhāvo. Responsibility for the maintenance and restoration of themaṇḍapa, in the event of damage or deterioration, was entrusted to these same threeguṭhīs. The construction took place during the tenure of Candravīra Siṃha Bhāro, who served as the Pradhan (chief administrator) of Khokanā.

Following the damage sustained by Jitāpura Gaṃcā during the 2015 CE earthquake, the structure was reconstructed in its original form. The reconstruction was funded by Chinīmayā Maharjan, a native of Khokanā who later settled in Dallu, Kathmandu. She donated NPR 700,000 in memory of her late husband, Aṣṭanārāyaṇa Maharjan, and her deceased parents, with the wish that their souls may find rest in the heavenly realm.
जनक कुमारीले कुमारीका नाउँमा एक घण्ट चढाए ।
कान्तपभा लामिछान्या (कान्तप्रभा लामिछाने) ले कुमारीको नाममा एक घण्ट चढाए ।
चनद्रवीर लामाले ८ धार्नीको घण्ट कुमारीदेवीको नाममा चढाए ।
झिल्टुङ्गका द्वारे छोतेलामाले कुमारीलाई प्रसन्न पार्न १९२ धार्णिको घण्ट चढाए ।
King Bhūpatindra Malla had constructed the Siṃhadhvākhā Durbar. The eastern part of the Siṃhadhvākhā Durbar was later transformed into the Lālabaiṭhaka.

In 1855 Dhīr Śaṃśer Rana had the central Malla-era palace dismantled and replaced with Lālabaiṭhaka, the Bhaktapur governor's reception building.The newly constructed Lālabaiṭhaka is documented in a watercolour by Henry Ambrose Oldfield, dated 1858.
Following the 2015 CE earthquakes, the Temple's outer walls developed numerous cracks.
Following the 2015 CE earthquakes, the Śreṣṭha family made minor repairs to the Temple.
The roofs of the temple leaked due to the lack of timely maintenance. A photo of the temple from 2014 CE shows its roofs covered by tarpaulin to prevent leakages.
