The 2015 CE earthquakes left the temple in poor condition although it did not collapse. Later in 2018 CE (VS 2076), the Department of Archaeology and the Sanātana Iṣṭadevatā Guṭhī (Maru Jośī), a social trust of the locals, collaborated on the renovation of the temple. Some of the stolen statues of other deities placed inside the niches in the sanctum were also replaced with new ones in the course of the renovation.
It was constructed in 1968 CE by Kṛṣṇa Bahādura and Gaṃgāmāna of Kirtipur.
The inscription mentions a one week long religious ceremony (Saptāha Kīrtana). Appaerntly this was organised by a Vaiṣṇava guru called Kavi Prasāda during the reign of King Mahendra.
A small bell was offered to Mahākāla.

event_name: Donation of construction materials and offering of a new pinnacle and ilā̃
event_description: During the restoration of the shrine, Mr. Rāmacandra Maharjana donated one tractor of sand and made an offering of a new pinnacle andilā̃.Mr. Kṛṣṇabhakta Maharjana donated cement and the funds for the workers' wages.
In 1939, Nārāyaṇa and others donated a bronzetoraṇaand clad the entrance of the sanctum in bronze.
Ratnamuni Vajrācārya from Nyākhācuka arranged for the construction of this Bāhāḥ and enshrined a statue of Śākyamuni Buddha in the sanctum.
In the same year, Ratnamuni Vajrācārya commissioned acaityain the courtyard and organised aguṭhīfor its yearly worship.
The statue of Śākyamuni Buddha was stolen. Some of thesaṅghamembers of the Kvāḥ Bāhāḥ made a cement statue to replace it.

Rājakumāra Bhāro, Vekhāsiṃha, Manahorā, and other members jointly dedicated a pair of stone lion statues in front of the shrine. Identical inscriptions bearing this description are engraved on both statues.

The inscription is engraved on both the left and right sides of the stonetoraṇa(MAN0010–014). Although the date of the inscription can be discerned, most of the letters have eroded. Among the legible portions, the name Ramakṛṣṇa appears as one of the donors.

An activity was carried out at the shrine, though the specific nature of the work remains uncertain due to the erosion of the inscription. Among the legible portions, the name Nārāyaṇī appears as one of the contributors.

Mucā Bhāro of Thã Bahī (Thamel) constructed a capāḥ on the eastern side of the open ground of Indrāyaṇī. He also endowed land to support the annual rituals associated with the newly built capāḥ. The inscription stipulates that, after his death, apiṇḍashould be offered annually on the anniversary of his passing from the income generated by the endowed land. Additionally, it prescribes offerings to be made on the occasion of the Indrāyaṇī palanquin festival.
During the reign of King Girvāṇayuddha Śāha, lands were endowed to provide a regular income for conducting the deity’s rituals. The endowment was made in the name of the king’s mother.

A wooden embossed inscription, now in the collection of a local resident, praises the then Prime Minister Candra Śamśera. It is believed that the inscription was installed on the occasion of his visit to the Indrāyaṇī Shrine. During the later reconstruction period, the inscription was collected and preserved by a nearby resident.
The shrine premises was renovated during the reign of King Mahendra.

Under the leadership of Śiva Khatrī, a bell weighing over 28 kilograms was installed in front of the Indrāyaṇī shrine. The names of all contributors and the details of the collected funds for this undertaking are recorded in the inscription.
A bell was installed in front of the shrine. This is the same bell mentioned in the inscription dated V.S. 2042 (1986CE). The date of the offering is also inscribed on the surface of the bell.
One of thepataḥs (banners) hung on the roof bears an inscription. The inscription records only the date of the offering, commemorating the offering of the banner on that particular day.
A bell was installed in front of the shrine; however, the inscription does not record the name of the donor.
One of thepataḥs (banners) hung on the roof bears an inscription. The inscription records only the date of the offering, commemorating the offering of the banner on that particular day.
In memory of Nhuchẽ Maharjana and Caityamāyā Maharjan, all members of their family jointly offered apatāḥ(sacred banner).

The Municipality rebuilt thephalcālocated in the south of the shrine. While the overall design follows the original structure, the roof has been replaced with copper sheets instead of the traditional tiles.

Thesataḥ(MAN0010-018), which has aphalcāon its ground floor, was reconstructed by the Municipality. While the overall design follows the original structure, the roof has been replaced with copper sheets instead of the traditional tiles.
Sūrya Kumāra Cakradhara and Sānumāyā Cakradhara of Thimi offered a banner in the name of Indrāyaṇī.

King Purandarasiṃha established the Duimāju Shrine at the Bhaṇḍārakhāla garden of the palace in memory of his deceased daughter-in-law Lalitalakṣmī. He also endowed land to form aguthifor the deity’s worship.​​

Chronicles mention that King Śrīnivāsa Malla established the Duimāju Shrine at the Bhaṇḍārakhāla garden. As the Shrine was already established by Purandarasiṃha in 1588 CE, King Śrīnivāsa may have renovated it.

During the reign of King Yoganarendra Malla, his courtier Cikuti Bhāro constructed the Phalcā to enshrine Duimāju and endowed land to form aguthifor the deity. It probably was an open shrine up until then.

event_name: Construction of a shrine for Duimāju
event_description: The details of this event are unclear from the inscription. It mentions the construction of a shrine for Duimāju and the installation of the finial. Also, some plots of land were endowed to form aguthito carry out sacrifices of ducks every year. Probably, the stone shrine inside the Phalcā was constructed on the occasion. The name of the donor is not mentioned but the event took place during the reign of King Yogaprakāśa Malla.
Gaṅgāśaṅkara established a trust by donating land parcels for the worship of Gopāleśvara and other deities of Pharping.

King Gīrvāṇayuddha introduced a new system for the operation of the trust formed for the worship of Gopāleśvara, Śeṣanārāyaṇa, Tilavikrameśvara, Aghoreśvara, Nandikeśvara, Siddhigaṇeśa, and Dakṣiṇakālī. The new system was enforced after the 128ropanīs of land parcels endowed for the trust were misappropriated. He also renovated thejalaharībase of the Gopāleśvara Śivaliṅga.

The 1934 earthquakes left the temple in a dilapidated condition with roofs falling off, necessitating reconstruction. However, during the reconstruction, the three-tiered temple was reconstructed into a dome-style structure while also reducing the size.
The temple sustained multiple cracks in the earthquakes and was on the verge of collapse.

The temple was rebuilt following the 2015 earthquakes, restoring its original tiered design instead of the domed style used in a previous reconstruction. The Department of Archaeology undertook the reconstruction at a cost of approximately NRs. 37.5 million.

A brass bull figure of Nandī, Śiva’s animal mount, was established at the temple in memory of the donor’s deceased father Rāmanātha Aryāla and his daughter Mañju Aryāla. The name of the donor is not mentioned in the inscription.

event_name: Consecration of a Vāṇaliṅga by Siddhimāna Before the Constraction of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Mandira
event_description: Subbā Siddhinārāyaṇa (Rājabhaṇḍārī), along with his wife Lānidhanalakṣmī, and sons Siddhimāna, Ratnamāna, Meharamāna, Baṣatamāna (Bakhatamāna), Kāśīnātha, and other family members, consecrated the Vāṇaliṅga on the bank of the River Bagmati.

Siddhimāna Rājabhaṇḍārī constructed Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Temple and endowed some plots of land to sustain the daily worship. Siddhimukteśvara Mandira (KAT2637) and Dhaneśvara Mandira (KAT2638) were also constructed by him.

An inscription is present at the site, but the portion containing the date and the section describing the specific act commemorated have become worn and illegible. Pruscha (1975, p. 87) and Locke (1985, p. 360) both state that an inscription dated 1679 CE (NS 799) existed here and that it was related to the construction of the caitya (KAT2390-002). It remains uncertain whether they were referring to the same inscription that is now difficult to interpret or to another inscription that has since been lost. On the basis of its script, the surviving inscription may be dated broadly to the late medieval period.यहाँ एक अभिलेख छ जसमा मिति भएको भाग र गरिएको ठिक कार्य दर्शाउने वाक्य खिइसकेको छ । Pruscha (1975, p. 87) र Locke(1985, p. 360) दिबैले यहाँ नेसं ७९९ (सन् १६७९) को एक अभिलेख भएको र सो चैत्य (KAT2390-002) निर्माणसँग सम्बन्धित भनेका छन् । तिनले हाल अर्थ लागाउन कठिन यसै अभिलेखलाई इंगित गरेको हो वा अन्य कुनै हराई सकेको अभिलेखका हो, भन्न मुस्किल छ । लिपिका आधारमा यो अभिलेख उत्तरमध्यकालीन भन्न सकिन्छ ।

Locke (1985, p. 360) and Pruscha (1975, p. 87) further report that the inscription of 1679 CE (NS 799) recorded that the caitya at this site was constructed by thePūrṇimā Sevāgroup.Locke1985, p. 360 र Pruscha (1975, p. 87) ले नेसं ७९९ (सन् १६७९) यहाँ भएको एक अभिलेखमा यहाँको चैत्यको निर्माण पूर्णिमा सेवा खलक भएको बताएका छन् ।
Thedevala, housing the Buddha image, was repaired in 1933.बुद्धमूर्ति भएको देवल सन् १९३३ मा मर्मत गरिएको थियो ।

More recently, in 2024 (VS 2080), oil-fired tiles were laid in the courtyard with funding provided by the Kathmandu Metropolitan City.हालसालै विसं २०८० (सन् २०२४) मा काठमाडौं महानगरको बजेटबाट चोकमा तेलीया इँट (टायल) बिच्छाइएको छ ।
Jasiṃ Siṃha, together with his sons Śivaduti and Rāmasiṃha, offered a bell (ghaṇṭā) to thepīṭha.जसिं सिंहले छोरा शिवदुति र रामसिंहसँग मिलेर पीठमा घण्टा चढाएका थिए ।

Karyāna (Kalyāṇa), Śujarāma (Sūryarāma), Jayakīnha, Bhavānī, and others jointly donated twomoharacoins and tenpāthīof rice to Naulina Bhadrakālī.कर्‍यान (कल्याण), शुजराम (सूर्यराम), जयकीन्ह, भवानि लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर नौलिन भद्रकालीलाई दुई मोहर र १० पाठी चामल चढाएका थिए ।

In the names of Dīlasīṃ (Dilsingh) and Viṣṇumāyā, Padama Bahādura, Kīrtī Kumārī (Kīrtikumārī), and others erected a stone pillar in front of thepīṭha.दीलसीं (दिलसिंह) र वीस्नुमाया (विष्णुमाया) को नाममा पदम बहादुर, कीरती कुमारी (कीर्तिकुमारी) लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले पीठअगाडि शिलास्तम्भ चढाएका थिए ।

In the names of his father Nar Bahādura Śreṣṭha and his mother Buddhimāyā Śreṣṭha, their son Sānukānchā Śreṣṭha donated a brasstoraṇato thepīṭha.बुबा नर बहादुर श्रेष्ठ र आमा बुद्धिमाया श्रेष्ठको नाममा छोरा सानुकान्छा श्रेष्ठले पीठमा पित्तलको तोरण चढाएका थिए ।

event_name: Offering of a pair of flags
event_description: Buddhimāna Śreṣṭha, together with members of his family, donated a pair of brass flags to the Bhadrakālī Pīṭha.बुद्धिमान श्रेष्ठले परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर भद्रकाली पीठमा एकजोडी पित्तलको झण्डा चढाएका थिए ।
The temple underwent restoration in the early 1970s.
The temple collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes and remained in ruins for seven years.

The Department of Archaeology completed the temple's reconstruction in 2023 CE (VS 2080). The reconstruction prioritized the use of original wooden materials, with new replacements only where necessary.
A woodentoraṇawas installed above the entrance to the sanctum. The name of the donor is unknown.

Vajrācārya Dhana Bande, Gopisiṃ Bhāro, Jayarāma Bhāro, and others collectively renovated thebāḥāḥ, paving its courtyard with bricks and offering atoraṇato the main deity. After the renovation, Vajrācāryas from Pasu Bāḥāḥ (BKT0220) performed the consecration rituals according to tradition.
A stone inscription was placed to record the renovation of thebāḥāḥ, the paving of the courtyard with bricks, and the offering of atoraṇato the main deity.
A pair of stone lions (BKT0490-004, BKT0490-005) was installed on either side of the staircase leading to the sanctum. The name of the donor who offered the lions is illegible.

Thepañcāvaliyuktacaityaat the premises was established by Helamati, Indralakṣmī, Bhājamāsiṃ, and Jyotamāyā. As the inscription is undated, it is unclear when thecaityawas established. However, the first structure of this type came into being only in 1831 CE.
Jagatabahādura Vaidya established aśivaliṅgaat the premises on the occasion of his son Jitendra Vaidya’s birthday.

Sanday(1994, 43) andGutschow(2011, 533) mention that the temple was built in 1792 by a merchant named Bhavman Singh Pradhan of Makhan Ṭol, but neither of them has revealed his sources. A stone inscription to the right of the sanctum's entrance is covered by thick layers of ghee and oil and cannot be deciphered. According to the priest, the inscription contains information related to the original construction of the temple.
The temple was rebuilt by the Vaiṣṇava family following the 1934 earthquake.

A tiled pedestal to the east of the temple supports a kneeling Garuḍa whose hands are held in thenamaskāragesture (mudrā). Two stone steles depicting donor figures and an inscription are embedded below the Garuḍa, in two niches on the west side of the pedestal. The stone inscription can no longer be clearly read. The date NS 913 is legible and might relate to the year when the Garuḍa was installed.

The monument was constructed in 1675 by two ministers of King Śrīnivāsa Malla. One was Bhagīratha Bhaiyāer (cautārā). The kings and princesses of Lalitpur, Kantipur and Bhaktapur including Bhaiyā(?) Rudrasena of Tanahu attended the inauguration ceremony of the Pāṭī.AYajñaritual was also performed at the same time. A person named Rājavãśa Rāvatta Narasiṁha is mentioned as the caretaker (chintāyāka) of the construction work.The inscription established in Taḥ Bahāḥ by order of King Śrīnivāsa Malla gives us a hint that the King placed great trust in Bhagīratha. Part of the inscription reads: “I see no difference between me and Bhagīratha Bhaiyā, [therefore] others also should not see any difference between him and me” (seeVajrācāryaVS 2056, 173 for the inscription). King Yoganarendra Malla, who succeeded Śrīnivāsa, accused Bhagīratha of mistreating the former’s queens and dismissed him from his post on the 5th bright fortnight of Māgha in NS 804 (seeRegmi1966, appendix III, p. 96). Bhagīratha Bhaiyā was killed by order of Yoganarendra on the 3rd dark fortnight of Bhādra in NS 805 (Regmi1966, appendix III, p. 95).
The pagoda style tower (pura) collapsed in the Great Earthquake of 1934 CE. The arcade survived (Gutschow 2011, 641). A few months later, the tower was replaced in a contemporary style.
In the 1980s CE, the upper floor of the monument was used as a police station. Afterwards, the Pāṭī became known as "Thanāpāṭī" (police-station pāṭī).

The Pāṭī was dismantled in 1994 and rebuilt with projecting windows and a pinnacle. The work was finished in 1995 with financial support from GTZ/UDLE.Gutschow(2011) reports that the upper storey with its projecting windows and the pinnacle were (re)constructed in 1995 with Henry Ambrose Oldfield's watercolour of 1855 used as a blueprint.

event_name: Donation of brass fringe of the roof (jhalara)
event_description: Thula Saṅkrāntiguṭhī, Kisamā̃, Siramã etc. donated the brass fringe of the roof (jhalara).
Rāmalāla Vyañjanakāra and Tuyumaiyā Vyañjanakāra donated two lion statues clad in brass. These are placed in front of the main entrance.
A special worship (pañcopacārapūjā) was performed.
The inscription is partially broken, and so it is not clear what event this commemorates exactly. The inscription mentions that something was established and land was bestowed upon theguṭhī.

event_name: Covering the upper roof with brass plate
event_description: Harṣamāna Vyañjanakāra and his other family members covered the upper roof of the temple with copper plate. The metal banners partially cover the place where the date is written, and so it could not be identified.

event_name: Fixing of the golden pinnacle and the flags
event_description: A golden pinnacle and two flags were fixed on top of the temple by Caturdaśīguṭhī.
The terracotta pinnacle of the temple was removed and a gilded pinnacle was installed by Jujumāna Vyañjanakāra.

event_name: Covering the lower roof of the temple with brass plates
event_description: Rāju Rājeśa and Lakṣmī covered the roofs of the temple with brass plates.
The temple was renovated, andkṣamāpūjāwas performed by Kulavīra Vyañjanakāra and Siṃtālī.
Āsāmadu Tepe donated a bell. This is fixed in front of the temple.
Mājuvīra and his family members donated a metal banner (patāḥ) to Gaṇeśa.

The Phalcā was initially constructed in 1844 by a donor named Rāota Nārāṃ and his wife Bhima Lakṣmī. The inscription reads that nobody must use this Phalcā as a shop. This underlines that the problem of encroachment ofphalcāshas been a challenge earlier.
The temple collapsed during the earthquakes.
Dayāla Bhāro (grandfather of Vīranārāyaṇa Siṃha who built Mahālakṣmī Mandira (LAL0020) in NS 821, i.e. 1701 CE) removed the temple’s pinnacle to renovate it.

event_name: Completion of the Renovation and Land Endowment
event_description: The renovation of the pinnacle by Dāyala Bhāro was completed in thirty-two days. He also established aguṭhīon that occasion.

event_name: Replacing Jhiṅgaṭī-tiled Roof with Copper Sheets
event_description: Sundaralāla Khaḍgī and his family replaced thejhĩgaṭī-tiles on the roof with the copper sheets.

event_name: Offering of a Metal Toraṇa and Metal Flags
event_description: Herālāla Tāmrākāra (text: Tamo), his wife Candrakumārī, and other family members offered a metaltoraṇa, crowning the entrance to the sanctum, and metal flags, flanking the entrance.
The 2015 CE earthquake severely damaged the temple. The temple is supported by the extra wooden columns provided by the local residents in the present-day.
Macchindra Bhāro repaired temple walls damaged by the earthquakes.

event_name: Collapse During the Earthquakes and Reconstruction
event_description: The temple collapsed during the earthquakes and it was reconstructed in the following year by Prime Minister Juddha Śamśera Rāṇā.

During the joint reign of King Siddhinarasiṃha and Srīnivāsa Malla, Dayāra (Dayāla) Bhāro offered two finials to the temple. On that occasion, thirty-eight buffalos and twenty-four goats were sacrificed to the Goddess.

A pond called Palesvā̃ Pukhū was constructed behind the temple on the eastern side. It is believed that Bālakumārī used to take bath in this pond (Śreṣṭha S. 2068, 24). However, this pond dried long ago and cannot be identified.

When tears flowed from the eyes of Rāto Matsyendranātha in Taḥ Bāhāḥ (LAL0060), thePañcarakṣātext was recited for eight days, and a special ritual followed by the sacrifices was performed in this temple, Vaiṣṇavī Temple of Yappā, and Mahālakṣmī Temple (LAL0020).
During the reign of King Yoganarendra, Īśvaradāsa Bhāro renovated this single storey temple and made it three-storied.

event_name: Reconstruction of the Temple and Offering of a Gold Pinnacle
event_description: The temple was reconstructed and a gold pinnacle was offered.

event_name: Donation of a Pinnacle and Land Endowment
event_description: Īśvaradāsa Bhāro performed thesahasrāhutifire sacrifice and added a pinnacle to the temple. King Yoganarendra Malla also participated in this event. Iśvaramāna also endowed some plots of land to theguṭhī. It was regulated that theguṭhīincome is used to organise a sacrifice to be conducted by the priests, Jośīs and Karmācāryas, on every fifth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Jeṭha.

During the reign of King Viśṇu Malla (1729-1745 CE), a famine broke out. The king made Sarvānanda Paṇḍita of Mahābauddha performpuraścaraṇaandnāgasādhanā(invocation of serpents) at Kvāche Bālakaumārī shrine. It rained following the rituals.
A newtoraṇawas offered after the old one was stolen.

event_name: Renovation of the Temple and Pavement with Telia Bricks
event_description: Macchindra Bhāro renovated the temple and paved its sanctum and courtyard with theteliyābricks.
Lakṣmīsiṃha Rājabhaṇḍārī and his family from Kathmandu renovated the temple and offered twenty-seven pinnacles.
Macchindra Bhāro offered a woodentoraṇato the temple.

event_name: Offering of a Toraṇa and Jewellery
event_description: Atoraṇa, a crown, and sevenkikiṃpā(the wings on the crown of an image of a deity) were offered to the Bālakumārī and kept in the sanctum.

event_name: Offering of a pair of lions
event_description: The inscription on the pedestal of the northern of the two guardian lions informs us about their installment, but it does not specify the name of the donor.

This inscription is unrelated to this monument; rather, it records a land endowment by Crown Prince Pratāpasiṃha Śāha to sponsor the celebration of Indra Jātrā in Nuwakot. It is unclear whether the inscription was originally installed here or relocated to this location at some point. Since it is unrelated to any specific monument and instead documents the land endowment for the procession, it is probable that it was originally located here.Interestingly, the topmost portion of the inscription features a carving of aviśvavajra, a doublevajra, which is a significant ritual object in Vajrayāna Buddhism. The inscription is documented in D. Vajrācārya and Ṭ. Śreṣṭha VS 2032, second part, p. 29 (inscription no. 34); D. Vajrācārya and Ṭ. Śreṣṭha VS 2037, pp. 74-75, and it reads as follows:[L1] श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥ ॥ शाके सायकनागभूप १६८५ तुलिते मासे नभस्ये सि-[L2] ते पक्षे वैष्णव ऋक्षयुग्घरितिथौ सिंहाधिरूढे रवौ ॥ श्रीशक्रध्वजसम्यगु-[L3] (च्छ्र)यमहप्रत्यब्दसंसिद्धये शालेयं सनयं प्रतापनृपतिः क्षेत्रं समुत्सृष्ट-[L4] वान् ॥१॥ पृथ्वीनारायणस्य क्षितिपतिमुकुटप्रोतमाणिक्यमालासं-[L5] स्पर्शाराधिताङ्घ्रे रिपुकुलगह(नो)द्दीप्तदावानलस्य ॥ सूनुर्विख्या-[L6] (तकी)र्त्तिर्दिशि दिशि महसा भास्करो याचकानां कल्पद्रुः कामिनीनां म-[L7] दन …. सिंहप्रतापः ॥२॥ क्षेत्रं भूपालपुत्रस्तु….[L8] …. ॥ खवाह …….. ॥३॥ प्रतापसिंह …….[L9] व …. मया न …. र्पितम् । यो हरे …. महापातकपंच-[L10] कम् ॥४॥ (स्वदत्तां) परदत्तां वा यो हरेत वसुन्धरां । (। षष्टि)वर्षसहस्राणि[L11] विष्टायां जायते कृमिः ॥५॥ षिंच्यातको आयस्ता मुरि एक सय[L12] चालिस श्रीइन्द्रदेवताकन जात्रानिमित्त गुठ चह्राञौ ॥ शुभम् ॥

यग्लभूमि (काठमाडौंको दक्षिणभाग) मा रहेको मण्ड टोर (मरु टोल) को उत्तरपट्टि रहेको घरमा बस्ने विमलेश्वरदासले महादेव मन्दिर निर्माण गरी जग्गा गुठी राखिदिएका थिए । जग्गाबाट हुन आम्दानीले नित्यपूजा चलाउनको साथै शिवरात्री, इन्द्रजात्रा र मन्दिरको वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गर्न व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । पूजाआजा गरिसकेपछि बाँकी बचेको रकमलाई मन्दिर जीर्णोद्धार गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था पनि गरिएको छ ।
The  inscription on the stone stele is severely damaged.

event_name: Building of the Sage Agastya Shrine
event_description: Śubharāja Mahājana established a shrine to Agastya above the central water spout.

This inscription is engraved on a brick located on the southwest edge of the Hiti. Although the inscription does not record an event, it can be assumed that it was intended to record the the hiti's paving with brick. The inscription doesn't record the name of a donor or craftsmen who might have carrfed out the work, however, it does state that Amātya Siddhirāma prepared the inscription with Harirāma, Nandurāma and Rāmeśvara Bhāro as witnesses.
The Lalitpur Sub-Metropolis and the Department of Archeology restored the hiti.

Tilakaram Kārkī, a resident of Cobhāra, along with his family, paved and improved the road from the bank of the Balkhu river to the banks of the Viṣṇumati river.चोभार निवासी श्री तिलकराम कार्की र सन्तानहरू मिली बल्खु नदीको पारी किनारादेखि विष्णुमति तीरसम्मको बाटो छापी राम्रो बनाएको थियो ।

Subedāra Gajesī Kārkī from Cobhāra had built a road from the confluence of the Sundarīghāṭa stream to the confluence of the Balkhu river.चोबार बास्ने सुवेदार गजे कार्कीले सुन्दरीघाट खोल्सी दोभान देखि बल्खु दोभान खोल्सीसम्म बाटो बनाएको थियो ।

event_name: Renovation of Dhārā and Phalcā built
event_description: The construction of the Ḍhikure Pāṭī and the restoration of the spout were carried out by the family of Subedāra Jagesī Kārkī from Kārkī village in Cobhāra.चोभार कार्की गाउँ बस्ने सुबेदार जगेसी कार्कीका परिवारबाट यस ढिकुरे पाटीको निर्माण र धाराको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो ।

In memory of his wife Kṛṣṇa Kumārī Kaṭuvāla, Hari from Bhājangālā renovated the dhārā area by laying concrete and plastering it.पत्नी कृष्ण कुमारी कटुबालको सम्झनामा भाजंगाल बस्ने हरिले यस धारा परिसरमा ढलान र पलास्टर गरी जीर्णोद्धार गरेको थियो ।

With financial support from Kīrtipur Municipality, ward no. 6, the restoration work was carried out by the Pāṭīdhārā Restoration User Committee.कीर्तिपुर नगरपालिकका वडा नं ६, को आर्थिक सहयोगमा पाटीधारा जीर्णोद्धार उपभोक्ता समितिबाट जीर्णोद्धार कार्य गरियो ।

Thisjaḥdhuṃ(water trough) was originally constructed by the main road connecting Cāpāgāũ and Theco, serving as a vital source of water for travelers and passersby. While the original inscription is no longer present, its text was published by D. Vajrācārya (VS 2056, p. 298). The inscription reveals that in 1697 CE (NS 818), four brothers—Lvaṃvā Bhāro, Vāsiṃha Bhāro, Pabhārāma Bhāro, and Devarāma Bhāro—from Capāla Livichẽ, Cāpāgāũ, built aphalcā(rest house). They dedicated a statue of Madhusudana in their father's name and installed statues of three deities in honor of their mothers, Sarasvatī Mayī and Maṇikarṇṇa Mayī. Concurrently, ajaḥdhuṃwas also established in the names of their parents.To ensure the upkeep of these structures and the continuation of cultural rituals, land was endowed as a trust. The inscription mandated various annual ceremonies, including ancestral worship (śrāddha), communal meals for Brahmin couples, Jośīs (astrologers), andācāryas (teachers), and other forms of worship. Furthermore, the trust was obligated to provide 67pāthīs of rice annually to the individual responsible for consistently refilling thejaḥdhuṃ's water trough.
दुई हरफको यस अभिलेखमा कुनै देवता स्थापना गरिएको कुरा लेखिएको छ तर विवरण स्पष्ट छैन । यस अभिलेखमा मिति उल्लेख छैन तर लिपिको आधारमा यो अंशुवर्माको समयको मानिएको छ ।
A Jaḥdhuṃhiti was constructed during the reign of King Rudradeva. Donor's name is not mentioned in the inscription.

पहिले कुम्भेश्वर महादेवको मन्दिर केवल छाप्रो मात्र थियो । ललितपुर निवासी जयभीम नाम गरेका महाजनकी श्रीमती अनन्तलक्ष्मी बिरामी भएपछि जयभीमले श्रीमती निको भएमा कुम्भेश्वरको सुन्दर मन्दिर बनाइदिनेछु भनी भाकल गरेका थिए । तर उनकी श्रीमतीको निधन भयो । तैपनि जयभीमले दिवंगत श्रीमतीको स्मृतिमा नेसं ५१२ (सन् १३९२) मा कुम्भेश्वर मन्दिरको निर्माण गरिदिएका थिए । मन्दिर निर्माण कार्य सम्पन्न भएको उपलक्ष्यमा जयभीमकी कान्छी श्रीमतीले सुवर्ण कोश चढाई लक्ष्याहुति यज्ञ गरी मन्दिरमा सुनको गजूर चढाइकी थिइन् । त्यस समयमा नेपालमण्डलमा जयस्थिति मल्लको शासन चलिरहेको थियो ।
Bahādula Malla Kumhala, a resident of the Gāḥ Bāhāḥ, had offered a trident to the north side of the Kumbheśvara temple.

राजा श्रीनिवास मल्लको राज्यकालमा सूर्य्यराम मुल्मी भारोले सर्वेश्वर महादेवको आग्नेय कोण (दक्षिण-पूर्व) मा फटकिरी (alum) को सूर्य्येश्वर महादेवको स्थापना गरेका थिए । उनले त्यस शिवलिङ्गमा सुवर्णको चतुर्मुख मूर्ति बनाई तीन तहको छत्र पनि चढाएका थिए ।
पहिले दुई तला मात्र भएको मन्दिरलाई राजा योगनरेन्द्र मल्लले तला थपी पाँच तलाको बनाइदिएका थिए ।

event_name: Endowment of lands to the guṭhī
event_description: राजा योगनरेन्द्र मल्लले पहिलेदेखि चल्दै आएको गुठीलाई हेरविचार गरी जग्गा दान दिई मन्दिरको धार्मिक गतिविधि सञ्चालन गर्न सहयोग गरेका थिए ।
राजा योगनरेन्द्र मल्लको राज्यकालमा कोट्याहुति यज्ञ गरी मन्दिरमा सुनको जलहरि र गजूर चढाइएको थियो । त्यस अवसरमा पूर्णानन्द उपाध्यायले कोट्याहुति गरेका थिए ।

event_name: Construction of the statue of Śrīdharanārāyaṇa and endowment of lands to Sarveśvara Mahādeva
event_description: शंकरबाबुको नाममा श्रीधरनारायणको प्रतिमा निर्माण गरी सर्वेश्वर महादेवको पूजा गर्न जग्गा गुठी राखिएको थियो ।
राजा विष्णु मल्लले सर्वेश्वर महादेवलाई सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको पाताले मोडेको बसाहा चढाएका थिए ।
Dhanasiṃha Mulmi Bhāro and his wife Mīlamha Lakṣmī दम्पत्तिले मिलेर मन्दिरको पश्चिम द्वारमा सुवर्ण खापा चढाएका थिए ।
राजा विष्णु मल्लले नेसं ८५५ (सन् १७३५) मा चढाएको बसाहा चोरी भएकोले राजा रणबहादुर शाह आफैले एक तोला सुन प्रदान गरी नयाँ बसाहा बनाउन लगाएका थिए ।
नेसं ८१९ (सन् १६९९) मा राजा योगनरेन्द्र मल्लले चढाएको घण्टा बिग्रेपछि Raṇodyota Sāha र Samaśera Sāha ले मिलेर घण्टाको जीर्णोद्धार गरेका थिए ।
नेसं ९२८ (सन् १८०८) मा आएको भूकम्पले मन्दिरमा क्षति पुगेकोले सरकार समक्ष विन्ति चढाई अमात्य हनुमन्तसिंहका चार दाजुभाइले मिलेर मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरेका थिए ।
Amātya Hanumantasiṃha, Bhājudhana, Sadaśiva and Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha had jointly offered golden toraṇa to Sarveśvara.
दौबहाल निवासी अमात्य जितगोविन्दले आफ्नी दिवंगत पत्नी सुवर्णकुमारीको मोक्षको कामना गरी सर्वश्वर महादेवलाई सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको तामाको जलहरि चढाएका थिए ।
The temple was completely collapsed in the 1934 earthquake. Daughter of Sāhu Jita Govinda of Daubahāl, Patan and the main priest of the temple were killed, as the temple collapsed then.

event_name: Offering repousse image of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva
event_description: हिरण्यवर्ण महाविहार, इतिलन्हेका मानिसहरूले अष्टमी व्रत बसी तामाको पातामा वज्रपाणि बोधिसत्वको प्रतिमा र कलश चढाएका थिए ।
राजा महेन्द्रको आदेशानुसार मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार कार्य गरिएको थियो ।
राजा महेन्द्रले मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरी घण्टा (LAL1050-007) चढाएका थिए ।

event_name: Replacing jhiṅgaṭī roofs with copper plates
event_description: मन्दिरका पाँचैवटा छानामा राखिएका झिङ्गटी झिकेर तामाको छाना हालिएको थियो ।

नेसं ८९१ (सन् १७७१) मा को बाहा: टोलका जयकृष्ण मुल्मी भारो र रामनारा दुईजनाले मिलेर चढाएको घण्टा नेसं १०५४ (सन् १९३४) को भूकम्पले गर्दा फुटेको थियो । दाताका सन्तति बेखालाल मुल्मीले छोराहरू रुद्रलाल र हरिबोल मुल्मीसँग मिलेर फुटेको घण्टा जीर्णोद्धार गरी चढाएको थियो ।
विसं २०७२ वैशाख १२ गते (सन् २०१५) आएको भूकम्पको पराकम्पले मन्दिरको सबैभन्दा माथिको छाना भत्केको थियो ।
भूकम्पले बिग्रेको मन्दिरलाई पुरातत्व विभागबाट जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो । जीर्णोद्धार कार्य सम्पन्न भएको कार्यक्रममा प्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवा उपस्थित भएका थिए ।

This weathered stone inscription is no longer in readable condition. The few letters that can be deciphered indicate that three donors jointly arranged a certain worship. Locals mention that this inscription was originally placed under a large nettle tree near the Candanabharāṭeśvara temple (Ś. Rupākhetī and Ś. Rājavaṃśī VS 2053, p. 85).

A group of locals pleased Thankot’s local administration chief of, Kāśīrāja Bhāro, and Cikati Bhāro to adorn the Gaṇeśa shrine with atoraṇa. The work was coordinated by Jevanasiṃ Bhābo, while Bisiṃ Bhābo, Biśvasiṃ Bhābo, and Bhāgisiṃ Bhābo took care of the arrangements.

PātravaṃśaRāutaVaikuṇṭha Bhāro, a resident of Datalhāche in Dhvākhābāhāra, constructed the temple for theśivaliṅgaand established a trust. Over time, the temple built by Vaikuṇṭha Bhāro fell into disrepair and was destroyed. Later, Lakṣmīrāja Bhāro, the grandson of Vaikuṇṭha Bhāro, reconstructed the temple, after Candanabharāṭeśvara Mahādeva appeared in a dream and instructed him to rebuild the temple. After consulting with his mother Lakṣmī and brother Lakṣmīdhara, he obtained permission from King Yoganarendra Malla and reconstructed the temple, while also offering a golden finial. Upon completion, Rāmacandra, a brahmin from Bakhanimha Ṭola in Lalitpur, performed a fire ritual.

Lakṣmīmai from the Dattarāche Ṭola built aphalcāin the name of Śiva. She further initiated a tradition of lighting butter lamps at thephalcāonŚivarātrīand distributesamaybajito locals. While the phalcā no longer exists at the site, locals say that it used to stand northeast of the temple.
Śrīrāma Thāpā installed a new bell in memory of his mother Surakumārī after the previous bell offered by Mahāvīra, son of Śerabahādura, was damaged.
With donations collected from the locals, stone slabs were laid on the floor of the temple premises.
A canopy was installed over the Candanabharāṭeśvara Śivaliṅga with Vijaya and Babitā Vaidya contributing coppers sheets and other devotees making cash donations.

event_name: Replacing jhĩgaṭī roof with brass sheets
event_description: The traditional jhĩgaṭī tiles on the temple roofs were replaced with brass sheets by collecting donations from the devotees.

In memory of his deceased parents Khilākumārī Thāpā and Hirāsiṃha Thāpā, Dilabahādura Thāpā renovated the stone water spout (hiti) southeast of the temple. Originally, there was only one spout. Two additional spouts were added during the renovation while the original one was replaced with a new one. The original spout lies unattended next to the water spouts.

The statue of four-armed Śiva (PPK0210-002) was established during the reign of King Pratāpa Malla. Due to the erosion of the text of the inscription, the name of the donor cannot be ascertained. However, his wife's name can be read as Kāmeśvarī.
Yogī Naraharinātha conducted research of the Virūpākṣa temple during the reign of King Mahendra.

Prime Minister Vīra Śamśera constructed the temple as his effort to showcase his effectiveness in governance following a tumultuous change in leadership. Vīra Śamśera assumed power by assassinating the incumbent Prime Minister Raṇa Uddīpa Siṃha, who also happened to be his uncle.
Kṛṣṇamāna Śreṣṭha enshrined a statue of Kṛṣṇa and his consorts Rādhā and Rukmiṇī in a niche on the northern wall of the Phalcā.

event_name: Offering of Various Objects to Caitya
event_description: Jayaśvara Bikṣu, Narahari Bhāro, Lakṣmīnātha, and others jointly offered a gilt crest-jewel (cūḍāmaṇi), parasol, and garland to the Caitya.
Stone steps were built in front of the Akṣyobhya niche.
Harṣa Maharjana and his wife Guṃkṣmi (Guṇalakṣmī ?) jointly renovated the Caitya.
Viśvasiṃha Bhāro installed a statue of Padmapāṇi (KIR0021-005) to the north of the Akṣobya shrine.  Unfortunately, the inscription date is illegible.

monument_name: Nāmasaṅgīti Phalcā (second half of 19th cent. CE)
event_description: There were three statues in the Phalcā: two of Mahākāla and Gaṇeśa and another unidentified one. All were stolen in the 1990s.

monument_name: Nāmasaṅgīti Phalcā (second half of 19th cent. CE)
event_description: The Phalcā was expanded and modified.
The Bāhāḥ was established by an individual named Padma Rāja Śākya. It takes its Sanskrit name, Padmavarṇa Vihāra, from the name of the founder.

Śākyavamśa Narendradhana and Ratnadhana renovated the Bāhāḥ and built a wall around it. After the renovation, a golden pinnacle in the shape of acaityawas installed and the daśakarma(ten rites of passage) was performed.
Harṣaratna and Khaḍgaratna of Hitiphusa Bāhāḥ renovated the Bāhāḥ.
Indrarāja Śākya paved thebāhāḥcourtyard withteliyabricks.

event_name: Hand over the Bāhāḥ to Tibetan monks
event_description: In order to run the Bāhāḥ smoothly, Ratnamāna Śākya and Harṣamāna Śākya of Hitiphusa Bāhāḥ handed over the Bāhāḥ to the Tibetan monks Śubhasāgara and Mañjuśāsana.

event_name: Extension of the Bāhāḥ and installation of the statue of Padmasambhava
event_description: A statue of Padmasambhava was installed on the first floor, extending the area of ​​Bāhāḥ to the right, left and back. Donations were raised to do these things.

By the year VS 2030 (1973 CE), the Bāhāḥ had become obsolete. During the reign of King Birendra, in VS 2037 (1980 CE), under the leadership of Bhikṣu Mañjuśasana, the work of demolition of Bāhāḥ was started. Reconstruction work was completed three years later, with donations from various individuals and the labor of the locals.
Bhājudeva (text: Bhājudeo), thedvāreof Sankhu, constructed it (see the description above for more information).
Kvātha Chẽ was a three-story building standing on all four sides with a courtyard at its centre. The building collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes except for the eastern wing.
Thebāhāḥand thecaityawere commissioned by Bekhārāja Vajrācārya.
The monastery was consecrated the year after the great earthquake (e.g. ca. 1935 CE).
The 12-year mask dance of Bhadrakālī commenced in 1485 CE (NS 605) during the reign of King Ratna Malla (J. VajrācāryaNS 1118, p.12).

event_name: Offering of statues and land endowment
event_description: King Raṇabahādura Śāha offered small masks of various deities to be taken around the city during the palanquin procession and also endowed land as an income for organizing the procession.
Dhīrjanārāyaṇa Śreṣṭha (text: Dhijanārāṃ) offered two statues of Bhadrakālī: one to be exhibited every Saturday and the other to be taken around for a procession.
Bhāranarasiṃha (text: Bhāranarasi) of Te Bāhāḥ endowed land to form aguthifor performing worship of two palanquins of the deity from Vaṭu and Te Bāhāḥ during the annual procession.

event_name: Addition of a prabhāmaṇḍala in sanctum
event_description: Buddhinārāyaṇa Maharjana (text: Buddhinārāṃ) installed a circle of rays or flames (prabhāmaṇḍala) behind the statues enshrined at thedyaḥchẽ.

The recent reconstruction of thedyaḥchẽtook place in 2014 CE (VS 2071) with funds provided by the Department of Archaeology, Guṭhī Saṃsthāna, Kathmandu Metropolis, and donations from locals. The height of thedyaḥchẽwas increased during the reconstruction.
The top roof collapsed in the 2015 earthquake.
As of January 2020 the temple is under reconstruction. The work is taking place under the management of the Department of Archaology, Government of Nepal.

Rudradevī Ṭhakurānī, a daughter of Śrīnivāsa Malla, renovated a Maṇḍapa of Bungmati with the help of her son Rudrendra Malla. The roof of one of the Bhairava temple of Bungmati was paved withteliyābricks. There are two Bhairava temples in Bungmati, Lindekunde Bhairava and Hayagrīva Bhairava. The inscription does not specify which temple was renovated.
Indra Malla and his wife Bhāgyavatī offered a golden statue of Bhairava to the temple.
The temple was renovated by Āsārāma, Māna Bahādura, Kīrtirāja, Gayā (Dayā) Prasāda and Hari Prasāda.

event_name: Renovation or restoration? of the temple
event_description: The earliest record found in the temple is of NS 776 (1656 CE). This date is engraved at the bottom of a strut which used to be part of the lower roof. However, it is not clear whether the date inscribed refers to the original construction or to a restoration effort.
The upper roof of the temple fell down in 1860.

After the roof was damaged, the government allowed locals to cut wood in the forest of Kaṭuvāla Daha to use for its restoration. The following year, the roof was restored by thepānejugroup of Bungmati among others (Munirāja, Dhanapati, Siṃhamuni, Buddhi Gubhāḥju, Lekhanadāsa Harṣa, Viṣadhaṃ). 21dhārnīsilver and 41dhārnīcopper was added to various parts of the temple during its reconstruction.
In 1995 CE, the hiti was renovated with the support from the Lalitpur Metropolitan City Office and Department of Archaeology.
The hiti was renovated in 1703 CE, during the reign of Yoganarendra Malla. The name of the donor who sponsored the renovation cannot be read.

This inscription is badly damaged. The legible part reads as follows: "If anyone destroys this roof, he will incur sins." Since the hiti has no roof, it can be assumed that this inscription is not related to the hiti, but may relate to the Gaṇeśa temple next to it.

Rādhākumārīdevī, Thira Śamśera Thāpā, Nara Śamśera Thāpā, Gaṃbhīra Śamśera Thāpā, and Raudra Śamśera Thāpā established the Śiva temple by consecrating Dharmamukteśvara Mahādeva in the sanctum in the name of their father Dharma Śamśera Thāpā Kṣetrī. They also established three additionalśivaliṅgas in the sanctum, namely, Śivamukteśvara in their mother Śivakumārīdevī's name, Śubhamukteśvara in Śubhakumārīdevī's name who probably was their father’s first wife (jeṭhīmumā), and Naramukteśvara in their grandmother Naranandakumārīdevī's name. The siblings also donated land for daily and periodic worships at the temple.

Narendra Śamśera Thāpā Kṣetrī added Rādhāmukteśvara Mahādeva, the fifthśivaliṅgain the sanctum named after his grandmother Rādhākumārīdevī, making it apañcaliṅgaensemble in the sanctum of Dharmamukteśvara. Narendra Śamśera also donated land for various rituals related to Rādhāmukteśvara.
The establishment of a trust, along with a comprehensive list of donated land parcels post the inception of Dharmamukteśvara, was documented through the installation of this inscription.
The Pashupati Area Development Trust reconstructed the temple, which was already in a dilapidated state before the 2015 earthquakes, which led to its destruction.

event_name: Historical mention of the area and possibly the temple/shrine
event_description: The upper portion of the Licchavi inscription features a carving of a conch shell (śaṅkha) and a discus (cakra), which are the implements associated with Nārāyaṇa. This suggests that the inscription was installed at the Nārāyaṇa temple that probably existed back then. However, the content of the inscription is more political than religious. King Gaṇadeva gave autonomy to the residents of this area on certain issues. The mention of the term “koṭṭa” in the inscription suggests that there may have been a fort here at that time. Scholars also presume that horses from the Himalayan region were brought here for sale.The inscription edited in D. Vajrācārya and Ṭ. Śreṣṭha VS 2032, second part, p. 3 reads as follows:L1 स्वस्ति मानगृहाद . . . . . .L2 …… भट्टारकमहाराजश्रीगणदेवः कुशली ….L3 व्राह्मणपुरस्सरान् ग्रामकुटुम्विनः कु(शलम्पृष्ट्वा)L4 समाज्ञापयति विदितमस्तु भवतां यथा सर्व्वदण्डनायक-L5 महाप्रतिहारश्रीभौमगुप्तविज्ञापितेन मया युष्माकं ….L6 …… लिङ्ग्वल् माप्चोक …. धिकरणैर्न्न प्रवे ….L7 …… करण ….L8 …… प्रेवेशो नास्तु यदा – अत्र म ….L9 …… वाहा .. आनीयन्ते …. प्रवेश ….L10 …… कोट्ट … नमित्यस्य चL11 प्रसादस्य चिरकालस्थितये शिलापट्टकशासनेन प्र-L12 सादः कृतस्तदेवमवगत्य यूयन्निर्व्वृतविश्वस्ताः सुखंL13 प्रतिवसतेति येपि च मदूद् र्ध्व राजानो भवितारस्तैरपिL14 धर्म्मगुरुभिर्गुरुकृतप्रसादानुवर्त्तिभिरियमाज्ञा सम्य-L15 क्प्रतिपालनीयेति, दूतकश्चात्र सर्व्वदण्डनायक-L16 महाप्रतिहारश्रीभौमगुप्तो वरीवर्त्ति संवत् ४००L17 ८५ कार्त्तिकमासे शुक्लदिवाद्वादश्याम् १२] [०] [L18 राजपुत्रवन्धुजीवे व्यवहरतीति ] [

event_name: Installation of gilded lattice window with toraṇa on the first floor
event_description: Cigaṭī Mānandhara and his family from the Mahābauddha Ṭola installed the window.
​The gilded window, which was in poor condition, was repaired by the descendants of the donor of the window.
The Dyāḥchẽ was rebuilt after being damaged by earthquakes in 2015 CE.

event_name: Installation of a pair of stone statues (see monument objects above)
event_description: The pair of stone statues were installed by Rubi Dāhāla and Rukṛti Dāhāla from the Upakāra Sevā Pharmā in honour to Lucubhulu Ajimā.

There is a stone inscription on the southern side of the Jaḥrūhiti. This inscription is not related to this monument but rather recounts the history of water management in this area. Because the Sunaguthi residents had no source of clean water, they were forced to drink water from the well. Juddha Śamśera's mother Juhārī Kumārī expressed interest in constructing a water spout in the Sunāguthi area. However, she passed away before she could carry this work out. After her death, her son Juddha Śamśera constructed a water spout to fulfill his late mother's wish.
Harṣamuni Śākya commissioned the construction of this Caitya.

event_name: Establishment of a Statue of Vyāghriṇī (KAT3180-036)
event_description: The name of the donor who established this statue is covered with cement plaster and thus illegible.

event_name: Establishment of a Statue of Siṅghinī or Siṃhinī (KAT3180-035)
event_description: A certain Jinadeva established this statue in the memory of his grandfather. The part of the inscription where the date is mentioned, is covered with plaster. However, we can assume that this and the aforementioned Vyāghriṇī statues must have been installed around the same time.

event_name: Installation of a Stone Pillar with Trident During the Reign of King Bhūpālendra Malla
event_description: Jayakalyāṇa, his wife Lukumanī, his two sons Jayakṛṣṇa and Jayaśaṅkara jointly installed this stone pillar with trident to the north of Ṭaṅkeśvara. This event took place during the reign of King Bhūpālendra Malla.
The Department of Archaeology (DoA) renovated the temple.

event_name: Establishing a Statue of a Female Donor
event_description: Rantamaya (Ratnamāyā) from Om Bāhāḥ, Kathmandu, established this stone statue of her mother, Chīniyādevī.
Sāphalya Amātya established this statue.
Mādhurī Pradhān Amātya established this statue of Umāmaheśvara in the memory of her parents.

event_name: Construction of the phlacā and endowment of land
event_description: यो फल्चा भोनिसंष्र भारोले निर्माण गरेका हुन् र उनले उनले फल्चा निर्माण गर्नुका साथै यसको नियमित सञ्चालन तथा संरक्षणका लागि फल्चाको नाममा खेत गुठीसमेत व्यवस्था गरेका थिए ।
विसं २०१७ (सन् १९६०) मा सडक फराकिलो बनाउने क्रममा उक्त ऐतिहासिक फल्चा भत्काइएको थियो ।
विसं २०७४ (सन् २०१७) मा सडक फराकिलो बनाउने क्रममा उक्त ऐतिहासिक फल्चा भत्काइएको थियो र पछि सडकको सीमाभन्दा केही भित्र पुरानै शैलीमा पुनःनिर्माण गरिएको थियो ।

A Śākya family (Motimāyā, Nemakara, Ratnakara, Bhairavakara, Najarakara, Devīmāyā, Jñānabāhādura, Kṛṇamāyā, Canakara, Budharatna, Cirīmāyā, Kīrtilānī etc.) from Patan Bu Bāhāḥ (LAL0440) commissioned the construction of a Dharmadhātujinālaya Caityaat the bank of the confluence.

An inscription on a marble slab attests to the construction of the newphalcāin VS 2058 (ca. 2001 CE) by Surajanātha, the third son of a certain Viṣṇucandra. It mentions that the originalphalcābuilt in VS 1981 (ca. 1924 CE) had collapsed. It is said to have been commissioned by Hirālāla, Viṣṇucandra, and Venimādho Rauniyāra, the three sons of Vaccurāma. Later on, thephalcāwas renovated by Śivaprasāda, the elder son of Viṣṇucandra. The VS 2058 reconstruction was supported by Surajanātha, the third son of Viṣṇucandra. It is further mentioned that the land located to the west of Silkhu Phalcā was bestowed upon thephalcāto support its religious functions and upkeep.

event_name: Installation of a stone statue of Śākyamuni Buddha
event_description: A donor from Kirtipur Pãngā established the statue of Śākyamuni Buddha.

event_name: Paving of terracotta tiles in front of the Phalcā
event_description: Terracotta tiles were paved in the Phalcā courtyard (Lũchẽ Nani).
The Phalcā was constructed.

The inscription dated NS 982 mentions that the street was paved with tiles and an additional bay and a spout were added. This inscription was installed 27 years after the initial construction of the Phalcā.Today, there is no spout in the surrounding area.
The earlier seven-bayed Phalcāwas dismantled and incorporated into a four-storey concrete building.
Three lines have been inscribed below an image of an eye. The meaning of the text is unclear.

event_name: Construction of the Phalcā and installation of two Viṣṇu statues
event_description: According to the inscription a certain Kṛṣṇa Mulmī Bhāro of the Cāphare Ṭola in Kirtipur built it and installed two Viṣṇu statues: the Śrīdhara Viṣṇu statue (see object number KIR4049-002) in memory of his father Hākudeva Mulmī Bhāro and mother Annpūrṇā, and the Viṣṇu statue flanked by his consorts Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī (see object number KIR4049-001) in memory of his first wife Kanyāvatī.
The 2015 earthquakes damaged the upper floor of the Phalcā. As a result, the Mānandhara family, who lived in the Phalcā, demolished the upper floor and covered it with corrugated tin sheets.
The state granted 150ropanīs of land in the name of Hanumantasiṃha Amātya for the expansion of the settlement in Kupondole and the maintenance of the Bagmati bridge.

Hanumantasiṃha Amātya received an additional 25ropanīs of land grant. It was stipulated that anyone settling on this land had to maintain the bridge. That same year, he, along with his brothers—Bhājudhana, Sadāśiva, and Lakṣmīnarasiṃha—established statues of Hanumaṃteśvara Mahādeva, Kṛṣṇa, Gaṇeśa, Bhagavatī, Kaumārī, Naṭyeśvara, Sarasvatī, and others, and also built asataḥ. Matching his own name, he established the Hanumaṃteśvara Mahādeva and Hanumān.
The Hanumān statue is flanked by lamps, one installed by the family of Rañjanā Pradhāna and the other by the family of Hemanta Rāṇā.
The family of Karṇa and Mirā Śreṣṭha offered a pair of brass flags to the Hanumān statue.
The shrine was renovated with the assistance from the locals.

The Hanumān Mandira Saṃrakṣaṇa tathā Vyavasthāpana Samitī, established by devotees, constructed an entrance gate for the shrine using funds collected from the donation box and savings from the temple's bank account.
Deva Buddhācārya, Jaya Buddhācārya, Muni Buddhācārya, and Rathana Buddhācārya jointly established the esoteric deity (āgaṃdyaḥ).
During the reign of King Pṛthvī Vikrama Śāha, Budhacāryya Jayanarasiṃ, his wife Mayjulāni, and son Bekhāmuni established adharmadhātujinālayacaitya(BKT0320-005) in thebāhāḥ's courtyard.
Four brothers Budhācāryya Amoghavajra, Jñā(na)vajra, Māhāvajra, and Paṃcarāja offered a bell (BKT0320-008).
Harṣa Budhācārje, together with his mother and son, offered a brass door for the sanctum, wishing for the heavenly abode of Sukhāvati Bhuvana for his deceased father Haṣamāna.

Maṃjumuni and his family members established acaityain the name of his deceased parents Amṛtamuni and Lataṃ Thakuṃ. They also endowed land to observe the anniversary ritual of thecaitya. It is not clear which of thecaityas at thebāhāḥis being referred to here.

Budhācārje Sākebhikṣu Bekhāmuni, the seniormost elder (thapāḥju) of thebāhāḥ, endowed oneropanīof land to continue the tradition of playing musical instruments throughout the holy month of Guṃlā (July-August).

event_name: Replacement of jhĩgaṭī tiles with brass sheets
event_description: Putali Thakuṃ, his son Harṣavajra and others replaced the traditional tiles on the roof of thebāhāḥ’s balconied tower (phucā) with brass sheets. They also covered the struts and other parts of thephucāwith brass sheets. The names of Mahāvaja, Paṃcarāja, Mohanamāyā, Visnumāyā, and others are engraved on the lower part of the struts.

event_name: Offering of a pair of metal flags and prayer wheels
event_description: Śākebhikṣu Jñānavajra vowed to offer a pair of brass flags and 10 copper prayer wheels. As he passed away before he could fulfill his vow, his wife Putalimāyā and her family members including son Sugatarājā offered flags and prayer wheels as per the vow of her late husband.

event_name: Establishment of a pair of metal lions (BKT0320-002 and BKT0320-003)
event_description: Maṃjumuni and his family members offered a pair of metal lions (BKT0320-002 and BKT0320-003).

The Temple was renovated using concrete and modern construction material.
Pūrṇa Bahādura Nakarmī, a resident of the Ṭola installed metal oil lamps around the Temple.

Muni Thakuṃ, along with her son Jumāsiṃ and their family, installed a metaltoraṇaon top of the entrance to the Cañcala Gaṇeśa temple in honor of her deceased husband Taḥdhi Maharjana. Thetoraṇaserves as a beautiful embellishment to the temple entrance.

event_name: Offering of a pair of gilded flags
event_description: Suṣucā, Byatīmayeju, and others from the Kilāgala Ṭola offered the pair of gilded flags to the temple.
The brass door was offered by Dasnārāṃ, Beṣānārāṃ, and others in memory of Bālakṛsna and Sānu, who were members of the Kilāgala Ṭola community.
The temple underwent reconstruction in 1994 CE with the support of the ward office and donations from the local community.

event_name: Consecration of a new statue of Gaṇeśa
event_description: In 2011 CE (VS 2067), a fire broke out at the residence of the temple's caretaker located in Tāhāḥ Nani, resulting in the destruction of the Gaṇeśa statue that was used for the annual procession, as well as its jewelry. A new statue and jewelry were made to replace the ones that were destroyed. Afterward, it was decided that the statue and jewelry would be kept at thetvāḥchẽinstead of the residence of the temple's caretaker, to ensure their safety and accessibility to the local community during festivals and other important occasions.

Thepāṭīwas partly dismantled in 2008 and subsequently rebuilt by the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust. The restoration was financed through a large grant from the US Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation (2009).The restoration report prepared by KVPT reads as follows:"Prior to restoration, Kot Pati rest house was a series of makeshift rooms separated by partition walls. After the successful completion of the restoration program, the rest house now appears in its original configuration as continuous long arcade as documented in historic photographs. As with most of the other buildings in the complex, the Pati’s historical tiled roof had been replaced with machine-made flat pan tiles laid onto the timber battens, causing significant water leakage right through the building. This meant that large sections of the structure had to be dismantled and reconstructed using new timber elements. Out of the 34 carved columns and capitals 31 could be restored and were professionally cleaned and reinstalled in their original positions. All historic pillars required new sections of timber to be grafted to their base sections. Two original windows in the western section of the Pati were restored whereas all other small openings above the arcade had to be made new. The new roof structure and cover were designed in the traditional manner. The redundant horizontal ceiling planks were removed to allow for a more spacious and luminous interior. 1 inch hardwood planking and 3/4 inch marine-grade plywood united the roof timber members to create a strong diaphragm and uniform surface for a water proof membrane. Traditional terracotta roof tiles were then placed on a mud-bed on top of the membrane. The fl ooring was covered with traditional terracotta tiles, fa.ades were rebuilt usingma-apabricks, and the buttresses supporting the brick wall were consolidated.""The restoration of Kot Pati progressed quickly. Partition walls were dismantled so that the space retained its original character as a long arcade. Tiling and soling of the floors was completed, and the back wall’s supporting buttresses were rebuilt. Finally, the entire roof structure and cover was replaced.Detailed Activities:- The existing Kot Pati needed to be almost completely dismantled as it was in a highly dilapidated condition. All redundant partition walls and horizontal ceiling planks were removed.- The missing or damaged stone pavement, plinth edges, and mouldings were recreated following existing historic examples.- The historic plinth was completely re-built along the face of the Pati using edge stones andteliatile.- The cement pavement was removed and the floor of the Pati was repaved with traditional floor tiles (cikã apā)in lime and brick dust (surki)mortar.- The existing roof was removed and a new roof structure was constructed in its place with new closely-space timber joists in a traditional configuration- Hardwood planks and marine-grade plywood unite the roof timber members, creating a strong diaphragm and uniform surface for a waterproof membrane.- Traditional terracotta roof tiles were laid on a mud-bed on top of the membrane.- New windows, designed to mirror the old ones, were installed on the principal facade.

As mentioned by D. Vajrācārya in his book 'MadhyakAbhiālakālekha' (2056, 87), an inscription formerly displayed in the Thabũ Phalcā indicated that it was renovated by Śrīmadhusūdana Deva and Govinda Bharo, after taking permission from the Śreṣṭha Bhāros of the Ṭola in 1672 CE (NS 762). The inscription is no longer available.
Since circa 2003, Thabũ Phalcā has been rented to a Kārkī family. The Kārkī family has been living on the first floor while running a tea shop in the basement.

An inscription dated 1957–58 (VS 2014) found at the site records that thephalcāhad been damaged in the great earthquake of 1934 (VS 1990).यहाँ प्राप्त विसं २०१४ (सन् १९५७-५८) को अभिलेखमा यो फल्चा सन् १९३४ को महाभूकम्पमा क्षति भएको प्रसंग छ ।

The inscription on the inner wall further states that Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa of Vambāhā (Om Bahāḥ), Kāntipura, renovated thephalcāin 1957–58 (VS 2014) in the name of his son. It also notes that the structure damaged in 1934 (VS 1990) was restored only twenty-four years later, indicating a considerable delay between destruction and repair.फल्चाको भित्री भित्तामा भएको अभिलेखमा कान्तिपुर वंबाहाः (ओम बहाल) का लक्ष्मीनारायणले आफ्नो छोराको नाममा विसं २०१४ (सन् १९५७-५८) मा फल्चा जीर्णोद्धार गरेको कुरा परेको छ । सोही अभिलेखमा विसं १९९० (सन् १९३४) मा क्षति भएको फल्चालाई जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको भनिएको छ । यसको अर्थ क्षतिको २४ वर्षपछि मात्र फल्चाले सवल हुने मौका पाएको देखिन्छ ।

Even before the major earthquake of 2015 (VS 2072), thephalcāwas in a severely deteriorated condition. After the earthquake, only the masonry walls remained standing. In 2023 (VS 2079), the structure was reconstructed under the supervision of Ward No. 12 of Kathmandu Metropolitan City. According to a ward representative (Kaḍgī, male, age 52), efforts were made to follow the earlier form; however, in comparison to the previous structure, the height of the rebuiltphalcāhas clearly been increased.पछिल्लो महाभूकम्प अगावै फल्चा निकै दयनीय स्थितिमा थियो । भूकम्पपछि फल्चाको गारोमात्र बचेको स्थितिमा थियो । विसं २०७९ (सन् २०२३) मा काठमाडौं महानगरपालिका वडां नं. १२ को रोहवरमा फल्चाको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको हो । विगतकै स्वरूपलाई अनुशरण गर्ने प्रयाग गरिएको दाबी वडा सम्बद्ध व्यक्तिको छ (one of the ward members, Kaḍgī, male, age 52) । विगतको तुलनामा फल्चाको उचाईमा भने वृद्धि गरिएको स्पष्ट देखा पर्छ ।
Punasīṃ Dhyake and Dhanasīṃ of the Lāchi Ṭola in Bode offered a bell to the temple.

Since a significant portion of this inscription has faded, its contents are not entirely clear. It seems to record the establishment of a religious trust in the name of the Śiva and Sarasvatī shrines. The donor’s name is decipherable as Hirānanda, though other details remain uncertain. Based on its style, the inscription likely dates to the Rāṇā period.
N. Gutschow's findings highlight the establishment of four temples in Patan by Mahāpātras (nobles) during the period between 1144-1597 CE, including the Keśavanārāyaṇa Mandira.

This is the earliest inscription found inside the temple. It records the installation of metal siṃha faces in the temple by queen. Moreover, She offered some vessels to be used for daily worship and endowed 12 ropanīs of land as a source to run the tradition.

event_name: Formation of a guṭhī  to run rituals
event_description: King Rāya Malla and other Royal members formed a guṭhī to run daily and annual rituals in the temple. Those whose duty it is to manage and perform prescribed rituals of the temple are mentioned as a group of seven persons including Raci Kasta (Khanimaṃ ṭola), Rathana (Tuyalachẽ  ṭola), Hrṣarāja( Tiprakvachẽ ṭola), Luṭu (Yolaṃ ṭola), Jopaci Maḍika (Kvāchẽ ṭola), Hera Sāhū (Golamaṇḍī ṭola), Ḍopa (Pvaṃḍulāchẽ  ṭola) and Jakharāja (Khanimaṃ).
The temple was renovated in 1998.
As perPruscha(1975, 217), The temple was renovated after the earthquakes of 1934 CE and again in 1968. But he has not given any source to justify this mentioning.
During the reign of King Tribhuvana, Prime Minister Bhīma Śamśera installed an iron water tap, known as Tri-Bhīma Dhārā (PPK1107-006), for the supply of drinking water to the public.
The temple underwent renovation by the Pashupati Area Development Trust in 2002 CE (VS 2059). A marble inscription installed after the renovation identifies the temple as the Rudreśvara Śivālaya.

Upon the initiation of the Jayavāgīśvarī Ṭola Sudhāra Samiti, a local committee formed for the preservation of the area, Rāmakumāra Śreṣṭha and his wife Sīta Śreṣṭha performed the reconsecration of both the Pādaveśvara Śivaliṅga and the temple. Interestingly, the inscription makes mention of theśivaliṅgaas Pādaveśvara. It is possible that theśivaliṅgawithin the sanctum was temporarily removed during the temple's reconstruction, and the inscription was installed after theśivaliṅgaunderwent reconsecration following the completion of the rebuilding. However, it's worth noting that the inscription does not contain any reference to the reconstruction itself.

event_name: The earliest mention of the Bāhāḥ
event_description: A palm-leaf manuscript dated NS 245 and archived in Rudravarṇa Mahāvihāra refers to Taṅgaḥ Bāhāḥ as Tanikvala Vihāra.
Thedharmadhātujinālaya caityawas constructed to the north of thedyaḥchẽ.
Thedharmadhātu maṇḍalawas constructed in the Bāhāḥcourtyard.
Taṅgaḥ Bāhāḥ was pulled down and replaced with a concrete frame structure.
Jikesiṃha Bhābo of Sunāguthi (text: Śuluṃthigrāma) and his wife built thephalcāin 1599 CE (NS 719) in memory of his deceased father, Hāku Bhābo.

event_name: Initial construction of a caitya? (see object number BKT0580-004 above)
event_description: Thecaityabears two inscriptions on its same façade. The first inscription mentions a date only. It is likely that this date refers to the initial construction of thecaitya. The second inscription is dealt with below.

This inscription was inscribed exactly one year later after the completion of the construction of thecaitya.Although the inscription does not record which event it refers to, it is very probable that the inscription was inscribed to record the first anniversary celebration of thecaitya.
Due to the poor condition of the building, thekvāḥpāḥchẽwas reconstructed by collecting donations from thesaṃghamembers. It lost its traditional Newar architecture during that reconstruction.

event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala A (see the object number LAL2680-011)
event_description: The name of the person who constructed this Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala cannot be deciphered from the inscription.

event_description: Ravindra Rājakarṇikāra constructed this Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala.

event_name: Renovation of the roof of the Śilpakāras' digichẽ
event_description: The roof of the Śilpakāras’digichẽwas renovated by adding a balcony to organize the feasts.

event_description: A pair of stone lions was donated by Dānapati Śilpakāra and his wife.
Motilāla Śilpakāra repaired the walls of theāgaṃchẽ.

event_name: Enlargement of the Sthāpitas’ digichẽ and replacement of its roof
event_description: The Sthāpitas’digichẽwas enlarged and its roof covered by the zinc pewter sheets was replaced by the concrete slabs.
