A newphalcāwas built here on a stone plinth that had survived from its previous construction. Commencing in November 2013 and in collaboration with UN-Habitat, CIUD, and local communities, a project named "Revitalization of Open Spaces in Kirtipur" oversaw the reconstruction of thisphalcāalong with the restoration of Deypukhū, and the erection of a boundary wall. The reconstruction, which was finalized in March 2014, also included the installation of a statue of Lokeśvara within thephalcā. As even the elderly residents of the area had no recollection of a properphalcāat this location, its former structure is unknown. There is no inscription shedding light on the initial construction of thephalcā.
यस मन्दिरमा भएको हालको शिवलिङ्ग यही विस. २०७९ (सन् २०२२) मा मात्र यहाँका श्रद्धालु भक्तजनहरूको पहलमा स्थापना गरिएको थियो ।

event_name: Covering the roof with copper sheet
event_description: A certain Narasiṃ, his son Jujuratna and other family members jointly covered the roof of the Devala with copper sheets.

event_name: Covering the sanctum's walls with ceramic tiles
event_description: The walls inside the sanctum were covered with decorative tiles by Naramāna and Nhukṣaratna.

event_name: Covering the outer walls of the Devala with ceramic tiles
event_description: The inscription on a tile records the date of this event, but does mention any other details.

विसं २०७२ को भूकम्प पश्चात् शहरी विकास मन्त्रलाय अन्तर्गत रहेको अधिकार सम्पन्न वागमती सभ्यता एकीकृत विकास समितिद्वारा एशियाली विकास बैंकको ऋण सहयोगमा यो धर्मशालाको पुनर्निमाण कार्यलाई पूर्णता दिइएको थियो । विसं २०७९ साल कार्तिक ६ गते (October 23rd, 2022) का दिन सतःको निर्माणकार्य सम्पन्न भएको थियो ।

Pūrṇasiṃha Bhāro, Basundharā Mayī, and Dhanadeva Bhāro were individuals who renovated aphalcāwithin thepīṭhapremises, although it is not known whichphalcāwas specifically renovated. In addition, Basundharā Mayī established aguthiby making a land endowment in Ithari, Bhaktapur to commemorate the anniversary ritual of thephalcā.

event_name: Offering of a gilt gilded pinnacle and construction of a phalcā
event_description: According to the inscription, King Raṇajit Malla and other noblemen (pañca, lit. 'five elders') wrote a play called Rukmiṇīharaṇa and presented thepīṭhawith a gilded pinnacle. Additionally, they constructed a five-bayedphalcāwithin thepīṭhapremises and directed that the occasion be commemorated every year on the 2nd day of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha (Jeṭha).
Thepīṭhawas renovated during the reign of King Mahendra in VS 2015.
Individuals named Maṇilāla and Rukmiṇī tiled thepīṭha’s floors and walls with modern tiles during its renovation in VS 2015.
Dated NS 690 (1570 CE), a document containing verses ofvajradhātumaṇḍalarefers to this Bāhāḥ (see the description above).

Prajāpati Jagatsiṃha Bhāro offered a goldenkalaśato the roof of the Bāhāḥ’skvāḥpāḥchẽ.On the same date, Jogasiṃha, Viśva, Tyātala, Viśvarāma, Pāhāna and Rāmacandra Bade jointly offered some ornaments to thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥof the Bāhāḥ.
During the reign of King Surendra, Muniratna, Rājalakṣmī and others jointly offered atoraṇa, which is placed atop the entrance to the sanctum.
The courtyard of the Bāhāḥ was paved with stones at the initiation of the Bāhāḥ members.

event_name: Repair of āgama and the sanctum
event_description: The Department of Archaeology, Bhaktapur Municipality, and local residents jointly sponsored the renovation of the main sanctum of the Bāhāḥ andāgaṃ.
The Caitya was repaired with the help of the Bāhāḥ members.
Lakṣmī Kau (Nakarmī) offered a copper moon to Vagalāmukhī.

event_name: Offering of a Pair of Lions
event_description: Colonel Muktinātha (text: Mugatinātha) Upādhyāya offered a pair of lions to the temple.

event_name: Offering of a Pair of Flags
event_description: An individual named Guruvācārya Baktabārasĩ and his son Keśava offered a pair of brass flags to the temple.

event_name: Installation of a Stone Pillar with a Lion on Top
event_description: Vyaṣārāja, Kularāja and their family members installed the stone pillar mounted by a lion statue in front of the Vagalāmukhī Mandira.

event_name: Construction of the Present-Day Temple Structure
event_description: Previously, there was no temple to house Vagalāmukhī. Prime Minister Bhīma Śamśera constructed the present-day temple to house her. Following the completion of the temple, a hundred and eight goats were sacrificed.
A devotee offered a brass sun to Vagalāmukhī. The name of the person who made the offering is not mentioned in the inscription.

Pātravaṃśa Gaṇeśa Lāla Rāvata from the Pātravaṃśa clan, who is the eldest son of Kṛṣṇa Sundara of Tum Bāhāḥ Ṭola, paved the Vagalāmukhī compound with stone slabs. On that occasion, he also repaired the shrine of the Goddess.

Some devotees of Vagalāmukhī established aguṭhīby collecting donations. Their aim was to buy threeropanīsof land to sponsor the ghee and oil required for the daily worship andbhajanachanting. The names of the donors are inscribed on the pillar.
Guṭhī Saṃsthāna renovated the temple.
Harṣarāja and his son Durgārāja offered apatāḥ(banner) to Vagalāmukhī.
Karṇa Bahādura Kārkī, his wife, and other family members from Kupandol offered a metal banner.
Ciḍhīkāji with his wife and other family members, living in Konti Ṭola, offered a metal banner.

event_name: Replacing Jhĩgaṭī Roof with Brass Sheets
event_description: Śarada Candra Śāhī, Reṇu Śāhī, and other family members replaced thejhĩgaṭīroof with brass sheets.

event_name: Repair of the Silver Shrine of Vagalāmukhī
event_description: With the financial support of the Department of Archaeology, District Development Committee, Lalitpur, and the devotees, the silver shrine inside the Vagalāmukhī Mandira was renovated. On that occasion, the pinnacle was also gilded. King Vīrendra Vīra Vikrama Śāha unveiled the inscription.
The temple caught on fire in 2009 CE (VS 2065) due to an electric short-circuit.

event_name: Formation of a Committee and Renovation of the Temple
event_description: Following the fire disaster, a committee was formed to prepare the information report and carry out the restoration work of the temple by raising donations.
Mhāsukhvāḥmāju was dismounted from her seat at the Dyaḥchẽ and brought to the town of Sankhu. This probably is the earliest historic record of thekhaṭajātrāof Mhāsukhvāḥmāju.

event_name: Kathmandu's victory over Bhaktapur with blessings of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju
event_description: King Mahendra Malla, the king of Kathmandu, had invaded Bhaktapur and was victorious after offering special worship to Mhāsukhvāḥmāju and having received her blessings.
During the reign of King Śivasiṃha Malla, Amṛtarāja Bhāro of Sankhu sponsored the renovation of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju’s statue.
King Lakṣmīnarasiṃha Malla got the statue of Ekajaṭā (Mhasukhvāḥmāju) renovated and gilded.

event_name: Death of King Pratāpa Malla halts Mhāsukhvāḥmāju's procession
event_description: King Pratāpa Malla died on the 11th/12th of the bright fortnight of Caitra in 1674 CE (NS 794). The annual procession of Mhāsukhvāḥmāju was not observed that year. It was possibly the only occasion in history when the procession was not taken out.

event_name: Palanquin of Svayambhū Caitya lands on the ground
event_description: The palanquin of Svayambhū Caitya lands on the ground, as the people carrying it failed to maintain their balance. It was not taken to be a serious incident and no ritual for auspiciousness was performed. Shortly afterward, King Pārthivendra Malla’s mother passed away in 1683 CE (NS 803).
The Mhāsukhvāḥmāju Dyaḥchẽ was renovated. The entry in the annals does not mention the name of the sponsor.
The statue of Vyāghrinī in the Dyaḥchẽ caught fire at its chest. The incident was reported to the king and special rituals for auspiciousness were performed.

event_name: Falling of one of the three finials
event_description: The western finial of the Dyaḥchẽ fell off. The king was informed and special rituals for auspiciousness were performed.

During the reign of King Tribhuvana and the prime ministership of Candra Śamśera, the Agnimaṭha at the Dyaḥchẽ caused a massive fire that gutted the statues in the building except the head-figure of the Buddha and the Karāhī. All the statues at the Dyaḥchẽ were then shifted to the Caugharā Sataḥ. Candra Śamśera disbursed necessary funds for reinstating the damaged statues and performing consecration rituals.
Although the Dyaḥchẽ did not collapse due to the earthquakes, the jolts left many cracks on the building.

The Department of Archaeology funded and managed the reconstruction of the Dyaḥchẽ. Upon completion, all statues including Mhāsukhvāḥmāju that were stored at Caugharā Sataḥ were brought back to the Mhāsukhvāḥmāju Dyaḥchẽ.

The family of Lieutenant Colonel Indra Bahādura Śāha of Bāhuna Gāũ in Sakuna Maijā of Salyāna offers a bell. As a portion of the inscription is covered by some substance, the full content of the inscription is unclear. But there is a name, Major Iśvarī Bahādura Śāha, inscribed above the main inscription, which is a later addition. Probably, Iśvarī Bahādura Śāha was the main donor and his name was inscribed again after it was covered by the substance in the original inscription.

The content of the three-line inscription does not record an event but only states the year and the name of the reigning king. It is so far the earliest inscription in a vernacular language (Newari) of Nepal. The year is given in words that literally mean ‘an excess of 3 [and] 9 in the era 200’ (Tamoṭa NS 1097, p. 34). When this is read in reverse, it becomes 200-9-3, i.e., 293. Any year given in non-numeral form or numeral words is read in reverse. The inscription only states ‘during the reign of King Rudradeva in the year 293’ (Tamoṭa NS 1097, p. 34). Therefore, the event is unclear. As the inscription is on the pillar, it probably is the record of its erection.

event_name: Construction of the Temple and offering of a golden pinnacle
event_description: An inscription dated NS 785 (1665 CE) records Bhavānīśaṅkara Bābu and Śivaśaṅkara Bābu, the brothers from Lalitpur, constructing the Vaiṣṇavī (Viṣṇudevī) Temple in Satuṅgala and offering a golden finial (D. Vajrācārya VS 2056, p. 138-139). This inscription is no longer available at the Temple premises.
Hāku Bhā of Satuṅgala sponsored gilding of the Temple's finial (D. Vajrācārya VS 2056, p. 160-161). The inscription recording this event too is no longer available at the Temple premises.

The inscription on the pedestal of the guardian lion (A) [see object number SAT0010-002 above] can hardly be deciphered due to erosion. Only the date when the inscription was issued and a few other letters are readable. Thus, its actual content remains obscure.
The 1934 earthquakes destroyed the Temple and was renovated by a person named Harikṛṣṇa Dvāre (Pruscha 1975, p. 265).

A copper-plate inscription posted on the door of the Temple records the offering of atoraṇain 1888 CE (VS 1945) [cf.Pruscha 1975, p. 265]. After the Temple was rebuilt in 2018 CE, the old door with the inscription was replaced by a new one. Thetoraṇaatop of the new door contains an inscription with the same date of the cooper-plate inscription. Thus, it is most likely that the newtoraṇainscription is a copy of the copper-plate.
Vīra Bahādura Jośī replaced the bell offered by his grandfather Govinda Jośī in VS 2017 (1960 CE).

event_name: Hosting of Śrīmadbhāgavata Saptāhā to collect funds for renovation
event_description: After the Temple remained in poor condition for a long period, the locals organized a religious program (week-long recitation of theŚrībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa) in 2014 CE to collect donations and began the renovation in 2015 CE. However, the renovation was halted due to a massive earthquake that struck two days after the works began.

event_name: Reconstruction of the Temple after the 2015 earthquakes
event_description: In 2018, the Śrī Viṣṇudevī Mandira Jīrṇoddhāra tathā Vyavasthāpana Samiti and the Department of Archaeology jointly reconstructed the Temple, which had suffered heavy damages during the 2015 earthquakes.

Inscription of four or more lines at the basis of pillar 004.According to Dilli Raj Sharma, the inscription bears the date ŚS 1423 (1501 AD) (Sharma 2012, p. 183). According to the same author, this pillar, or pillar 005 inscription's reads the following:sakunamālā puṇyākrit putra suvaṃ, translated as 'on the pious work of Sakunmālā (her) son be well'.

A group led by Dāphā leaders Devanārāyaṇa Bāsukalā and Ratnavīra Suvāra of Byāsī collectively restored this arcaded platform. They also established an endowment in the name of the adjacenthiti(water spout), stipulating that the annual maintenance of both the Phalcāandhitishould be funded from the interest generated by this capital.
Dāphā leader Devanārāṃ Bāsukalā added further funds to the endowment established for the benefit of thehitiand Dāphā Phalcā.
The reconstruction of Dāphā Phalcāwas carried out with the financial assistance from Bhaktapur Municipality.

After suffering damage from the 2015 CE earthquakes, the temple underwent renovation through collaborative efforts. The Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust led the restoration, with funding from the US Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation, and in cooperation with the Department of Archaeology.

event_name: Offering a pair of stone pillars for lighting lamps
event_description: Jayata Gvāra, along with Rukesiṃṅa, Jakerāma, Gvapāra Gvāra, and others, established a religious trust to fund the temple's lamp lighting and also installed two stone pillars for the cause.
Together with their son and grandchildren, Jītalāla and Herākumārī installed a bell west of the temple.
Kṛṣṇagopāla Maharjana, Kiraṇa Maharjana, and others installed an oblong banner (patāḥ) of metal at the temple.
The Bauddha Sūtra Vācana tathā Homārcana Samiti, a religious organization, installed a metal oblong banner at the temple.
Prime Minister Candra Śamśera Rāṇā’s last wife Bālakumārīdevī oversaw the construction of Bālaprakāśeśvara and was responsible for the installation of a temple bell.

event_name: Initial construction and endowment of land
event_description: Siddhimāna Rājabhaṇḍārī built the temple in the memory of his father Siddhinārāyaṇa Rājabhaṇḍārī and endowed some plots of land to aguṭhīto sustain the performance of the daily rituals. He also built Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa (KAT2636) and Siddhimukteśvara Mandira (KAT2637).

Viṣṇudevī Rājabhaṇḍārī, a fifth-generation daughter-in-law of Siddhimāna, established a home for the elderly as ‘Siddhi Sevā Āśrama’ in thesataḥnext to the temple. As of January 2021, Siddhi Sevā Āśrama hosts seven elderly people. Viṣṇudevī together with her son and daughter-in-law take care of the temple and the elderly. They also perform the daily rituals.

During the reign of King Raṇa Bahādura Śāha, Ghanavīramāna (text: Ghnavilamāna) along with his wife Gunamati, son Vīrasiṃhadeva (text: Virasiṃghadeo), and daughter Pammalakṣmī renovated the Bāhāḥ’s main building (kvāḥpāḥchẽ). A broken arm of the Kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ was also fixed by performing the ten rites of passage (daśakarma) on the statue on the occasion.

event_name: Replacing wooden kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ with stone one
event_description: During the reign of King Rājendra Vikrama Śāha, Amṛtamuni Vajrācārya and others replaced the worn-out statue of the Kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ made of wood with a stone one.

During the reign of King Surendra Vikrama Śāha, Bha Thakuṃ of the Olāchi Ṭola renovated (?) thecaityatogether with her daughter Bekhālakṣmī.(The inscription does not mention the event. Only few letters survive from another inscription on the plinth of the Caitya, which probably records the constructions of the Caitya. Therefore, this inscription of 1859 CE (NS 979) is possibly the record of the Caitya’s renovation.)
A resident of the Olāchi Ṭola renovated thecaitya. Due to the breakage of the inscription, the name of the donor is no longer readable.
Around 2003 CE, Thapāḥ Phalcā was jointly renovated by the municipality and a donor (someone by the name of Kumāle, i.e. from the clan of the Avāle).
Divilachami, Jitamāna, Bhimanālāṃ and Lachiminālāṃ donated the bell to the Dharmadhātu Caitya on Sunday, the bright fortnight of Caitra in NS 985.

event_name: Construction of the śivālaya and offering a bell
event_description: Prime Minister Vīra Śamśera built the temple and offered a bell together with his wife.
Kulaonta of the Olāchi Ṭola, his wife Dhinaramati, and their son Lakṣmīnala offering a stonetoraṇato Nṛsiṃha.
The northeastern among the four corner pillars was renovated.

event_name: Encasing of Nṛsiṃha's head in brass
event_description: Sthāpita Lakṣmidhaṃ and Syalālika Dhijavirasiṃ, residents of the Olāchi Ṭola, jointly encased the stone head of Nṛsiṃha in brass.
Keherasiṃ Śreṣṭha and his wife Nhukṣe Thakuṃ, originally hailing from Thimi’s Kvāko Ṭola but residing in the Olāchi Ṭola, installed a bell (KAT0370-006) to the east of Nṛsiṃha.
A religious trust formed to offer lamps every Saturday installed a bell (KAT0370-007) at the temple.

A proper temple was built for Nṛsiṃha with funding from the Kathmandu Metropolitan City and local residents. The Nṛsiṃha temple began as a simple roadside shrine. Over time, as the road was repeatedly paved, the level of the Nṛsiṃha shrine gradually sank below the road's surface, leading to water accumulation and an unclean environment. During this construction, the floor level was raised above the road to prevent future water problems. Reflecting its origins as an open-air shrine, the new temple incorporates a small opening in the roof.
The base stone (āśana) of the Indrāyaṇī statue was covered with silver by a group of Tulādhara of Thamel, Kathmandu.

event_name: Renovation of the temple, land endowment, and cash donation
event_description: Mukti Mādhava and his wife Cikidhi Thakuni of Kilāgala Ṭola, from the house called Sālaṅhechẽ, renovated the temple, endowed some plots of land, and donated two-hundredmohorasfor the continuation of the annual rituals. The inscription also records the position of the planets and a list of things that must be used in the annual rituals.
Tarī Bābu, Śrīmāyā, Puna Nārāyaṇa, and Teja Māyā of Jyāṭhā Ṭola, Kathmandu, offered one hundred and eight brass oil lamps to thecaitya.
Most of the stone inscription is illegible. However, it looks relatively old.

Kulanārāṃ (read. Kulanārāyaṇa) Mānandhara of Thahiti, his wife Jogamāyā, son Buddhinārāṃ (Buddhinārāyaṇa), daughter Sirimāyā (Śrīmāyā), Purṇamāyā (Pūrṇamāyā), and Kṛṣṇamāyā installed the lion pillar in front of the temple.

The peacock pillar was installed in front of the temple. The full date of installation and names of the donors are unknown because most part of the inscription has been covered with a thick layer of clarified butter.

event_name: Installation of a pair of metal flags
event_description: A pair of flags were installed on either side of the main entrance to the temple.
The bell offered by Kīrti Narasiṃha Rājabhaṇḍārī was repaired in 1977 CE. It was again repaired in 1987 CE by Rāma and Cena Bahādura, descendants of the original donor.

event_name: Offering a golden statue or crown to Indrāyaṇī
event_description: The inscription records that the sons of Mahaṃtarāma—Bhavānīnārāyaṇa, Śivasundara, and Jogamāna—living in Tãlāchi Ṭola, Ṣābahāla, offered a golden mukaṇa. It is not clear whether the term 'mukaṇa' refers to a statue or a crown. The inscription also directs their descendants to offer a golden roof to the temple if they can, and if they cannot, they should not hinder anyone who wants to offer one. A part of the inscription also mentions that this family originally came from Bhaktapur, and one of their ancestors served as a minister in the royal court of King Jagata Prakāśa Malla. They have also inscribed their genealogy on it.
Commander Colonel Śoṇajaṅga Rāṇā built the Bakhatamukteśvara temple in memory of his father Bakhatajaṅga Kũvara Rāṇā, along with anotherśivālaya, Rakṣāmukteśvara, together on a single plinth.
The Pashupati Area Development Trust initiated restoration efforts after the temple walls were damaged during the earthquakes in 2015.

Rāmahari Bhāro, his wife Rudrāyani and nephew Viśveśvara Bhāro jointly constructed a phalcā and established a statue of Triratna inside the Phalcā. Moreover, they also constructed the caitya in front of it. At the end of the inscription text it is mentioned that 23 persons had also contributed to establishing these monuments. They also made an arrangement of regular income for the annual rituals and the renovation of the caitya and Phalcā whenever necessary. Those whose duty it is to take care of the temple are mentioned as a group of four Bhāros, including Cikuti Bhāro, Viśvarāma Bhāro, Śaśideva Bhāro and Rāmarāja Bhāro. Members of the guṭhī include Bhāro (Śreṣṭha) community from across Kirtipur. Other details recorded are the position of the planets, the people to be invited and the list of things that must be used in the annual rituals.

There was a three-bayed Phalcā exactly at the place where the concrete building has been erected today. As remains from the older phalcā, an inscription and a statue of Triratna have been embedded into the new building. The Phalcā was dismantled and replaced by a water tank in the middle of the 1990s. Thereafter, a two-storeyed building was erected on the water tank. That building has been using by a social organization - Kirtipur Vācanālaya for decades.

Kirtipur municipality planned to beautify the two-storey building in a "traditional" way. The facade of the building was covered withdāci appā, struts and sãjhyāḥ were installed and the concrete slab of the top was replaced with a tiled roof. The task was completed in 2020 September and inaugurated by the Mayor of the municipality on the 30th day of November 2020.
The monument was seriously damaged by the 2015 earthquakes.
The Temple was demolished and rebuilt by the Bhaktapur Municipality.

The phalcā was built by Kṛṣṇanārāṃ Dhvaṃvacā, together with his son and nephews. He also endowed a plot of land to establish aguṭhīfor thephalcā’s upkeep and to support associated social and religious activities. These included the daily lighting of a lamp at the Kvasimāināy Gaṇeśa Mandira and the distribution of rice, paddy, andcatāṃmarī(thick pancake made of rice flour) on the 1st day of Vaiśākha during the Biskeṭa Jātrā.
Munsī Lakṣmīdāsa installed a new bell after the previous one installed by Bhavānīdāsa was broken.
Subbā Rāmabhakta installed the bell in honor of Bhīmasena.

event_name: Construction of shrine for lineage deity (LAL4237-005)
event_description: An inscription (LAL1100_I_001) posted ondurgatipariśodhanacaitya(LAL1100-002) in front of Micchu Bāhāḥ (LAL1100) records the construction of a stone shrine for the Digudyaḥ of the Śākyas of Micchu Bāhāḥ.
a person by the name of Devajyoti and a group of local residents renovated the Phalcā.
Dhanajyoti, Dharmanaśrī, and others initiated the renovation of the Phalcā.
The Phalcā collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes. Only the base of the Phlacā remains. Bricks and stones are piled up on the structure that survives.
The inscription is badly eroded and cannot be read.
Renovation of thehitiby the local community
Renovation of the water supply lines and installation of a storage system with funds provided by the German-funded Urban Development through Local Effort (UDLE) Project.
The renovation was managed by the Nāga Bāhāḥ Hiti user group with funds from the US Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation

Thecaityawas established by families living southeast of Yaśodharā Mahāvihāra, including Jagajyoti Vajrācārya and Lakṣmījyoti Vajrācārya. Statue of Mahāmañjuśrī, Gaṇeśa, and Mahākāla were also installed to the east of thecaitya.

event_name: Establishment of the caitya and procession
event_description: The inscription fixed on the wall of the house east of thecaityarecords that in NS 941 (1821 CE), Jagajyoti Vajrācārya, Lakṣmījyoti Vajrācārya, and other families established thecaityaand installed Mahāmañjuśrī, Gaṇeśa, and Mahākāla on the house wall. The inscription also mentions the construction of the house and courtyard along with the well. After the consecration of thecaitya, the Vajrācārya families and locals jointly performed worship and conducted a city circumambulation (parikramā) in 1822 CE (NS 942).
Puṇyarāja Vajrācārya, together with his brothers Vajrarāja and Śubharatna, and their mother Sānumāyā, installed a Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala to the north of thecaitya.
For the protection of thecaitya, all the Vajrācārya brothers of Taḥjaḥ jointly installed an iron railing.
The well currently located behind the house was originally inside it. Around 2022 CE (VS 2079), when the house was reconstructed, the well was relocated to the area behind (east of) the house.

While the exact construction date of themaṭharemains undocumented, a surviving stone inscription from 1748 CE (NS 868) records that Rāma Girī formally donated his residential property, including a house, garden, and land in Kvāthandau Ṭola to Vāṇeśvara Mahādeva consecrated within themaṭha. Notably, it mentions the installation of a copper plate inscription documenting this endowment during the reign of Raṇajita Malla - though this inscription appears to remain unpublished in scholarly literature. Academic consensus, based primarily on this epigraphic evidence, maintains that Rāma Girī founded the monastery around 1748 CE (NS 868). The inscription's detailed account of property transfer and deity installation strongly supports this interpretation as historically accurate. The inscription further stipulates specific succession rules: “As long as Rāma Girī's direct descendants exist, no external claims to themaṭha(particularly regarding themahantaposition) shall be recognized; should his lineage cease, authority would transfer to members of Rāma Girī's own sect; in the absence of qualified individuals from his original sect, responsibility would pass to any member of the broader Daśanāmī tradition; and failing all these possibilities, the inscription designates the king as the ultimate guardian of themaṭha.”
Teja Girī offered a bell to Vāṇeśvara, the main deity of themaṭha.

In the 1980s, Götz Hagmüller, who was leading the Bhaktapur Development Project, obtained permission from the thenmahantato use two floors of the monastery for residential purposes. He renovated themaṭhaduring that decade to make it more suitable for living. He continued to carry out minor renovations from time to time thereafter.
A project was launched in 2008 for the conservation of the murals in the Gaddi room within themaṭha.

The conservation project focusing on the Gaddi room paintings was implemented with the participation of Martina Klinkert, a student from the University of Applied Arts, Vienna. Klinkert documented this conservation work in her thesis, completed in 2024 CE.
The local community raised funds to repair the Phalcā's roof.

Bhimasiṃ Poḍe, his wife, and sons ommissioned the construction of the Phalcā to perform hymns and devotional songs (bhajana)in front of the Nṛtyeśvara. The couple also established a fund to finance the lighting butter lamps (ghyaḥdevā)during the performance ofbhajanas.
Bāucā Deulā offered a bell to Nṛtyeśvara.
The Lalitpur Metropolitan Office financed the reconstruction of the Phalcā with eightlakhsrupees.
The monument was seriously damaged in the 2015 earthquakes.
As of January 2022, the Phalcā is being reconstructed funded by the Shankharapur Municipality.
The 2015 earthquakes badly damaged the Dyaḥchẽ but it did not collapse.
The last renovation following the 2015 earthquakes jointly carried out from the Department of Archaeology and the Shankharapur Municipality was completed in 2020 CE.
The sataḥ was dismantled and replaced by a three-storey concrete structure. Its front face has been given a 'traditional' look.

The construction of Kvaylāchi Phalcā was made possible by the donations made by several people named in the inscription. These are Dhanta Bhāva, Dhanju Bhāva, Dhaneśvara Bhāva, Dhanmān Bhāva, Bīrvanta Bhāva and Bhagijani Mai. Land was also donated to fund the construction.

Kvaylāchi Phalcā was reconstructed with the support of the Mohr Foundation (Hamburg, Germany) and local donations. The supervision was conducted by heritage architect Padma Sundar Maharjan from Sunāguthi. Many meetings were held with different community stakeholders, politicians, representatives of the Department of Archaeology and the like, because the Kvaylāchi Phalcā is located at a very particular site. This site has long been under contestation due to road widening plans that would demands its - and many other heritage buildings' - demolition. The reconstruction process took substantially longer due to the long process of negotiations. Dozens of meetings were scheduled, ranging from general discussions about the relationship between road widening and heritage reconstruction, the reconstruction procedure as such, and schedules for financial arrangements. The local youth were also much involved in discussing the work plan, as were the ward presidents. Women, too, were involved in the reconstruction process.
Thestūpawas renovated after having performed thedaśakarmasacrifice.
A stone (or brick?) Caitya plastered in cement was constructed in the eastern side of the Aśoka Stūpa (east).
Thebahīcollapsed in the 1934 earthquake. Members ofsaṅghareconstructed it about four to five years later.

Harṣarāja and his family established twodharmadhātu maṇḍalasin two different places on the same date. One was established in Mū Guitaḥ Bahī and the other was established in the nearby Cīdhã Bahī (LAL1970). The inscription regarding the establishment of themaṇḍalais located in Cīdhã Bahī.
During the reign of King Ratna Malla, Jakharāja and his wife Māṇamayi Bhari donated funds for the installation of the Mahākāla image in memory of their son Vijayasiṃha Bhāro.
Thebahīwas repaired by itssaṅghamembers.

One of the inscriptions in the Phalcā from 1806 CE (NS 927) records something done to acapāḥby Cikidhika Mānandhara (text: Mannadhara), the donor from Phasikyaba in Thãhiti, and others from Kathmandu. Unfortunately, the content of the inscription is not clear due to the illegibility of the text. It refers to acapāḥbut it is unclear if a newcapāḥwas constructed or a pre-existing one was renovated.
The inscription from 1840 CE (NS 960) in the Phalcā records that Buddha Nārāyaṇa (text: Budhanālāṃ) of Majipāta and his wife Thaku renovated it after getting permission from Guru Śāntikara.

Thesataḥwas already in a dilapidated state prior to the earthquakes of 2015 CE. The seismic events in 2015 CE inflicted further severe damage upon thesataḥ. Consequently, the Vāgamatī Sabhyatā Ekīkṛta Vikāsa Samiti, operating under the Ministry of Urban Development, undertook the reconstruction efforts with financial support from the Asian Development Bank. The reconstruction project was completed on October 23, 2022 CE (Kartik 6, VS 2079).
Thehitiwas repaired by the Lalitpur Metropolitan City with funding from the World Bank.
The information board, installed by PURPP/LMC, a project by the Lalitpur Municipality and the World Bank, records the location of thehiti. The installation date of the board is not mentioned.

The information board was installed by the Heritage Conservation Centre, Lalitpur Metropolitan City, and the Centre for Integrated Urban Development (CUID). It is a part of a project inventorizing heritage sites in Lalitpur.
The gate collapsed in the 1934 CE earthquake and was rebuilt in a different design.

event_name: Painting of Aṣṭamātṛkā and Kīrtimukha on the gate
event_description: In 2018, a group of artists led by Loka Citrakāra painted the eight mother goddesses (Aṣṭamātṛkā) and Kīrtimukha on both sides of the gate.
Karṇaila Karabahādura Varman's wife and his mother Lakṣmībhaktakumārī a established a park and planted the trees of Vaṭa and Aśvattha.

The content of the inscription is unclear due to the erosion of the text. However, names like Rāja Malla and Biramādevī (daughter of Ratna Malla), and terms likemaṇḍapaare legible. This probably is the inscription that King Yakṣa Malla installed after converting acapāḥinto a temple.

event_name: Establishing statues of Jayamala (BKT0280-002) and Patā (BKT0280-003)
event_description: Mahanta Lokanātha Giri established a pair of large stone statues of a sturdily-built man (kutuvaḥ) named Jayamala and Patā (Pratāpa) flanking the steps leading to the verandah on the temple’s ground floor.

event_name: सुवर्ण ढोका र मन्दिरको छानामा बुर्जा थपेर गजूर चढाउनु
event_description: Devanārāyaṇa Giri built a projectile balconied tower topped with a metal finial that is set against the roof of the front side on the first floor. Giri also installed a gilded door at the temple.
Mahanta Devanārāyaṇa Giri erected a tall pillar standing right in front of the main entrance with a large gilded statue of Garuḍa on top.
Mahanta Lokanātha Giri offered a bell installed south of the temple.

Phulamatī Brahmaṇī endowed land to set up a trust (guthi) to ensure the continuation of various rituals at the temple. The inscription also includes the names of Mahanta Kṛpāla Giri and Lokanātha Giri.
Prime Minister Raṇoddīpasiṃha issued an order prohibiting the killing of birds staying in the temples of Bhaktapur including the Dattātraya Mandira.

Canakamāna Bandepālī and Mathurādevī erected two pillars in front of the temple with the implements of Viṣṇu on top. One of the pillars contains a mace (gadā) and discus (cakra) on top while the other one is topped with a conch shell (śaṅkha) and lotus (padma).
A silver crown was offered to Dattātraya by collecting donations from devotees.

Rānīmati, her son Jogaratna, and other family members renovated the Śikharakūṭa Caitya.

event_name: Signing over the Bāhāḥ to a Bhikṣu Saṅgha
event_description: Since it was not possible to run the daily operations of the Bāhāḥ, itssaṅghamembers, Yogaratna Śākya, Munirāja Śākya, Teja Bahādura Śākya, and others, handed over the Bāhāḥ to a Bhikṣu Saṅgha (an organization of some monks who practice at the Therāvāda school of Buddhism)in 2000 VS (1943 CE). Later in 2007 VS (1950 CE), it came under the jurisdiction of this organization.

event_name: Construction of Indreśvara and Jagadīśvara Śivālayas
event_description: The inscription recording this event is not directly related to thesataḥ. It rather documents the construction of nearby temples; Indreśvara Śivālaya (PPK1939) and Jagadīśvara Śivālaya (PPK1938) by Jayabahādura Kũvara, who also constructed thesataḥ(see 'description' above).

The above inscription also records Jayabahādura Kũvara constructing Jayabhakteśvara Śivālaya in Gokarṇa. It further documents his land endowments for sponsoring daily, annual, and other periodic rituals at the temple.
Two couples, Lokamuni Buddhācārya (text: Buddhācāryye Lokamuni) and his wife Dhanamāyā, and Bhaktamuni and his wife Ratnamāyā constructed the Caitya.

Kuvera Siṃju, his mother Dhana Thakurī, wife Manathakunī and younger brother Bhīmanarasiṃ established the Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (see the object LAL2560-003 above) in the Bāhā’s courtyard. The inscription records that certain plots of land were endowed to theguṭhīin order to celebrate anniversary rituals of the Caitya.
The Bahā’s wall to which the Mahākāla, Sarasvatī and Gaṇeśa statues (see the objects LAL2560-004, LAL2560-005 and LAL2560-006) are affixed, was plastered using cement.
The Phalcā was reconstructed as part of the Bhaktapur Development Project launched in the beginning of 1974 CE with joint funding from the Nepal and German governments.

monument_name: Tvāya Bāhāḥ (built before or around 15th century)
event_description: Local residents donated cash and other objects such as praying wheels, wind bells, clock, mirror, canopy etc. to the Bāhāḥ.

monument_name: Tvāya Bāhāḥ (built before or around 15th century)
event_description: Amṛtjoti and Jekīrti of Noglabhonta renovated the Caitya and performed a night and day long sacrifice in front of it.

monument_name: Tvāya Bāhāḥ (built before or around 15th century)
event_description: Cirimāyā and Buddha Ratna Śākya constructed the Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala at the Bāhāḥ’s courtyard.

monument_name: Tvāya Bāhāḥ (built before or around 15th century)
event_description: It was renovated by the Department of Archaeology upon the request of Buddhi Rāj Śākya, a local social worker.

monument_name: Tvāya Bāhāḥ (built before or around 15th century)
event_name: Renovation of the shrine of the Bāhāḥ's main deity
event_description: The shrine was renovated by the Lalitpur Metropolitan City office with the help of local residents. The renovation work was started in VS 2072 (February 2016) and completed in VS 2073 (August 2016).

The earlier inscription, from the late Malla period, records that a local resident named Narasiṃha installed images of Mahādeva (Śiva) and Vaṃśagopāla at the site. To ensure thehiti’s long-term maintenance, he endowed land in locations such as Bālegrām (present-day Bālagāũ).ता:खेलमा स्थानीय श्री नरसिंह भन्ने व्यक्तिले यस धारामा महादेव र वंशगोपालको मूर्ति स्थापना गरेका थिए । उनले हिति ब्यवस्थापनको लागि बालेग्राम लगायत अन्य ठाउँहरूको जग्गा गुठी पनि राखेको अभिलेखबाट थाहा हुन्छ ।

Descendants of Narabahādura, together with the daughters and sisters of Motilāla, undertook the cleaning of the spring source and installed the water pipe system to restore thehiti’s function.ताहाखेल बस्ने नरबहादुरको सन्तानहरु र मोतीलालको छोरीहरू र बहिनी सबै मिली यस हितिको मुहान सफा गरी पाईप लगाई जीर्णोद्धार गरेको थियो ।
Thehitihas undergone renovation with support from Chandragiri Municipality.चन्द्रागिरि नगरपालिकाको आर्तिक सहयोहमा हितिको जीर्णोद्धार कार्य भएको छ ।

यस बाहाःका शाक्य भिक्षु भयदेवले नेसं ६१४ (सन् १४९४) मा आफ्नो पिन्खा (प्युखा) अन्तर्गतको ६ आना बारी तीन वर्षका लागि बन्दकी राखी आफ्नी बज्यै यिकुलिमयीबाट ३२ दम्म सापटी लिएको विवरण सम्बन्धित ताडपत्रमा उल्लेख भएको पाइन्छ ।

आगंछेँको मुख्य प्रवेशद्वारमाथि नेसं ७४८ (सन् १६२८) को अभिलेख अंकित एक सुन्दर तथा कलात्मक तोरण स्थापना गरिएको छ । उक्त तोरणको केन्द्रभागमा षडक्षरी लोकेश्वरको आकृति कुँदिएको छ भने दायाँ–बायाँ क्रमशः मणिधर र लोकेश्वरका मूर्तिहरू सुन्दर ढंगले उत्कीर्ण गरिएका छन् । तर तोरणमा अंकित अभिलेखका अक्षरहरू स्पष्ट रूपमा पढ्न नसकिने भएकाले त्यससम्बन्धी अन्य विस्तृत विवरण बुझ्न सकिएको छैन ।
ज्ञानमाया शाक्यको छोरा श्री कृष्णमान शाक्यको सहयोगमा यस बहीको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो ।

यस बहीको प्राङ्गणमा एउटा ढुङ्गाको अभिलेख रहेको छ । उक्त अभिलेख अन्य अभिलेख भन्दा भिन्न देखिन्छ । ढुङ्गाको एउटा पाटोमा अभिलेख कुँदिएको छ भने अर्को पाटोमा एउटा भक्तको मूर्ति (KAT0620-011) कुँदिएको छ ।  अभिलेखमा कुँदिएको अक्षरहरू खिई नबुझिने भएकोले यसमा भएको विवरण बुझिँदैन । अभिलेख नियाल्दा एक ठाउँमा 'कामदेव' उल्लेख भएको देखिन्छ । 'कामदेव' नाम गरेको भक्तले यस बहीमा केही निर्माण वा दान दिएको हुनु पर्दछ ।

ज्ञानमाया शाक्यको छोरा कृष्णमान शाक्यको सहयोगमा यस बहिमा जीर्णोद्धार कार्य सम्पन्न गरिएको थियो । आगंछेँ अगाडी रहेको सिंह (KAT0620-005) को पेटिमा राखिएको अभिलेखमा यो विवरण उल्लेख भएको छ भने अभिलेखमा कुनै मिति उल्लेख गरिएको छैन ।
Indravadana, the last wife of Prime Minister Bama Bahādura Kũvara, built thesataḥtogether with a temple (KAT2650) to the south.

Fifteen years after the construction of thesataḥ, Indravadana set up a trust with a land endowment. Income from the endowment was to be used for daily, annual and periodic rituals and the maintenance of thesataḥand temple.
The well was constructed by Bhīmanārāṃ of Vaṭola in Dhulikhel.

event_name: Construction of the well and Śivaliṅga
event_description: An inscription from 1799 CE (NS 840) mentions that a Śivaliṅga and a well were constructed here in the names of Makaranda Purī and his disciple Sundara Purī.नेसं ८४० (सन् १७१९) को अभिलेखमा मकरन्द पुरी र उनका शिष्य सुन्दर पुरी दुईका नाममा यहाँ शिवलिङ्ग र इनार निर्माणको कुरा परेको।
Sundara Purī installed stone footprints (caraṇapādukā) of Guru Datrātraya.सुन्दर पुरीले शिलाबाट निर्मित दत्रात्रय गुरुको चरणपादुका स्थापना गरे ।

An inscription from 1743 CE (864 VS) records land grants by Sundara Purī for performing various rituals. One year after Amara Girī donated land for the annual rituals of Triliṅgeśvara in Bāhālakhu, Sundara Purī also donated land in the name of Guru Dattātreya and the caraṇapādukā. The inscription instructs that the income from the land should be used to operate the sarāvarta. On the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, the day the inscription was installed, it is further instructed to invite Daśanāmī Sanyāsīs for a pañcopacāra worship and a feast. The inscription refers to the Śivaliṅga here as Mukteśvara and outlines the proper ritual for its worship on this occasion.नेसं ८६४ (सन् १७४३) मा सुन्दर पुरीले यस मठमा विविध सांस्कृतिक कर्म सम्पन्न गर्नका खातिर प्रसस्त जग्गा दान गरेको अभिलेख प्राप्त छ । बाहालखुमा त्रिलिङ्गेश्वरका नाममा अमर गिरीले जग्गा दान गरी वार्षचक्रमा विविध सांस्कृतिक कर्म निर्धारण गरेको एक वर्ष पछि सुन्दर पुरीले यहाँ गुरु दत्तात्रय र चरण पादुकालाई सम्बोधन गरी जग्गा दान गरेका थिए । प्रशस्त जग्गाको आयबाट प्रतिवर्ष मठले सरावर्त खुवाउनु पर्ने कुराको निर्देश परेको छ । अभिलेख राखिएकै दिन अर्थाय् फाल्गुण शुक्ल अष्टमीमा सदावर्त बाँढ्नुका साथै दशनामी सन्यासीहरूलाई डाकी पञ्चोपचार पूजा लागाई भोज खुवाउनु पर्ने पनि भिनएको छ । अभिलेखमा याहँ भएको शिवलिङ्गलाई मुक्तेश्वर भनिएको छ जसलाई यस दिन विधिपूर्वक पुज्न विधि बताइएको छ ।
Sundara Puri's disciple, Sudāma Puri, dedicated a bell in the premises of the maṭha.सुन्दर पुरीका शिष्य सुदामा पुरीले मठको प्रङ्गणमा एक घण्ट चढाए ।

Mahant Sundara Puri's disciple, Vada (or possibly Buddha?) Purī, built a stone idol of his preceptor (guru) in the premises of the maṭha.महन्त सुन्दर पुरीका शिष्य वद (बुद्ध ?) पुरीले आफ्ना गुरुको शिलामूर्ति निर्माण गरी मठ प्राङ्गणमा स्थापना गरे ।

On the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna in 1805 CE (NS 926), Sundara Purī and Sudāmā Purī granted additional land for the operation of the sadāvarta. According to Pande (VS 2059, p. 43), 62 years after the establishment of the guthi, further land was added by Sundara Purī's grandson, Pāhalvaṃ (Pahalamāna) Purī, the son of Sudāmā Purī.नेसं ९२६ (सन् १८०५) मा फागुन शक्ल अष्टमीकै दिन पारी पुनः सुन्दर पुरी र सुदामा पुरी दुबैका नाममा सदावर्तका खातिर प्रशस्त जग्गा ठपिएको थियो । सुन्दर पुरीबाट गठित गुठीमा ६२ वर्षपछि जग्गा थप्ने कार्य सुन्दर पुरीका नाति, सुदामा पुरीका छोरा पाहल्वं (पहलमान) पुरीले गरेको विचार  (Pande VS 2059, p. 43) को छ ।

The disciple Vaṣada (possibly Vāsudeva?) installed a statue of his preceptor (guru), Mahant Śudāmā Purī, in the maṭha premises.शिष्य वषद (वासुदेव ?) ले आफ्ना गुरु महन्त शुदामा पुरीको प्रतिमा मठ प्राङ्गणमा स्थापना गरे ।

King Rājendra issued a lālamohara to Pahalamānā Purī, authorizing him to manage the income from all the maṭha’s lands and oversee its traditional customs and practices (K_0117_0004).पहलमान पुरीलाई राजा राजेन्द्रले मठका सम्पूर्ण जग्गाको आय र चली आएको चाल-चलन व्यवस्थापन गर्न लालमोहर सुम्पेका थिए (K_0117_0004) ।

A stone statue of Mahanta Pahalamāna was installed. As with previous statues of mahantas, which were installed by their disciples, it is likely that the statue of Pahalamāna was also installed by one of his disciples. However, due to significant damage to the inscription, details about the individual who installed the statue are illegible.महन्त पहलमानको शिलाको प्रतिमा स्थापना गरियो । यहाँ भएका विगत स्थापित महन्तका प्रतिमाहरू शिष्यहरूबाट स्थापित भएकाले पहलमानको यस प्रतिमा पनि कुनै शिष्यबाट स्थापित जस्तो देखिन्छ । अभिलेखको धेरै भाग खिइसकेकाले प्रतिमा राख्ने व्यक्तिको विवरण जान्न सकिएको छैन ।
Mahanta Mukteśvara statue was installed in the maṭha premises.महन्त मुक्तेश्वरको शिलाको शालिक मठ प्राङ्गणमा स्थापना गरियो ।

After the earthquake in 2015 (V.S. 2072), the western building of the maṭha was severely damaged and completely demolished. As of December 2024, it has not yet been rebuilt.विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पमा मठको पश्चिमी भवनमा क्षति पुगे पश्चात् पूर्णतः भत्काई पाताल पारिएको थियो जुन हालसम्म (डेसेम्बर 2024) बन्न सकेको छैन ।

According to a copperplate inscription on the third floor, the Dyaḥchẽ was built by Subbā Dharma Nārāyaṇa Mānandhara of the Maru Ṭola. As the building was in a poor state, it was renovated with funds from the Kathmandu Metropolis and donations collected from the trust members.
The Aśoka Vināyaka Guthi initiated the reconstruction of Maru Gaṇeśa Mandira (KAT1930) after its condition deteriorated. The reconstruction was completed in 2012 CE (NS 1132).

event_name: Inauguration of renovated Maru Gaṇeśa Mandira
event_description: After the completion of the reconstruction of Maru Gaṇeśa Mandira, it was inaugurated in 2013 CE.
After the Dyaḥchẽ was badly damaged in the 2015 CE earthquakes, it was rebuilt with funds mainly from the Kathmandu Metropolis and the trust of Maru Gaṇeśa.
Rāya Bhāratī (text: Rāya Bhārthi) offered the bell to Kāśī Viśveśvara enshrined at the Maṭha.
Rāya Bhāratī (text: Rāya Bhārthi) offered the bell to Kāśī Viśveśvara enshrined at the Maṭha.

Rāya Bhāratī Gosāīṃ (text: Rāya Bhārathi Gosāyi) endowed land to form aguthifor performing daily rituals and other activities at the Maṭha. He arranged for providing 1 kuruvā of rice and some salt for the devotees coming for worship at the Maṭha to be served dinner. Sitārāma Bhaṭṭa was the priest at the time.
Mahanta Hirālāla Bhāratī offered a pair of lions covered with copper sheets.

Mahanta Hirālāla Bhārati endowed lands for daily rituals and worships at the Maṭha. The inscription also mentions about the territory of the Maṭha, names of annual festivities which were observed in honour of the deity and procedure for daily worships. The inscription states that themahantas who abide by the rules of the arrangements shall attain the virtues that will never be lost and warns those who discontinue the tradition that doing so will equal committing the five great sins (pañcamahāpāpa).
The northeastern and eastern sections of the Maṭha were damaged in the 1934 earthquakes.
Kharidāra Bhāvalāla Bhāratī installed a ring bell (ghaḍi) to the west of the entrance to the sanctum.

event_name: Repair of oil lamp balustrade and steps
event_description: Mahanta Hirālāla Bhāratī offered lamps (dalūpāḥ) together with Mohanamāyā Devī in 1907 CE (VS 1964). Later in 1915 CE (VS 1972), Nandalāla Bhāratī renovated the lamps. Kharidāra Bhāvalāla Bhāratī again renovated the lamps by installing stone balusters for them. He also renovated the steps of the temple.

event_name: Covering the main temple with marble
event_description: Bhāvalāla Bhāratī laid marble tiles on the floor and walls of the temple.
The earthquake damaged the southeastern corner of the Maṭha. Members of the Maṭha repaired the damage themselves.
Narasiṃha Bhāro had donated land in the name of Dvādasī Guṭhī for annual worship of the temple along with some utensils.

event_name: Replacing Jhĩgaṭī Roof with Copper Sheets
event_description: Ikhānārāyaṇa jīrṇoddhāra Samiti replaced thejhĩgaṭīroof with copper sheets.

The temple was renovated by collection donations. On the same occasion, a new statue of Nārāyaṇa was installed inside the sanctum sanctorum and a new statue of Garuḍa was installed on a pillar in front of the temple. Iron railings were also installed around the temple for security.

event_name: Offering of toraṇa to the caitya (PNG0030-008)
event_description: Jigisiṃha, Kinharāma, and others offered atoraṇato the Akṣobhya statue in the eastern niche of thecaitya(PNG0030-008).
Lakṣmīsiṃha Bhābo, together with 15 other individuals, renovated the dilapidatedcaityaestablished by his grandfather.
Binārā, Lakṣimi, and others established acaitya(PNG0030-009) south of the temple.
Due to the erosion of text, the content of this inscription cannot be deciphered.
Jogalāla Maharjana offered a bell to thecaitya(PNG0030-008) east of the temple.
The temple was renovated with the assistance from the Department of Archaeology and copper sheets were laid on the roof.
The Sataḥ suffered serious damages during the 1934 CE earthquakes.

Sahayogī Mahilā Didī Bahinī Samūha (a local social organisation working for women) established a Saptarṣi  Shrine. It is mentioned that the Shrine was constructed for theTījafestival, which is widely celebrated on the third day of the bright fortnight of Bhādra.

event_name: Establishment of Saptarṣi, Gaṇeśa and Kumāra statues
event_description: Sahayogī Mahilā Didī Bahinī Samūha (a local social organisation working for women) established the statues of  Saptarṣi  Shrine. It is mentioned that the Shrine was constructed for theTīja(Teej) festival, which is widely celebrated on the third day of the bright fortnight of Bhādra.

Viṣṇu, Narasiṃha Bābu, Nārāyaṇa Bābu and other residents of Lagana Ṭola, Kathmandu donated funds for the construction of thesataḥand also bestowed land upon the monument. The inscription instructs devotees to perform a fire ritual (homa) and a sacrifice (bali) on the anniversary day of thesataḥ.
The descendant of the initial constructor, Nā.rā (official position?) Govindadāsa Bābu Rājavaṃsi renovated the Sataḥ after the devastations from the 1934 CE (VS 1990) earthquakes.
The monument was severely damaged in the 2015 CE earthquakes.
Thesataḥwas dismantled and rebuilt by the Department of Archaeology.

The temple priest Abhayānanda Rājopādhyāya (also known as Abhayānandopādhyāya) set up a trust for performing daily rituals on Dakṣiṇāmūrti by donating 20ropanīs of land that he received as a royal grant three years earlier. He also intended the donation to be used for cleaning the temple area and renovating the rest house there.
The 1934 earthquakes incurred some damage to the temple. During the renovation that followed, the traditional tiles of the roof were replaced by corrugated metal sheets.

On the occasion of the 18th year of King Virendra’s accession to the throne, the Department of Archaeology and the Pashupati Area Development Trust jointly renovated the temple at a cost of NRs. 745 thousand.
This water spout was constructed by Śivaśaṃkara Koirālā.
Murārī Prasāda Koirālā carried out the restoration in 1954 CE (VS 2011).
Kṛṣṇa Prasād Koirālā repaired and maintained the spout in 1914 CE (VS 1871).
Mādhav Prasād Koirālā carried out the restoration in CE 1990 (V.S. 2047).
The statue of Rāma was installed inside the Capāḥ.

event_name: Collection of donations for bhajana performances
event_description: Donations were collected from devotees to supportbhajanaperformances at the Capāḥ. The amount hence collected was deposited to a financial institution with 70% of its interest to be used for renovations and refurbishments and the remaining 30% to be added to the principal amount.

event_name: Raising funds to continue the procession of Bāghabhairava
event_description: Funds were raised to support the annual procession of Bāghabhairava observed on the 10thof the dark fortnight of Bhādra.
Dalūlamps were installed around the Bāghabhairava temple on the occasion of the 42ndbirthday of the late King Birendra. The inscription is not related to the Capāḥ but is installed in it.
The Capāḥ was renovated with the funds collected from a grand fire oblation together with a sermon delivery program.
The clay statue of Bāghabhairava was renovated.
Nepāla Nandana Siṃha Pradhāna, head of the Munsī clan, donated NRs. 1 million to set up a non-expendable fund to financially support the annual procession of the Bāghabhairava.
Śera Bahādur Maharjana of Kritipur installed the metal statue of Kṛṣṇa inside the building.

An stele inscribed in Nāgarī script is installed on the right side of the temple's door.Bishwo Pokharel recently published the following reading of the inscription (Pokharel 2011, p. 107):oṁ maṇi padme huṁetatpuṇyakalājjīyātpūthvīmallanūpaśicaram | jayasiṁghena bāḍākṣaryabhi nirmāpitā śilā || śrī śā 127(9)||
Jitalakṣmī and Ragurāja jointly installed a golden statue. The golden statue mentioned in the inscription is missing.

event_name: Installation of a Statue of Devotees
event_description: As the inscription is concise, the details are not clear. A woman named Parvatī seems to have offered this statue on the first death anniversary of her parents.

A fire broke out in the Vagalāmukhī Temple on March 15th, 2009 CE. It caused extensive damage to the Vagalāmukhī Temple and partial damage to the Temple of Unmatta Bhairava. Donations were raised for the renovation of the temple by forming Vagalāmukhī Temple Renovation Committee. In care of donations, both ​​temples were renovated.
Guṭhī Saṃsthāna renovated the temple.

event_name: Replacing the Jhĩgaṭī Roof with Brass Sheets
event_description: Śarad Candra, Reṇu Śāhī, and other family members replaced thejhĩgaṭīroof with brass sheets in both Unmatta Bhairava and Vagalāmukhī temples.

Cvachẽ Phalcā was renovated using a donation of 90,000 Nep. Rupees. These funds were donated by Urban Development Through Local Effort (udle) and GTZ, and bricks were donated by a kiln. The local people assisted in the reconstruction as volunteers. The original beams and pillars were kept.
Pillar 004 bears an inscription of 3 to 4 lines. The script used is a form of Nāgarī.Only the year and era are readible. They must correspond to the date of installation of the pillar.
The inscription is unreadable. However, given the dates of other similardharmadhātujinālaya caitya,it could be that this monument was built around 1979 CE.
With the exception of the dates, the inscription is unreadable.

event_name: Installation of a New Akṣobhya Statue
event_description: The stone statue of Akṣobhya, enshrined in the sanctum inside thegandhakuṭī,was stolen long ago. Around VS 2072-2073 (2015-2016 CE), Satya Vajrācārya, a resident of Bhindya Bāhāḥ (LAL1880), installed a new Akṣobhya statue at the same place where the stolen statue was enshrined.

event_name: Renovation of the Bahī's Northeast Part
event_description: The Lalitpur Metropolitan Office gave thirty-two lakhs rupees for the renovation of the northeast part of thebāhīin VS 2071 (2014 CE).

event_name: Renovation of the Bahī's Southeast Part
event_description: The bahī's southeast part is under renovation as of September 2020 with the financial support of twenty-four lakhs rupeesthe of Lalitpur Metropolitan City Office. Since the allocated budget was not sufficient to complete the renovation process, the Metropolitan City office has recently decided to allocate an additional twenty-five lakhs rupees.
Two statues of a male and a female donor were established on thebahī’s courtyard.

event_name: Installation of Statues of Vajrasattva, Vasundharā, and Nāmasaṅgīti
event_description: The local residents installed the statues of Vajrasattva, Vasundharā, and Nāmasaṅgīti on the ground floor of one of thebahī’s buildings which is under construction.

Purṇarāja (text: Punarāja) and his younger brother Nhukṣerāja constructed the Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala at thebahī's courtyard in the memory of their deceased father Harṣajyoti (text: Harṣajoti) and mother Ratna Thakũ.
On the request of the locals, the Department of Archaeology rebuilt thedyaḥchẽin VS 2044 (1987 CE).

The shrine was established in 1684 CE (NS 810). Although the inscription does not mention the name of the donor, it probably was established by the ancestors of a Śreṣṭha clan from Satuṅgala, who come here for the annual worship of their patron deity.
Bhāravi, grandson of Licchavi King Mānadeva, constructed the Satyanārāyaṇa Hiti for public benefit, providing clean, cool water.

A pair of stone lion sculptures (siṃha-pratimā) was installed in the name of Viṣṇudevī and Indrāyaṇī. An inscription bearing the donors’ names and further details of this installation is preserved together with the lions (MCG0020_I_002).
Under the leadership ofduvāra(guard?) Saterāma (Satyarāma?) and his wife Vimmarā, residents of Macchegāũ, two lion images were consecrated in the name of Viṣṇudevī and Indrāyaṇī.

An unidentified donor from Macchegāuṅ performed some act of dedication in the name of Viṣṇudevī. Since the lower portion of the inscription is worn away, the precise nature of this act is unclear. Dhanavajra (VS 2056, p. 425) records the full text, although with numerous inaccuracies. Judging from that corrupted reading, it seems that amukha(possibly an icon or mask) of Viṣṇudevī was established and certain ritual elements (pusidhāma,gatutadhika?) were affixed. The act was carried out by theGopālī(also calledGopārikaorGwālā) group, including Dhanarāma Gopārika of Macchegāuṅ. Although theGopālīcommunity has long inhabited areas such as Kīrtipura, Macchegāũ, Cobhāra, and Thānakoṭa, there are very few inscriptions attesting to their historical presence; therefore, this record is of particular importance.

Thedāphā khalaḥ(musical association) of Nhutanikvātha (Macchegāũ) offered a bell (ghaṇṭa) in the name of Viṣṇudevī. This act was led by Manahora Thārra and Yatimanisiṃha Tharrā. In addition, several men and women together presented silver coins as offerings to Viṣṇudevī.
Sūryanārāyaṇadeva and Jagatanārāyaṇadeva, sons of the late Jītanārāyaṇadeva Mānandhara, paved the forecourt of the Viṣṇudevī temple with a black stone slab.
The family of Rāmakṛṣṇa Lavata, residents of Macchegāũ, dedicated onepatāḥ(ceremonial banner) in the name of Viṣṇudevī.
The family of Kālu Bahādura Deśāra, inhabitants of Macchegāũ, offered oneghaṇṭa(bell) in the name of Viṣṇudevī.
In 2019 CE (VS 2076), the same family of Kālu Bahādura Deśāra, who had previously donated a bell, again dedicated onepatāḥin the name of Viṣṇudevī.
The inscription engraved on thetoraṇarecords the date and person(s) who presented it to the Bāhāḥ (note that the names of those presenting thetoraṇacannot be deciphered).

event_name: Repair of the main deity (kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ) and offering of ritual objects
event_description: Binayaśvarī Tulādhara (text: Tulādhari Vinyaśvarī) and her sons Chatrasiṃha Tulādhara (text: Turādhra Chatrasiṃ), Jayalundrasiṃ, Bālagovindasiṃha (text: Bālagvaviṃdrasiṃ), and other family members refurbished and painted the Bāhāḥ’s main deity (kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ). On the occasion, they also presented two bells, a flywhisk (cāmara), a plate, a ceremonial mirror (jvalānhāykaṃ), and a pair of copper-made ritual slippers (pādukā) to the Bāhāḥ.

event_name: Repair of the main deity (kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ), construction of balconied pinnacle and installation of Vajrasattva statue
event_description: Bālagovindasiṃha Tulādhara (text: Tulādhara Bālagoviṃdasiṃha) refurbished the Bāhāḥ's main statue (kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ) in memory of his father Dharmānaṃdasiṃna, mother Vinayaśvarī, and elder brother Chatrasiṃha. He also built a balconied pinnacle (phucā) on the Bāhāḥ’s roof and installed a statue of Vajrasattva there.

event_name: Construction of a dharmadhātujinālaya caitya (object number KAT0430-005)
event_description: Gajaratna and his family members built thedharmadhātujinālaya caityain the courtyard in memory of his deceased parents Jīvaratna Tulādhara (text: Torādhara Jīvaratna) and Muni Thakuṃ.

Sunasiṃha Prajāpati established thecaityain front of the temple. Although the date of the inscription on thecaitya’s western plinth remains illegible, it appears to belong to the early-medieval period.
Jayamohana Duvāra built thephalcānear the Nārāyaṇa temple.
Kaviprasāda Gautama erected a stone pillar in front of the temple.

Only the date (NS 1125) is mentioned on the lower part of the temple's pinnacle, from which no details are clear, but it can be assumed that the temple’s roof or pinnacle was renovated on the date mentioned.
The temple underwent renovation through a collaborative effort between the German UDLE program (GTZ) and local community members.
Kuladeva and his younger brother Caityarāja jointly offered a bell to the Vajradhātu Caitya (see object number LAL2590-005 above) before they established the Bāhāḥ.

event_name: Foundation of the Bāhāḥ and establishment of a Dharmadhātu Manḍala
event_description: Two brothers, Kuladeva and Caityarāja (supported by Kuladeva’s son Mānadeva), had jointly built this Bāhāḥ, installed the aforementioned stone statue of Akṣobhya in the sanctum, and established a Dharmadhātu Manḍala in the Bāhāḥ’s courtyard in 1928 CE (NS 1048).

event_name: Covering the Vajradhātu Caitya with brass plate
event_description: After the upper part of the Vajradhātu Caitya was stolen, Aṣṭarāja, a local resident, reconstructed the stolen part by using cement and wrapped it in brass.

event_name: Installation of a new statue of Akṣobhya as Bāhāḥ's primary deity (kvāḥpāḥdydaḥ) and renovation of the temple (kvāpāḥdegaḥ)
event_description: After the previous stone statue of Akṣobhya enshrined askvāḥpāḥdyaḥwas stolen in 2012 CE, Jñānadeva Śākya, a resident of the area, installed the current brass made Akṣobhya statue in the sanctum. During this time, thekvāḥpāḥdegaḥwas also renovated.
The 2015 earthquakes caused significant damage to the Phalcā.
The Department of Archaeology rebuilt the Phalcā from the ground up.

event_name: The earliest mention of the Vidyāpīṭha
event_description: TheGopālarājavaṃśāvalī(folio 41b) records an invasion of Banepā, which probably was a separate kingdom back then, on Cochẽ of Bhaktapur that was defended from the house of Vidyāpīṭha. Both warring parties reached an agreement later.
Karmācārya Joticandra, Sahasarāma, and others jointly consecrated the door-pedestal to the Tripura Vidyāpīṭha Āgama.
During the reign of King Viśva Malla, Karmācārya Kuśumarāma renovated Vidyāpīṭha and offered a pinnacle and umbrella. He also endowed land to set up a trust for the timely renovation of Vidyāpīṭha.
Viśvarāja constructed the Vidyāpīṭha Hiti to the west of the Vidyāpīṭha complex.
Kriṣṇācāryya repaired the Vidyāpīṭha Hiti.
Chatradhara and his wife Māneśvarīlakṣmī endowed lands to Vidyāpīṭha, wishing for good health during their lifetime and salvation in the afterlife.
Manimayaju donated Rs 51 to Vidyāpīṭha for feeding priests during the annual worship of Vidyāpīṭha out of the interest of the donation.
Karmācārya Haribhagata and his wife Lakṣi Thaku donated seven and a halfropanīs of land to Vidyāpīṭha.
Karmācāryya Ratnamāna, with his two sons Māna Bāhādura and Ratna Bāhādura, endowed land to fund the daily worship in theāgaṃ.

event_name: Offering a pair of metal lions
event_description: In memory of his father Mānavīra Karmācāryya and mother Lānī Thakuṃ, Kājimā[na] Karmācāryya offered a pair of metal lions.
A gildedtoraṇawas offered to theāgaṃ.
Some lands were donated to Vidyāpīṭha in order to observe various worships.
Bāhādura Karmācāryya performedLakṣāhuti Yajñain theāgaṃand donated land.
On the occasion of her 68th birthday, Rukamaṇī Karmācārya offered a balustrade of 108 oil lamps around the Vidyāpīṭha Gaṇeśa Temple in memory of her late husband.

event_name: Construction of a caitya and installation of some deities
event_description: Cikāji Tulādhara (text: Torādhra Cikāji) Dānavirasiṃ, Sameratna, and his other family members built a caitya in front of the Bāhāḥ and laid floor tiles (cikaṃaḥpā) in the courtyard. On the same occasion, they also installed statues of two of the Buddha’s closest disciples Sāriputra and Maudgalyāyana, Sarasvatī, and Gaṇeśa, and covered the sanctum door with brass sheets.
Gyānī Thakuṃ, her son Gaṇeśa, daughter-in-law Prānamāyā, and daughter Bekhārānī, built the caitya (KAT0530-010) in memory of her husband at the Bāhāḥ premises.
Manīlānī Tulādhara built thedharmadhātujinālaya caityaon the Bāhāḥ premises in memory of her parents Harṣaratna Tulādhara (text: Haraṣaratna Tulādhara) and Devīmāyā.
Bhāirājā Tulādhara of Raṃga Bhuvana Mahāvihāra repaired the clay statue of Akṣobhya, the Bāhāḥ'skvāḥpāḥdyaḥ.
Bhāirājā Tulādhara and his family of Raṃga Bhuvana Mahāvihāra offered the toraṇa (placed above the sanctum door) to the Bāhāḥ.
The monastic building is currently being renovated (as of October 2022). The renovation is funded by the aforementioned Vajrācārya family.
A broken inscription inside the Phalcā may mention its initial construction. However, the text can no longer be deciphered.

event_name: Donation of a pair of lions
event_description: A pair of lion statues were donated. The names of the donors could not be figured out from the effaced inscription.
Sākevaṃśa Bhisiṃha, Sākevaṃśa Guna, Kāsirāma Bhāro and others donatedilā̃(golden canopy) to thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥ.

event_name: Donation of golden canopyand other utensils
event_description: Ratnamāna Lakṣmī Thakuṃ and other family members donated gild bronze canopies and other utensils.
The Sarasvatī Shrine was renovated by locals. They were able to gain financial support from the Lalitpur Metropolitan City and collect donations to fund this.
The family of Sidhīrāja donated two metals flags. These now flank the entrance of the sanctum.
Sidhirāja and his son Lachimi Joti made feet of Mañjuśrī besides thedharmadhātu maṇḍala(LAL0870-009).

event_name: Installation of new statue of kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ
event_description: Thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥstatues of Gaganagañja and Samantabhadra Bodhisattva were stolen.ThapāḥjuLakṣmījyoti Śākya installed this new statue of thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥ.To commemorate this, an anniversary ritual worship of the deity is performed on the 12th day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna. Lakṣmījyoti Śākya also donated Rs 4000 for this worship.
Siddhilakṣmī Vajrācārya and her family commissioned the construction of an oil lamp to be placed on the plinth of the god house.
Siddhirāja, his wife Nāni Thakuṃ and their family commissioned adharmadhātu maṇḍalafor the courtyard of the Bāhāḥ.
Chatrasiṃha Dharmacandara and Ghanaśyāma Bhāro pavedteliyābricks on the courtyard of the Bāhāḥ.

event_name: Cladding the toraṇa with brass plate
event_description: Setinānī donated funds to clad thetoraṇawith brass plate.

The chariot of Indrāyaṇī used for yearly proccesion was covered with coper and brass sheets by Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Bhāro. Moreover, he also offered a pinnacle on the chariot. Again, two pinnacles by Bharalakṣmī and four (?) are offered by Kṛṇasiṃ Jugi (Duṣi ?). Those whose duty it is to take care of the offered thins are mentioned as two Bhāros including Mira Bhāro and Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Bhāro.
The roof of the chariot (Gaṇeśa khata), which is used during Indrāyaṇī jātrā had been covered with brass sheets. The readable names of the donors in the inscription are Jaganārāṃ Bhāvo and Bālakṛsna.
In the beginning of 1970s, the brass statue of Indrāyaṇī was stolen from thedyaḥchẽ.

event_name: Replacement of new statue after the theft
event_description: After been stolen of the older statue, a newly made brass statue with an elephant throne was established in thedyaḥchẽ. It is mentioned in the inscription that the statue with the throne bears 10dhāranīand 8-pound weight.
Thedyaḥchẽwas rebuilt by a Maharjana family. This renovation task was done in the name of late Suśīlā Maharjan.

The same Maharjana family (who had rebuilt the temple a year ago) added a pair of the lion in front of thedyaḥchẽand also established a bell at the upper plinth. Moreover, a newly made wooden toraṇa was also fixed over the entrance. The toraṇa was funded by Gaṇeśa Taṇḍukāra of Kutujvaḥ tole and entire task was handeled by United Youth Club.
Indrasiṃha Duvāra constructed the Bhavānīśaṅkara temple in honor of his son, Purṇṇarāma.

The inscription on the pillar is partially eroded, making it unclear for what specific purpose it was originally installed. However, it can be inferred that the pillar was erected to mark a boundary. A warning is inscribed stating that if anyone damages the pillar, they will incur the sin of the five great offenses (pañcamahāpāpa), equivalent to the sin of defiling the sacred Cā̃gunārāyaṇa. According to locals, this pillar does not originally belong to the Bhavānīśaṅkara temple but was brought from somewhere else and placed in the temple's southwest corner.

event_name: Reconstruction after the earthquake of 2015 CE
event_description: The metal-plate inscription records that following the damage caused by the 2015 CE earthquake, a committee was formed to oversee the reconstruction of the temple. The reconstruction work was inaugurated in 2016 CE (VS 2073, on the 14th day of the month), and the temple was reconsecrated in 2020 CE (VS 2077, on the 11th day of the month of Āṣāḍha). The inscription also lists the institutions and individuals who contributed donations toward the reconstruction.
Yogendramāna Vajrācārya and Jñānakumārī Vajrācārya offered praying wheels around the caitya.
The Caitya was painted by the Lalitpur municipality.
Since a pipal tree was endangering the Caitya, locals repaired it.
चैत्यको त्रयोदशभुवन चर्किएकोले टोलवासीहरू मिलेर जिर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो ।

Thieves stole the clay and gold idol of Buddha. They took out the gilded plates and left the clay part on the road. The clay was found four days after the theft. After some time, a new idol was made by carrying new clay from Mhepi of Kathmandu and mixing it with the old clay.

During the reign of King Siddhinarasingh Malla, the chief monk of the Bahī (Thapaḥju) offered a goldenkalaśato the main deity of the Bahī. Mukundarāja Bhāro, Jivasaṃkha Bhāro, Viṣṇuśrī Kalyāṇa and Vitu Siṃha were given the responsibility of caring for it.

During the reign of King Yoganrendra Malla, Bhāṇi Siṃha, Kṛṣṇasiṃha Bhāvo, Harisiṃha Bhāvo, Kalyāṇasiṃha Bhāvo and Maṇirāma Bhāvo pavedteliyābricks in the sanctum. At that time the chief monk of the Bahī was Dhanadeva.
Unknown

event_name: Construction of pavement in the bahī courtyard
event_description: Minister Kisnarāma Bhāro, Dharmmarāma Bhāvo, Maṇirāma Bhāvo and Kamalasiṅ Bhāvo made a plinth in the Bahī.

event_name: Pavement with teliyābrick at the bahī courtyard
event_description: A group including Śrīju Bhikṣu, Śaṃkhamura Bhāvo, Dhaneśvara, Parisiṃ and others paved the courtyard withteliyābricks.
The 1934 earthquakes destroyed most of the Bahī. Later thesaṅgha-members of the Bahī restored it.

event_name: Construction of Mañjuśrī Pādukā and Caitya
event_description: Bekhāratna Khaḍgī established Mañjuśrī Pādukā (LAL0101-007) and the Caitya (LAL0101-008) in the Bahī.
After the old idol was stolen, Sanukaji Shakya made a new clay idol and installed it at his own expense.

event_name: Reconstruction of the esoteric god house
event_description: The esoteric god house (dyaḥchẽ) of the Bahī was dilapidated and so rebuilt with the financial support of the Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan Municipality. The locals bore 15 per cent of the cost and the Municipality took on 85 per cent of the cost.
The 2015 earthquakes damaged the eastern, southern and northern parts of Bahī. Later, the upper floors of the damaged houses were demolished.

event_name: Reconstruction of southern part of bahī
event_description: The monument is under reconstruction. Province No. 3 (Bagmati Province) provided 5 million rupees for the first phase of reconstruction. The reconstruction work on the southern part of the Bahī is still ongoing (2020).
Dharmarāja and Aindrarāja erected a statue of Amitābha Buddha in memory of Dharmadeva Bhikṣu.
A repoussetoraṇawas added above the main entrance of thedyaḥchẽ.

event_name: Handover of the Historical Statues to National Museum of Chhauni and Guṭhī Saṃsthāna
event_description: Several historical statues were stored in this Bahāḥ, one of which dates between sixth and seventh century. A long internal debate amongst thesaṅghamembers took place in 1980 CE and resulted in the division of thesaṅghain two different groups. These groups decided to hand over some of the historical statues to the Guṭhī Saṃsthāna in 1980s and some to the National Museum on a later date.
Akvatāḥ(lower part of the wooden door or window) was added to the main doorway of thedyaḥchẽby Harṣa Gubhāju.

Following the 2015 CE earthquakes, the Department of Archaeology and thesaṅghamembers of the Bāhāḥ signed an agreement on the thirty-first day of Aṣāḍha, VS 2074 (2018 CE) for dismantling and rebuilding thedyaḥchẽ.The project had been successfully completed.
Ś. Śreṣṭha(VS 2057, 120) mentions that one of the struts supporting the balcony was replaced in NS ‘800 Caitra’ (1680 CE) by Paṇḍava. It is likely that thedyaḥchẽwas renovated at that time.
Locke(1985, 180) mentions that one of the struts supporting the balcony of thedyaḥchẽwas replaced in 1629 CE (NS 749). It could be the case that thedyaḥchẽwas renovated during that time.

The inscription on the strut supporting the balcony at the centre of thedyaḥchẽrecords the date ‘NS 800 Jeṣtha’ (1680 CE). It is likely that the temple was renovated at that time. Inscribed name of the strut donor is Dhanadeva.
The lion statue (KIR0002-004) was installed in front of thedyaḥchẽby Moṃmuni, Dhanapatī, Cakravati, Mahāmuni, Śrāghana, Maṃnirāja, Dhanarāja, Gunajvati, and others.
The lion statue (KIR0002-005) was installed in front of thedyaḥchẽby Śilajoti Vajrācārya, his wife Lakṣanā, son Muṃtadeva, and daughter-in-law Kamarāvati.
The roof of thedyaḥchẽcovered with corrugated pewter sheets was blown away in 1989 CE. It was rebuilt by Candrabahādura Vajrācārya, asaṅghamember of the Bāhāḥ.

event_name: Thievery of the Repousse Statue of Śāriputra and Maudaglyāyana
event_description: The doorway was flanked by the repousse statues of Śāriputra and Maudaglyāyana before they were stolen in 1980s.

event_name: Offering of golden ornaments and crowning jewel
event_description: King Bhūpālendra Malla's reign, gold ornaments and a crowning jewel (cūḍāmaṇi) were offered to "Khatadeva," likely referring to Kumāra, as he is worshipped on the 6th lunar day, with "ṣa" often pronounced as "kha." These offerings were probably for the Kumāra temple, whose finial still bears similar ornaments. A finial was also offered to the thrice-venerated Parameśvarī, though the goddess receiving this offering remains unclear, possibly indicating a previous statue in the temple.

The inscription (KAT3070_I_002) under discussion documents collective renovation efforts by trust members. Due to its damaged condition, it is unclear whether the renovation focused on the temple or the adjacentsataḥ.
Following the 2015 earthquakes, the Department of Archaeology initiated a restoration project in 2023 CE (VS 2080), preserving the temple's original architectural style.

A lālamohara issued by King Surendra records the donation of 4 ropanīs of land for the Sataḥ constructed by Kāśinātha. This document provides evidence that the Sataḥ was constructed before this specified date (K_0021_0016).विसं १९३१ (सन् १८७४-७५) मा राजा सुरेन्द्रबाट जारी एक लालमोहरमा काशीनाथले बनाएको सतःका खातिर ४ रोपनी जग्गादान सिफारिस भएको थियो । यस प्रसंगबाट यस मिति अगावै यहाँ सतःहरू बनिसकेको तथ्य खुलदछ (K_0021_0016) ।
The Lalitpur Sub-metropolitan office renovated the pond and the gatewayphalcā(LAL4218) at the cost of 50.000.00 Lakh Nepali rupees.
Following its collapse in the 2015 earthquakes, thephalcāwas reconstructed in 2016. The Lalitpur Metropolitan Office contributed 800.000 rupees and local private donors 160.000 rupees.

Jagamaru Pukhū Phalcā is said to have been built by Lākhes from Pimbahal, though the concrete date is unknown. According toU. Śreṣṭha(2012), thebhajana phalcāand the small Kṛṣṇa temple were destroyed during the earthquake of 1934and later rebuilt by Subbā (government officer) Motilal Shrestha (Lākhe). It is said that Subbā brought a tree over the river Bagmati to Pimbahal with the permission of the then Rana Prime minister Juddha Shamsher and consequently rebuilt the temple andphalcāin 1940 CE.

Subbā Motilāla Śreṣṭha (from the Lākhe clan) of Pimbahal reconstructed Jagamaru Pukhū Phalcā and the small Krishna temple in the 1940s.According to Ratneswor Lal Shrestha, 76, his grandfather Motilal Shrestha rebuilt thephalcāin the 1940s CE. The donors of thephalcāare unknown. Jagamaru Pukhū Phalcā's was converted into a one-story building with door and windows and covered with a tin roof. A library was run inside.

In circa 1998, GTZ/udle supported thephalcā's reconstruction to its original configuration: supported by 12 newly carved pillars, open to all sides and covered with a traditonal tile (jhĩgaṭī) roof. The pillars were carved in a hybrid design with modern carvings on the shafts and traditional motifs on the upper registers.

The Jagannātha temple, along with other structures surrounding the Tīna Devala complex, underwent reconstruction following the earthquakes of 2015 CE. The High-Powered Committee for Integrated Development of the Bagmati Civilization, operating under the Ministry of Urban Development, received financial support from the Asian Development Bank for the reconstruction efforts. The completion of the reconstruction works was officially declared in October 2022 CE.

event_name: Construction of the temporary shrine of Buṅgadyaḥ
event_description: The collapse of Karuṇāmaya Mandira (BUN0001) in the devastating earthquakes of 2015 left Buṅgadyaḥ without a home. Thesaṅghaof 31pānejusof Bungmati built this shrine on the dance platform to temporarely house the deity. Four stone lions and a bell were also moved to this temporary shrine.
The Pashupati Area Development Trust undertook the temple's reconstruction in the aftermath of the 2015 earthquakes. The temple had already collapsed prior to the seismic events.

event_name: Donation for annual ritual and renovation
event_description: The inscription attached to the wall of the Phalcā mentions that Chatrasiṃ from Itiṭoladonatedmohara sikkā ṭaṃkā101 for its management in 1823 . The inscription also contains regulations for the reconstruction of the Phalcā.

Lalitpur Metropolitan City provided RS 2,000,000 for the reconstruction of the Phalcā. The previous structure was dismantled and reconstructed in its earlier style. The base of the Phalcā was heightened by two feet. The Local Consumer Committee and local people also donated funds for its reconstruction.
The house was dilapidated and uninhabitable even before the 2015 CE earthquake. The northern section had already collapsed. It completely collapsed during the 2015 CE earthquakes.
The building underwent renovation after the 2015 earthquakes. The demolition of an adjoining structure also caused damage to the building. The restoration was overseen by the Guṭhī Saṃsthāna.
A person named Dhanasiṃha Mulmī constructed the path and thejaḥdhuṃ(water tank). Thisjaḥdhuṃis now embedded into the wall adjacent to thecaitya.

monument_name: Dathu Hiti Phalcā (c. mid-19th. cent. CE)
event_description: The Lalitpur Metropolitan City rebuilt thephalcāwith the financial support from the World Bank.

Gyānasiṃha initiated the construction of the Phalcā and established ahāthvaṃ guṭhīwith Dharama Bhavo. The persons who looking after the amintenance of the custom and the Phalcā are named on the inscription (Devajoti Vajrācārya, Adika Bhābo, Gyāna Bhābo, Jevasiṃha Bhābo, and Jyāna Bhābo).
N. Gutschow (2011, 238) mentions that Ubāhāḥ was established in 1660. However, he does not mention how he came across this date.

Dānajyoti and his wife Lakṣmī constructed a temple for Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara, offered adhvaja(a flag) to it and organised a feast for the members ofsarvasaṅghaalongside their son Dānajyoti and their daughter Sarvvāṇī.
At some point, thevihārawas renovated by Ratna Dhaju Dhana, but the exact date this took place is unknown.

Dhīra Śamśera Rāṇā, the youngest brother of Jaṅga Bahādura, erected Dhīrabhakteśvara as an expression of his reverence to Lord Śiva. Additionally, he donated land parcels along with water and oil mills to generate income for the temple, covering the costs of daily and occasional rituals, as well as compensating the priest, cleaners, and musicians for their contributions to the temple.
King Surendra formalized the donation of 50ropanīs of land for the trust of Dhīrabhakteśvara by issuing alālamohara.
Dhīra Śamśera Rāṇā installed a bell at the temple.
