Dhanamaiju Bhavānī Sundarī Śāhī Śreṣṭha reconstructed it from the ground up by collecting donations. The roof was laid with copper sheets and a metal banner (patāḥ) was also offered on the same occasion. Ceramic tiles were also set on the walls of the Temple.
Locals renovated it and also removed ceramic tiles from its walls.
Three brothers named Jagatajita, Raṇajita, and Śatrubhañjana Pā̃ḍe built the Pā̃ḍe Pāṭī during the reign of King Raṇabahādura Śāha.

event_name: Repairing the Hiti and Establishment of Umāmaheśvara (KAT0970-004)
event_description: Thehitiwas repaired and a statue of Umāmaheśvara (Bhavānīśaṅkara) was established.

Although there is a stone inscription from NS 812 (1692 CE) embedded in the eastern wall of the compound, it is not associated with the shrine. Rather, the inscription commemorates the restoration of aphalcāby Danasiṃha Bhāro and Gaṃgārāma from the Kvahiti Ṭola. The current or former location of thephalcāis unknown.

event_name: Addition of a Vasundharā statue (object number KAT0851-003)
event_description: The Nepal Yuvā Bauddha Pariṣad arranged a Vasundharā fasting event and erected the statue of Vasundharā at the shrine.
King Mukunda Sen from Papla attempted to set the Bāhī on fire eight times, but could not succeed. He also tried to set Svayambhū, Ṭhamel, Naksāl, and Dharmasthalī on fire.
Yaraṣārāma constructed the caitya in the Bahī courtyard.
During the reign of King Bhāṣkara Malla, a person called Dhanakutu Bhāro, a resident of Podetora (Poḍe Ṭola) made land endowment to renovate the Bahī.

During the reign of King Bhāṣkara Malla, Dhanakutu Bhāro, a resident of Podetora (Poḍe Ṭola) renovated the Bahī. Although the date of this inscription is unknown, names of Dhankutu and King Bhāṣkara Malla are mentioned, so it must have been placed around NS 825.

The Bahī suffered heavy damages during the 2015 CE earthquakes. Itssaṅghamembers started reconstruing the Bahī following the earthquakes.  Later, the Kathmandu Municipality extended its support for the reconstruction process, allocating 2,032,000 rupees.
As stated in the 'description' above, the Phalcā was renovated by the Bhaktapur Development Project.
The roof of the Phalcā was repaired by locals after it was damaged in the 2015 CE earthquakes.
This inscriptions (NWK0760_I_001) within the temple complex has completely eroded, making its content undecipherable.
This inscription (NWK0760_I_002) bears some visible characters but their meaning and its date remain undecipherable.

event_name: Reconstruction of temple and rest houses
event_description: A team led by Kṛṣṇajaṅga Pā̃ḍe, a member of the donor Pā̃ḍe family, collected NRs. 1.8 million and reconstructed the temple and the rest houses.

A joint effort by the descendants of donor Kularāja Pā̃ḍe and the Kulabhakteśvara Saṃrakṣaṇa Samiti, a local committee formed for the conservation of the temple, led to the reconstruction of the rest houses in the temple premises.

event_name: Dharmadatta's vow to build a temple
event_description: As mentioned in the inscription on the site, Dharmadatta Pauḍela (the son of Jayanārāyaṇa, grandson of Lakṣmaṇa, and great-grandson of Harinārāyaṇa Pauḍela), made a ritual vow (saṅkalpa) to consecrate aśivaliṅgaat Phirkyāpa on the banks of the Trishuli river in Devīghāṭa. This vow was made while he was taken to the Āryaghāṭa cremation ground at Paśupati during his final days, after falling gravely ill, with the aim of attaining Śivaloka (the world of Śiva) after his death. Unfortunately, he was unable to fulfill his vow and passed away in Āryaghāṭa.The inscription is edited in D. Vajrācārya and Ṭ. Śreṣṭha VS 2032, second part, pp. 60-64, and their edition reads as follows:
Following his father Dharmadatta's vow, Muktinātha built the temple and established a trust by donating land parcels to ensure the performance of daily and periodic rituals at the temple.
The Triveṇī Mahilā Samūha, a group of local women, rebuilt the temple after it was badly damaged by a pipal tree that had engulfed the monument.3.5

Lakṣmīdevī, the third concubine of King Raṇabahādura Śāha, undertook the initiative to build the temple. Alongside the temple, she also oversaw the construction of thecaugharā sataḥ, the cluster of rest houses encircling the temple. Lakṣmīdevī hailed from the lineage of Gaṇeśadatta Bauḍīdvā, a notable figure from the Garmiñā village in Patna, India.

event_name: Construction of the sattalas around the temple
event_description: Lakṣmīdevī, the third concubine of King Raṇabahādura Śāha, initiated the construction ofcaugharā sataḥ, a series of rest houses encircling the temple. This space served as both a refuge for devotees and a place to house additional deities.
A team led by Bhāñjī Maiyā offered the crown to Lakṣmīśvara Mahādeva by collecting donations from locals.
Both the temple and thecaugharāsataḥaround it were destroyed in the 2015 CE earthquakes. The structures were already in poor condition due to the lack of proper care and timely renovations.

The Department of Archaeology began rebuilding the temple andcaugharāsataḥaround it in 2017 CE (VS 2074), two years after the earthquake. However, the reconstruction was completed only in 2021 CE (VS 2078). The rebuilt structures were formally inaugurated amid a formal ceremony.

event_name: Bhāi Degaḥ, initial construction of the Temple
event_description: Bhagīratha Bhaiyā made this temple. 12 kings of 12 countries were invited to the consecration ceremony.

event_name: Bhāi Degaḥ, destruction of the temple
event_description: The temple was levelled in the 1934 earthquake. It was later rebuilt as a simple one-storey structure with a domed roof. The KVPT is now reconstructing the temple in its original pagoda style (in 2019).

event_name: Bhāi Degaḥ, reconstruction of the Temple
event_description: The temple is being rebuilt using traditional methods and materials. After thekṣamāpūjāwas conducted, cultural expert Satya Mohan Jośī symbolically began the reconstruction by using a hammer andchisel on the lime plaster.

According to the details recorded, thejaḥdhuṃwas renovated, as its source of water in a place called “Sūtigala” had been damaged. The inscription clearly mentions the event taking place during the reign of King Abhaya Malla, it currently is not in readable condition.
दिवंगत बुबा मुनिधं, आमा ज्ञानि थकुंको स्मृतिमा दिव्यमानधं र उनकी श्रीमती महालक्ष्मीले बाहाः प्राङ्गणमा धर्मधातुजिनालय चैत्य स्थापना गरेका थिए ।
शाक्यभिक्षु हर्षमांसिं (हर्षमानसिंह) ले बाहाः प्राङ्गणमा ढुङ्गा छापेर धर्मधातु मण्डल स्थापना गरेका थिए ।
Candra Śamaśera Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā had restored this spout.
King Mahendra had restored this spout.
The Śaleṣanāntaka Samāja undertook the renovation with the sponsorship of the Nepal Water Supply Corporation, and the inauguration was performed by Ambikā Basneta.
A local youth club called the Mirmire Youth Club had renovated the spout.
The Sināmaṅgala Foreign Employment Entrepreneurs’ Group had renovated thehiti.

Although the illegibility of the text hampers a comprehensive understanding of its content, this inscription indicates the donation of land parcels, likely for establishing a trust associated with the temple.

A pair of guardian lions, flanking the sanctum was installed (note that name of the donor who commissioned these statues is not readable in the inscription). The legible part of the inscription records that Vijaya Bhāva, Ṅakurisiṃ Bhāva and Manasiṃṅa Bhāva are supposed to take care of these guardian lions.
Indrāyaṇī is represented by an aniconic stone placed in the centre of the sanctum. The stone bears an inscription recording that a certain Śivarāma Bhāro installed it in 1670 CE.

event_name: Constructing road, its renovation and pavements of stones
event_description: The inscription records that Bhāginātha (Bhāgīnātha) Bhāva, Dharmmanātha Bhāva, Dhanadeva Bhāva and Siddhinātha Bhāv renovated the stone-paved road which was constructed by their grandfather, Vijaya Bhāro of Thaṃbāhāḥ. The inscription further mentions that Vijaya Bhāro had also paved the courtyards of other nearby shrines with stones.

Around the year 2005 CE, the Khanāla family disassembled the temple structure and erected a concrete square room on the site. Asserting ancestral land rights, this action resulted in the incorporation of the temple grounds into their private property. Additionally, the family placed the temple's statues within the confines of the newly constructed concrete room.
The inscription embedded in the western facade records that a person named Lakṣmīnarasiṃ renovated the Shrine.
The monument was seriously damaged in the 2015 earthquakes.
The Shankharapur Municipality reconstructed the Shrine in 2021 CE.

In June 2019 CE, thephalcāwas renovated and all wooden elements were painted. The project was initiated by Rājana KC, a parliamentarian from Kiripur, and funded by the Parliamentary Development Fund (Sāṃsada Vikāsa Koṣa/ सांसद विकास कोष).

In 1677 CE (NS 797), during the reign of King Śrīnivas Malla, Minister Bhagīratha Bhaiyā initiated extensive renovations of Kvachu Hiti. His efforts also included paving stone roads, repairing gateways in Pharping, and installing a stone entrance at the nearby Śikharanārāyaṇa (Śeṣanārāyaṇa) temple (PRN0010). As part of thehitirestoration, he ensured that water from the spring was divided equally between the two spouts and issued regulations to maintain the water infrastructure. Local residents were made responsible for caring for drainage canals, gates, and paths. Activities such as grazing cattle or collecting wood near the water source were forbidden, and violations were deemed offenses against the king. A team of caretakers—including Narahari Bhāro, Māna Siṃha Bhāro, Hākudeva Bhāro, Nhavana Bhāro, Tulasīrāma Bhāro, Gvavinda Bhāro, Viśvasiṃha Bhāro, and Viśvahari Sūjja—was appointed to oversee these tasks.राजा श्रीनिवास मल्लको मन्त्री भगीरथ भैया आफै अग्रसर भई चिन्ता गरी फर्पिङमा रहेका ढोकाहरू मर्मत गरी बाटोमा ढुङ्गा छापेका थिए । त्यसैबेला उनले शिखरनारायण (शेषनारायण मन्दिर) (PRN0010) मा पनि ढुङ्गाको ढोका हाली क्वछु हिति जीर्णोद्धार गरिदिएका थिए । जीर्णोद्धारपछि क्वछु हितिमा रहेका दुईवटै टुटीलाई मुहानबाट बग्ने पानीको तीनभागमध्ये एक-एक भाग पानी पठाउनुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिदिएका थिए । फर्पिङमा रहेका जनताले जलप्रवाह हुने ढलहरूको मर्मत गर्नुपर्ने, बाटो र ढोकाको हेरविचार गर्नेपर्ने नियम पनि बनाइएको थियो । पानीको मुहान रहेको ठाउँमा गाई चराउन नहुने, त्यहाँबाट काठ ल्याउन नहुने विधान पनि बनाइएको थियो । ती नियमहरूको पालन नगरेमा राजाविरुद्ध अपराध गरेको ठहरिने चेतावनी पनि दिइएको थियो । ललितपुरका नरहरि भारो, मानसिंह भारो, हाकुदेव भारो, न्हवन भारो, तुलसीराम भारो, ग्वविन्द भारो, विश्वसिंह भारो, विश्वहरि सूज्जलाई कामको रेखदेखको जिम्मेवारी दिइएको थियो ।
The Pashupati Area Development Trust reconstructed the temple after it collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes.

event_name: Recitation of the Pañcarakṣā (the main event is unknown)
event_description: The earliest inscription found at the Bāhāḥ is almost unreadable. Only a small portion of it can be deciphered. The readable part states: A Vajrācārya(s) should be invited and asked to recite thePañcarakṣā.

event_name: Construction of Aśoka Caitya (see object number KAT0210-004 above).
event_description: Vajrācārya Bhikṣu Rāmadeva, his wife Duyiṇīlakṣmī, son Ratanadeva and other family members constructed the Caitya in the Bāhāḥ courtyard.

event_name: Covering the old Caitya (see object number KAT0210-004 above) and construction of a new caitya
event_description: During the reign of King Mahendra, Lakṣmīnānī and her family covered the old Caitya and constructed a new one over it. She constructed it in memory of her father-in-law Prarśamuni and mother-in-law Mohanamāyā.

It was constructed with the financial support from the Kathmandu Metropolitan City. Although the reconstruction work has been completed, it has not yet been handed over to the community (as of August 2021).
King Mahendra Malla was responsible for the construction of the Koṭiliṅgeśvara Temple. Additionally, he showcased the Rāmāyaṇa dance, a performance rooted in the epic Rāmāyaṇa, during this period.

Although situated within the temple premises, the inscription documenting this event is not directly related to the monument itself. The inscription commemorates the establishment of a monastic retreat (maṭha) for ascetics by Harikeśara Vana Gusāyi. However, the exact identity of themaṭharemains unclear.
Some plots of land were endowed to establish a trust (guthi) aimed at conducting daily and other scheduled rituals at the aforementioned monastic retreat (maṭha).

event_name: Construction of building to the west of Bāhāḥ
event_description: Nun Saṅgharakṣitā constructed the building on the west part of Bāhāḥ for nuns. Many merchants from Lalitpur had donated for it.

event_name: Construction of building to the north of Bāhāḥ
event_description: Motilāla Śilpakāra donated to construct the building on the north part of the Bāhāḥ for nuns.

Once people had forgotten that there was a Bahāḥ and used it as a female latrine. Harṣa Bahādur Śākya from Oku Bāhāḥ rebuilt it and developed it as a Theravāda Vihāra for nuns. On that occasion he had consecrated adharmadhātujinālya caiyaat the Bāhāḥ courtyard.

There is no inscription recording the initial phase of construction. The inscription transferred to the Phalcā dates back to 1889 CE (1009 NS) records the restoration of the phalcā carried out by the son of Amitanārā (Amita Nārāyaṇa) and Mayajumunī. The inscription also reveals that Kvāṭhanāyaka Āsāmadu Bhāro initiated its construction.

The renovation of the dilapidated phalcā was undertaken byKvāṭhanāyakaḌhuṇḍirāja Bhāro, who also installed the idol of Umāmaheśvara in 1716 CE (NS 836). A guṭhī has been established, allocating land for conducting anniversary ritual on the day of Bhīmā Ekādaśī (Māghaśukla ekādaśī, day of renovation) as well as for the daily worship of the statue by Brāhmaṇa.

The inscription transferred to the Phalcā dates back to 1889 CE (1009 NS) and records the restoration of the Phalcā as facilitated by the son of Amitanārā (Amita Nārāyaṇa) and Mayajumunī. The inscription also records that tmembers of the clan that is responsible for the restoration of the Phalcā are exempt from rent obligations, while those living within the Phalcā are requested to distribute ritual food (samaybaji) and to place lights in the Phalcā during the full moon of Bhādra.

Based on the photograph showing the remnants of the Phalcā and memories of the community’s older members, the Phalcā was reconstructed in 2015 CE (2075 VS). During this reconstruction, one of the inscriptions taken to the nearby Nārāyaṇa temple was reinstalled in the Phalcā. but the other inscription and the Umāmaheśvara statue have not been moved.

event_name: Enhancement with golden doorway and gilded artifacts
event_description: Maṃgalalāla Bhomī from Yātāchẽ Ṭola added a touch of grandeur to the temple by affixing a gilded covering to the entrance andtoraṇas, and gilding the statue of a goddess.

Due to erosion affecting certain letters of the inscription, the complete content remains obscured. However, indications suggest that it pertains to an event undertaken by individuals including Āśārāma, Ratnabahādura, Candrabhakta, and others.

event_name: Installation of gilt plate for lower roof
event_description: Āśālāla Śreṣṭha of Cochẽ oversaw the renovation of the temple's lower roof by replacing it with gilt metal sheets.
Gaṃgākṛṣṇa, Govinda, Rameśa, and other residents of Sāgāchẽ in Bhaktapur contributed by offering a sizable bell to the Mahālakṣmī temple.

event_name: Consecration of statute for Biskāḥ Jātrā
event_description: Bhājudeva Bhāro, together with his wife Dhanalakṣmī and son Bhājukutu, commissioned an image of Vārāhī for use during the Biskāḥ Jātrā.भाजुदेव भारोले श्रीमती धनलक्ष्मी र छोरा भाजुकुतुसँग मिलेर बिस्का:मा जात्रा गर्नको लागि वाराहीको मूर्ति बनाइदिएका थिए ।

Deva Bhālo and Dhantalakṣmī, together with their sons Vidyāpati, Kṛttisiṃha, and daughter Dayālakṣmī, endowed agricultural land as aguṭhīfor the Dakṣiṇa Vārāhī temple. The income from this land was to be used annually for the temple’svarṣavardhanapūjā(annual renewal ritual). On that day, any damage to the temple was to be repaired, a goat was to be offered in sacrifice, and theguṭhīyāras(trust members) were to be served a ritual feast after the proper worship.देव भालो र धंतलक्ष्मीले छोराहरू विद्यापति, कृत्तिसिंह लगायत छोरी दयालक्ष्मीसँग मिलेर दक्षिण वाराही मन्दिरको लागि खेत गुठी राखिदिएका थिए । उक्त खेतको आयस्ताले प्रत्येक वर्ष मन्दिरको वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । त्यस दिन मन्दिरमा केही बिग्रेको छ भने मर्मत गरी वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गर्नुपर्ने, एउटा बोका बलि दिई विधिपूर्वक पूजा गरी गुठीयारहरूलाई भोज खुवाउनुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो ।

Bhānna Siṃha, Siṃgha Bhālo, his wife Budhi Thakuṃ, Jagatamā Siṃha, and others jointly dedicated a stonetoraṇa(ornamental gateway) to Dakṣiṇa Vārāhī.भान्नसिं, सिंघ भालो, उनकी श्रीमती बुधि थकुं, जगतमासिं लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर दक्षिण वाराहीलाई ढुङ्गाको तोरण चढाएका थिए ।

Tulsīnārāyaṇa Galu of Thimi, together with his wife Kṛṣṇakumārī, sons Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, Harṣanārāyaṇa, Beṣanārāyaṇa, Āsanārāyaṇa, and daughter Candramāyā, offered a gold-plated finial (gajūra) to the Dakṣiṇa Vārāhī temple.थिमि निवासी तुल्सीनारां गलुले श्रीमती कृष्णकुमारी लगायत छोराहरू लक्ष्मीनारां, हर्षनारां, बेषानारां, आसनारां र छोरी चन्द्रमायासँग मिलेर दक्षिण वाराही मन्दिरमा सुवर्णलेपित गजूर चढाएका थिए ।

Kislāla Maharjana of Gaḥcheṃ Tole, Lalitpur, together with his wives Nānīmāyā Maharjana and Nhucemāyā Maharjana, dedicated a bell within the temple premises.ललितपुर, गःछेँ टोल निवासी किसलाल महर्जनले आफ्ना श्रीमतीहरू नानीमाया महर्जन र न्हुछेमाया महर्जनसँग मिलेर मन्दिर परिसरमा घण्टा चढाएका थिए ।

Kṛṣṇa Kāji Bhāsimā and Pañcalakṣmī Bhāsimā of Nayā Thimi, along with others, jointly offered a metalpatāḥ(ritual plate or plaque) to the Dakṣiṇa Vārāhī temple.नयाँ थिमि निवासी कृष्ण काजी भासिमा, पञ्चलक्ष्मी भासिमा लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर दक्षिण वाराही मन्दिरमा धातुको पताः चढाएका थिए ।

As the temple was damaged by the 2015 CE (VS 2072) earthquake, it was reconstructed by the Department of Archaeology at a total cost of 6.3 million rupees. However, at the time of completion, the installation of metal roofing sheets (pātā) remained unfinished.विसं २०७२ को भूकम्पले मन्दिरमा क्षति पुगेकोले पुरातत्त्व विभागबाट मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । उक्त कार्यमा ६३ लाख खर्च भएको थियो । उक्त पुनर्निर्माण सम्पन्न गर्दा छानामा पाता राख्ने काम भने बाँकी नै थियो ।

In memory of their late grandfather Amara Nātha Kilaṃna and late father Kedāra Nātha Kilaṃna, Juna Kilaṃna and Amara Kilaṃna dedicated a brasstoraṇato the temple.दिवंगत बाजे अमर नाथ किलंन, दिवंगत बुबा केदार नाथ किलंनको सम्झनामा जुन किलंन र अमर किलंनले मन्दिरमा पित्तलको तोरण चढाएका थिए ।
Rameśa Kumāra Śreṣṭha offered a metal flag (THI0170-004) to the Dakṣiṇa Vārāhī temple.रमेश कुमार श्रेष्ठले दक्षिण वाराही मन्दिरमा धातुको झण्डा (THI0170-004) चढाएका थिए ।
Nānīmāiyā̃ Śreṣṭha also dedicated a metal flag (THI0170-005) to the Dakṣiṇa Vārāhī temple.नानीमैयाँ श्रेष्ठले दक्षिण वाराही मन्दिरमा धातुको झण्डा (THI0170-005) चढाएकी थिइन् ।

The 2015 earthquakes completely destroyed the arcaded platform, which, at that time, was already in a dilapidated condition. The Department of Archaeology reconstructed Sāmarī Pauvā and installed a colored metal sheet roof in place of the original tiled roof. Despite the completion of the reconstruction, it has not yet been formally inaugurated (as of June 2024).

Numerous medieval inscriptions refer to the completion of temple construction through a ritual known as"Suvarṇa Kalaśa Dhvajārohaṇa"(raising of a golden finial) or"Pāṣāṇa Kalaśa Dhvajārohaṇa"(raising of a stone finial). The inscription found at the Pāṣāṇa Gaṇeśa (Stone Gaṇeśa) suggests that the installation of thekalaśa(finial) was regarded as marking the completion of temple construction. This date, therefore, may be taken as the initial construction date of the temple.
The outer edge of the temple's sanctum (garbhagṛha) has been ornamented with sheets of brass.
Thebhajanagroup from Ikhā Tole offered a golden plaque (patā) andbhaṅgī(arched decorative elements) for the upper part of the temple.

Although the date is legible, the inscription is heavily worn, making it difficult to determine its exact content. However, since the inscription is dedicated to the music master Nāṭyeśvara, it is particularly intriguing that a carving of akhiṃ(a traditional drum) appears at the top of the inscription.
During the reign of King Pṛthvī Vīravikrama Śāha, Halinārāṁ (Harinārāyaṇa) of Itāchẽ Tole decorated the middle tier roof of the temple with brass sheet.
During the reign of King Pṛthvī Vīravikrama Śāha, Halinārāṁ (Harinārāyaṇa) of Itāchẽ Tole decorated the lower tier roof of the temple with brass sheet.
The sides of the Nāṭyeśvara shrine were also adorned with sheets of brass, a work carried out by Rāja Taṇḍukāra and Rāmadā’s family from Haugaḥ Tole.
Bhavānīdāsa and Indralāla together offered a bell in the name of Nāṭyeśvara.
To please Nāṭyeśvara, Vidyarāja offered a golden banner (patā) to the temple.

In 1851 CE, thesataḥwas restored by members of the Jośī family from Nhulachẽnani on the eastern side of Kvālkhu Ṭola. The following names could be gleaned from the inscription: Daivajña Jaya Kṛṣna, Dhana Kṛṣna, Rāma Kṛṣna and Rāma Sundhara.

The erosion of the inscription has made it difficult to read. The mention of Vaṃśīdhara Nārāyaṇa suggests he may have built the temple, while another name, with the ascetic caste title Gusāyi, appears below, possibly indicating his role in temple rituals and care (see'description').
Āsāmadu Karmācārya offered a bell (BKT0140-009) at thepīṭhain memory of his deceased parents.
Mānavīra Karmācārya and his wife Lānithakuṃ offered a bell (BKT0140-010) at thepīṭha.

event_name: Offering a pair of metal lions
event_description: Lakṣmīkumāri offered a pair of metal lion statues established on either side of thepīṭhain the name of her deceased parents-in-law Rudranārāṃ and Dhana Thakuṃ, along with her deceased husband Āsāmadu.

Commander-in-Chief Raṇa Śamśera's wife built the Ḍambaramukteśvara temple in memory of her late husband. Her identity is unclear, as she is only referred to as "Śrī Rānī" (lit. venerated queen) in the inscription.
Raṇa Śamśera's wife set up a trust by donating land parcels to ensure the temple's financial stability for the performance of daily and periodic rituals.
The temple's bell was added only later in 1938 CE (VS 1994) by a state trust named “Śrī 3 Sarakāra Guṭhī.” It is smaller than those of other nearbyśivālayas.
The temple collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes but was rebuilt by the Pashupati Area Development Trust in 2019 CE (VS 2076).

The stele in the second chamber of the fountain contains a 9-line eroded Tibetan inscription. The inscription appears to be an edict, possibly written between the ninth and twelfth centuries. Archaeologist David C. Andolfatto discovered the stele in 2014 CE. It is currently being translated.

event_name: Theft of the main statue of Nārāyaṇa
event_description: The statue was stolen.
A stone statue of Garuḍa was placed in front of the monument. There is an eroded inscription dated NS 809 on the base of the statue.

event_name: Construction of the phalcā near the temple
event_description: An inscription dated NS 843 can be found inside the sanctum. This mentions that Siddhinātha made aphalcāand donated some land. The top image of Nārāyaṇa shows that thephalcāwas related to the deity. Local elder people say that there was once aphalcāclose to the temple. It seems that thephalcāinscription was placed inside the temple after thephalcāwas destroyed.
The temple was renovated and aguṭhīwas formed. The donors also donated land to fund the daily worship and annual rituals of the temple.

The courtyard of the temple was paved in stone and the base of the Garuḍa statue was renovated. On the same day, a sacrifice was performed and a golden pinnacle with flags was fixed on top of the temple.
Prime Minister Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā built the Sataḥ as part of the Jaṅge Hiraṇya Hema Nārāyaṇa Mandira.

While the Sataḥ did not collapse in the 2015 earthquakes, it was deemed unsafe to live in. In 2022, it was completely demantled and consequently reconstructed. This was carried out by the High-Powered Committee for Integrated Development of the Bagmati Civilization under the Ministry of Urban Development with the loan assistance of the Asian Development Bank.

Jītajaṅga Rāṇā, the second son of Jaṅga Bahādura, Lalitamukteśvara along with Jītajaṅgaprakāśeśvara Mandira (PPK0706) at the cremation ground of Rājarājeśvarī Ghāṭa and established a trust for carrying out daily and other rituals at these temples.
Candra Śamśera, the Rāṇā prime minister, commissioned this pond in memory of his late wife Mahārānī Candrabhakta Lokarājyalakṣmī Devī.

Nārāyaṇa Bhāro, Buddhinārāyaṇa, Rājavīra, Tribhuvana Nārāyaṇa, Jñānavīra and their family members constructed thiscaityain 1863 in memory of their late parents. They also established aguṭhīfor its maintenance.

The pond was renovated with the help from the Shankharapur Municipality (it had disbursed an amount of NRs. 1 million for this purpose). Locals also contributed with cash donations to meet the shortfall.
Sthāpita Jyeṣṭhadhija and his wife Devarakṣmi (Devalakṣmī) constructed this Vajradhātu Caitya (KAT1030-002) to the north of the Gaṇeśa Temple.

The temple was renovated with the support from the Kathmandu Municipality and local community members. The Municipality donated 300,000 rupees and the necessary rest was locally fundraised. The then Deputy Mayor, Nabindraraj Joshi, played an important role in the renovation process.
The Hanumāna Ḍhokā Preservation Committee, which is under the Kathmandu Municipality, offered this bell to the temple. It was established with the support of the Ward No.19 Office.
Viṣṇusiṃha Bhāro of Asana Ṭola's Jhyālakochẽ built acaturvyūha caityaat thebāhāḥduring King Pratāpa Malla’s reign.
Jiyūrāja carried out certain work in thebāhāḥduring King Pārthivendra Malla’s reign, but its damaged letters prevent deciphering the full content of the inscription.
At the center of the sanctum is a niche where the main images of Gaṇeśa are kept. The brasstoraṇaabove the niche was added by Suraja Māna Jośī and Ratnalāla Jośī.

event_name: Construction (probably the initial construction of the temple)
event_description: There is an inscription on the base of a strutat the south-west corner of the first floor. It mentions that a group of nine member led by Keśavarāja Bhāro constructed something in NS 802. The construction work it refers to was most likely the initial construction of the temple.
The temple used to have two storeys. The third storey was added by Keśavarāja Bhāro and Siddhirāja Bhāro.
A woodentoraṇawas installed above the eastern bay of the ground floor by Durgārāja Daivajña.

event_name: Addition of embossed eaves boards to the edges of the roofs
event_description: Embossed eaves boards were added to the edges of the roofs by Maĩñā Jośī and her family.
A bell was added in front of the temple by Akavara Siṃ, the son of Dhuna Siṃ from Ṅyāta Ṭola.

event_name: Renovation of the two lower roofs by replacing the tiles with copper plates
event_description: There used to be a tiled roof (jhĩgaṭī) on the two lower storeys. However, the tiles were removed from roofs and replaced with copper plates by ValkhuGaṇeśa Upabhokttā Samiti. The President of the Samiti was Mohana Prasāda Jośī. The old tiled roofs can be seen inPruscha's (1975, 177) inventory.

event_name: Covering of the crafted wooden frame with embossed brass plate
event_description: There is a niche at the centre of the sanctum where the main images of Gaṇeśa are kept. The outer part of the niche is decorated in a crafted wooden frame. This frame was covered with embossed brass plate by Kīrtimāna and his wife Padmāvatī.
Brass flags were erected in front of the temple by Lakṣmīsudha and his wife Tutakī.

This inscription is from the late Malla period, but is too eroded to decipher its content. As it features a carving of a trident, Śiva’s implement, suggesting a connection to this Śiva temple. This suggests the temple’s late Malla origins.

This inscription from 1695 CE (NS 816) is legible but unrelated to the temple. It refers to a Kumāra temple in the area where Kṛṣṇamatī, granddaughter of King Śrīnivāsa Malla, installed an Umāmaheśvara statue and endowed land for a trust. While this Kumāra temple later disappeared, its inscription appears to have been relocated here. Kunu Śarmā’sKīrtipatākāmentions the presence of a temple dedicated to Kārtikeya, another name of Kumāra, west of the Nugaḥ Ṭola. This inscription is from that missing temple.
Reconstruction with the support of the Association of Assistance for Education in Nepal, Mitra Japan and Dupāt Tol Sudhār Samiti.
This inscription has nothing to do with theDāphāBhajanaPhalcā. However, it records the paving of the path that passes in front of the Phalcāin 1651 CE.
The inscription informs readers that Rachimaṃ, Bhimanasiṃ and the other residents of Sunaguthi who enabled the construction of Kulima built this Phalcā and established aguṭhīfor its management.
The inscription states that local residents collected donations for the reconstruction of the Phalcā under the coordination of the Guru Harṣalāla group.

This inscription at the site only mentions that a group including Hāku Juvāra "established" something here. However, the full details are not disclosed. They probably established theirdigudyaḥhere on that occasion.
Mārika and others jointly offered one woodentoraṇaand two stonetoraṇas to Goddess Vaiṣṇavī.मारिका लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर वैष्णवीदेवीलाई काठको एउटा तोरण र ढुङ्गाका दुईवटा तोरण चढाएका थिए ।
Tusiṃrāma Bhāro, a resident of Satuṅgala, donated a large stonetoraṇato Vaiṣṇavī at Baḥkhu Pīṭha.सतुंगल निवासी तुसिंराम भारोले बःखु पीठका वैष्णवीलाई ढुङ्गाको ठूलो तोरण चढाएका थिए ।

event_name: Offering of a pair of lions (KAT3420-008, KAT3420-009)
event_description: Hīrālāla Khatrī, Raṇamehera Khatrī, Motīlāla Khatrī, and others jointly offered a pair of stone lions to thepīṭha.हिरालाल खत्रि, रणमेहेर खत्रि, मोतिलाल खत्रि लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर पीठमा एकजोडी ढुङ्गाको सिंह चढाएका थिए ।

Thepīṭhawas renovated through donations collected from devotees. The shrine, which had previously been open, was covered with a roof and fitted with a door after renovation.भक्तजनसँग चन्दा उठाएर पीठको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो । पहिले खुल्ला रहेको पीठलाई जीर्णोद्धारपछि छाना राखेर छोप्नुका साथै ढोका पनि राखिएको थियो ।

In memory of the late Jaṅgabahādura Ḍaṅgola, his grandmother Dhanamāyā Ḍaṅgola and father Rājakājī Ḍaṅgola offered a bell.दिवंगत जङ्गबहादुर डङ्गोलको स्मृतिमा हजुरआमा धनमाया डङ्गोल र बुबा राजकाजी डङ्गोलले घण्टा चढाएका थिए ।

Ratnajyoti Vajrācārya of Bu Bāhā, Vaṅkuri (southeastern direction), together with his sons Mānajyoti and Bhagavānajyoti, offered a stonetoraṇato thepīṭha.बु बाहार, वंकुरि (दक्षिण-पूर्व दिशा) बस्ने रत्नजोति वज्राचार्यले छोराहरू मानजोति, भगवानजोतिसँग मिलेर पीठमा ढुङ्गाको तोरण चढाएका थिए ।

Siddhisiṃha installed the Caitya in front of the Phalcā after an overnight fire oblation conducted by the priest Devarāja Vajrācārya, and also formed aguthifor the Caitya's anniversary ritual and its upkeep.

The male donor, Siddhisiṃha, offered relevant utensils related to the Caitya in front of the Phalcā to theguthi. He also started the tradition of lighting up oil lamps around the Caitya and distributingsamaybaji,syāḥbaji, meat and rice bearfrom here on the day of arrival of Buṅgadyaḥ at Lagankhel.

The first and second floors of the Phalcā were added when it was reconstructed into a three-storey modern building in 1995 CE (VS 2052) with donations from local residents. Its present structure has no remains of traditional architecture.
Samacā, his wife Saganī, son Āpulāla and other family members jointly offered 108 lamps andilā̃to the Caitya.
The building is attributed to Bahādur Śāha who acted as the regent from 1785 to 1794.

event_name: Use of the building for the Earthquake Loan Branch
event_description: After the earthquake of 1934, the building housed the Earthquake Loan Branch in charge of providing loans to those affected by the earthquake.
A school was established in the building.
The building was leased to the Tripadma Vidhyāśrama School.
Ādarśa Kanyā Niketana (Girl's school) was formally established.
The monument was damaged in the 2015 earthquakes.
The monument was restored by the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust with funding from the U.S. Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation.
Licchavi inscription
The Hiti was renovated (UN-HBITAT2008, 47-48). According toPruschathis happened in 1610 CE.
The stonemaṇḍala(āsana) was offered by the son of a certain Bhīmadāsa Jogī.

A certain Dhavavira Siṃha, a resident of Dunchẽ Bāhāḥ (text: Duchebāhāra) in Dhũllā Ṭola, sponsored the Shrine’s reconstruction along with his wife Dhaṃthakuṃ and his sons (see ‘description’ above for more information).
Kālidāsa of Baniyānani and family members supported the gilding of a copper statue and offered a gilt pinnacle, a bell and two lions (siṃhas).
Sidhīlāla Vṃsī offered the bell (SKH0120-004) to Gaṇeśā.
It is probable that the date corresponds to the donation of the bell.
Thedharmadātuin front of the shrine was constructed by Bekhāratna Sikarmī

event_name: Construction of Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (object number KAT1070-004)
event_description: The Caitya in the courtyard was built by Motimāna Śākyabhikṣu (text: Motimāna Sākyebhīkṣu), Nānīmāyā, Kṛṣṇadevī, and others.

event_name: Installation of Akṣobhya statue (initial construction of the bāhāḥ)
event_description: The inscription on the pedestal records its installation by Pūrṇamāna (text: Purnamāna) and his wife Ratnamāna in memory of his father-in-law, also marking the initial construction of thebāhāḥ. Due to erosion, the date in the inscription can no longer be deciphered. Pruscha, writing in 1975 CE, reads the date as 1936 CE (NS 1056), which contradicts the account of thebāhāḥ'ssenior-most elder who claims thebāhāḥwas built in 1926 CE (NS 1046).
This inscription records Jagajyoti (text: Jayajyoti) Malla’s selection of stones for the construction of certain work of art.

Trivikrama Śarmmā reconstructed the Cā̃guJaḥdhuṃ, and the inscription installed during the reconstruction warns that anyone who damages it will be guilty of the five great sins. It also states that failing to fill theJaḥdhuṃwith water on the twelfth lunar day, full moon, and Wednesday will result in sin.

Budharāja (Buddharāja) founded a caitya (LAL1082-002) dedicated to his late father Maṇirāja, securing funds for its yearly ceremonies.आफ्ना बाबु मणिराज दिवंगत भएको कारणले बुधराज (बुद्धराज) ले बाबुका नामले चैत्य (LAL1082-002) स्थापना गरी वार्षिक कर्मको व्यवस्था मिलाई आयको व्यवस्था गरे ।

On Buddha Jayantī, the stone lamp stand (dalupā) surrounding the Malla dynasty's Caitya (LAL1082-002) is installed.बुद्ध जयन्तीका दिन मल्लकालीन चैत्यको (LAL1082-002) चौतर्फी ढुङ्गाको चाक्रमत (चाकःमत) स्थापना गरियो ।
A stone lion was added into Śikharakūta Caitya(LAL1082-002)of Malla dynasty.मल्लकालीन शिखरकूट चैत्य(LAL1082-002)मा सिंह प्रतिमा थप्ने कार्य गरियो ।
A piṭha near the stambha was reconstructed.यस स्तम्भ समीपैमा रहेको पीठलाई पुनर्निर्माण गरियो ।

Under the initiative of a Rañjitkāra couple, metal railings and poles were constructed along the steep staircase leading to the Ādīnātha temple, to make the ascent easier for devotees. Other devotees also contributed to this project.

event_name: Construction of cemented wall and other structures
event_description: In 1994–95 CE (VS 2051), a small cemented structure, boundary wall, and externalcautārā(resting platform) were built surrounding the well. At that time, public access to the well was restricted; instead, arrangements were made for the water to collect in an external tank for common use. The overflow from this tank was directed through a pipe to another tank located about 400 meters downhill near thecautārā. This renovation was carried out under local leadership with donations collected from devotees.

In memory of the late military officer (senānī) Tilaka Bahādura Kārkī and other deceased members of his family, sixphalcā(resting pavilions) and shrines of four Nārāyaṇa and four Vināyaka deities were constructed along the stairway leading to the Ādīnātha temple. This work was undertaken by his descendants.
A Maharjana family from Dugaṃbahī, Kathmandu, established a shrine containing fourKaruṇāmayaimages near this well in honor of their deceased ancestors.
Amātya Raghuvīra Siṃha, Jitamāna and other family members jointly endowed land to run daily worship (nityapūjā) and other pūjās.
Bāsibā Guṭhī donated apatāḥto the temple.
Amṛtarāja Mahāta (Amātya) repaired the temple during the reign of king Siddhinarasiṃha Malla.

Śrīpatideva Rāvura (Ravuta) का छोरा देव भारोले आफू र आफ्नो छोरा Narasiṃha Bhāro को प्रतिमा बनाई स्थापना गरेका थिए । त्यसैमा अर्की एक महिलाले छोरा Manohora Siṃha र छोरी Rambhāvatī को मूर्ति पनि थपेकी थिइन् ।
Narasiṃha Bhāro endowed land to observe annual worship of own statue. He also donated some money for the repair the statue.

The inscription only mentions that it was offered in honor of the goddess Pūrṇacaṇdī, but it is not written who offered what. The inscription is inscribed on the lower part of the metal toraṇa on the back of the goddess Pūrṇacaṇdī inside the sanctum sanctorum, so the toraṇa should be placed on the occasion of the donation of the toraṇa.

event_name: Donation of a stone pillar with a lion
event_description: Kṛṣṇalāla Bhāro donated a stone pillar with a lion in front of the temple with his mother Jagannātha Lakṣmī and two brothers Viṣṇulāla and Śivalāla during the reign of King Surendra Śāha.

event_name: Donation of a toraṇa and cladding door
event_description: Amātya Raghuvīra Siṃha and Jitamāna Siṃha donated a toraṇa and cladded the inner door with brass.
Amātya Kulamāna donated metal flags to the either side of the temple.
Amātya Raghuvīra Siṃha donated toraṇa covered with brass plate.

event_name: Replacing jhiṅgaṭī roof with brass sheet
event_description: Top roof of the temple with jhĩgaṭī-tile was replaced with brass sheet.

event_name: Donation of metal tree and a toraṇa to Mānabhairava
event_description: Dhirjamānasi donated metal tree and toraṇa cladded with brass plate for Mānabhairava.
Kulavīra Sĩ Mullī performed Yaśvomera yajña in front of the temple.
Amātya Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, his son Subbā Raghuvīra and other family members covered a pair of stone lions with brass plate.

event_name: Renovation of the temple and replacing jhiṅgaṭī roof with brass plate
event_description: Although the renovation work of the temple was started as per the wish of King Mahendra, his son King Birendra was present at the closing ceremony of the temple renovation as his father died. During the renovation,jhiṅgaṭīroof was replaced on the second floor with brass sheets.
Hārā Bhāī Sresta (Śreṣṭha) and Nānimeju donated gold platedpatāḥto Siddhilakṣmī in memory of their deceased family members.

event_name: Cladding the sanctum wall with brass plate
event_description: Hārā Bhāi Rājabhãnāri (Rajbhaṇḍārī), Candramāna, Nāni Meju (Mayaju) and Lakṣmi jointly cladded the sanctum wall with brass plate.
Balarāma Śreṣṭha, Ravi Rāma Śreṣṭha, Pūrṇa Kumārī Śreṣṭha and others jointly donated a metalpatāḥto the Pūrṇacaṇḍī.
The inscription cannot be read because it is covered with thick layer of oil.
Inscription cannot be read because it is completely damaged.

The inscription, preserved on the first floor of thedharmaśālā, documents its initial construction by Brahma Samasera Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇa in memory of his wife Durgā Kumārī. Additionally, the inscription indicates that no land was allocated to thedharmaśālā, and nogūṭhī(trust) was established for its maintenance. The founder earnestly requests the king, subjects, and nobles to assume responsibility for its renovations whenever necessary.
Dharmanārāyaṇa, along with his wife Dhanalakṣmī, sons, and daughters, renovated the Gaṇeśa temple and offered a gilded finial.
The shrine was constructed by Nandīkeśvara Bhāro and Manaharisiṃha Bhāro.

event_name: Renovation of the shrine and endowment of land
event_description: The shrine was renovated along with an endowment of land for the formation of aguthiwishing for eternal emancipation (mokṣa) of a deceased person named Dayālakṣmī.

event_name: Re-establishment of Gaṇeśa statue (object number: SKH0400-010)
event_description: The statue of Gaṇeśa was re-established with the donations collected at the initiation of Śivaprasāda Śreṣṭha and Vinoda Śreṣṭha.
The inscription contains figures of 16 donors in four lines with their names. However, it does not mention any events.
Dhīra Śamśera's wife Indrakumārīdevī built Indrabhakteśvara over a decade after her husband built Dhīrabhakteśvara (PPK1966) in Mṛgasthalī in 1854 CE (VS 1911).
Indrakumārīdevī donated a bell to the temple. In the bell inscription, she is referred to as “pūrvatarphakākamyānḍīṅajanaralanī,” meaning “the wife of the eastern commanding general.”
The temple collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes but was rebuilt by the Pashupati Area Development Trust in 2019 CE (VS 2076).

Together with his wives Lānidhaṃ and Cakralakṣmī, Jagannātha Kāyaṣṭha, resident of Khaumā Ṭola, had the Phalcā constructed. Then he endowed 2ropanīs and 2karṣas of land for observing the anniversary and other rituals, along with offering meals to the five elders of the localdāphābhajanagroup.
The Phalcā was rebuilt as part of the Bhaktapur Development Project. The project was started as a joint venture of the Nepal and German governments.
The Phalcā was dismantled in 2010 and rebuilt by the Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan City and Department of Archaeology.

event_name: Construction of a maṇdapa (phalcā) and establishment of a śivaliṅga
event_description: The oldest inscription in the complex, dated to 1669 CE (NS 789), is affixed to the southwest corner of the site but is unrelated to the present Tileśvara temple. Installed during the reign of King Śrīnivāsa Malla, it records that descendants of a Brahmin named Śakatāja—who had accompanied King Jayahariśivadeva—built a maṇḍapa and installed a deity at this site. It includes a brief genealogy and mentions land endowments (guṭhī) for temple rituals. However, neither the Śivaharīśvara-liṅga nor the endowed lands survive today.
The inscription on the outer west wall of the temple names Vaṃśamuni Ācārya as the founder and records a renovation carried out by his descendant Hari Ācārya.

The inscription recording this event states that the temple, renovated in 1819 CE (VS 1876), was damaged in the 1934 CE (VS 1990) earthquake and subsequently restored by Nārayaṇamaṇi Ācārya, the great-grandson of Harinārāyaṇa Ācārya, who had overseen the earlier renovation.

Near the Sarasvatī Kuṇḍa, some inscriptions can be seen carved on the base of a stone structure. The names of some donors are mentioned in the inscription, but as some parts are cracked and unclear, further details cannot be discerned.

Bhavānidāsa of Bakū Nani, Caṃki Ṭol, Lalitpur, together with his wife Mānakumārī and sons Īśvarīdāsa and Kṛṣṇadāsa, built the Jaḥdhuṃ in dedication to Bālakumārī Devī and in memory of his ancestors. To maintain the water supply, he endowed 1.5ropanīof land at Ṣonāthau as aguṭhī, with a clause allowing reclamation in case of neglect. During the annualvarṣavardhana pūjā, offerings ofSamaybaji—beaten rice (ciurā),syāḥbaji,boḍe, meat, and ginger—were made under the supervision of the localpañcas(elders) of Caṃki Ṭol.

The Department of Archaeology reconstructed Kutisāḥ Gaṇeśa Phalcā in 2021 CE. Until the early 1990s, only a rectangular plinth existed at the location (no other remnants of the Phalcā were found). Even senior members of the locality do not recall a complete phalcā on the site. The Kutisāḥ Gaṇeśa Phalcā was inaugurated by the Mayor of the Kiritpur municipality on August 30, 2021.
A group of six individuals–Bhāgīrāma, Jayahari, Bhāyarāma, Durja, Saterāma, and Kavirāma–built the temple.

Three brothers—Dālita, Labikala Sāhu Bhāro, and Bilananda Sāhu Bhāro—donated land for thephalcāwest of the temple in honor of their parents, Tadhi Sāhu and Bakhalakṣmī. They also established a non-expendable trust to support thephalcā. The income from the land and fund was used to organize the worship of Gaṇeśa on the final day of Caitra during theBiskāḥ Jātrāfestival, followed by the distribution of various food offerings on the next day, the 1st solar day of Vaiśākha.
A worship for the welfare of the community was organised in the courtyard on the 21st day of Māgha VS 2018. Donations were collected for the construction of thecaitya.

event_name: Consecration of the statue of Aparimitā
event_description: तपादेवले अपरिमिताको मूर्ति स्थापना गरेका थिए ।
राजा त्रिभुवनको राज्यकालमा वज्राचार्य लोकमानले दिवंगत बाजे कुलमान, बज्यै राजेलक्ष्मीको नाममा बाहाः प्राङ्गणमा ढुङ्गा छापेका थिए ।
फ्रेण्ड्स अफ जर्मनीको आर्थिक सहयोगमा बाहाः द्यःछेँ जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो । पुरातत्त्व विभागमा कार्यरत गुह्यहर्ष वज्राचार्यको प्रयासमा उक्त आर्थिक सहयोग प्राप्त भएको थियो ।

नेसं ११०१ भाद्र कृष्ण १२ मा दिवंगत भएका बुबा राजगुरु रत्नमान वज्राचार्य लगायत दिवंगत पुर्खाहरूको सुखावती भुवनमा बास होस् भन्ने कामना गरी वज्राचार्य पुष्परत्नले आमा इन्द्रकुमारी, श्रीमती तारादेवी, छोराहरू मञ्जुश्रीरत्न, शान्तश्री लगायत परिवारका सदस्यहरूले मिलेर बाहाः प्राङ्णमा धर्मधातुजिनालय चैत्य स्थापना गरेका थिए ।
न्यूरोड निवासी चन्द्रदेव शाक्य र रेगुनी शाक्यले परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर बाहाः द्यःछेँको छानामा राखिएको झिङ्गटी निकालेर तामाको छाना राखिदिएका थिए ।

मरु टोल निवासी भक्तानन्द वज्राचार्य र उनकी श्रीमती रञ्जनाले मिलेर क्वाःपाःद्यःको शिरमाथि चाँदी र पित्तलको इलां चढाएका थिए । त्यसभन्दा अघि उनीहरूले क्वाःपाःद्यःलाई चाँदीको कण्ठी, नित्यपूजा गर्न चाँदीको थाल, चामर पनि चढाइसकेका थिए ।

Construction of the Phalcāwith the support of the Bhāvo and Prajāpati communities of the Khapiṁchẽ area. A stone inscription attached to the eastern wall provides further information about its construction, which took place in 1840.
This reconstruction led to the addition of another storey and the inclusion of the shrine into the building.
The temple was rebuilt after the 1934 earthquake. According to local informants, Sūryavīra Śreṣṭha and a Tāmrākāra were responsible for its reconstruction.

event_name: Initial Construction of the Temple, Hiti, and Phalcā, and Establishment of a Guṭhī
event_description: The inscription records that a certain donor from Kirtipur constructed this temple along with the nearbyhitiand one of twophalcās,and established aguṭhī.Unfortunately, the part of the inscription where the date and the name of the donor were recorded, is severly damaged.  Its legible part mentionsKvāṭha NāyakaCaṇḍī Rāja Bhāro (Ś. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2057 182-183) as one of theguṭhīmembers.'Kvāṭha Nāyaka'refers to a post which was given to the head officer of Kirtipur by Malla King of Patan in the Late Malla Period. On this basis, it can be assumed that the temple was built in the Late Malla Era.

event_name: Addition of a Phalcā to the Temple Premises
event_description: Mitanārā and his other family members jointly constructed aphalcāadjacent to the temple.
The monument was severly damaged during the 2015 CE earthquakes.
The temple was rebuilt after the 2015 CE earthquakes by the Department of Archaeology (DoA).
The old building of the Bāhāḥ was renovated by selling a piece of its land. The remaining amount of the money was distributed among thesaṅghamembers. Aṣṭarāja Śākya coordinated this.
Jñānajoti, Puṇyarāja and Nhukṣarāja established adharmadhātumaṇḍalain the memory of Harṣajoti inside the courtyard.
Acaityainside the Bāhāḥ was renovated.

Matsyendrasimha of Dattalācheṃ (Dhālācheṃ) Ṭola, Lalitpur, constructed aphalcain the name of Lakṣmīramaṇa Upādhyāya and his three wives Dhanthakuṃ, Lakṣmī, and Pālulakṣmī. He also endowed threeropanīsof land as guthi for its upkeep. The income generated from this land was designated to fund annual worship of Dāmodara (Gaṇeśa), Sarasvatī, and Lakṣmī on 3rd of bright fortnight of Kārtika, followed byśrāddharituals. It was mandated that Brahmins, Brāhmaṇīs, Jyotiśīs, and Karmācāryas be invited to these ceremonies. Any remaining funds after the rituals were to be used to provide a feast for the guthi caretakers. The inscription lists these caretakers as Bhajusimha Bhāro of Olā Ṭola, Gajendrasimha Bhāro of Kobahā Ṭola, Vīranarasimha Bhāro of Sātiglā (Saugaḷ) Ṭola, and Cikiti Bhāro of Dattalācheṃ Ṭola. At present, only asataḥ(raised platform) remains within the Dhantila Vārāhī shrine precinct; nophalcasurvives, indicating that the pavilion built by Matsyendrasiṃha has likely disappeared over time.
Jita Govinda Amātya of Daubāhā Ṭola, Lalitpur, together with his sons Kīrtigovinda and Pūrṇagovinda Amātya, constructed aghāṭa(riverbank platform) at Dhantila on the Bagmatī River.

event_name: Installation of a new statue of Vārāhī
event_description: After the original image of Vārāhī housed in the sanctum was stolen, Kṛṣṇanātha Māske and his wife Śakuntalā Māske of Bālīphala Ṭola, Lalitpur, commissioned and installed a new cast-metal image of the goddess. On this occasion, they also tiled the sanctum floor, added copper sheeting (ilāṃ), applied gilding (jalapa) to the toraṇa, and installed an iron fence around the temple for security.

In memory of the late Gajanārāyaṇa Śāhī and the late Harkhamāyā Śāhī, Kṛṣṇabahādura Śāhī, Jvālādevī Śāhī, and others installed a Dharmadhātujinālaya caitya in the temple courtyard.

After the temple sustained some damage in the 2015 CE (VS 2072) earthquake, Balrām K.C. of Kopaṇḍola undertook its restoration in memory of his late father Kālugaṇḍe K.C., his late mother Kāñchī K.C., and his late wife Bhagavatī K.C.
Bīrena Khaḍgī, Rośanī Khaḍgī, and others from Kumbheśvara Ṭola, Lalitpur, jointly installed brasspatāḥs (decorative metal leaves) on the temple.

The reconstruction of the temple was undertaken by the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust, funded by the US Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation, in collaboration with the Department of Archaeology. An inscription from another Śiva temple (KAT1550) of similar size situated north of this monument records the reconstruction of that temple in 2018 CE (VS 2074), in response to the damages caused by the 2015 CE earthquakes. Although the inscription does not make reference to this particular temple, it too underwent reconstruction during that period. In the process of restoration, the struts were repurposed, while some of the carved windows were replaced with new ones.

This inscription is not related to thehiti. Although the date of this inscription has already eroded, it is clear that it was installed during the joint rule of King Bhīmārjunadeva and Jiṣṇugupta. It declares the reduction of levies onmalla(a kind of pet animal) and their babies to facilitate the residents of Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma (D.Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 425).

This inscription is unrelated to thehiti.It was installed during the joint rule of King Bhīmārjunadeva and Viṣṇugupta, dated Mānadeva Samvat 64 (640 CE). It documents the rulers' pleasur with the efforts of people for having pulled a large stone for carving a statue of Viṣṇu. Viṣṇugupta granted the residents of Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma the privilege to wear jewelry, with the exception of anklets and armlets of specific kinds. The inscription also highlights Viṣṇugupta's commissioning of a large reclining statue of Viṣṇu in a pond at the base of the northern hills (Gopālarājavaṃśāvalīfol. 22). The inscription confirms what is recorded in the chronicle. Moreover, the inscription reveals a shift in Viṣṇugupta's approach toward justice. He showed leniency towards the residents of Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma concerning theft, murder, and crimes against the state. The decree in the inscription specifies that only the individual convicted of these crimes would face punishment, excluding their family members. This contrasts with the prevailing practice at the time, where even the family members of convicts were punished as accessories to the crime (D. Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 447).

This inscription is unrelated to thehiti. It records the retention ofbirtālands by King Narendradeva in the name of the residents of Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma. This retention is granted as a recognition of their service in caring for the temple of Māneśvara. The land was seized from them by Bhaumagupta (D. Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 467).
In 2008-2009, thehitiwas renovated by the Department of Archaeology.

In 2018 CE, in commemoration of the anniversary of their movement, the Save Nepa Valley group organized the cleaning of thehiti. Thehitihad been neglected, leading to an overgrowth of weeds and bushes, and the poor drainage system resulted in a flooded floor. The Nepal Army actively contributed to the cleaning initiative, and the deputy mayor of the Kathmandu Metropolitan City attended the program.

The inscription also states that the Śivaliṅga should be worshipped on various festivals throughout a year.मठ अगाडिको यस लिङ्गमा नित्यपूजाका खातिर नेसं ८६३ (सन् १७४३) मा सन्यासी अमर गिरिले जग्गा दान गरेका थिए । मन्दिरमा नित्य पूजाका खातिर नीलकण्ठ भट्टलाई टोकिएको थियो । नित्यपूजाका साथै वर्षचक्रका विविध पर्वमा पनि शिवलिङ्गमा विशेष पूजाहरू गरिनु पर्ने कुराको उल्लेख अभिलेखमा परेको छ ।

In 1760 CE (NS 880), Amara Girī donated his entire residence, and a piece of land with dilapidated house  in the name of Mahādeva (NHDP_0001_0010).जग्गा दानको १७ वर्ष पश्चात् उनै अमर गिरिले वर्ष पश्चात् अर्थात् नेसं ८८० (सन् १७६०) मा आफ्नो सम्पूर्ण निवासस्थल र भग्न घर सहितको एक पाटो जग्गा पनि महादेवकै नाममा दान गरेका थिए (NHDP_0001_0010) ।

Thus, due to the Mahant’s great reverence, by donating lands from various places and his own residence, a distinct relationship was established between the nearby temple and the maṭha. In 1811 CE (1868 VS), King Gīrvāṇayuddha granted 10 ropanī of land to Triliṅgeśvara. Mahanta Lakṣmī Girī was entrusted with managing rituals and administration (K_0012_0031A/K_0014_0023B).यसरी मठ समीपैको मन्दिरलाई महन्तबाट ठुलो श्रद्धाले विविध ठाउँका प्रशस्त जग्गा र आफ्नै निवास दान दिएदेखि मन्दिर र मठको विशिष्ट सम्बन्ध स्थापना हुँद पुगेको थियो । पछि विसं १८६८ मा राजा गीर्वाणयुद्धबाट त्रिलिङ्गेश्वरलाई थप १० रोपनी जग्गा दान भएको थियो । राजाले तत्कालीन महन्त लक्ष्मी गिरि गोलाईँलाई पूजा एवं सम्पूर्ण कार्य सम्हाल्ने अधिकार पनि सुम्पेका थिए ।

event_name: Covering door wings (khāpā) with brass sheets
event_description: Kṛṣṇagopāla, Bekhālakṣṃī, and Lakṣmīnānī, along with their family members, presented a brass cover for the entrance to the sanctum on the first floor of the Dyaḥchẽ. They also gave 21 brass lamps and two small drums (ḍamaru).

event_name: Completion of the reconstruction of the Dyaḥchẽ and its inauguration
event_description: The Dyaḥchẽ was reconstructed in 2013 CE. Satyamohan Joshi, a cultural expert, was invited to the event.
The earthquakes in 2015 CE caused some damage to the Dyaḥchẽ. The damage was minor because it had only been rebuilt two years before.
Rājendralāla Śreṣṭha, a resident from Baluwatar repaired the palanquin of Kaṅgaḥ Ajimā, which is used in her annual procession.

event_name: First phase of renovation of the Dyaḥchẽ
event_description: The Kathmandu Metropolitan City Office and the Hanumandhoka Palace Conservation Program funded the first phase of the Dyaḥchẽ's renovation.
The second phase of the Dyaḥchẽ’s renovation was also funded by the Kathmandu Metropolitan City Office and the Hanumandhoka Palace Conservation Program.

monument_name: Hitigāḥcā (built during the late Malla Period)
event_name: Initial Construction of Htigāḥcā, Śiva Mandira, and Phalcā, and Establishment of a Guṭhī
event_description: The inscription records that a certain donor from Kirtipur constructed Hitigāḥcā along with the nearby Śiva Mandira (KIR0078) and one of the twophalcās,and established aguṭhī.Unfortunately, the part of the inscription where the date and the name of the constructor were recorded, is badly damaged. Its preserved part mentions thatKvāṭha NāyakaCaṇḍī Rāja Bhāro as one of theguṭhīmembers (cf.Ś. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2057 182-183).

monument_name: Hitigāḥcā (built during the late Malla Period)
event_description: The nearby Śiva Mandira (KIR0078) was rebuilt after it suffered serious damages during the 2015 CE earthquakes. During this rebuilding project, Hitigāḥcā was also renovated by the Department of Archaeology (DoA).
Narahari Bhāro and his wife Vasumuni, residents of Dhopogatra (present Dhaugala ṭola) facilitated the construction of this Phalcā.

event_name: Recitation of Guṇakāraṇḍavyūha text and renovation of the Phalcā
event_description: A ritual expert from Hiraṇyavarṇa Mahāvihāra recitesGuṇakāraṇdavyūhaat the chariot procession of Matsyendranātha. This was related to the renovation of the building that took place one year later.

Lalitpur Metropolitan City and Lumanti (a NGO) provided some necessary equipment to locals that may be useful in a natural disaster. Some of this is still stored haphazardly in the Phalcā. An iron fence was also fixed around the Phalcā.
The roof was renovated and some of the original struts and joists were replaced with new ones. The main donor was a person from the Khaḍgī caste, Thati ṭola.

event_name: Donation of finials and a lotus flower
event_description: Devajoti, his wife Hālāvati, son Amṛtjoti and grandson Śubhajoti performed a fire ritual worship and made an offering of two finials. Amṛtajoti also donated a lotus flower, which was placed at the center of the goldenilā̃.

event_name: Donation of ghee lamps and a statue
event_description: Dhãcā Thakũ and other family members donated 32 ghee lamps and an image. Land was also bestowed upon the temple to fund its management.

event_name: The earliest mention of Guji Bāhāḥ
event_description: The name Guji Bāhāḥ was mentioned in a manuscript entitledKriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā,preserved in the Asiatic Society, Calcutta. This was written during the reign of King Abhaya Malla. In this manuscript, Guji Bāhāḥ is referred to as Vaiśya Śrī Divākara Varmma Mahāvihāra.

event_name: Donation of a pair of lion
event_description: A pair of stone lions were donated and placed on either side of the entrance to sanctum. This occured whilst Bhimapāla was theThapāḥjuof thevihāra. The donation was made by Amṛtasiṃhadeva, Bitusiṃhadeva, Adikara and others.

event_name: Donation of deities with golden toraṇa
event_description: Deva, Devajoti and Amṛtajoti donated funds to gild the statue of thebāhāḥ'smain deity. The door of the sanctum and thetoraṇawere also gilded. Images of the Five Buddhas, Vajrapāṇi and Ratnapāṇi were also installed at this time.

A golden robe was donated to thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥby Devajoti, his son Amṛtajoti and his grandson Śubhajoti.A goldenilā̃was donated to Trailokya Vijaya Āḥju by Devajoti, his son Amṛtjoti and his grandson Śubhajoti.A new storey was added to the esoteric shrine by Thapāḥju Guṇarāja and otherāḥjusof thebāhāḥ.

event_name: Donation of a golden window to Trailokya Vijaya Āḥju and Hevajra
event_description: A golden window was donated to Trailokya Vijaya Āḥju and Hevajra.
Pañcaratna Śākya (Sānukājī Śākya), his wife Jñānīśobhā Śākya and his family donated thelāḥphaḥcāthat is fixed at the threshold of the sanctum's entrance.

event_name: Donation of door and wooden toraṇa to Trailokyā Vijaya Āḥju / Donation of hegā to kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ
event_description: Śākyavamśa Manisiṃha, Deva and others donated a woodentoraṇato Trailokyā Vijaya Āḥju and ahegātokvāḥpāḥdyaḥduring the reign of King Śrīnivāsa Malla.

event_name: Donation of a pair of flag
event_description: Āsāmadu, his son Budharatna, and his daughter Āsāmāyā donated a pair of metal flags.
Candrajoti, Prammani, Dhamasāri and others donated a pair of brass door leaves. These were used for the entrance to the sanctum.

event_name: Donation of statue of Sāriputra and other images
event_description: 1. Munajoti donated a statue of Sāriputra. This was established at the east of the sanctum.2. Munajoti donated atoraṇaand images of Kākāsya-Ulakāsya to Trailokya Vijaya Āḥju.
Āsāmadu and his younger brother Sigharāja donated the image of Maudagalyāyana that is placed at the western corner of the sanctum.
Joganarasiṃha, his son Mutinarasiṃha and the rest of his family built thedharmadhātujinālaya caityain thebāhāḥcourtyard.

event_name: Donation of archway in front of the sanctum
event_description: Āsāmadu and his wife Hyerāmāyā donated an artistic archway with a floral design and apūrṇakalaśa.These are installed in front of the entrance to the sanctum.

The monastic building was renovated. Total Rs. 11, 90,939.66 was expended for the renovation. Lalitpur Metropolitan City donated Rs. 4,00000, Rs. 6,46,939.66 was gathered in donations, and Rs. 1,35,000 came from the voluntary labour of local people.
Thegumbāon the east of thebāhāḥwas renovated by Lalitpur Sub-metropolitan City and donations of local people.

event_name: Covering of upper part of Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala with brass plate
event_description: The upper part ofdharmadhātu maṇḍalawas covered with brass plate in the memory of the deceasedthapāḥjuDhana Śākya.

event_name: Donation of a maṇḍaḷa in front of sanctum
event_description: Thesaṅghamembers of the Guji Bāhāḥ donated a brassmaṇḍalawhich is placed in front of the sanctum.
Pūrṇa Bahādur Śākya donated 32dalūpāsfor the lamps to be lit in memory of his father Punadeva Śākya and his mother Lakṣmīmāyā Śākya.

Thedigiwas renovated. Rs. 14,29,629 was expended for the renovation. UDLE donated Rs. 4,50,000, Rs. 2,45,277 came from thebāhāḥ'streasury, Rs. 5,52,852 was collected in donations, and Rs. 1,81,500 came from the voluntary labour of local people.
The inscription on the plinth of the Nandī statue mentions that it was offered in the name of Śiva by a donor (name illegible due to erosion of text) from the Gaḥchẽ Ṭola.
Before the present Temple structure was constructed in the 1980s by local residents, theśivaliṅgaand the Nandī statue used to be under the open sky.
Hirāmāna Maharjana and his wife Kānchī Maharjana jointly offered the bell to the Temple on the occasion of Śivarātrī.

The Temple area had remained unattended amid bushes for a long time. In 2021 CE, the Kirtipur Municipality renovated the Temple along with a nearbyhitiand water tank. Stones were laid around the Temple area and an entrance gate was also constructed on that occasion.

Thetoraṇa, as stated above in the description, is only surviving remnant of the old Bāhāḥ architecture. Except for the date, the inscription on it is illegible. Therefore, what is recorded there remains a mystery. We can assume, however, that the inscription must have recorded the name(s) of the person(s)  who donated  thetoraṇato the Bāhāḥ.
Śākyabhikṣu Cikadhi of Aśokaśrī Mahāvihāra, Hvakhā Bāhāḥ constructed thedharmadhātujinālaya caityaat the Bāhāḥ premises with his wife Buddhamāyā and sons Sañjīva and Śaṃkhara.
Thekvāpāḥchẽ(main building) of the Bāhāḥ was renovated with donations from the locals. During the renovation, thejhĩgaṭītile roof was replaced with a concrete roof.

event_name: Repair of entrance, roof and pillar
event_description: Rāmaprasāda Prajāpati renovated the entrance, roof, and columns of the temple. The roof above the sanctum was made of concrete on the occasion.
Together with his wives Juluma Pradhāna and Satyabhāmā Pradhāna, Kṛṣṇaprasāda Pradhāna of Khicāpokharī offered a bell at the temple.

event_name: Offering a pair of metal pānasa (oil lamp)
event_description: Omkāralāla Śreṣṭha and his family from Naradevī offered a pair of metal lampstands in the name of the deceased family members Sanakalāla and Rambādevī.

An inscription details thephalcā's original construction. It states that Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa, a resident of Capāḥkva ṭola near thephalcā, built it with the belief that the merit from constructing thisphalcāwould ensure his deceased ancestors and future generations would attain heaven after death.

Prior to the earthquake of VS 2072, thephalcāwas in a dilapidated state. The earthquake caused significant damage to the upper portion of the structure, and it remained in disrepair for nearly seven years. In 2024 CE (VS 2081), Godavarī Municipality undertook the reconstruction of thephalcā, restoring it to its original form.
Devarāja Vajrācārya built the Akṣobhya shrine. Its inauguration ceremony lasted a whole day and night.
Devarāja Vajrācārya built the Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya in the courtyard of his house.

An inscription indicates that Guṇasiṃha Bābu had endowed some money and land asguṭhīfor this site. However, the letters are unclear, and it is not possible to determine the exact purpose for which the money and land were endowed.गुणसिंह बाबुले केहि पैसा र खेत गुठी राखेको अभिलेखबाटा थाहा हुन्छ तर अक्षरहरू स्पष्ट नभएको हुनाले के प्रयोजनका लागि पैसा र खेत राखेको हो बुझिँदैन ।

This inscription from the reign of Raṇabahādura Śāha records that a certain Movāṣīlāla, resident of Jahānāvāda, India, installed a rest-house (dharmaśālā) north of Narāyaṇa Hiti along with a Lakṣmī-Narāyaṇ image (KAT3270-010). The Lakṣmī-Narāyaṇ image he installed faces east, behind the hiti.रणबहादुर शाहको शासनकालको यस अभिलेखमा भारतको जाहानावाद निवासी मोवासीलाल भन्ने व्यक्तिले नारायणहितिको उत्तरपट्टि धर्मशाला तथा लक्ष्मीानारायणको मूर्ति (KAT3270-010) स्थापना गरेको विवरण उल्लेख भएको छ । उनले स्थापना गरेको लक्ष्मीनारायणको मूर्ति हितिको पछाडि पूर्वाभिमुख गरी स्थापना गरिएको छ ।

event_name: Installation of Garūḍanārāyaṇa (KAT3270-001) and gilded spout
event_description: Dhīra Samśera Jaṇgabahādura Rānā installed the central golden spout at thishitiand established the Garuḍa-Narāyaṇ image above it.धीर सम्शेर जङ्गबहादुर राणाले यहाँको बीचको सुवर्ण हिति र हितिमाथि स्थापना गरिएको गरूडनारायणको मुर्ति स्थापना गरेका थिए ।

King Mahendra later restored thehitispouts where water had stopped flowing, reactivating the water supply from these spouts.राजा महेन्द्रले पानी आउन बन्द भएका यहाँका हितिहरूको जीर्णोद्धार गरी हितिहरूबाट पुन: पानी आउने बनाएका थिए ।

This inscription is one among several affixed to the upper part of Narāyaṇa Hiti. The upper portion of this particular inscription is decorated with a carved image of Buddha, which suggests that some activities of Buddhist devotees may have taken place here.यो अभिलेख नारायण हितिको माथिल्लो भागमा रहेको अभिलेखहरूमध्ये एउटा हो । यस अभिलेखको माथिल्लो भागमा बुद्धको आकृति कुदिएको छ । यसबाट के अनुमान लगाउन सकिन्छ भने बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीहरूले यहाँ केहि गतिविधि गरेको हुनुपर्दछ ।

The inscription is badly damaged, and many of its letters are illegible, making it difficult to discern the full details of its content. The mention of “gājola dayakā” appears in the text, from which it can be inferred that some construction or installation for ritual worship was carried out at Narāyaṇa Hiti.यस अभिलेख पनि नराम्रोसंग फुटेको र अक्षरहरू नदेखिने भएकोले यसमा उल्लेख भएको विवरण प्रष्ट हुँदैन । यद्दपि 'गाजोल दयका' भन्ने प्रशंग आएको छ, यसबाट नारायणहितिमा केहि निर्माण गरी पूजा गरेको कुरा उल्लेख गरिएको हो को भनी अनुमान लगाउन सकिन्छ ।
A monk named Nityadhana from Sikhamuḍi Ṭola established Amitābha Buddha here and donated land to conduct the annual worship of thebāhāḥ.

After thebāhāḥwas destroyed in the earthquake of 2015 CE (VS 2072), Buddharatna Śākya, a member of thisvihāra saṃgha,renovated it in 2017 CE (VS 2074), and additional structures were built above thebāhāḥ.
12moharas were donated by Rameśvara Bāro, Kausiṁha Bāro and other Bāros for the annual worship of the temple.

Kājī Marīcamānasiṃha constructed the water spout to honor the wish of his late father, Kājī Balavānasiṃha (text: Balavānsi). Balavānasiṃha had planned to build a water spout at Baṭārabajāra square but passed away before he could accomplish this goal.

event_name: Restoring the supply of water to the spout
event_description: Building activities – likely te construction of new homes – damaged the water supply channels from the source in  Mulī. The government water corporation office in Bidur Municipality installed new metal pipes to restore the spout's functionality.
A Nāmasaṅgīti shrine was established on the eastern wall of the Phalcā.

event_name: Placement of stone statue of Guru Lekhamāna Maharjana
event_description: A statue of Guru Lekhamāna Maharjana, who used to reciteNāmasaṅgītiin the Phalcā, was donated and erected.
The Phalcā was renovated, and the sloped and tiled roof was replaced by a concrete slab roof.
The Phalcā was reconstructed by Lalitpur sub-metropolitan city. The concrete slab roof installed in 1984 was replaced by a sloped and tiled roof.

Three individuals Budhimānsi (Buddhimānasiṃha) Rajaka, Rāmadāsa Rajaka, and Herā Rajaka together with their families, renovated Hiku Hiti. After the renovation, they performed worship and the installation ritual (pratiṣṭhākarma) of the hiti. Responsibility for the care of the hiti was entrusted to the descendants of Budhimānsi, Rāmadāsa, and Herā Rajaka.

During the rule of King Pārthivendra Malla, a person from the Tulādhara caste, hailing from a specificbāhāḥin Kathmandu, undertook a certain act in reverence of Ṅatamaru Ajimā. Unfortunately, due to the deteriorated state of the inscription, many details regarding this act remain obscure.

event_name: Offering brass covers for temple door
event_description: A person named Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa enhanced the temple door by affixing a covering made of brass sheets, wishing for the salvation of his clan's ancestors.

Kapardāra Bhoṭu Pā̃ḍe made a solemn vow to offer special worship and make charitable contributions to Ṅatamaru Ajimā. This commitment arose during his detention in China while serving on a diplomatic mission in response to an offer of a treaty from the Chinese army that had already entered Nepalese territory named Ghaibung in 1792 CE (VS 1849). After his release, he honored his pledge by endowing numerous parcels of land and various brass items in the goddess's name, designating them as a source of income for daily and annual rituals.

Kapardāra Bhoṭu Pā̃ḍe enriched the two-tiered temple by adding a gilded roof and made a generous donation of more than 150ropanīs of land. As per the inscription, the income generated from these land parcels was earmarked for the exhibition of the mask dance and the execution of various rituals during major festivals. Interestingly, a historical document at the Guṭhī Lagata Jā̃ca Aḍḍā, a government office that formerly oversaw religious trusts, dating back to 1932 CE (VS 1989), provides insights into the financial transactions of this trust.

Bhoṭu Pā̃ḍe also contributed 12ropanīs of land to establish a trust dedicated to laying a special carpet along the path of the dancers during the mask dance procession when it departed from the Ākhāḥchẽ and when the troupe performed at other locations in the valley. Remarkably, a record preserved at the Guṭhī Lagata Jā̃ca Aḍḍā from 1878 CE (VS 1935) elucidates the financial activities of this trust.

Bhoṭu Pā̃ḍe established a trust by donating 6ropanīs of land with a specific purpose: to facilitate the periodic renewal of two distinctive banners known assulupuludhvajāandaṣṭamaṅgalapatākāduring the 12-year dance presentation of Ṅatamaru Ajimā. The trust's financial resources, generated from the donated lands, were designated to ensure that these banners were replaced with new ones every 12 years, just prior to the commencement of the dance performances. The inscription further directed the trust members to accompany these banners alongside the dance troupe during their performances at various locations. An additional copperplate bearing identical content, now held in a private collection by an individual taking on the role of Mahālakṣmī within the dance troupe, exists; however, its current whereabouts are unknown. Furthermore, a historical record from 1915 CE (VS 1972) at the Guṭhī Lagata Jā̃ca Aḍḍā, an administrative office previously responsible for religious trusts, details the financial activities of this trust.

A separate copperplate inscription, bearing the seal of King Gīrvāṇayuddha, is stored within the private collection of one of the dance troupe members. This inscription commemorates Bhoṭu Pā̃ḍe's donation of 6ropanīs of land for the maintenance of the aforementioned banners utilized during the 12-yearly performance of Ṅatamaru Ajimā.
Kālidāsa, a resident of the Ṅata Ṭola, offered a gildedtoraṇato his tutelary deity Ṅatamaru Ajimā.

event_name: Addition of a gilt toraṇa and doorway
event_description: The descendants of Bhoṭu Pā̃ḍe offered a gilded door andtoraṇato the temple.
Lachimāyā, Mānabādura, Sirīmāyā, and the family members covered some portions of the sanctum with brass sheets while also offering four brass statues of guarding lions.
Jogakumārī and her son Sārjyelāla Śreṣṭha installed a pair of brass lions in the sanctum.
King Mahendra commissioned the repair of broken statues from the temple.

event_name: Covering an object with brass sheet
event_description: Sīvalāla covered an item from the sanctum with brass sheets.
In memory of Sanakalāla and Rambādevī Śreṣṭha, their sons Omkāra, Śānti, Āṣiśa, and Aruna Śreṣṭha installed white tiles in the sanctum.

During the reign of King Virendra, a restoration project was initiated for the temple, necessitating the disassembly and reconstruction of the upper tier. This endeavor received financial support not only from the local community but also from the Guṭhī Saṃsthāna. The record pertaining to this renovation is inscribed on the western façade of the Naradevī Sataḥ (KAT1111).
Jokakumārī offered a brass canopy (ilāṃ) in the sanctum.

event_name: Covering an object with silver sheet
event_description: In memory of his wife Tārādevī Tulādhara, Jyotiratna Tulādhara of the Makhana Ṭola and his family members covered a portion of the main shrine with silver sheets.

event_name: Covering an object with brass sheet
event_description: Gaṇeśakumārī Mānandhara enhanced the primary deity's seat by affixing brass sheets to it. This seat is revered as Bhairava.
Omkāra, Śānti, Āṣiśa, and Aruna Śreṣṭha offered a silver statue of Ṅatamaru Ajimā, the main statue of the temple.

Mānasiṃha Bhāro of the Solaṃkī dynasty built thephalcā(BLG0020-002) to the east of the Bālāgāũ Caitya in the name of his deceased parents. He also installed a statue of Bhavānīśaṅkara in thephalcāand established a trust for the deity’s worship.
The Indra Guṭhī led by Hākudeva Bhāro built aphalcāand established a statue of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa. however, it is unclear whichphalcāthe inscription refers to.

Pandava Bhāro and his wife Dharmmāvatī of the Solaṃkī dynasty, residents of Pithagāma, built aphalcāand donated 2ropanīs of land to set up a trust for thephalcā’s upkeep. The income from the land was also to be used for hosting a feast for the trust members on the new moon day of Caitra.

The inscription states that Bhavānīśaṅkara installed images of Akṣobhya, Śāriputra, and Maudgalyāyana in his house of his own volition. It does not clarify whether these images were installed within the conceptual framework of abāhāḥ. Thus, the inscription reveals only that a Buddhist triad was originally established devotionally and at his own initiative within a private residence. Before installing the images of Akṣobhya, Śāriputra, and Maudgalyāyana, Bhavānīśaṅkara had installed his own portrait image (KAT1850-010), along with those of other family members, in Lāykū Bahī on nineth of bright fortnight of Kārtika of the same year. This fact is confirmed by the inscription carved on the pedestal of that portrait (KAT1850_I_001). Interestingly, the inscription found at the present site also records the details of this portrait installation. In it, Bhavānīśaṅkara allocates plots of land as sources of income and stipulates various ritual provisions for the annual observances related both to the images of Buddha, Śāriputra, and Maudgalyāyana, and to his own portrait installed in Lāykū Bahī.
हेमलाल ताम्राकार र उनका अन्य परिवार सदस्य मिली मन्दिरमा कंकालको मूर्ति स्थापना गरे ।

event_name: Addition of statues and architectural elements
event_description: सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएका तीन मूर्ति सहित पित्तलको तोरण र थाम चढाउने कार्य पाटनका जुजुमान र उनकी पत्नी सिदिकुमारि (सिद्धिकुमारी) तमोटले चढाए ।
पाटन, हौगलका धनवीर ताम्राकारले आफ्ना इष्टदेवीलाई लक्षित गरी एकजोडा ध्वज चढाए ।
पाटनका सिद्धिनारायण र सिद्धिलाल दुईजना मिली उग्रचण्डीलाई लक्षित गरी तामाका कंकाल र ख्याकका मूर्ति स्थापना गरे ।
दीवंगत अभिभावक एवं अन्य परिवार सदस्यका नाममा गजाधर ताम्रकारले मन्दिरमा सुवर्ण गजुर सहित छत्र र नाग स्थापना गरे ।

event_name: Addition of a pair of flag
event_description: दीवंगत पिता बेषानरमान र माता लानीथकुंका पुत्र स्येरमां र उनकी पत्नी हीरामायाको समूहले पित्तलका एकजोडा ध्वज चढाए ।
भगवतीननिका धर्मनारायण ताम्राकारको नेतृत्वमा गंगाधर, मानसिंह, धनसिंह लगायत अन्य पाटनका ताम्राकार सदस्य मिली मन्दिर काष्ठतोरण चढाए ।
विसं २०७२ सालको भूकम्पले क्षति भएको यस मन्दिरको दुई तला भत्काई ताम्राकार समाजबाट पुनर्निर्माण गरियो ।
मन्दिरको तल्लो छानालाई पाटनका मात्र नभई वीरगञ्ज र भारतका सुगौली सम्मका ताम्रकार समुदायबाट सहयोग प्राप्त गरी सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइयो ।
गजुसिंह भाजु, अनतराय, मानसिंह लगायत १८ जनाको समूहले यस मन्दिरमा काष्ठ तोरण चढाए ।

उग्रचण्डी मन्दिर परिसरमा आगम घर बनाउनका खातिर विमानझ्याः, सिंहमूर्ति, खादलू एवं नगद रकम दान गर्नेको नामावली यस अभिलेखमा टिपोट भएको छ । अभिलेखमा मिति उल्लेखित छैन तर यहाँ प्राप्त अर्को अभिलेखबाट यो कार्य विसं २०६२ मा भएको थाहा हुन्छ ।

विगतको सतःलाई भत्काई कंक्रिडको संरचनाबाट आगंछेँ नाम दिई पुनर्निर्माण कार्य गरियो । यसै भवनभित्र ‘ताम्राकार कुलदेवता उग्रचण्डीमाई संरक्षण समिति’को कार्यकक्ष रहेको छ । यस अभिलेखमा पुनर्निर्माणका खातिर भूमिका खेल्ने दाता एवं अन्य व्यबस्थापकीय भूमिकामा रहेका व्यक्तिहरूको नाम उल्लेख गरिएको छ ।
ताम्राकार समुदाय मिली मन्दिर परिसरमा जीर्ण अवस्थामा रहेको सतःलाई जीर्णोद्धार गरियो । शिलापत्रमा यस कार्यमा विविध तवरले योगदान गर्ने व्यक्तिहरूको नामावली दिइएको छ ।
पाटन, तंगः टोलका हर्षनारां (हर्षनारायण) र उनका अन्य परिवार सदस्य मिली मन्दिर अगाडि एक घण्ट स्थापना गरे ।
दीवंगत कृष्णगोपाल तमोत लगायत अन्य मृतकका नाममा जीतबहादुर, सानुलाल, विष्णुलाल, सिद्धिलक्ष्मी आदिले उग्रचण्डी मन्दिर अगाडि एक घण्ट थपे ।
पाटन, इताछेँका हरिगोविन्द ताम्राकारले आफ्ना परिवार सदस्य एवं दीवंगत भैसकेका पूर्वजका नाममा शिलास्तम्भ र त्यसमाथि धआतुको सिंहमूर्ति स्थापना गरे ।
उग्रचण्डी सेवा समितिको रोहवरमा राजा विरेन्द्रको शासनकालमा जम्मा १६३ दाताका सहयोगबाट मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण गरियो ।
यस मन्दिरको अगाडि रहेको ढुङ्गाको शिव देवललाई पाटन, तंगः टोलका प्वास्याः खलः (ताम्राकारभित्रको एक विशेष खलक) ले जगैसम्म भत्काई पुनर्निर्माण गरे ।
मन्दिर अगाडि ठुलो आकारको धातुको दियो स्थापना गरियो । ताम्राकार समुदायका विविध व्यक्तिको सहयोगमा यो दियो स्थापना भएको हो ।
स्वर्गीय पति मोतिलाल ताम्राकारको समृतिमा तुयुनानी ताम्राकारले सरस्वती मूर्तिको स्थापना गरे ।
मन्दिरको उत्तरतिर रहेको क्षेत्रपालको देवल (shrine) लाई पुनर्निर्माण गरी पित्तलको छाना र गजूर चढाइयो । पाटनका प्वाःस्याः कहलिने ताम्राकार खलकबाट यो कार्य गरिएको थियो ।

उग्रचण्डी मन्दिर अगाडिको माम्रेश्वर मन्दिरभित्र भएका तामाका सामग्रीहरू (achritectural elecents) मर्मत गर्नुका साथै आवश्यक पित्तर थपियो । पाटनका प्वाःस्याः कहलिने ताम्राकार खलकबाट यो कार्य गरिएको थियो ।

event_name: Covering the inner wall with brass
event_description: भीमलाल, पद्मलाल र अर्का भीमलाल तीनजना मिली ताम्रेश्वर महादेव देवलको भित्री भित्तामा पित्तलको पाताले मोड्ने कार्य गरे ।
The foundation was laid for the reconstruction of the Phalcā.
Yogalakṣmī, the wife of the Late Pannāmānasiṃha Malla, had funded NRs. 600,000 for the reconstruction.
