The shrine was repaired by a local individual, Bakhata Bāhādura.

The construction of the Phalcā was carried out as a replacement for the erstwhile structure, differing in shape, size, and location. The foundation stone for the recent reconstruction was laid in 2021 CE (VS 2078).
The construction of Lāncā Phalcā was completed in a span of 10 months and the monument was inaugurated amid a formal program.

event_name: Endowment of lands for feeding ascetics
event_description: Bālanātha Yogī donated land and a garden to establish a trust for conducting special worship and providing food to ascetics. The trust was responsible forpañcopacārapūjā, a special worship that involves offering five items like flowers and incense to Gorakhanātha on the 8th of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha and to Buṅgadyaḥ on the day after his chariot arrived at Lagankhel. A copperplate inscription recording the donation deed mentions King Pratāpa Malla as its witness.

King Gīrvāṇayuddha Vikrama Śāha and his mother Suvarṇaprabhādevī offered a bell (PPK1969-017) weighing 59dhārnīs (approx. 134 kgs) to the temple. The bell was crafted by Taodhikaju and his son Dhanividhiju from Naḥ Bāhāḥ Nani (LAL0520) of Patan.

event_name: Renovation of the temple and endowment of lands
event_description: Rakṣakumārī, the last wife of Jaṅga Bahādura’s father Bālanarasiṃha Kũvara, renovated the temple and offered a golden finial. She also donated over 22ropanīs of land she received from her father Nayanasiṃha Thāpā to set up a trust for future renovations of the temple and the performance of various rituals.

event_name: Endowment of lands for anniversary ritual
event_description: Rakṣakumārī endowed land parcels to form another trust for performing anniversary rituals at Gorakhanātha, along with worships at the Rakṣeśvara Śivālaya (PPK1937) and Raṇabāleśvaradevī.
Prime Minister Vīra Śamśera installed a bell (PPK1969-013) weighing 85dhārnīs (approx. 193 kgs) at the temple.
Prime Minister Candra Śamśera offered a trident (triśula; PPK1969-020) at the temple.

The Pashupati Area Development Trust replaced the bell (PPK1969-017) offered by King Gīrvāṇayuddha Vikrama Śāha and his mother Suvarṇaprabhādevī after the bell was damaged. The new bell was made identical to the original one by Ratnarāja Śākya of Oku Bāhāḥ (LAL2260) in Patan.
During the reign of King Mahendra, the Gorakhanātha temple underwent renovations.
The Phalcā was renovated by the Bhaktapur Development Project as the rest house was in a poor state and in need of repair.
Minor damages are related to the 2015 earthquakes. Accordingly, locals initiated the renovation of the Phalcā’s roof and base plinth.
गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामाथि काष्ठतोरण चढाइएको थियो । तोरणमा कुँदिएको अभिलेख खिइएकोले दाताको नाम पढ्न सकिँदैन ।

event_name: Offering of statues of Sāriputra and Maudagalyāyana
event_description: वज्राचार्य जिनश्वरि, परिष, जसिदेव लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर बाहाःको प्रवेशद्वार दायाँबायाँ सारिपुत्र र मौदगल्यायनका मूर्तिहरू चढाएका थिए ।
जीवनमाया तुलाधर, ज्ञानमान, राजमान लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर बाहाः अगाडि धर्मधातुजिनालय चैत्य निर्माण गरेका थिए ।
बाहाःका दिवंगत चक्रेश्वर पुष्प रत्न वज्राचार्यको सम्झनामा उनकी श्रीमती लक्ष्मी देवीले छोराहरू दिपक रत्न, दिनेस रत्न लगायत परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर अक्षोभ्यको लागि पित्तलको इलां चढाएका थिए ।

Indra Vadana, the last wife of Prime Minister Bama Bahādura Kũvara, built the temple along with asataḥ(KAT2651) to the north and a garden in close proximity. The main deity, aśivaliṅga, is revered as Indrabhakteśvara Mahādeva, named after her.

An inscription on the bell at the nearby Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa temple (KAT2640) mentions that it was offered to Indrabhakteśvara Mahādeva in 1864 CE (VS 1921). However, it appears that the bell originally dedicated to Indrabhakteśvara was later relocated to the nearby temple, likely after the early 1970s.

Fifteen years post the temple's construction, Indra Vadana established a trust, endowing it with land. This initiative aimed to facilitate the execution of daily, annual, and other periodic rituals at the temple.
The recent restoration of the temple took place in 2013 CE (VS 2071).

event_name: Construction of plinth and offering of a cākaḥdalū
event_description: Vyaṣāsĩ Jyāpu and his family members from the Guitaḥ Ṭola constructed a plinth encircling the Temple and offeredcākaḥdalū.

event_name: Suffered damages during the 1934 CE earthquakes
event_description: The Temple as well as the bell placed in front of the Temple had suffered damages during the 1934 CE (NS 1054) earthquakes.
A certain Khidavi Bhāva, his wife and sons renovated the bell (placed in front of the Temple) which had suffered damages during the 1934 CE earthquakes.

event_name: Wrapping toraṇa and main door in brass
event_description: In the memory of his father Bhimasundha (Bhīmasundara) and mother Siri (Śrī) Thaku, a certain Simicī sponsored to warp thetoraṇaand main door in brass.

Subedāra Jāiphala Adhikārī built the Hastikeśvara temple in the name of his mother Hastikā. He also built the Kālikā shrine (object no. NWK0530-012) and a rest house at the temple premises besides setting up a trust by donating land parcels.

The Department of Archaeology rebuilt the temple, along with the Kālikā shrine (object no. NWK0530-012) and the rest house following the destruction of the structures in the 2015 CE earthquakes. The reconstruction of the rest house is still underway as of May 2024 CE.

Dīpakumārī Śāha initiated the construction of this temple in memory of her late husband, Prāṇa Śāha. She was also instrumental in setting up a trust by filing a petition to Prime Minister Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā to conduct religious and cultural activities in the temple.
Following the 2015 earthquake, which damaged the temple, it was reconstructed in its original form in 2018 CE (VS 2075).

The origins of the temple's establishment have been marked by ambiguity and scholarly debate. According to theDevamālāvaṃśāvalī, a subsequent historical account, the temple's creation is attributed to the reign of King Pratāpa Malla, who is said to have erected the temple and introduced the enshrinement of the Jagannātha triad. However, this assertion has been challenged by the presence of an inscription dating back to 1563 CE (NS 683) on the Caturvyūha statue within the temple premises. This inscription provides evidence that the temple predates the era of King Pratāpa Malla, whose rule spanned from 1641 to 1674 CE.

A copperplate inscription can be seen adorning the upper part of the temple's eastern entrance. This inscription imparts a directive to thedaśanāmīascetics. The inscription emphasizes the importance of harmony and unity among the ascetics, stipulating that disputes and conflicts among them are to be unequivocally avoided. The royal command further calls for a collective commitment to peaceful coexistence and the adherence to appropriate conduct. This inscription serves as a testament to the socio-religious governance of the time, highlighting the influence of the royal authority in fostering a cohesive and disciplined spiritual community within the temple's precincts.

In the history of the temple, an event involves inscriptions found on large stone tanks along its eastern side. These inscriptions, dating back to 1654 CE (NS 774), were written by King Pratāpa Malla. In these writings, the king expresses his deep respect for various goddesses through his poetry. King Pratāpa Malla's words carry an important message: he believes that being a true scholar goes beyond reading words. He suggests that understanding and connecting with the meaning of the verses is what truly matters. He even mentions that those who can not grasp this meaning lead less meaningful lives.
The 1934 CE earthquakes caused part of the temple's upper tier to collapse. The temple was subsequently renovated to repair the damage and restore its structure.
The Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust renovated the temple and documented the inscriptions.
Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha built the Bhaktapur Burjā.
The 1934 earthquakes badly damaged the Bhaktapur Burjā.
A restoration project, coordinated with the Government of Nepal and supported by the UNESCO, renovated the Bhaktapur Burjā and three adjacent towers.
The 2015 earthquakes caused significant damage to the upper portion of the Bhaktapur Burjā.

A comprehensive restoration project, initiated in 2017 CE (VS 2074), restored the Bhaktapur Burjā and the other towers. The project received full financial and technical support from the Chinese government, with the Chinese Academy of Cultural Heritage (CACH) overseeing its execution. The restoration was completed in 2019 CE (VS 2076).
TheDyaḥchẽof Cāmuṇḍā was constructed by a group of fourteenguṭhiyāras, including Punasiṃ, theThakālīof the Cāmuṇḍā Guṭhī, and Kṛṣṇasiṃ, the secondThakālī.

event_name: Installation of iron fence around the Caitya
event_description: Nalināsiṃha Śreṣṭha installed metal bars around the Caitya for its protection.

event_name: Installation of statues of Umāmaheśvara and Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa
event_description: The inscription on the Sarasvatī statue records that a certain Jayarāma Bhāro installed Hariśaṅkara and Umāmaheśvara inside the Shrine. As mentioned above in the description, the Statue of Hariśaṅkara could not be found at the site.

During the reign of King Mānadeva (r. 464-505 CE), Ratnasaṅgha, a prominent tradesman leader (sārthavāha), consecrated theśivaliṅga, naming it Ratneśvara after himself and endowing numerous land parcels in its honor.

Aniṣkalaliṅga, an unadorned form ofśivaliṅga, was unearthed while digging the foundation for a private building located approximately 50 meters northeast of the Ratneśvara Śivaliṅga and was subsequently placed within the concrete chamber designated for the Ratneśvara Śivaliṅga. This newly foundśivaliṅgafeatured an inscription dating back to 486 CE (ŚS 407), documenting the donation of land parcels by Vimala Saṃgha, asārthavāha, for theśivaliṅgaestablished by an individual named Sutenātri (Ś. Rājavaṃśī VS 20, pp.43-56). As a result, theśivaliṅgawas named Vimaleśvara in honor of the donor Vimala Saṃgha.

ThehitiID plaque was installed by the Heritage Conservation Centre, Lalitpur Metropolitan City, and Centre for Integrated Urban Development (CUID). It is part of their project of inventorizing such heritage sites of Lalitpur.
Vāsaḥ Hiti was repaired through the initiative of Jayarāja Śreṣṭha.
PURPP (Pro-Poor Urban Regeneration Pilot Project) and Lalitpur Metropolitan City installed this introductory signboard at thehiti. Its date is not mentioned.

In 2011 CE (VS 2068), local residents, with the financial help from the Lalitpur Sub-metropolitan City, established a system to collect water into a reserve tank and to distribute it proportionately. This system is still functioning.
Thehitiwas repaired by the Lalitpur Metropolitan City with funding from the World Bank.

event_name: Construction of the Dolã Māju Shrine
event_description: The shrine of Dolã Māju must have been initially constructed in an open space. In 1704 CE (NS 824), the present-day temple was built on the same spot and developed as a shrine.

event_name: Chariot of Rāto Matsyendranātha Caught in Fire
event_description: While the chariot of Rāto Matsyendranātha was circumambulating the Mā̃simā (Mother Tree) in Lagankhel, it suddenly caught on fire which lasted for two hours. The fire did not only damage the chariot and other materials, but also the statue of the deity. The procession continued after offering a sacrifice on the spot.
Mohanavīra Siṃha and Bekhālāni from Asan, Kathmandu renovated the Nhavã Dabū.

A police station was established in the Dolã Māju premises. However, locals protested against it, arguing that it is inappropriate to set up a police station in a holy place. Thus, it was removed in 2014 CE (VS 2071).
The statue of Lokeśvara with his consort was installed over the water spout (see 'description' above).

In the 1980s, thehiticeased flowing and became buried due to prolonged neglect. A pipal tree grew on thehiti, surrounded by bushes around the spout (local resident, Śreṣṭha, male, age 66/see photo). The Ward Number 6 Office of the Shankharapur Municipality undertook the restoration of thehitiin 2021 CE.
Kvātha Nāyaka (chief of fort) Dharaṇidhara constructed the Phalcā in the style similar to Kaṣṭhamanḍapa of Kathmandu.
A statue of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa was also installed during the construction of the Phalcā by Kvātha Nāyaka (chief of fort) Dharaṇidhara.
Sevenropanīsof land were endowed to perform the annual and daily worships.

event_name: Preliminary worship for the Phalcā’s reconstruction
event_description: Preliminary worship (kṣamāpuja) was performed at the site ahead of the commencement of the Phalcā’s restoration due to take place with the financial assistance of the US Embassy. The ‘Khyālidyaḥ Saṃrakṣaṇa Guthi’, an association of the locals formed for the conservation of Khyālidyaḥ, and the Kirtipur Municipality are also involved in the reconstruction of the Phalcā that will also see the seismic strengthening of the Phalcā pavilion.

The Mahādevasthāna Pokharī along with monuments at the Jyotirliṅgeśvara Mandira complex were renovated with the financial assistance provided by organizations from the Netherlands and Vajrayogini Village Development Committee. A local organization named Friends of Sankhu had coordinated the renovation works.
Jaya Kṛṣṇa, Lanhavatī, Dhanalakṣmī, Viṣṇumatī and other family members supported the construction of the Phalcā.

In 2012, Lalitpur Metropolitan City provided financial support for Chusikānani Phalcā's reconstruction. The local community reconstructed it after dismantling the previous structure, making substantial changes to the architectural structure.
The temple was constructed by Bālakṛṣṇa Bhāro from Vonde Ṭola, during the reign of King Bhāṣkara Malla. Bālakṛṣṇa Bhāro also donated land to provide income for the upkeep of the temple.

The inscription states the name of Bālakṛṣṇeśvara and the date as the full moon day in the month of Vaiśākha, NS 832. The meaning of the inscription is not clear. This date might refer to an unknown event that happened 6 months after the temple was established.Gutschow(2011, 566) interprets this as the date of its consecration.
Jayasiṃha Maharjana of the Thathu Ṭola renovated the oldmaṇḍapain due to its dilapidated condition.

Hirālāla Jhā, Pṛṭhvīlāla Jhā, Bhairavalāla Jhā, Harṣalāla Jhā, and others covered the upper roof of the temple with gilt-copper sheets, wishing for the heavenly abode of their parents Kulānanda Jhā and Vidyālakṣmī from the Kilāgala Ṭola.
A brass threshold was installed at the main entrance of the temple.

event_name: Offering of a pair of copper flags
event_description: Māna, Kulabila, Rājamati, and Tuyu from Patan offered a pair of copper flags to the temple.
Jhakabahādura, Yajñabahādura, Jhaṅkabahādura Thāpā Kṣetrī, and Umādevī offered frill pattern carved on brass sheets to the temple.

event_name: Installation of lion statues at four corners of the temple
event_description: Sons of Tejabahādura and Lalitakumārī established a lion statue of metal on each of the four corners of the temple.

event_name: Covering of lower roof with brass sheets
event_description: King Mahendra and Queen Ratna had copper sheets placed on the lower roof of the temple.
Raviprasāda Kasaḥju, a resident of the Jyāthā Ṭola in Kathmandu, renovated the temple.
The people of Lalitpur erected this pillar in memory of the 1934 earthquake and in honour of Juddha Śamśera.

The temple was constructed by Prime Minister Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā in VS 1931 (1875 CE). In the sanctum of the temple, he installed metal statues of Satyanārāyaṇa, Sarasvatī, and Lakṣmī. On the stone pillar in front of the temple, an inscription detailing the construction of the temple is carved, and on top of the pillar, a full-sized statue of Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā is placed.
The temple was damaged in the great earthquake of 1990 VS. Therefore, it was renovated in 1992 VS.

The temple was damaged in the great earthquake of 1990 VS (1934 CE), and it was renovated two years later, in 1992 VS (1935 CE). However, Pruscha (1975, p.96) mentions that the renovation of the temple took place in 1936.
विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पमा देशको थुप्रै मठमन्दिरहरू ध्वस्त भए भने केही मन्दिरहरू जीर्ण भएका थिए । यो मन्दिरले पनि उक्त महाभूकम्पका कार ठूलो क्षति बेहोरनु पर्यो ।

विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पले ठूलो क्षति पुगेको यस मन्दिरको भित्ताहरू सबै चर्केको र छानो पनि भत्कने खतरा थियो त्यसैले विसं २०७४ (सन् २०१७) देखि पुरातत्व विभागले मन्दिरको पुनर्णिर्माण कार्य गर्न सुरु गरेको थियो । हाल (अप्रिल, २०२३) पुनर्निर्माणको कार्य अन्तिम चरणमा पुगिसकेको छ ।

event_name: Endowment of land and setting up regulations
event_description: Karavīra Pā̃ḍe, the son of an influential courtier in the late 18thcentury Dāmodara Pā̃ḍe, formed aguthiby endowing land and set up a cash fund for performing daily and anniversary rituals.

event_name: Installation of statue of Dāmodara Pā̃ḍe
event_description: Statues of Dāmodara Pā̃ḍe and his wife Ayodhyādevī are placed next to the statue of Bhagavatī inside the sanctum. Their son Karavīra Pā̃ḍe established these statues but the inscription does not mention the year of the establishment (G. Karmācārya2005, p.317).
A resident of the Tyaḥra Ṭola Dravyalāla Śreṣṭha (text: Dravyelāla Śreṣṭha) installed metal frills on the temple’s roof during the reign of King Tribhuvana.
Nārāyaṇabhakta and his wife Nārāyaṇadevī Śreṣṭha installed ceramic tiles on the floor and walls of the temple’s sanctum.
Jvālāmāī Bhajana Maṇḍala, a local group of devotional singers, collected donations and renovated the temple.
Resident of the Taumādhi Ṭola in Bhaktapur, Harṣanārāyaṇa Dhaubhaḍela (text: Dhaubhaḍī), together with his wives Nhukṣe Thakuṃ and Hirā Thakuṃ, built Harṣamukteśvara temple.

event_name: Construction of Aṣṭamātṛkā Dyaḥchẽ and sataḥ
event_description: Harṣanārāyaṇa Dhaubhaḍela built the god-house (dyaḥchẽ) with theaṣṭamātṛkādeities and asataḥ.

event_name: Establishment of Ekādaśarudra and endowment of lands
event_description: Harṣanārāyaṇa Dhaubhaḍela established 11śivaliṅgas (Ekādaśarudra) behind the temple and donated 32ropanīs of farmland to sustain daily and anniversary rituals at the Śiva temple, along with timely renovations and upkeep of the temple andsataḥ.
Harṣanārāyaṇa Dhaubhaḍela, second son of Rāmakṛṣṇa Bhani and Cakuṭi Thakuṃ of Bhaktapur’s Gālahiti Ṭola, installed a bell together with his wife Hirā Thakuṃ.
Harṣanārāyaṇa Dhaubhaḍela installed a stone inscription, recording the establishment of the temple,dyaḥchẽ, and 11śivaliṅgas, along with the formation of a trust by donating 32ropanīs of farmland.

Member of Parliament Jagadiśa Śamaśera Rāṇā allocated NRs. 250,000 from the MP Fund for the construction of aphalcānortheast of the temple. Thephalcāwas built to host singing and musical instrument performances by the Department of Music at the Kathmandu University.

This inscription dates back to the reign of King Yakṣa Malla (r. 1428–1482 CE), long before the construction of the Harṣamukteśvara temple. The inscription bears King Yakṣa Malla's name and praises his glory. The inscription was probably engraved on the pedestal when the statue of Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa (BKT0460-017) was installed. However, since part of the inscription has eroded and the lower portion is buried, the donor's name and the exact date could not be determined.
Śākyavaṃśa Rāya and Pūrṇasiṃha donated a golden door to Cakrasaṃvara and Vajravārāhī. The copper plate inscription recording this event is not accessible.

event_name: Donation of a pair of lion
event_description: A pair of lion statues were donated. These now sit in front of the main entrance to thebāhāḥ.

event_name: Repair of the image of Cakrasaṃvara
event_description: Dhanapati, his wife Vidyā, and their sons Jñānapati, Dinapati, Padmapati and Cakrapati reconstructed the statue of Cakrasaṃvara which is located in theāgamaof thebāhāḥ. The statue was painted and consecreted after a fire ritual worship was performed in which an offering of flesh was made.
Thedharmadhātu maṇḍalawas constructed inside thebāhāḥcourtyard in memory of Cakrarāja Śākya and his wife Jogamāyā Śākya's deceased family members.
Cakrarāja Śākya donated funds for the construction of the main entrance of thebāhāḥ.
See the social and religious activity above.

event_name: Consecration of the statue of the donors
event_description: Statue of Kīrtirāja and his two wives was established.

monument_name: Kani Bāhāḥ at Oku Bāhāḥ (1702 CE)
event_description: Thisvihārawas constructed by Devarāja Śākya at the same time as the images of Gaṇeśa, Mahākākla and Hanumān. The images of theāgama devatāandkvāḥpāḥdyaḥwere also consecrated at the same time.

monument_name: Kani Bāhāḥ at Oku Bāhāḥ (1702 CE)
event_name: Construction of the tower over the roof
event_description: Devarāja Śākya and his wife Manoharā constructed the cover over the roof and raised a metal flag.

monument_name: Kani Bāhāḥ at Oku Bāhāḥ (1702 CE)
event_description: A Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala was consecrated at thevihāra-courtyard by Harṣaratna, Devarāja, Dhanavīra and other family members
Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha built the Kirtipur Burjā.
The 1934 earthquakes badly damaged the Kirtipur Burjā.
A restoration project, coordinated with the Government of Nepal and supported by the UNESCO, renovated the Kirtipur Burjā and three adjacent towers.
The 2015 earthquakes caused significant damage to the upper portion of the Kirtipur Burjā.

A comprehensive restoration project, initiated in 2017 CE (VS 2074), restored the Kirtipur Burjā and the other towers. The project received full financial and technical support from the Chinese government, with the Chinese Academy of Cultural Heritage (CACH) overseeing its execution. The restoration was completed in 2019 CE (VS 2076).
Bekhārāra, Dāna, Lana Bahādura, Bhima Bahādura, Bhuyucā Kaḥmi of Hāmanani Ṭola in Balambu established the statue in the memory of their parents Narasiṃ and Nānīmāyā.

event_name: Renovation and regular maintenance of the Temple
event_description: Pūrṇa Maharjana renovated the Temple in NS 1123 (2003 CE) in the memory of his father. He is also taking care of it for the past few years.
Acaityawas constructed and land was endowed. The inscription has been lost, however, and it is not clear whichcaityawas constructed.
Siddhirāja Śākya, asaṅghamember of Guji Bāhāḥ, his wife, two sons, and three grandsons founded Siddhi Bāhāḥ.
With the financial support from the Lalitpur Metropolitan City, the Bāhāḥ courtyard was paved with bricks.

After capturing Nuwakot and consolidating his financial position, King Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha constructed the Sātatale Durbar. In the inscription installed after its completion, he proudly proclaimed that he had broken the arrogance of the kings of Nepal (the Kathmandu Valley), captured King Trivikrama Sena of Tanahũ, and slain the Muslim customs officials stationed at the checkpoint upon his return from Kāśī.पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले नुवाकोट कब्जा गरेर आफ्नो आर्थिक अवस्था सुदृढ बनाइसकेपछि साततले दरबार निर्माण गरेका थिए । दरबार बनाइसकेपछि राखिएको अभिलेखमा उनले नेपाल (काठमाडौं उपत्यका) का राजाहरूको घमण्ड तोडेको, तनहुँका राजा त्रिविक्रम सेनलाई बन्दी बनाएको र काशीबाट फर्केर आउँदा भन्सारमा बस्ने मुसलमान अधिकारीहरूलाई मारेको भनी गर्व गरेका छन् ।

event_name: Releasing funds to repair the palace roof
event_description: During repairs to the palace, King Pratāpa Siṃha Śāha sent nine rupees to thedhāmīto purchase thatch for the roof.राजा प्रतापसिंह शाहले दरबारको मर्मत गर्ने क्रममा छानाको लागि खर किन्न नौ रुपैयाँ धामीलाई पठाएका थिए ।

event_name: Developing the palace as a museum
event_description: With the aim of preserving and exhibiting historical objects, images, and other archaeological materials from the time of Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha, the Sātatale Durbar was developed as a museum. The inauguration of the museum was carried out by the then Minister for Information and Communications and government spokesperson, Gaṅgālāla Tulādhāra.पृथ्वीनारायण शाहको पालाका ऐतिहासिक सामग्री, मूर्ति र अन्य पुरातात्विक वस्तुहरूको संरक्षण र प्रदर्शन गर्ने उद्देश्यले साततले दरबारलाई संग्रहालयको रूपमा विकास गरिएको थियो । तत्कालीन सूचना तथा सञ्चार मन्त्री एवं सरकारका प्रबक्ता गंगालाल तुलाधारले संग्रहालयको उद्घाटन गर्नुभएको थियो ।

China expressed its commitment to assist in the restoration and reconstruction of Nuwakot’s heritage sites damaged by the earthquake. Accordingly, an agreement was signed between China and Nepal for the restoration of the Sātatale Durbar. On behalf of China’s Agency for International Economic Cooperation (AIEC), Zhang Fan signed the agreement, while Pitāmbara Ghimire signed on behalf of Nepal’s National Reconstruction Authority. Responsibility for the restoration was assigned to the Chinese Academy of Cultural Heritage. The agreement stipulated that the restoration would be completed within 45 months of the signing.भूकम्पले क्षति भएका नुवाकोटका सम्पदाहरूको जीर्णोद्धार र पुनर्निर्माण गर्न चीनले सहयोग गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको थियो । त्यसै क्रममा साततले दरबारको जीर्णोद्धार गर्न चीन र नेपालबीच सम्झौता भएको थियो । सम्झौतामा चीनको Agency for International Economic Cooperation (AIEC) को तर्फबाट Zhang Fan ले हस्ताक्षर गरेका थिए भने नेपालको राष्ट्रिय पुनर्निर्माण प्राधिकरणको तर्फबाट पिताम्बर घिमिरेले हस्ताक्षर गरेका थिए । जीर्णोद्धारको जिम्मेवारी चीनको Chinese Academy of Cultural Heritage लाई सुम्पिएको थियो । सम्झौता भएको ४५ महिनाभित्र दरबारको जीर्णोद्धार सम्पन्न गर्ने सम्झौता भएको थियो ।

Akṣamāpūjā(ritual of atonement) was performed prior to the restoration and reconstruction of the Sātatale Durbar and other earthquake-damaged heritage sites of Nuwakot. The ceremony was attended by Rājana Śreṣṭha, Mayor of Bidur Municipality, and Deputy Mayor Prabhā Bogaṭī, among other representatives.चीन सरकारको सहयोगमा पुनर्निर्माण भइरहेका साततले दरबार लगायतका सम्पदाहरूको जग संरक्षणको लागि भूमिपूजा गरिएको थियो ।उक्त पूजामा बिदुर नगरपालिकाका प्रमुख राजन श्रेष्ठ र उपप्रमुख प्रभा बोगटी पनि सहभागी भएका थिए ।

Abhūmipūjā(ritual to strengthen the foundation) was conducted for the foundation conservation of heritage structures being renovated the Sātatale Durbar, and the Taleju Ghara, which is being reconstructed with the support of the Government of China. The ceremony was attended by Saubhāgya Pradhānāṅga, Director General of the Department of Archaeology, Rājana Śreṇṭha, Mayor of Bidur Municipality, Deputy Mayor Prabhā Bogaṭī, and other public representatives.चीन सरकारको सहयोगमा जीर्णोद्धार भइरहेको साततले दरबार एवं पुनर्निर्माण भइरहेको तलेजु घरको जग संरक्षणको लागि भूमिपूजा गरिएको थियो । उक्त पूजामा पुरातत्त्व विभागका महानिर्देशक सौभाग्य प्रधानाङ्ग, बिदुर नगरपालिकाका प्रमुख राजन श्रेष्ठ, उपप्रमुख प्रभा बोगटी लगायत जनप्रतिनिधिहरू पनि सहभागी भएका थिए ।

event_name: Donation of a toraṇa to the esoteric deity (āgama devatā)
event_description: Tariddha (Taridhana) donated a woodentoraṇatoāgama devatāCakrasaṃvara and Vajravārāhī.
Adharmadhātu maṇḍalawas constructed between thevimba caityaand thepūrṇakalaśoparipadma caityaby Dhījamuni and his wife Beṣālakṣmī.
The Bāhāḥ was renovated after the 1934 earthquake.
There used to be two stone lions guarding the entrance. They were stolen and have not been found yet.
The temple collapsed during the 1934 earthquake.

This caitya bears no inscription, however, an inscription on the caitya to its north (BUN0016) mentions that two of the fivecaityaswere constructed at the same time. It can therefore be surmised that this monument was also commissioned by Harṣamuni Śākya in 1964.

Thecaitya(LAL1921-004) in thehitipremises has Mānadeva Era 182, which corresponds to 758 CE, inscribed on it. Other details have already eroded. The inscription probably recorded the establishment of thecaitya.

At the site of the Subāhāḥ Hiti, a merit-givingjaḥdhuṃ(water trough) was established. An inscription mentions the term "jareṃ" for thejaḥdhuṃ, which later evolved into "jaḥdhuṃ" in Nepalbhasa. Currently, no trace of thisjaḥdhuṃremains at the location. According to locals, a wall once stood east of thehiti, and thejaḥdhuṃwas attached to it.
The well was built northeast of thehiti.Only the year is inscribed without any other details.
The inscription is completely eroded and nothing can be deciphered.

In the past, when this phalcā fell into disrepair, it was rebuilt under the leadership of two brothers, Devadatta Thāpā and Relāja Thāpā. The reconstruction took place during the tenure of Rhituvaṇa Thāpā, the then pramāṇa of Thecho settlement, with the participation of local jyāpu and mālākāra communities.विगत ब्रह्मायणी देवीको अग्र भागमा भएको फल्चा जीर्ण भएकाले देवदत्त थापा र रिलाज थापा दुई दाजुभाईको अगुवाईमा थेच्व बस्तीका तत्कालीन प्रमान रीथुवण थापाको समयमा अन्य स्थानीय ज्यापु र मालाकारको सहभागितामा फल्चाको पुनर्निर्माण गरियो ।

In the 1990s, the traditional phalcā was demolished and replaced with a concrete structure. After the earthquake of 2015 CE, most of the heritage structures in the Kvaylāchi area were restored to their original forms (one of the ward members, Maharjana, male, age 32) . This phalcā was also reconstructed in its traditional style. Currently (November 2024), the reconstruction of the phalcā is underway with a budget of 6 million rupees allocated by Godāvarī Municipality.फल्चालाई सन् १९९० को दशकतिर भत्काई कंक्रिडको संरचना उठाइएको थियो । पछिल्लो भूकम्प पश्चात् क्वय्‌लाछि परिसरका धेरैजसो सम्पदाहरू पुरानै स्वरूपमा बन्दै गर्दा यो फल्चालाई पनि मौलिक स्वरूपमा फर्काइएको हो (one of the ward members, Maharjana, male, age 32) । हाल (नोवेम्बर २०२४) गोदावरी नगरपालिकाबाट छुट्याइएको ६० लाख बजेटबाट फल्चाको पुनर्निर्माण कार्य भैरहेको छ ।

This was a historical site with a remnant of a traditionalphalcāprior to the construction of the current structure, as stated in the 'description' above. As part of the current heritage revival movement, the Kirtipur Metropolitan City built it based on the memory (of the plinth) of local elders. The foundation stone was laid on the 26th of Phālguna in 2022 CE ((VS 2078). The building took seven months to complete.
Pruscha (1975, p.19) mentions that the temple was constructed in 1679 CE. However, he does not refer to any sources (see ‘description’ above for more information).
The inscription embossed on the eaves fascia of the lower roof from VS 1996 informs us that the Temple was renovated in 1939 CE.
Prakāśaratna Mānandhara, Renukā, Pratibhā, Pratimā, and Pralitā jointly offered amaṇḍalāto Gaṇesa.

event_name: Offering of copper sheets for the maintenance of the temple
event_description: The inscription records only the date of this event. According to the caretaker of the temple, a local resident had offered copper sheets to repair the roof of the temple.
A person named Mohana Ḍhevāju and his wife Saritā offered the bronze bell to Gaṇeśa in memory of his parents Jhalaka Bahādura and Bhima Māyā Ḍhevāju.
A Tāmrākāra family offered thepatāḥto the temple in 2007 CE (VS 2064). Since the inscription is not legible, the name(s) of the family remain obscure.

event_name: Installation of brass repousse on wooden toraṇa
event_description: On the brass inscription, only the name and address (Vimalā Vaidya, VS 2067/06/21) are mentioned. According to thedyaḥpāḥlāḥ, it is the record of brass repousse on the woodentoraṇaof the sanctum.
A person named Candramāna and his wife Saritā Maharjana, the son and daughter-in-law of Cakrapāna and Satyadevī Maharjana offered the brass repousse of Gaṇeśa.

event_name: Repousse the statue of the Gaṇeśa with brass
event_description: Candramān and Saritā Maharjana, the son and daughter-in-law of Cakrapāna and Satyadevī Maharjana have offered the repousse of brass on the statue of the Gaṇeśa.
The caretakes of the Temple Candramāna and Saritā Maharjana jointly renovated the stone statue of the Bhagavatī statue.
The son of Macākāji and Maṃgalamāyā, Nilakaṇṭha had done the repousse on the stone lion of the sanctum.
The son of Macākāji and Maṃgalamāyā, Nilakaṇṭha had done the repousse on the stone lion of the sanctum.

event_name: Beautifying and placing tiles in the Mandira
event_description: The dyaḥpāla, Puṣpa Ratna Maharjana had beautified by placing tiles inside the Mandira.
Due to erosion of the inscription the context could not be read.
Due to erosion of the inscription the context could not be read.
Originally, the roof of thedyaḥchẽwas tiled withjhĩgaṭī.After it started leaking, the aforementioned Vajrācārya family replaced it with corrugated pewter sheets in or after 2001 CE.

The Bhoṭes, who are of Tibetan origin, forcibly opened the door of the Vajrayoginī Temple and stole the jewelry belonging to the deity. Upon discovering the theft, Priest Bābudeva reported the incident to King Amṛta Malla, who took action and successfully apprehended the thieves. As a part of purification process, a ritual was performed since the thieves had touched the statue of the deity.

King Pratāpa Malla initiated the construction of the temple and allocated lands for aguthito oversee the daily rituals at the site. Although the inscription documenting this event does not explicitly specify the architectural style of the temple, it does reference an annual tradition of applying lime to the temple on the full moon day of Caitra. Given that lime coatings are unnecessary for tiered temples, this suggests that the temple erected by Pratāpa Malla followed theśikharastyle. The inscription is divided into two separate steles, with the first one  positioned north of the Jogeśvara Mandira, and the second one affixed to the west-facing wall of the Jogeśvara Mandira.

event_name: Offering pinnacle to the later temple
event_description: A later reconstruction of the Temple, dated to 1670 CE (NS 790), included the installation of a finial. However, it is unlikely that a finial was added just 15 years after the initial construction of the Temple in 1655 CE. It is possible that the Temple was rebuilt prior to the addition of the finial, but there are no historical sources available to confirm this hypothesis.

The process of repairing and repainting the face of Vajrayoginī began on the 11th day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, with the removal of her vital essence from the statue. This event, known as (Nev.)lãpu chāygu,lasted for a month until life was ritually placed back into the statue on the 11th day of the bright fortnight of Caitra.

Jayadharma and Ugramāla Malla presented King Pratāpa Malla with 398tolāsof sterling silver and 229tolāsof pure silver as a contribution towards making atoraṇa. It is likely that the silver was deposited at the temple by various devotees on separate occasions as offerings to the deity.
King Pratāpa Malla offered a goldentoraṇato Vajrayoginī. A silvertoraṇamade out of the silver deposited at the Temple was also offered to the deity on the same occasion.
A special ritual for auspiciousness was performed after the blue lotus on the left hand of Vajrayoginī was broken.
During the reign of King Nṛpendra Malla, the vital essence of of Vajrayoginī was removed from her statue to repair and repaint her face.

The Vajrayoginī Temple experienced strange noises resembling the sound of large utensils falling, but the source of the noises could not be determined. King Pārthivendra Malla was notified of the incident, and a special ritual for auspiciousness was performed in response.
The vital essence of Vajrayoginīwas removed from the statue to repair and repaint her face.

The Gũ Bāhāḥ premises were struck by lightning. Fortunately, the priest of the temple was unharmed as he lay prostrate on the ground. However, when the Temple's door was opened the following day, soot marks were observed on the statue of temple andits left earring (kuṇḍala).
Thecakrainstalled on the northern side of theśikhara-style (granthakūṭa) Temple of Vajrayoginī fell off.
Naka Mayaju, Queen of King Pārthivendra Malla, offered atoraṇato Vajrayoginī along with utensils required for the worship of the deity.
The vital essence was removed from the statue of Vajrayoginī to repair and repaint her face.
The inscription at the Vajrayoginī Temple is eroded, making it unclear what event took place there.Something was done at the Vajrayoginī Temple.

event_name: Converting Śikharakūṭa temple into tiered temple

King Amṛta Malla had commissioned the construction of asataḥat the Sālkhā Ṭola and donated many plots of land to feed ascetics from foreign lands at the Sataḥ (N. YogīVS 2012, p. 61-62). The King got the Sataḥ made in the name of his deceased wife Lakṣmīdevī and two of his late sons Abhayasiṃha and Kṛṣṇasiṃha, along with his daughters-in-law Jayatudevī, Phikudevī, and Herādevī. A line of an inscription installed at the Sataḥ refers to Śaṅkarapaṭṭana (Sankhu) as the capital city, suggesting that Sankhu also became a capital city in the medieval period. Statues of Viṣṇu and Lakṣmī carved on a single stone is placed atop thejalaharīthat contains this Inscription. The Statue also contains a one-line inscription that refers to the figure of Lakṣmī as Lakṣmīdevī, the wife of King Amṛta Malla, and Viṣṇu as the King’s son Abhayasiṃha. The figure of Lakṣmī appears larger than that of Viṣṇu to highlight the greater importance of the mother in comparison to the son. The portrayal of Lakṣmī as the mother of Viṣṇu in the Statue is interesting, as the Hindu mythology considers Lakṣmī as Viṣṇu’s consort. It also reveals that there was a tradition of installing statues of deities based on their iconography but referring to them as one’s family members. Another interesting object present at the Sataḥ is a stone palm exhibiting theabhayamudrā. An inscription on the back of the Palm outlines the activities to be carried out by the respectiveguthiannually.N. YogīVS 2012, p. 62 refers to this inscription asdātṛhastābhilekha(lit. the inscription on the donor’s palm).

Lo Gekhar's foundation is recorded in the Pema Katang (pad+ma bka’ thang ), a text containing the biography of Padmasambhava, the teacher credited with taming of local deities across the Himalayas. This text was discovered by the treasure revealer Orgyen Lingpa (o rgyan gling pa; b. 1323), his date thus providing a terminus ante quem for the original temple. The relevant account is found in canto 62, recording the completion of Samyé Monastery, and is translated as follows (with explanatory additions in square brackets):“At Lobo [= Mustang], the place which is as if a rakṣasī [a demoness] were lying on her back,place on her heart a monastery with nine floors,a stupa on her navel,another small and black one on her head,and one hundred and eight on her four limbs!In Malgro is the naga king called Shines in Malgro [= mal gro gzi can ].He has great influence in Tibet;I will establish for him a naga treasure; I want his life philtre [= srog chu - life water]."And the Guru came along into Malgro.Keeping his promise, shaking the depths, giving solid explanations,and having given treasure and a place of worship for the nagas, he received the life philtre.However, no oath bound the mind of the nagas, so to keep them silent,he erected at Lobo the monastery of White Virtue [= dge dkar, Gekar].”Accordingly, Lo Gekhar is this monastery of White Virtue, and the surrounding chörten and springs are part of the holy site. This account also explains why Lo Gekhar is of great cultural and religious importance to the Mustang region and to Tibetan Buddhism at large. The temple is frequently visited by pilgrims from the region and beyond.
In 1956 Snellgrove visited Upper Mustang and recorded a detailed description of Lo Gekar in his bookHimalayan Pilgrimage.

His daughters—Kumārī, Devamatī, Mayajumatī, and Māyā—endowed land asguthifor the deity’s maintenance. The income from thisguṭhīwas designated to fund the monthly lighting of lamps in the name of the Mānandhara family. This same Bhīmasiṃha Mānandhara had earlier, in 1846 CE (NS 967), financed the gilding of the temple’s uppermost roof using his Tibetan trade earnings.भिमसिंन मानन्धर (भीमसिंह मानन्धर) ले लोकेश्वरको लागि नागले ओढाइएको, भित्र सुन राखिएको तायो नाम गरेको गहना चढाएका थिए । उनले लोकेश्वरलाई मोहरको माला, ढलोटको पानस, चाँदीमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको ल्हासाबाट ल्याइएको जन्तर पनि चढाएका थिए । उनका छोरीहरू - कुमारी, देवमति, मयजुमति र मायाले लोकेश्वरलाई जग्गा गुठी राखिदिएका थिए । उक्त गुठीको आयस्ताले भिमसिंन मानन्धरको परिवारको नाममा महिनाको एकपटक बत्ती बाल्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । यी उनै भीमसिंह मानन्धर हुन् जसले नेसं ९६७ (सन् १८४६) मा तिब्बत व्यापारबाट कमाएको पैसाले मन्दिरको सबभन्दा माथिल्लो छानामा राखिएको झिङ्गटीको ठाउँमा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको छाना राखिदिएका थिए ।
A group of five donors offered another bell (BKT0570-003) to the Lokeśvara temple.पाँचजनाको समूहले लोकेश्वर मन्दिरमा घण्टा (BKT0570-003) चढाएका थिए ।

Śākyabhikṣu Buddhācārya Suśu, together with his wife Rājakumārī and other family members, donated a metal lion figure (BKT0570-006).शाक्यभिक्षु बुद्धाचार्य सुषुले श्रीमती राजकुमारी लगायत परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर धातुको सिंह (BKT0570-006) चढाएका थिए ।

Śākyabhikṣu Buddhācārya Suśu, with his wife Rājakumārī and family, also offered another metal lion image (BKT0570-007).शाक्यभिक्षु बुद्धाचार्य सुषुले श्रीमती राजकुमारी लगायत परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर धातुको सिंह (BKT0570-007) चढाएका थिए ।

Kṛṣṇa Bahādura and his brother Kājī Bahādura Mānandhar established a field asguṭhīso that thejugīs could receive payment for playing instruments during the temple’s morningnityapūjāand eveningāratī. The income from this field was also to cover ritual bathing of Lokeśvara withpañcāmṛtaon auspicious festival days, especially duringBiskāḥ. Any remaining funds were to be spent on communal feasting for thedāphā bhajanaensemble.कृष्ण बहादुर, उनका भाइ काजी बहादुर मानन्धरले मिलेर लोकेश्वर मन्दिरमा बिहान नित्यपूजा गर्दा र बेलुकी आरती दिँदा जुगीहरूले बाजा बजाउनको लागि खेत गुठी राखिदिएका थिए । खेतको आम्दानीले बाजा बजाउने जुगीहरूलाई पारिश्रमिक दिने, बिस्का:को क्रममा देवताहरूलाई सगुन प्रदान गरिने दिनमा लोकेश्वरलाई पञ्चामृतले स्नान गराउनुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । त्यति गरिसकेपछि यदि पैसा बचेको खण्डमा दाफा भजनले भोज खुवाएर उक्त पैसा खर्च गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो ।

Samantarāja, a resident of Khaumā Ṭola, together with his wife Putalī, son Munirāja, and other family members, erected a column with acaityain front of the temple. They also endowed oneropanīof land asguṭhīto ensure the performance of daily and annual worship at thecaitya.खौमा टोल निवासी समन्तराजले श्रीमती पुतलि, छोरा मुनिराज लगायत परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर मन्दिरअगाडि चैत्यसहितको स्तम्भ स्थापना गरेका थिए । उनीहरूले स्तम्भमाथि रहेको चैत्यको नित्यपूजा र वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गर्न एक रोपनी खेत पनि गुठी राखिदिएका थिए ।

Mohanamayā Vajrācārya of Caturbrahmā Mahāvihāra (BKT0400), Bhaktapur, with her son Herāratna, daughter-in-law Aṣṭamāyā, and other relatives, sponsored the stone paving of the temple courtyard.भक्तपुरको चतुर्ब्रह्म महाविहार (BKT0400) निवासी मोहनमाया वज्राचार्यले छोरा हेरारत्न, बुहारी अष्टमाया लगायत परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर मन्दिरमा ढुङ्गा छापेकी थिइन् ।

event_name: Covering doors with brass plates and gilding toraṇa
event_description: Jugalakṣmī Buddhācārya (probably Jagatlakṣmī Buddhācārya) together with her sons Dharmarāja and Herārāja, and other family members, sheathed the three ground-floor doorways of the temple with brass plates and overlaid thetoraṇasabove them with gilded metal.जुगालक्ष्मी बुधाचाजे (जगतलक्ष्मी बुद्धाचार्य हुनुपर्ने) ले छोराहरू धर्मराज, हेराराज लगायत परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर मन्दिरको भुइँतलामा रहेका तीनवटा ढोकामा पित्तलको पाताले मोडिदिएका थिए । त्यसैबेला ती ढोकामाथि रहेका तोरणहरूमा सुनको मोलम्बा पनि लगाइएको थियो ।

Dharmarāja Buddhācārya, together with his mother Jagatlakṣmī, renovated thephalchā(BKT0570-018) on the north side of the temple in memory of his late father Harṣamāna. The accompanying inscription repeats that one year earlier, in 1932 CE (VS 1989), three of the five ground-floor doorways had been fitted with gildedtoraṇasand covered with brass plates.धर्म्मराज बुधाचार्य्यले आमा जगतलक्ष्मीसँग मिलेर दिवंगत बुबा हर्षमानको सम्झनामा मन्दिरको उत्तरपट्टि रहेको फल्चा (BKT0570-018) जीर्णोद्धार गरिदिएका थिए । जीर्णोद्धार गर्दा राखिएको शिलापत्रमा एक वर्षअगाडि विसं १९८९ (सन् १९३२) मा मन्दिरको भुइँतलामा रहेका पाँचवटा ढोकामध्ये तीनवटा ढोकामाथि सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको तीनवटा तोरण चढाएको र ती तीनवटै ढोकामा पित्तलको पाताले मोडिदिएको कुरा पनि दोहोर्‍याइएको छ ।

To ensure the temple’s security, iron railings were installed around the precinct through public donations. A copperplate affixed during this work records the popular belief that when King Narendra Deva’s wish to install Buṅgadyah in Bhaktapur could not be fulfilled, his son Varadeva established Padmanātha Lokeśvara there in Kaliyuga 500 CE (3601), naming the monasteryJētavarṇa Vihāra.मन्दिरको सुरक्षाको लागि चन्दा उठाएर वरिपरि फलामे बार लगाइएको थियो । फलामे बार लगाउँदा राखिएको ताम्रपत्रमा बुङ्गद्य:लाई भक्तपुरमा स्थापना गर्ने राजा नरेन्द्रदेवको इच्छा पूरा नभएकोले उनका छोरा वरदेवले कलिगत सम्वत् ३६०१ (सन् ५००) मा भक्तपुरमा पद्मनाथ लोकेश्वर स्थापना गरी जेतवर्ण विहार नाम राखिदिएको लोकविश्वास पनि कुँदिएको छ ।

Ratnamuni Śākya, grandson of Harṣajyoti Śākya of Khaumā Bāhāḥ, Bhaktapur, and son of Candrajyoti Śākya, together with his wife Degulakṣmī Śākya, offered apatāḥ(ritual banner) to the temple.भक्तपुर खौमा बाहा: निवासी हर्षज्योति शाक्यका नाति, चन्द्रज्योति शाक्यका छोरा रत्नमुनि शाक्यले श्रीमती देगुलक्ष्मी शाक्यसँग मिलेर मन्दिरमा पता: चढाएका थिए ।

Budhācārya Kuberasiṃ, together with his wife Dhaṃlāni and other family members, installed a coppertoraṇaabove the inner door leading to the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagṛha).बुधाचार्य कुबेरसिंले श्रीमती धंलानि सहित परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने भित्रपट्टिको ढोकामाथि तामाको तोरण चढाएका थिए ।

Mānabira Siṃ, with his son Sukumā and daughter Tavdhi, and other relatives, dedicated anāsana(pedestal) for the image of Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara.मानबिरसिंले छोरा सुकुमां, छोरी तवधिक लगायत परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर पद्मपाणि लोकेश्वरको लागि आसन चढाएका थिए ।

Kabiṃnarasiṃ and his wife Mati Thakuṃ, along with their family, offered a pair of brasskhasipanels on both sides of the inner doorway of the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagṛha).कबिंनरसिं र उनकी श्रीमती मति थकुंले परिवारका सदस्यहरूसँग मिलेर गर्भगृहको भित्रपट्टिको ढोकाको दायाँबायाँ पित्तलको पाताले मोडिएको खसि चढाएका थिए ।
The 2015 earthquakes left the Phalcā with multiple cracks.

The Phalcā was recently rebuilt with the fund provided by the Shankharapur Municipality. The Suntvāḥ Ṭola Sudhara Samiti, a local committee formed for the conservation of the area, had also contributed some money that was insufficient for the reconstruction.

monument_name: Dugaṃ Bahī Gaṇeśa Mandira (built ca. 19th Cent.)
event_description: The government renovated the Temple in 1986 CE. A photograph published in the inventory of C. Pruscha 1975, p.27 (see, the photo above) shows its original state before the renovation.

Prajāpati Jeta, Amita, and Dhana, among others, collectively built aphalcarest house for their lineage deity Viśvakarmā to the east of the temple. Thephalcāmention in this inscription is the god-house (dyaḥchẽ) east of the temple. Thedyaḥchẽwas previously aphalcāand was dismantled in 1988 CE (VS 2045) to be converted into adyaḥchẽ, which has now been rented out.

The Aṣṭamī Sevā Guthi, a religious trust of 28 people including the guru of the Jyāthā Ṭola Devānanda Prajāpati, senior Tuisiṃ, and manager Visuṃdla, constructed another rest house (sataḥ) in front of the temple.
Beṣāsiṃha, Dhanaontasiṃha, Dhanasiddhi, and others built anotherphalcaand installed an inscription bearing their own figures.

A donor erected a rest house (phalcā) in memory of his late father, Mahaṃtasī, and dedicated it to him, his mother, wife, and son, with prayers for their eternal peace. The donor's name was unfortunately illegible, as it was obscured by concrete.

event_name: Establishment of new statue of Viśvakarmā
event_description: Matyaṃsiṃ Prajāpati and his wife, Manamati, along with their sons and grandsons, replaced the old, worn-out statue of Viśvakarmā with a new one, wishing for the eternal peace of their deceased family members. They also established a religious trust with land and money for the statue’s anniversary rituals.

event_name: Repair of the statue of Viśvakarmā
event_description: The Digusivā Guthi, a religious trust responsible for serving the Prajāpati community's lineage deity, headed by Cidhisiṃha, renovated the dilapidated statue of Viśvakarmā and gilded it. The statue was taken around the city before being established inside the sanctum.
The Pañcadāna Guthi of the Prajāpatis in Jyāthā, with financial assistance from the Kathmandu Metropolitan City, renovated the dilapidated temple.

A bell offered by Mānakumārī and others is kept in front of the temple. The iron grill covering the bell for protection makes a reader difficult to read the inscription. One name that could be read is 'Mānakumārī'.

monument_name: Bhājaṅgala Lvahaṃ Degaḥ East (built in 1684 CE)
event_description: Rāmakṛṣṇa Bhāro and a group of individuals constructed the temple by establishing Goddess Bhairavī as their patron deity. Alongside the temple's construction, they dedicated tworopanīsof land at Namkhvāḥcā, located south of the temple. This land was intended for conducting the temple's anniversary rituals on the full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa. The inscription also includes a provision directing concerned individuals to allocate a sum of 1mohararupaiyā̃and 10dāmasfrom the earnings for future renovations of the temple.

monument_name: Bhājaṅgala Lvahaṃ Degaḥ East (built in 1684 CE)
event_description: Due to the deteriorating condition of the temple, community members gathered a total of NRs. 3,666 and offered their voluntary labor to initiate the temple's renovation. Their efforts encompassed not only the restoration of the temple but also the construction of a brick plinth for its foundation.
Śilpakāra Muni Rāja, his elder son Kṛṣṇa Rāja and family made thisdharmadhātu maṇḍala.
Śilpakāra Sukha Bhāju and his wife Rāj Māyā donated this bell.

monument_name: Misā Hiti (probably built during the Licchavi period)
event_name: Repair of the hiti and construction of the caitya (LAL1051-015)
event_description: A certain Suvarṇakāra Jasarāja Brahma and his two wives renovated thehitiand also constructed acaitya(LAL1051-015) during the reign of King Jagajjyoti Malla.

monument_name: Misā Hiti (probably built during the Licchavi period)
event_name: Establishment of a pair of lions
event_description: A pair of lions were was established to the west of thecaitya(LAL1051-016).

monument_name: Misā Hiti (probably built during the Licchavi period)
event_description: Members of the community renovated the waterspouts and the retaining walls.
The bell was offered in the memory of Babulāla Upretī and Santakumārī Upretī.
Jagatanārāyaṇa Kāyastha and other people jointly offered a brass roof along with a pinnacle to the Bhagavatī.
Maheśa Māna Siṃha Daṃgola beautified three side-walls of the Temple with marble stone in the memory of his parents.
Aguthiassociated with the Temple renovated it by collecting funds from locals.
In the memory of his parents, Maheśa Māna Siṃha Daṃgola installed statues of Gaṇeśa and Kumāra, which are flanking the entrance to the sanctum.
A person called Dr. Rājeśa Gautama and his family members offered a brass statue of Bhagavatī in the name of his parents.
A person named Rohita Mānandhara offered a brass face of Bhagavatī in the name of his grandmother Rāmadevī Mānandhara.
Theguṭhīmembers collected funds and deposited (as fix-deposit) into a bank for a long tern sustainability and maintenance of the Temple.
The Bāhāḥ was renovated by Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan city.

event_name: Addition of the Mānes (Turning prayer wheels)
event_description: Sānu Keśarī Tāmrākāra donated the twomānes(prayer wheels) which now flank the Dharmadhātuin memory of her late husband Mohanadāsa Tāmrākāra.
The Dharmadhātu was commissioned by Kṛṣṇadāsa, Premkumārī and other family members as mentioned in the inscription from NS 1089.
Sānu Keśarī Tāmrākāra donated an oil-lamp balustrade in memory of her late husband Mohanadāsa Tāmrākāra.
The Bāhāḥ was renovated by Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan city.

Ancient inscription carved on the entablement of the temple, to the right above the door.Yogi Naraharinath mentions an inscription of Udhyot Chand dated of ŚS 1313 (1391 CE) (Naraharinath 1956, p. 208, cited inSharma 2012, p. 67). It is currently unclear whether this is the inscription in question.

event_name: Replacing clay statue with stone one
event_description: Previously, the sanctum of thebāhāḥhoused a clay statue of Akṣobhya. However, when this clay statue became damaged, Dānamāyā Vajrācārya replaced it with a new statue made of stone, preserving the representation of Akṣobhya within the sanctum.

The base plinth of the Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (object number KAT1440-005) located in front of thebāhāḥbears an inscription accompanied by carved statues of seven individuals. These individuals are identified as Dasanārāṃ, Budhalnana (possibly Budharatna?), Rakṣmitārā, Budhamāyā, Bisunuprabhā, Māyādevi, and Choti. However, the inscription itself does not provide any further information regarding their role or relationship to thecaitya. It remains unclear whether these individuals were the donors of thecaityaor if thecaityawas established in their memory.

Up until the mid-1970s, thebāhāḥ-dyaḥchẽ(god house) retained its traditional architectural elements, which included a three-story main building featuring a tile roof and a small balconied tower known as apula. The roof was supported by intricately carved struts. Around 2007 CE, thebāhāḥunderwent reconstruction, resulting in its present-day form (see 'description' section above).

event_name: Construction of a capāḥ and endowment of lands
event_description: Mahantasiṃ Bhāro from the Nhulache Nani at the Indulācheṭolain Devapattana built a rest house (capāḥ) south of the Piṅgalāmāī shrine in the name of his mother Padmāvati. He also endowed tworopanīs of land in the name of Vajreśvarī, another name for Piṅgalāmāī.
Parikṣitamāna Rājabhaṇḍārī offered 34 pieces ofdalūlamps in memory of his deceased parents Gaṇeśamāna and Ratnamāyā Rājabhaṇḍārī.
Ratnalāla Karmācārya and his family members offered 108 pieces ofdalūlamps at the shrine.

event_name: Initial construction, land endowment and formation of guthi
event_description: Bhāgīsiṃha Bhāro (Amātya) and his brother Siddhisiṃha Bāro jointly sponsored the initial construction of the Phalcā and Jaḥdhuṃhiti in memory of their father Manoharasiṃha Bhāro. They had also endowed sixropanīsof land and formed aguthito continue annual and other rituals at the Phalcā.

The Department of Archaeology reconstructed Sāḥgaḥ Mandaḥ Phalcā in 2008 CE under the leadership of Sukra Sagar Shrestha (Shokoohy and others2014, p. 162). Before it was rebuilt, only a square plinth along with theśivaliṅga andjaḥdhuṃhad persisted for decades, but no other remnants of the older strcuture.

monument_name: Sera stone inscription of Ripu Malla (early 14th century)
event_description: Transliteration of the inscription, based on Y. Naraharinath's reading (1956) and direct observation.1. Oṃ maṇi padme hum||ripu[malla] … (Tibetan)2. …ripumalla rājaranī(ti)…lekośa3. …likhapitā 1 nirjitāhitapakṣeṇa ripumallenabhūbhu4.sādhanījinakatvā…ripumalla cirajya||lekanathapadadhyānalavu5.ratnatrayāmidhā||likhitāripumallena vi… sarvāth sādhanī

Gönpa Gang (dgon pa sgang), its full original name being Göngang Künzang Chöling (dgon sgang kun bzang chos gling) was built by Künzang Longyang (kun bzang klong yangs; 1644–1696) in memory of his brother between 1684 and 1695. (see Harrison, Luczanits, Ramble 2018: 55).On the founder and his teacher, Orgyen Pelzang (o rgyan dpal bzang; 1617–1677) see Ehrhard 2013a: 207–10, and Harrison, Luczanits, Ramble 2018: 101–116. Details about the construction are revealed in the founder’s autobiography summarised by Ramble.
The autobiography of Künzang Longyang recounting the author's decicion to found Künzang Chöling (Gönpa Gang)

Two stone statues of the gatekeepers flanking the entrance to the sanctum were installed in 1668 CE. Since the inscriptions inscribed on the pedestals of the gatekeeper statues are eroded, their contents remain unclear.

event_name: Installation of Umāmaheśvara statue (see object number THK0010-010 above)
event_description: The inscription mentions that Rāmacandra Duvāra Bhāro, Pāṇḍava Duvā Bhāro and Acintana Bhāro jointly installed this statue . It also records some ritual instructions to be followed.

An inscription has been inscribed on the pedestal of the donor statue (B) [see object number THK0010-009 above]. Since large part of the inscription is eroded, only its date can be read. However, we can assume that the inscription records the installation of this donors’ statue and offering(s) to the Temple made by them.
Gaṃgārāma Bhārodha, Mādhava Duvāra Bhāro, Candra Rāma Bhāya, Rāmsāhi Duvāra jointly formed the Pūrṇamāsī Guthi.

event_name: Offering of a stone pinnacle to the shrine of Mahālakṣmī in the sanctum
event_description: The stone pinnacle of the Mahālakṣmī Shrine in the sanctum contains an inscription. Since only the date is inscribed there, we can assume that this date refers to the offering of the pinnacle.

event_name: Offering of bell (object ID number THK0010-004)
event_description: The content of the inscription inscribed on the stone bell stand is not clear. However, we can assume that it records the offering of the bell with its stone stand to the Temple.
In memory of Caita Bahādura Śreṣṭha, his son Nārāyaṇa Praśāda and daughter Nārāyaṇa Devī offered this bell to the Mahālakṣmī Mandira.
This inscription is badly damaged thus, its date and content could not be identified.
This inscription inscribed on the pedestal of the donors’ statue (see object ID number THK0010-008 above), too, is badly eroded. Therefore, its date and content also remain unidentified.
This inscription found nearby the Gaṇeśa Shrine is also completely damaged.
Aguthiwas established by Jayānanda, his wife Candra Lakṣmī and their son Pṛthvīpati when the Caitya was consecrated for annual worship. Theguthidonated 4ropanīland in Mhayakhu, and 3ropanīin Balama.

event_name: Offering a pair of stone lions
event_description: Nāti Karṇamāna, son of Kermāna (Keharamāna) offered a pair of lions with his wife Herāmāyā and other family members.
Kājimāna, along with his son Astamāna and daughter Āstamāyā, offered dalūcā around the caitya (KAT2460-005).

Lakṣmī Kumārī from Kṛtipunya Vajradhātucaitya Mahāvihāra had established a Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya inside the bahī premises. In order to observe annual worship of the caitya on the 14th day of the bright fortnight of jyeṣṭha, an arrangements have been made for income.

Sānumāyā, Motimāyā, Mohanamāyā and others jointly consecrated a Dharmadhātujinālaya Caitya (KAT2460-006) in the memory of their grandfather Kājīmāna, father keharamāna and other deceased family members.

Cidhi, Juju, Muni and their mother Bha Thakuṃ had jointly offered carved stone toraṇa with Hariharihariharivāhana Lokeśvara and other deities over the entrance to the sanctum. Together they offered carved pylons to Lokeshwar and other deities.
Bhakta Bahādura Tāmrākāra, a resident of Taṃgala Ṭola, repaired the bell offered by Jagadvīpeśvarī. In doing so, he wished for the late Keśarīmāyā Tāmrākāra to find enlightenment.
The temple was commissioned in 1860 by Jagata Śamaśera, one of the brothers of Prime Minister Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā.
The empty stone plate was probably made to inscribe a certain event.
Jagadvīpeśvarī, the wife of Jagata Śamaśera’s eldest son, offered this bell to the temple.
As mentioned in the description, adjacent to the spout is the resting place (cautāro), which bears an inscription recording its construction by a certain Narendra Bahādura Khaḍkā Magara.

monument_name: Cilancva Phalcā South (built around the 19th cent.)
event_name: Theft of silver jewels and new offering
event_description: The silver jewels worn by the Nāmasaṅgīti statue were stolen at the beginning of 2022 CE (VS 2079). As a result, the descendants of late Maṅgalalāla and Sunamāyā Maharjana offered the missing items.

event_name: Addition of Stone Lions and Śārdūlas
event_description: The inscription which records the name of the founder of this temple also mentions the installation of the lions and Śārdūla statues flanking the main entrance, and thetoraṇacrowning the wooden windows. According to this inscription, an individual named Balirāma was the chief to execute this installation task, and he was assisted byKvāṭhanāyakaKāśīrāma Bābu, Dharaṇīdhara,KvāṭhanāyakaViśvarāma Bhāro[1], and Hākudeva.Footnotes^He constructed the Umāmaheśvara temple in Kirtipur (seeKIR0006).

event_name: Construction of a Phalcā, Installation of a Viṣṇu Statue, and Land Grant
event_description: This inscription is not related to this temple. It records the initial construction of aphlalcāin the south-eastern corner of the temple by a person called Mādhava Siṃha Kājī and his wife Padminī (text: Padumini). It also mentions that the founders of thephalcāinstalled a Viṣṇu statue in it and granted some plots of land to finance the annual rituals during the Indrajātrā Festival. Thephalcāwas incorporated into a private house in around 1987 CE, and the inscription was then shifted inside this temple.

This inscription which is kept inside the sanctum of this temple is also not related to it. According to the local elders, the inscription used to be kept inside thephalcāwhich was built in front of this temple. Following the collapse of thephalcā,[1]the inscription was shifted to its present-day place. It records the renovation of thephalcā,installation of an Umāmaheśvara statue inside it, and land grant to finance its annual rituals byKvāṭhanāyakaDṛṣṭirāja.Footnotes^They could recall the exact date when it collapsed.

Kājīmāna Pradhāna rebuilt the temple between 1920 and 1921 CE. The reconstruction work was supervised by Bahādura Vajrācārya, who was also responsible for rebuilding theSātatale Darabāra'Seven Storey Palace' in Nuwakot after the earthquake in 1934 CE.
The temple was renovated in 1999 CE.

The inscription in the sanctum records that Lakṣasiṃha and his brother, the sons of Śukrasiṃha Bhāro, established the statue during the reign of King Śivasiṃhadeva. It also reveals that the main settlement of Nuwakot was formerly known as Brahmanagara, and Jagatasiṃha Bhāro served as the main administrative officer (pramāna) of the region at that time.The inscription is edited in D. Gajendrarāja Devakoṭā from Gorkha offered the bell to the temple.
The current temple structure, featuring a metal roof, underwent reconstruction over a span of four years from 2010 to 2014, funded by local communities.
